full_text:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has commissioned a demonstration network that distributes a secure, tamper-resistant Indian Standard Time (IST) signal using "White Rabbit" precision timing technology, a move aimed at reducing dependence on foreign timing sources for critical infrastructure.
The network, launched at the Regional Reference Standard Laboratory (RRSL) in Bengaluru, is part of the government's broader "One Nation, One Time" initiative and has been developed jointly by the department of consumer affairs, CSIR-national physical laboratory (CSIR-NPL) and Isro.
What does it mean?
The project is aimed to provide a single, indigenous and highly accurate time source for sectors where even microsecond-level differences matter, including banking, stock markets, telecom networks, power grids and transportation.
Currently, many digital systems rely on foreign satellite-based timing services such as GPS for synchronisation. The government says an indigenous time dissemination network will make these services more secure and resilient by reducing dependence on external sources.
The system distributes Indian Standard Time, traceable to India's official time-keeping authority UTC (NPLI), using White Rabbit technology, an advanced precision timing protocol capable of delivering highly accurate synchronisation.
The government believes this will improve the reliability of financial transactions, telecom services and power systems while strengthening cybersecurity and protecting critical infrastructure from disruptions.
As part of the project, the department of consumer affairs, CSIR-NPL, Isro, Sebi, the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and BSNL have successfully completed a verification test of secure time transmission between the Bengaluru laboratory and NSE's Chennai facility.

NEW DELHI: Medical colleges across the country will now decide faculty appointments and promotions on their own, with the National Medical Commission (NMC) ending routine eligibility clearances. Only exceptional cases involving regulatory ambiguity will be taken up by the regulator for a fee of Rs 25,000 plus GST.
The decision comes after it was observed that a large number of requests from faculty members, medical colleges, universities and NBEMS-accredited hospitals were being referred to it despite the Medical Institutions (Qualifications of Faculty) Regulations, 2025, clearly laying down the qualifications, teaching experience, research publication and training requirements for teaching posts. Officials said the responsibility for deciding whether a candidate is eligible for appointment, promotion or designation rests with the appointing authority, medical institution or university concerned. 
The Post-Graduate Medical Education Board (PGMEB) will no longer entertain cases where eligibility can be decided directly under the regulations.
 Individuals may approach NMC directly only if their institution fails to forward a genuine case within 60 days. 
"Many candidates approached NMC even in straightforward cases because an NMC eligibility certificate was rarely questioned," said Medical Assessment and Rating Board president Prof M K Ramesh.
NMC has also introduced a review mechanism for applicants dissatisfied with an institution's decision. They can seek a review within 30 days. The changes are aimed at improving institutional accountability, reducing unnecessary referrals and litigation and allowing it to focus on complex cases.

NEW DELHI: At 213 marks, NEET-UG recorded its highest ever qualifying cutoff, even as the number of candidates clearing the medical entrance examination fell by 1.15 lakh, a divergence driven by a smaller-appearing pool and a sharp upward shift in the score distribution. Moreover, the total qualified candidates for EWS and OBC for the first time breached 60% of their 'appeared' cohort, and the percentage of unreserved qualifiers now rests below 50%. The qualifying cutoffs for unreserved and EWS candidates rose to 213 from 144 in 2025 - a 69-mark jump. For OBC, SC/ST candidates, the threshold increased by 64 marks, from 113 to 177.
The UR/EWS qualifying range moved from 720-162 in 2024 to 686-144 in 2025 and 715-213 this year. For OBC, SC and ST candidates, the lower end moved from 127 in 2024 to 113 last year before surging to 177.
Highest Success Rate In EWS; 9% Skipped Retest
Registrations remained virtually unchanged at 22.8 lakh, compared with 22.76 lakh in 2025. But only 19.99 lakh candidates appeared, down from 22.09 lakh - a decline of nearly 2.1 lakh. Attendance consequently dropped from 97.1% to 87.7%. The number qualifying fell from 12.37 lakh to 11.21 lakh, a decline of 9.3%. 
Yet the success rate among those who appeared remained virtually unchanged at about 56.1%, showing that the fall in qualifiers was largely an absentee story rather than a collapse in performance. Under the category-wise qualifying criteria, UR and EWS candidates must secure at least the 50th percentile, while OBC, SC and ST candidates require the 40th percentile. For candidates with benchmark disabilities, the qualifying requirement is 45th percentile for UR/EWS and 40th percentile for OBC, SC and ST.
Highest Success Rate In EWS; 9% Skipped Retest
In marks, the 2026 ranges were 715-213 for UR/EWS, 212-177 for OBC, SC and ST, 212-194 for UR/EWS-PwBD and 193-177 for most reserved-category PwBD candidates. The ST-PwBD range was 191-177. NTA's table shows 9.97 lakh candidates clearing at the UR/EWS threshold, while 81,111 OBC, 29,947 SC and 12,452 ST candidates qualified within the lower score band. These are score-band figures and not the total number qualifying from each social category.
Separately, category-wise results show that 61.8% of EWS candidates who appeared qualified, the highest rate, followed by 60.7% of OBC candidates. The qualification rate was 52.4% among SC candidates, 51.2% among general candidates and 49% among ST candidates.

full_text:
Heavy overnight rain triggered flash floods in Jammu and Kashmir's Rajouri district early on Sunday, forcing hundreds of residents to move to safer places after rivers overflowed and flooded low-lying areas.
Officials said floodwaters entered several parts of Rajouri town, including the new bus stand, after rivers burst their banks. Dozens of vehicles were either swept away or left submerged, causing widespread disruption.
Rescue and relief teams, assisted by the district administration, were deployed to evacuate affected families and assess the damage. Congress MLA Iftkhar Ahmad said the flash floods had caused extensive damage to both public infrastructure and private property.
'Everything is lost. Everything is gone'
The flooding followed continuous heavy rain that began on Saturday evening. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast moderate to heavy rainfall across Jammu and Kashmir until July 23.
"Everything is lost. Everything is gone. Everything we had has been washed away. One woman is missing," a local resident told news agency ANI.
Ahmad, who was scheduled to attend a Congress protest in Jammu demanding the restoration of statehood, returned to Rajouri after the floods.
"I have abandoned my party programme to stand with my people, as the flash floods have caused extensive damage to public and private property," he said, urging the administration to begin relief and rehabilitation work immediately.
Officials said the Darhali, Khandli, Suktoh and Jamola rivers overflowed, with several flowing close to or above the danger mark. The Darhali River breached a flood protection wall near Bela Colony, sending floodwaters into the new bus stand where several vehicles were swept away or submerged.
More than 50 families living near Abdullah Bridge were forced to leave their homes after floodwaters flooded the settlement. Another locality near Tariq Bridge was also affected, prompting police to respond to distress calls and help residents move to safer places away from the riverbanks.
"Our teams are responding to almost every SOS call. At this stage, our priority is to prevent any loss of life. While there has been significant damage to property, the extent of the losses will be assessed once the floodwaters recede," a police official said.
Police teams patrolled flood-prone areas, made public announcements and urged people living near rivers and in low-lying localities to evacuate immediately. The district administration also issued an advisory asking residents to remain alert, while police control rooms were activated to coordinate rescue and relief operations.
Red alert in Himachal
Meanwhile, the IMD has issued a red alert for parts of Himachal Pradesh on July 20 and 21, warning of extremely heavy rainfall, flash floods, landslides, rising river levels and widespread disruption.
Speaking to ANI, Sandeep Kumar Sharma, Senior Scientist at the IMD's Meteorological Centre in Shimla, said the weather is expected to become active from the night of July 18 and continue until at least July 24.
He said Chamba, Kangra, Mandi and Sirmaur are likely to receive the heaviest rainfall, with red alerts in place on July 20. On July 21, the red alert will also cover Kullu, while several other districts remain under orange and yellow alerts.
Sharma warned that continuous rainfall could trigger flash floods, landslides, mudslides and rockfalls, especially in vulnerable areas.
"Water levels in rivers and streams are expected to rise significantly. Even small seasonal streams can swell suddenly, increasing the risk of flash floods. People should stay away from rivers, nullahs and other water bodies," he said.
He advised residents and tourists to avoid unnecessary travel during periods of heavy rain, follow official traffic advisories and keep track of weather updates issued by the IMD and district administrations.
The weather office also warned that heavy rainfall could damage standing crops and horticulture, disrupt essential services, cause traffic congestion and reduce visibility on roads across the state over the coming days.

LEO is very important for any country for strategic purposes and earth mapping requirements as this orbit houses military and defence surveillance satellites, earth observation and remote sensing satellites for high-resolution imagery (used in environmental monitoring, agricultural tracking and disaster mapping), and satellites for atmospheric and space science research.
With more successful flight-tests, Vikram-1, a four-stage rocket, will soon cater to the rising demands of the Indian private sector to launch small satellites at LEO. With Isroâs hands full with so many other space programmes, including Chandrayaan, Gaganyaan and Bharatiya Antariksh Station, Skyrootâs rocket can also fulfil the satellite demands of the govt and military. Besides Isroâs PSLV, GSLV, LVM and SSLV rockets, Skyrootâs Vikram-1 will soon turn into a commercial launcher.
The global commercial satellite launch service market size is currently estimated between $8.65 billion and $12.1 billion. Elon Musk-owned SpaceX holds a dominant position in this launch market, controlling 80%- 85% of global commercial launch capacity. In 2025 itself, SpaceX launched an estimated 3,500 to 3,800 satellites across over 160 successful orbital missions. Indiaâs commercial space footprint is currently estimated at less than 2% of the global market share.
Getting a big boost from Vikram-1 success, other space startups will now accelerate their orbital rocket programme and attempt to get a piece of the global market pie. full_text:
NEW DELHI: Drawing a distinction between using abuse language and the offence of obscenity, Supreme Court has said that use of mere swear words, profanities and vulgar expletives, however distasteful or uncivil they may be, cannot be equated with obscenity and is not an offence. It set aside conviction under Section 294 for a person who had used abusive slurs for mother and sister during an altercation.
A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Vipul M Pancholi said obscenity which is an offence under IPC is not synonymous with "vulgarity", "abuse" or "profanity". "Words which are merely vulgar or abusive may evoke a feeling of disgust, revulsion or shock, but that by itself does not make them obscene in law. It is for this reason that this Court, through various judicial pronouncements, has held that the use of abusive, vulgar or profane language does not necessarily constitute obscenity. 
 Abusive words lacked lascivious element: SC 
 This Court in Samaresh Bose v. Amal Mitra case, while considering a Bengali novel, held that the use of slang, unconventional words or vulgar language may create a feeling of disgust or revulsion, but that does not necessarily amount to obscenity," the bench said.
It said the test to determine whether the words complained of are obscene or not is to see whether the words fulfil three ingredients - (i) it should be lascivious; (ii) appeals to prurient interests of people; and (iii) has a tendency to deprave and corrupt persons who are likely to see, hear or read it. "Further, it must also be shown that the use of such words has caused annoyance to others. Unless presence of essential ingredients is established, the offence of obscenity cannot be said to be made out," the court said while examining the ambit of Section 294
Section 294 says Whoever, to the annoyance of others, (a) does any obscene act in any public place, or (b) sings, recites or utters any obscene song, ballad or words, in or near any public place, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months. The court said that in order to constitute an offence under the Section, the words uttered must contain some lascivious element capable of arousing sexual thoughts or feelings and must further be shown to have caused annoyance to others.
"In the present case, during an altercation, the appellant allegedly uttered: 'Hey Mother...r! You son of a w....e! Are you coming in support of your elder sister's son? Just f...k off, you 'K....a' F...r'...'. It is this which is sought to be invoked under Section 294(b) of the IPC. Going by the version of Prosecution witnesses-1 himself, the words and verbal slang used by the appellant were, at best, abusive or vulgar in nature. The Collins English Dictionary defines the word "abusive" as a language which 'is extremely rude and insulting' Whereas the word 'vulgar' is defined by the Cambridge Dictionary as "rude and likely to upset or anger people, especially by referring to sex and the body in an unpleasant way" These definitions clearly show that words may be insulting, offensive or unpleasant without necessarily being obscene in law," the bench said.
"For an utterance to be considered obscene, it must be shown that it was lascivious, appealed to prurient interests and had the tendency to deprave and corrupt the minds of those who are exposed to it. Tested on this anvil, even if all the allegations levelled in the complaint are taken at their face value and accepted to be true in entirety, the same cannot be held to be obscene. Such words, howsoever abusive, unpalatable or uncivil, do not satisfy the requirement of Section 294(b) IPC for there being nothing on record to show that they had any one or all three elements referred to hereinabove. Further, it is nobody's case that use of such words causes annoyance to others in a public place, which is a mandatory ingredient of the Section, much less to the complainant . In absence thereof, we find that the offence under Section 294(b) IPC is not made out," the bench said.

The highest number of seed balls, nearly 28 lakh, were dispersed in Rajamahendravaram Circle, including 2.26 lakh dropped by drones. Distribution of 7.50 lakh seed balls was completed in the Visakhapatnam Forest Division and 8.67 lakh in the Kurnool forest area.
Depending on weather conditions, seed balls were being dispersed in Chintoor, Atmakur, Giddalur, Markapur and Kadapa divisions, the officials said, adding that drones were being effectively used in this massive exercise.

The Students’ Federation of India (SFI) State president P. Rammohan and State secretary K. Prasanna Kumar saluted every student, youth, and democratic force that fought relentlessly until the Union Education Minister was compelled to resign. “This is a historic victory achieved through the unity and determination of students. The movement has once again demonstrated that no government or ruler is invincible before the collective strength of an organised student community,” they said.
They said the student movement that continued over the past two months had shaken the arrogance of the Narendra Modi government. “We particularly appreciate the leadership of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and all progressive student organisations for playing a pivotal role in transforming students’ anger into a peaceful yet powerful democratic movement across the country,” they said.
The SFI leaders demanded the immediate abolition of the National Testing Agency (NTA), which they claimed was responsible for a series of failures that allegedly claimed the lives of more than 20 students. They further demanded complete justice for the students and their families who suffered due to examination irregularities and administrative failures.
Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) State secretary Ramanna said the resistance would continue until every student in the country was guaranteed equal, fair and inclusive access to education.
“The student movement has shattered the perception that Gen Z is a passive generation absorbed in mobile phones and indifferent to the world around them. Their sustained protests have caught politicians off guard, demonstrating that the country’s youth is politically aware, organised, and prepared to hold those in power accountable,” said Nitta Swarnalatha, an advocate from Andhra Pradesh High Court, participating in the victory celebrations.

The two-day Telugu Mahotsavam, organised by the Andhra Pradesh State Creativity and Culture Society, commenced with grandeur at the historic Undavalli Caves in Guntur district on Saturday. The programme aims at preserving and promoting the richness of the Telugu language and its cultural heritage for future generations,
The festival began with Suryodaya Suprabhatham at 6:30 a.m., as students of the Ghantasala Venkateswara Rao Government College of Music and Dance welcomed the sunrise with Telugu devotional and literary compositions. The classical musical performances presented atop the caves created a serene atmosphere, setting the tone for the cultural celebrations.
The inaugural was attended by NTR District Collector Lakshmisha, former Zilla Parishad Chairperson Gadde Anuradha, APMSIDC Chairman Chillapalli Srinivas, ghazal singer Ghazal Srinivas, NTR district DCP K.G.B. Saritha, and Telugu Sahitya and Culture Academy Chairman M.D. Wilson (Sharath Chandra).
Mr. Lakshmisha stressed that preserving Telugu, one of India’s ancient classical languages with a rich literary and cultural legacy, was a shared responsibility. He said the festival would inspire younger generations to develop a stronger appreciation for their mother tongue.
Ms. Anuradha observed that bringing Telugu literature, folk traditions and fine arts onto a common platform was a significant step towards strengthening the language’s cultural identity.
One of the major attractions of the festival was a literary discussion Aame Maata – Akshara Baata,” which featured eminent women writers including Bhavani Devi, Mandalapu Haimavathi, Tella Aruna, Vasudha Rani, Sushilamma and Simhadri Jyothirmayi.
The panel explored the evolution of women’s contribution to Telugu literature, from the works of the medieval poet Molla to contemporary writer Volga, and discussed how women continue to shape literary values and social thought through their writings.
Poets and literary personalities from across Andhra Pradesh participated in the open-air poetry session Chettu Needana Chirugaali Kavithva Gaana Karyakramam, presenting poems on the glory of the Telugu language, the historical significance of the Undavalli Caves and contemporary social issues.
Participating poets were honoured with certificates by Andhra Pradesh State Creativity and Culture Society Chairperson Podapati Tejaswini.
The festival also featured storytelling sessions by former All India Radio Director Munjaluri Krishnakumari, who narrated Panchatantra and moral stories while encouraging children to tell stories creatively.
A traditional Tholu Bommalata (shadow puppetry) performance based on the Sundarakanda captivated the audience, while “Telugu Swarala Sangeeta Sambaram” delighted music lovers with timeless Telugu film songs, audience sing-alongs, lyrical appreciation sessions and live musical performances.
The first day of Telugu Mahotsavam concluded with a vibrant showcase of Andhra Pradesh’s literary, artistic and cultural heritage.

Protest marches and dharna were witnessed in several districts of Bihar on Friday (July 24, 2026) by the students and locals demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged NEET paper leak.
Protesters holding banners, posters and placards carried out the protest marches in Vaishali, Muzaffarpur, Khagaria, Darbhanga, Bettiah (West Champaran), Supaul, Jamui, Samastipur, Madhubani and Buxar. In Vaishali, the protesters burnt the effigies of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Dharmendra Pradhan.
Last evening, in Jehanabad, police had to open 20 to 30 rounds of fire after protesters pelted stones on the official residence of the District Magistrate. Jehanabad SP office on July 24, 2026, released the photographs of over a hundred protesters urging locals to identify them so that legal action could be taken against them.
Jehanabad SP Kota Kiran Kumar today carried out a flag march along with 300 police jawans in view of the ongoing security challenges and protests in the State. Mr. Kumar asserted that the police are on high alert to maintain peace and public safety. He added that police from all stations in the district are continuously patrolling major intersections.
Patna police has also published the photograph of over 100 miscreants who vandalised public properties and beat up police and press personnel.
“On July 22, 2026, during the demonstrations that took place in Gandhi Maidan and the Income Tax Circle areas of Patna district, some unruly elements attacked the police force. Police vehicles were damaged. Ordinary citizens and media personnel were also assaulted with sticks, batons, bricks, and stones, “a press statement from the office of Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Patna stated.
It further said, “Through social media, such miscreants are being identified, and their photos/pictures are being published. Please assist the Patna Police in identifying these unruly elements. Identify the individuals according to the serial number of the photo and provide this information to the Patna Police at 0612-2217000, 9939919191, so that legal action can be taken against them.”
Heavy deployment of the police force has been done in all districts of Bihar after All India Students’ Association (AISA) called for a Bihar Bandh on July 25, 2026, against police lathi-charge on the students in Patna on July 22.
Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Bihar State Secretary Kunal has strongly condemned the police lathi-charge, firing and arrests of the students protesting against alleged NEET paper leak across various districts of Bihar, stating that such suppression of democratic rights is a matter of grave concern for any democratic system.

Mr. Kunal asserted that AISA State Secretary Dipankar Mishra and State Vice-President Saba Afrin have been arrested by the police in Patna and there has been no information regarding their whereabouts.
“It is a blatant violation of the rule of law and civil rights. The police must immediately share the details of their arrest and release them unconditionally, along with all other arrested students,”Mr. Kunal said.
He mentioned that fabricated cases have been filed against several AISA leaders and activists, including CPI(ML) MLC Shashi Yadav and MLA Sandeep Saurabh.
He added that the CPI(ML) will extend its moral support to the Bihar Bandh.
“The party appeals to students, youth, parents, and citizens who believe in democracy across the state to support the Bandh. He added that the Bihar’s overall development has gained new momentum.

People’s servant
In his address, the Chief Minister asserted that the government belongs to the people of Bihar and that he is the people’s servant. He pointed out that every decision taken during the first 100 days has been dedicated to the public interest, good governance, and the all-round development of Bihar.

full_text:
As the student protests over paper leaks spread across different States and snowballed into a major political crisis for the Narendra Modi government, Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as the Education Minister on Saturday (July 25, 2026), prompting the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) to call off the protests at Jantar Mantar, which had become the epicentre of the agitation for the past 36 days.

President Droupadi Murmu accepted Mr. Pradhan’s resignation on the Prime Minister’s advice and appointed Pralhad Joshi as the new Education Minister, a communique from the Rashtrapati Bhavan said in the evening.
In his resignation letter addressed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, posted on X, Mr. Pradhan said he was resigning on his own account, so that “anti-national” elements do not exploit the situation created by the protests.
As soon as the news of the resignation broke in the afternoon, protesters at Jantar Mantar erupted in joy. “We have done it,” CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke told the jubilant crowd.
Thank you all, says Wangchuk
Activist Sonam Wangchuk, whose hunger strike gave momentum to the protests, termed it a victory of democracy, peace, patience, and perseverance. “Congratulations CJP, Gen Z of the nation, and thank you all citizens for shedding fear and the fear of fear, and rising up from every corner of the nation,” he posted on X.
The resignation came moments before Union Ministers J. P. Nadda and Jitendra Singh met CJP spokespersons Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das for talks to end the protests.
Govt. assurance
At a joint press conference with the Ministers, the CJP spokespersons said they are calling it off in “good faith” as the government had agreed to their two demands: ₹1 crore to the families of all students who died by suicide because of NEET paper leaks and no action against any of the student protesters.
Mr. Nadda said the government will give “honourable compensation” within rules to the families of the students who died by suicide after the NEET test was cancelled and ensure withdrawal of all FIRs registered against the protesters.
“As far as their [CJP] charter for broader education reforms is concerned, we will deliberate upon and engage with them,” Mr. Nadda said at a press conference.
PM should apologise: Congress
Congratulating the students on their victory, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said removal of Mr. Pradhan is a “symbolic” but huge step in rebuilding the education system.
The Opposition leader, however, said there are still two more demands: anyone who beat up the students should be held accountable and that the Prime Minister should apologise to the students.
“It is also a signal to other parts of society, farmers, labourers, poor people, anybody whom this regime is attacking and oppressing, there is wisdom and courage in standing up. Daro mat (don’t fear). Let’s get rid of this regime,” Mr. Gandhi said.
In a post on X, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said: “Prime Minister Narendra Modi should apologise to youth. There should be strict action against those who unleashed lathis and pellet guns.”
With the first week of the Monsoon Session of Parliament washed out over the Opposition’s insistence on Mr. Pradhan’s resignation, the government is now expecting both Houses to function.
Three police personnel injured
Amid the jubilation at Jantar Mantar, there were also tense moments, as three senior police officials were injured in stone-throwing close to the protest site, at the intersection of Tolstoy Marg and Sansad Marg. However, the police personnel quickly restored order by using tear gas and resorting to a mild lathi-charge.
Sources said the government had come around to the view on Friday evening that it would be necessary for Mr. Pradhan to resign in order to end the protests, which appeared to be spreading across the country.
With Delhi University set to open soon and protests spreading to tier-II cities, discretion was considered the better part of valour, the sources added.
Mr. Pradhan received much support from his Cabinet colleagues, with Defence Minister Rajnath Singh posting on X that the former had contributed to public service and the creation of an inclusive, future-ready India.
Mr. Pradhan is the second Union Minister in Mr. Modi’s tenure to resign following a public controversy. The first was M. J. Akbar, who stepped down as the Minister of State for External Affairs in 2018 after sexual harassment allegations surfaced against him during the #MeToo movement.

Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who toured Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh’s Drass on Saturday (July 25, 2026), said the intentions of the enemies have not changed, and the proxy war remains a security challenge in the region.
Without naming Pakistan, Mr. Singh, while speaking at Shaurya Bhoj in Drass, said, “As we celebrate the Kargil War victory, we have to remind ourselves of the challenges. The intention of our enemy remains the same. Proxy war is still used as a tactic. Our Army is ready to foil these nefarious designs,” said Mr. Singh.
The Defence Minister arrived in Srinagar on Saturday (July 25, 2026) morning on a two-day tour of the region. He was received by J&K Lieutenant-Governor Manoj Sinha. Officials said they discussed the current security situation in J&K, especially in the wake of the Anantnag attack that left one policeman dead three days ago.
Later, Mr. Singh visited the war memorial at Ladakh’s Drass on the eve of the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas. He paid tributes to the soldiers who laid down their lives in the line of duty in the 1999 Kargil War against Pakistan, as he attended the ‘Shaurya Sandhya’.
“It’s these sacrifices that make people of India feel safe. When oxygen levels dropped in 1999, the guns of our soldiers did not fall silent till the Tricolour was unfurled as a mark of victory. We are proud of the valiant soldiers and their degree of courage,” said Mr. Singh.
He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had ensured that the morale of soldiers remains high. “We are investing in modernisation of equipment and training. We are hopeful to see the Indian Army among the leading forces in the world,” he said..
Mr. Singh said the Indian armed forces were fully prepared to face every challenge posed by the country’s adversaries. “India’s military remains vigilant, battle-ready, and capable of protecting the nation’s sovereignty,” he said.
He said no one dares cast an evil eye on India as long as the patriotism and determination of the country’s soldiers remain unshaken, adding that their sacrifices ensure every Indian can pursue dreams without fear.
Ten families of Kargil War bravehearts were felicitated on the occasion. Commemorative events were held at ‘Yudh Sansmaran’ at Lamochen View Point, where the Kargil War veterans and families of fallen soldiers remembered the sacrifices made during Operation Vijay. A documentary and special presentations highlighting the valour of 40 war heroes were screened during the event.

Addressing a press conference here, Mr. Sreenivas said that 20,629 Booth Level Officers (BLOs) distributed enumeration forms to more than 2 crore electors, out of which over 1 crore enumeration forms have been digitised.
“However, the names of 33,84,568 electors could not be recorded. Of these, 13,75,278 had permanently shifted, 7,66,205 were found to be deceased, 2,04,916 were already registered as electors, 9,36,646 electors were found absent, while 1,01,523 electors did not submit their enumeration forms due to other reasons,” he said.

If an elector is aggrieved by the decision of the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), an appeal may be filed before the District Magistrate within 15 days. If the grievance still persists, a further appeal may be filed before the Chief Electoral Officer within 30 days,” he added.
The final electoral roll will be published on October 3, he said. He said that 37,055 Booth Level Agents (BLAs) appointed by various political parties are also assisting in the process. “These include 19,051 appointed by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), 15,818 by the Indian National Congress, 1,476 by the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD), 54 by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), 314 by the Communist Party of India (CPI) and 342 by the Jannayak Janata Party (JJP),” he said.

He then grabbed a microphone, walked to the front of the stage and addressed the thousands gathered at Jantar Mantar protest site: “We have done it.”
With his fists closed and raised in the air, he declared, “Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned. It was said that resignations do not happen in this government. Even the world will bow if there is a person to make it happen.”
The protest site erupted in celebration. Protesters hugged one another, broke into tears, and danced to patriotic Bollywood songs as chants of victory echoed through the crowd and slogans like “Haar gaye, haar gaye, Tanashah haar gaye [dictator has been defeated]” reverberated across the venue.
For many students who had spent days braving rain, heat, and sleeping on roads while demanding accountability, the announcement was more than a political development. It was an emotional affirmation that their voices had finally been heard.
Despite the resignation, which was one of the major demands, the crowd at Jantar Mantar continued to swell as people wanted to celebrate the “historic victory”.
Dozens gathered in front of the main stage to take selfies, while long queues were seen outside the entrance of the venue as thousands of people continued to stream in to the protest site.
Inside the protest site, slogans of “Inquilab Zindabad” and “Bharat Mata ki Jai” filled the air. Some also chanted “Jang abhi bhi jaari hai, E20 ki baari hai” (the fight is not over, E20 is the next target) even as organisers repeatedly appealed to the gathering to maintain peace.
As A.R. Rahman’s ‘Vande Matram’ played from the stage, people sang along, as Mr. Dipke waved the national flag from the centre of the stage. People continued to celebrate as “Chak De! India” blared from the stage.
People distributed “Melody” chocolate in celebration, an apparent reference to Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifting the confectionery to the Italian Prime Minister earlier this year. Mr. Dipke, who had been unwell, soon left the area.
At around 6 p.m., CJP spokespersons Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das returned after meeting Union Ministers and announced that “we have won”, triggering another round of applause.
About half an hour later, Mr. Ranka urged people to disperse peacefully as the protest had been called off. “We will meet you soon,” he said, as both of them left the area.
While many people started to leave, hundreds continued to pour in to celebrate, forcing the volunteers to close the entries to the protest site. Thousands of people who were still coming to the protest site gathered at the Sansad Marg leading to Connaught Place.
By 8:30 pm, workers had started to dismantle the main stage. But, still people climbed on it to click selfies, amid chants of “Vande Bharatam” and fluttering of national flags.

However, not all protesters agreed with the decision to call off the agitation.

The driver of such a vehicle should have five years of driving experience with a valid licence. Primarily, the vehicles should maintain records of travelling students with their name, class of study, residential address, contact number and blood groups,” Mr. Pandve said.

The newly constituted District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) of Vijayanagara district formally commenced operations on Saturday with the objective of providing speedy, free and accessible legal services to the public, particularly economically weaker and marginalised sections of society.
Inaugurating the new office at the Principal District and Sessions Court complex in Hosapete, Pradeep Singh Yerur of the Karnataka High Court and administrative judge for Vijayanagara district said the establishment of a separate legal services authority for the district marked a significant step towards ensuring quicker access to justice.
He noted that legal services for the region were earlier administered from the undivided Ballari district and said the new authority would enable people in Vijayanagara district to avail themselves of legal assistance more conveniently.
Judge Yerur said the effective functioning of the judicial system depended not only on judges but also on lawyers, the police, the civil administration and litigants working together. Referring to the four pillars of democracy, the legislature, executive, judiciary and the media, he said each played an important role in upholding the rule of law.
Stressing the need to make justice accessible to the last person in society, he said the district had a sizeable population of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, backward communities, farmers and labourers, for whom prolonged litigation could be financially burdensome. To address this, the authority has empanelled more than 64 advocates and para-legal volunteers to provide free legal aid, legal advice and assistance to eligible persons.
Mr. Yerur said the authority would not remain confined to its office but would also take legal services to the people’s doorstep. He said disputes would be encouraged to be resolved through pre-litigation counselling, mediation and conciliation so that cases could be settled amicably before reaching the courts.
Calling for greater public awareness on the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, he said awareness programmes should be conducted in schools, colleges and villages to prevent sexual offences against children.
He also appealed to the public to participate in the State-wide plantation drive aimed at planting five crore saplings, including five lakh in Vijayanagara district, to promote environmental conservation. Even if not for the present generation, a healthy environment should be preserved for future generations, he said.
Recalling Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s vision of education, organisation, struggle and equal justice, Justice Yerur expressed confidence that the District Legal Services Authority would work continuously to ensure that legal assistance reached every deserving citizen.
Deputy Commissioner Kavitha S. Mannikeri urged the public, particularly socially and economically disadvantaged sections, to make full use of the services offered by the authority. She said the establishment of the DLSA would make free legal aid and legal counselling more accessible to poor and vulnerable people.

Subramanya, member-secretary of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority H. Shashidhar Shetty, District Bar Association president Gujjala Nagaraj, Superintendent of Police S. full_text:
The Karnataka government’s proposal to include Kambala, the traditional slush-track buffalo race native to the coastal districts, for the first time in this year’s Mysuru Dasara has sparked a controversy.
Those opposed to it have pointed to what they call Kambala’s “incompatibility with the heritage and cultural identity” of Dasara and questioned the need to include a cost- and water-intensive sport when Karnataka is staring at a severe drought. The argument in favour of it has been that Dasara is celebrated as a State festival (Nada Habba) in Mysuru and that the buffalo race, being one of the oldest folk traditions in the State, should be showcased.
Preparations begin
Preparations for the Kambala have, in fact, begun, with the organising committee, headed by Ashok Kumar Rai, Puttur MLA, chalking out a plan to lay a slush track, gallery and other facilities. A plot, measuring around 17 acres, in Sathagalli in Mysuru, has been identified as the venue for the Kambala and is being readied.
Meanwhile, stakeholders — buffalo owners, jockeys, referees, helpers and organisers — at a meeting held in Moodbidri in Dakshina Kannada on July 19, agreed to participate in the Mysuru Kambala, likely to be held on October 18 and October 19, said Belapu Deviprasad Shetty, president of the Karnataka State Kambala Association.
“The Mysuru event will be an opportunity to showcase the culture of Kambala to others who are not familiar with it,” said N. Vijayakumar Kanginamane, general secretary of the association.
Two kinds of Kambala
Experts point out that while ‘Devara Kambalas’ are strictly ritualistic events bound to the land and tradition, other Kambala events held across coastal Karnataka have acquired the character of a competitive sport involving prizes. A majority of the race Kambalas organised in the coastal region are held on artificially built tracks and not on the traditional paddy fields. As many as 27 such race Kambalas are scheduled for the 2026-27 season (November-May) in the coastal region; about 20 Kambalas would be held on the artificial tracks, said Mr. Kanginamane.
Speaking to The Hindu, Muralidhara Rai, a member of the Kambala Organising Committee in Mysuru, said that around 100 buffaloes are expected to participate in the Kambala here, with around 15-20 support staff coming with each buffalo pair.
He argued that traditions like Kambala need to be encouraged on platforms like Dasara, which attracts lakhs of people. “Let Mysuru Dasara introduce Kambala to the global audience, as many foreign tourists come here to witness the celebrations,” he said.
Mr. Rai claimed that the footfall may go up due to the Kambala, thereby increasing tourism revenue. “The expenditure incurred in organising the Kambala would not be much when compared to the revenue the event generates,” he contended. Mr. Rai said the Kambala organised in Bengaluru ïn 2023 attracted nearly 10 lakh people.
Continued opposition
Meanwhile, Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Mysuru MP, several local organisations, green activists, and farmers’ groups have continued to urge the government to withdraw the event.
Organisations opposing the Kambala have formed a Joint Action Committee (JAC) to continue debating and protesting the government’s move. Besides questioning bringing a ‘’region-specific’’ cultural tradition to Mysuru, the JAC has also criticised the government’s priorities at a time when several districts are facing drought-like conditions due to monsoon failure and that it is wasting lakhs of litres of water for a sport amidst water scarcity.
During his recent visit to Mysuru, the Puttur MLA said that the Kambala event is expected to cost between ₹5 crore and ₹8 crore, and that the State government is likely to set aside a special budget for it.
Parashurame Gowda of Parisarakkagi Naavu, Mysuru, a member of the JAC, said that they continue to oppose the Kambala during Dasara celebrations. He also alleged that nearly 36 trees had been illegally felled and a few more have been marked for felling to establish a venue for hosting the Kambala.
“We don’t want an event at the expense of the environment. The Forest Department has already registered an FIR for illegally felling trees. We will continue to oppose the Kambala until it is dropped. A campaign on the lines of the Appiko movement will be held if more trees are chopped,” Mr. Gowda warned, while underlining that it is particularly ironic in a drought year.

Sharana writer, teacher and journalist Linganna Satyampete was remembered as a fearless thinker and uncompromising writer who relentlessly exposed corruption, political misconduct and the hardships of farmers, at a function organised to mark his 14th death anniversary in Kalaburagi on Saturday.
In the programme organised by the Sharana Marga Charitable Trust, the State-level Basava Marga Award was presented to Bengaluru Central Crime Branch (CCB) officer B.S. Sudhakar in recognition of his services. A book ‘Appana Odanata’ authored by Santosh Satyampete was also relased.
Former Minister S.K. Kanta, who presented the award, recalled his long association with Satyampete and described him as an uncompromising journalist who remained steadfast despite facing harassment for his writings.
“Satyampete was a schoolteacher who wrote fearlessly in Lankesh Patrike about political corruption and the plight of farmers. His bold writings often invited transfers and even suspension from service, but he never compromised with his principles. I had the opportunity to help revoke some of those punitive orders,” Mr. Kanta said.
Expressing concern over the condition of farmers and workers, he alleged that while ordinary labourers continued to struggle, governments extended generous financial concessions to large industrialists. “What justice is there when farmers are denied adequate support while industries receive loans with massive subsidies?” he asked.
Legislator B.R. Patil, who released Appana Odanata, said Satyampete was a committed follower of Basava’s philosophy and possessed an explosive spirit against injustice.
“He fearlessly exposed the wrongdoings of politicians and religious institutions in this region. His writings reflected courage, conviction and commitment to social justice,” Mr. Patil said.
Recalling his father’s dedication to journalism, Vishwaradhya Satyampete, son of Satyampete, said the Basava Marga newspaper founded by his father had once reached a circulation of nearly 25,000 copies.
“He never bothered about profit or loss. If he came to know of a potential reader, he would send the newspaper to that household regardless of whether they subscribed. He continued making corrections to the paper until it finally went to press,” he said.
Mahanta Swami of Kalyan Ashram, Mudgal, recalled travelling extensively with Satyampete to spread the message of Sharana philosophy.
“We visited villages together, sometimes even boarding whichever bus was available, to meet people and propagate Basava’s ideals. He was a true Sharana in thought and practice,” the seer said.
Earlier, journalist Shivaranjan Satyampete, another son of Satyampete, welcomed the gathering and delivered the introductory address. A special issue of Sharana Marga was released on the occasion.
Basava Samiti president Vilasavati Khooba, Sarvajna Education Institutions’ chairman Channareddy Patil, Karnataka Sahitya Akademi member Siddharam Honkal, Karnataka State Science and Research Council’s district unit president Ravindra Shahabadi, social activists Suresh Badiger and Vitthal Chikani and others were present.

Our union has been pressurising the Tourism and Transport departments to display in hotels government orders on the need to provide such infrastructure for drivers, who often ferry tourists for days together to various destinations,” he added.

Vishnunadh. Highlighting the plight of drivers who often had to sleep in their vehicles overnight, speakers here had expressed concern at the state of affairs in many luxury and other hotels.

Political parties, youth organisations and innumerable others joined the victory celebrations of the student-led agitation in New Delhi which culminated in the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, by hosting solidarity meets at different parts of the city, on Saturday (July 25, 2026).
The Ernakulam District Congress Committee (DCC) staged ‘Janadhipathya Sangamam’ while the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) took out a victory march in the city.
Inaugurating the Congress meet at Rajendra Maidan, Kunnathunad MLA V.P. Sajeendran hailed the protesters for forcing the Union minister to step down, while adding that the issues concerning the NEET question paper leak were yet to be resolved. “All the culprits behind the paper leaks must be brought before the law and punished in an exemplary manner. The Congress will launch more aggressive protests if the Centre fails to take strict action against the culprits, especially since several other examinations are pending,” Mr. Sajeendran said. DCC President and Kochi MLA Mohammed Shiyas, who chaired the meet, termed the Minister’s resignation ‘a victory of democracy’.
Congress activists, led by MLAs T.J. Vinod and Anwar Sadath and Kochi Mayor V.K. Minimol and other leaders, took out a victory procession from Menaka Junction to the Gandhi Statue at Rajendra Maidan, ahead of the meet.
A group of youngsters, meanwhile, gathered at Kaloor celebrating the triumph of the Delhi protests. The participants, who came together through calls on social media, took out a march from Kaloor Metro Station to the JLN Stadium holding placards hailing democracy.
The DYFI district committee took out a celebratory march from Ernakulam North to the High Court Junction. District secretary Nikhil Babu inaugurated a solidarity meet which was chaired by district committee member T.S. Shifas. Students’ Federation of India activists, led by district secretary Asish S. Anand, also held celebrations in the city.
The district committee of the All India Professional Congress (AIPC) held a gathering at Queen’s Walkway. Former Indian Ambassador to the Netherlands, Venu Rajamony, addressed the meet that called for strong legislation to bring a permanent solution to issues like question paper leaks. AIPC district president Eldho Chirackachalil and leaders including Nobi Thomas and Fazalu Rahman addressed the meet.
The Aam Aadmi Party’s district committee took out a protest march and organised a solidarity meet at Aluva.

full_text:
A sub-divisional magistrate (SDM) in Madhya Pradesh’s Panna district has sent a delivery executive to jail after he did not find the items he had ordered through an online platform. The district administration is considering issuing a show-cause notice to him.
A video of the purported incident that took place on July 21 and a conversation has surfaced on the internet where the executive, Vijay Kushwaha, can be heard telling Ramnivas Choudhary, SDM, Shahnagar, that he had delivered a sealed packet and that he could file for a refund under the platform’s the return policy.
The incident took place at Mr. Choudhary’s office. He had ordered two sets of two mobile covers but received only one in each box.
“You will go to jail within two seconds. You have taken the money for two [mobile covers], but there is only one inside the box. Are you returning the money or not? I am not filing for a return,” Mr. Choudhary tells the executive.
Mr. Kushwaha then says, “I have given a packed box and there is a return policy in this and you can return it. I cannot do anything about it.
“Why did you abuse me? You are using me in the wrong way,” Mr. Kushwaha says, after which the SDM’s staff tells him to get out of the room as Mr. Choudhary directs them to call the police.
After this, the delivery executive narrates the incident in the video.
Panna Collector Usha Parmar told The Hindu that while the delivery executive was released on bail on July 22, the district administration is going to issue a show-cause notice to the SDM.
When contacted, Mr. Choudhary alleged that Mr. Kushwaha was “talking rudely” and also “banged his hands on the table”.
“He gave the parcel to my staff and left. When we called him within minutes, he said he had travelled far and refused to come back initially. So, I scolded him. When he came back, he entered my chamber with mobile video recording on. I asked him for a refund but he refused and said we could call the police,” the SDM said.
“He is a resident of Pawai area in Panna district but lied that he is from Uttar Pradesh,” he said.
Panna Superintendent of Police (SP) Nivedita Naidu said that “prima facie the incident seemed to be a case of abuse of power”.
She said that while the police did not arrest the delivery executive, the local Tehsildar prepared a jail warrant against him under Section 170 of the BNSS, based on statements from the SDM and his staff, after which he was sent to jail.
“The SDM and his staff did not tell the police that the matter was related to online delivery. In their statements, they just alleged that the man was disturbing peace inside the SDM office. They did not tell us the whole matter,” Ms. Naidu said.

full_text:
The primary reason behind Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation on Saturday (July 25, 2026) was not security concerns, but the erosion of the ruling party's political capital caused by the burgeoning, organic crowds at Jantar Mantar, government sources told The Hindu.
The continuous sit-in by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which started on June 13, was called off on Saturday (July 25, 2026) after the government accepted its demands, including withdrawal of criminal cases against protesters.
Taking cue from the July 20 march to Parliament, during which several unarmed protesters were beaten up by the police, the Union government had made elaborate security arrangements for the next few days to contain the crowd at Jantar Mantar, the protest site in the heart of Delhi.
An analysis of the social media chatter, which was found to have unsavoury remarks, particularly against the Prime Minister, after videos of police excesses on students and young people surfaced, also played a role in government conceding to the CJP’s demands, the foremost being Mr. Pradhan’s resignation.
Diverse crowd
“The police were underprepared on July 20 as the crowd, which reached the protest site following a call given by the CJP, was much beyond the initial estimate. However, there was little concern that the protests could lead to a Nepal- or Bangladesh-like situation, as the crowds were largely organic and socially diverse. Some unruly elements were mixed in the crowd, but the police had taken adequate measures post-July 20,” said a government source.
At least eight Internet shutdown orders were issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) between July 20 and July 25, blocking communication in a radius of 1.5 km around Jantar Mantar.
An Internet ban was imposed briefly on July 18, too, when activist Sonam Wangchuk, who had been on a hunger strike for more than 20 days, was forcibly removed from Jantar Mantar to Safdarjung Hospital by the police.
“The police were prepared to hold and manage the crowd at Jantar Mantar for the next few days, coinciding with the ongoing session of the Parliament. The gathering was largely peaceful, and the possibility of unruly elements wanting to take advantage of the situation is always there,” said another government source.
Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda said on Saturday (July 25, 2026) that the CJP delegation submitted a written proposal covering cases related to the agitation along with its five-point charter.
“The government assured the team that no action will be taken against the organisers and protesters, and no new cases will be registered in connection with the agitation. It also expressed condolences to the families of the students who lost their lives and assured them of the highest possible compensation as per the rules,” Mr. Nadda said, adding that discussions will continue with the delegation. This was Mr. Nadda’s third meeting with the delegation.
For a first information report (FIR) to be cancelled, the Delhi Police will have to withdraw the case and send a report to the court saying that it no longer wishes to pursue the case.

[SEP] Opposition parties on Saturday (July 25, 2026) termed the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, following widespread student protests over the NEET paper leak, a “victory for the youth” and a step towards rebuilding the country’s education system.
full_text:
Opposition parties on Saturday (July 25, 2026) termed the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, following widespread student protests over the NEET paper leak, a “victory for the youth” and a step towards rebuilding the country’s education system.
Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi urged other groups to show courage like the students and stand up against the government. “It is time to remove the government,” he said.
“Symbolic but big step”
He said Mr. Pradhan’s resignation was a significant step towards rebuilding the education system. “It’s a symbolic step because he was a symbol, but it is still a big step,” he said.
The Congress leader also said the resignation is a signal to other communities, including farmers, labourers, and the poor, who are allegedly being oppressed by the government. “There is wisdom and courage in standing up. “Daro mat [don’t be afraid]. Let’s get rid of this regime that is attacking India, destroying our Constitution and capturing all our institutions,” Mr. Gandhi said in a video message posted on X and later, while speaking to the media.
Congress MP from Wayanad Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said this was the day when the people started “claiming their country back”. “The youth did not bend; the government had to bend. It is a victory for the youth and students of India. I was truly happy when I heard the news. I even got a bit emotional,” she told the media in her constituency. “This is the day when the people of our country have started claiming the country back. This is a victory for the youth of India. They have done it in the way Mahatma Gandhi had taught us.”
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge described Mr. Pradhan’s resignation as a defeat of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s “stubbornness”. He added that the PM should apologise and take strict action against all those who used force against the agitating students.
Congress General Secretary (organisation) K. C. Venugopal said the Opposition had been spearheading the protest in a united fashion, while party general secretary (communication) Jairam Ramesh said the Opposition had demonstrated “rock-solid unity and solidarity” with the students.
Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said the resignation was a major victory for the new generation. “The government had to bow down,” he said.
Education reforms sought
Speaking to the media in Uttar Pradesh, Mr. Yadav said the movement had underlined the need for serious reforms in the education sector, from primary schooling to higher education.
Aam Aadmi Party supremo and former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal said Mr. Pradhan’s resignation was a “big win for democracy”.
The Left parties also welcomed the resignation and demanded a comprehensive reform in the education sector.
CPI General Secretary D Raja said the resignation was a rare moment of democratic accountability. “It is a rare moment of democratic accountability, achieved not through the goodwill of an arrogant government, but through the sustained struggle of students and youth across the country. The students’ movement has defeated the arrogance of the BJP and compelled the Modi-Shah regime to answer for its failures,” he said.
CPI(M) congratulated the students who were part of the protest and demanded, in a post on X, a comprehensive reform in the education sector, including the scrapping of the National Testing Agency (NTA) and the rollback of the National Education Policy (NEP).
“(Mr Pradhan’s) resignation is only the first step. Now the NTA has to be disbanded, and the anti-student, commercial and communal NEP 2020 has to be rolled back. Cases foisted on the protesters have to be dropped, and action has to be taken against all police personnel who brutally attacked our students,” CPI(M) General Secretary M A Baby said.
Deepankar Bhattacharya of the CPI(ML) said the resignation was “the only sensible thing” Mr. Pradhan had done. “The only sensible thing you have ever done, even though you have not shown the minimum courage and honesty to admit that your resignation has been ordered by the youth of India,” he said.

headline: For the second time, the Centre has ruled out a Metro Rail system for Coimbatore and Madurai cities, and recommended the implementation of a Bus Rapid Transit System (BRTS) instead.

full_text:
For the second time, the Centre has ruled out a Metro Rail system for Coimbatore and Madurai cities, and recommended the implementation of a Bus Rapid Transit System (BRTS) instead.
In November last year, the Centre rejected the request of the Tamil Nadu government to implement a Metro Rail system in both these cities, stating that there might not be significant time savings or high projected ridership and that the cities did not have the mandated population of two million as per the 2011 Census.
Following this, in May this year, the State government yet again wrote to the Centre, justifying and emphasising the need for a Metro Rail system in both the cities, sources said.
The government said Tamil Nadu was one of the most urbanised States in the country, that Coimbatore was an industrial-cum-tourist hub and Madurai a tourist hub, and hence, resident population aside, both cities would benefit from having a Metro Rail as they attract floating population and tourists as well, sources added.
A few days ago, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs communicated to the State government that it had turned down the proposal again, and said the State could build an elevated or at-grade BRTS for both cities.
It said population was not the ‘sole criteria’ to implement the Metro Rail system and that they returned both proposals after examining them ‘in entirety’.
The Ministry said a Metro Rail system would not result in any significant time savings for commuters in both cities and instead wanted the bus system to be strengthened.
It is to be noted that in the cities such as Agra, Bhopal, Patna, Jaipur and Indore, Metro Rail systems have been implemented in the last five years. In April this year, Jaipur Metro Phase-2 was also approved by the Cabinet.
“If the BRTS plan is going to be implemented, then it is possible to build it elevated. There is no adequate right-of-way to build it at-grade in both cities. The cost estimates may have to be reworked,” a source said.

full_text:
After about two years of functioning with temporary principals, Grade II government arts and science colleges are set to get full-time principals. The Collegiate Education Department has drawn up a panel of 129 eligible associate professors to be appointed as principals in Grade II colleges in the State.
A Government Order (G.O.) dated July 21, 2026, stated that the estimate of vacancy for the post of principal Grade II in government arts and science colleges and colleges of education under the Tamil Nadu Collegiate Educational Service has been fixed at 129.
The list of eligible associate professors would be included in the regular panel for promotion to the post of principal Grade II for the year 2026-27. However, this was subject to the outcome of ongoing court cases, the G.O. read. It has given a time frame of two months for claims and objections to be received on the panel.
Grade I vacancies
Meanwhile, at least 24 Grade I colleges continue to languish without full-time principals, while two posts of Joint Director of Collegiate Education (equivalent to Grade I principal) were vacant as well, which will have to be filled through promotion of Grade II principals.
The government had drawn up a panel of 14 Grade II principals for promotion to the post of Grade I principal/Joint Director of Collegiate Education in June.
According to a G.O. dated June 29, 2026, the officials were empanelled for the year 2025-26.
“This panel was sent by the Directorate of Collegiate Education to the government twice in January and in March,” said S. Suresh, general secretary, Tamil Nadu Government College Teachers’ Association.
At least four of the empanelled principals have since retired and another is due for retirement at the end of this month. “I am not sure what took them so long to make these appointments. Due to this delay, these teachers were deprived of a chance to retire as principals,” Mr. Suresh lamented.

A 36-year-old man from Godavari in Andhra Pradesh died of cardiac arrest while trying to exit a narrow passage for worship at Vinayagar temple on the girivalam path near Arunachaleswar temple in Tiruvannamalai on Saturday.
The police said the deceased devotee was identified as S. Manikumar.
The police said that as part of worship, Manikumar visited a Vinayagar temple on the 14-km-long path. As he tried to exit from the temple through a narrow passage, he reportedly got stuck. Other devotees and temple authorities managed to pull him out of the passage.
However, the police said that Manikumar fainted and was rushed to Government Medical College Hospital where doctors said that he was brought dead. A case was registered by Tiruvannamalai Town police. A probe is under way.
Saturday’s incident was the third incident in recent years after a 47-year-old man from Bengaluru died of cardiac arrest while climbing steep staircases at the Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy temple atop the hillock in Sholinghur town near Ranipet in May 2024.
In April 2024, 14-year-old S. Harish, died while climbing down from a hillock temple in Ratnagiri town near Arcot in Ranipet.

full_text:
In the 11th phase of excavations currently underway in Keeladi, continuous brick structures and over 1,300 artefacts have been discovered.
The Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology (TNSDA) is conducting the 11th phase of excavation at the Keeladi archaeological site, located near Madurai in Sivagangai district. While the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) conducted the first three phases, subsequent phases have been carried out by the TNSDA.
This 11th phase of excavation began on March 18 of this year, south of the area where the on-site museum is located. A total of nine quadrants were dug in this area. Ramesh Masethung, Director of Keeladi Excavations, told The Hindu that continuous brick structures were found across all nine quadrants. He mentioned that these structures, extending towards the west and north, stretch beyond these nine quadrants.
“Brick structures were previously found in the area where the on-site museum is located. In the adjacent area excavated later, no structural remains were found. However, structural remains have been uncovered once again now,” says Mr. Masethung.
Apart from these brick structures, several other important features have come to light during the current excavation. In one quadrant, a terracotta pipeline and a closed drainage system were discovered. In addition to the structural remains, more than 1,300 artefacts have been recovered. These include clay hopscotches, terracotta beads and spindles, iron knives, chisels, swords, and nails, as well as semi-precious stones such as amethyst, carnelian, agate, banded agate, and ivory dice.
Furthermore, tiny gold ornaments measuring less than a centimeter have been found. In addition, intact pots were discovered in four locations, one of which includes a handle. One of these pots features a fish symbol inscribed on its shoulder portion.
“Since an open drainage system was also found in one quadrant, this might have been an industrial area as well. However, this can only be confirmed after the studies are completed,” says Mr. Masethung. He also added that organic materials found here will be sent for carbon dating.
Depending on the rain, this 11th phase of excavation may continue until September.

After nearly a decade since it got administrative sanction (in 2018), work to construct ₹8.5 crore Tangedco 33/11 KV sub-station in Yelagiri Hills in Tirupattur district has commenced.
Officials of Tangedco, which executes the work, said that a new sub-station was a long-standing demand of residents in the hills. Of the total 5,286 consumers, 1,400 are commercial establishments, mostly hotels, restaurants, and resorts. “Power shutdowns and fluctuations have been common in hamlets in the hills. The new sub-station will end the ordeal of residents, especially students, who can study under better lights,” said G. Somu, a tribal.
Around 200 consumers are farmers. . “Civic works for the substation have commenced. Thereafter, installation of transformers, feeders, and other electrical equipment will be done. The new facility will be ready in 2027,” Rajan Murugesan, Assistant Engineer (AE), Tangedco (Yelagiri Hills), told The Hindu.
At present, permanent sub-stations in Jawadhu Hills are located in Kavalur and Pudur Nadu village near Yelagiri Hills. The sub-station in Kavalur village was established in 1960s to operate Vainu Bappu Astronomical Observatory, which was relocated from Kodaikanal in 1968.
The Pudur Nadu substation was opened in 2020 after bifurcation from the Vaniyambadi power station.
Against this backdrop, Tangedco proposed to set up a sub-station at Yelagiri Hills mainly to promote domestic tourism as the hill station has more than 150 hotels and resorts. Initially, the project got its nod for a budget of ₹3.5 crore in 2018.
However, Tangedco officials said that project was halted since then before it was revived with a revised estimate of ₹8.5 crore in January 2026. A ceremony to lay the foundation stone was held in March. After polls, work to construct the new facility was expedited.
Bifurcated from the Vaniyambadi 110 KV sub-station in April 2022, the Tangedco office at Yelagiri Hills was functioning as a section office with meager staff. Daily power supply was monitored by officials at Vaniyambadi office, around 30 km away in the plains. It resulted in delay in attending complaints and repair of power lines on the route which is lined with forests.
Tangedco officials said that the new sub-station will help attend to power faults immediately. Power fluctuations will be prevented as power supply will be given directly from the sub-station in the hills. The new facility will lessen dependence on diesel-run generators in the hills and prevent pollution.
