headline: Not 24x7 entertainment channel: SC bars sharing of hearing videos without prior nod
cluster_text: Not 24x7 entertainment channel: SC bars sharing of hearing videos without prior nod [SEP] Not 24x7 entertainment channel: SC bars sharing of hearing videos without prior nod
full_text:
Not 24x7 entertainment channel: SC bars sharing of hearing videos without prior nod
Taking note of the misuse of audio and video recordings of court proceedings, the Supreme Court barred their unauthorised posting, editing, sharing and uploading on social media and digital platforms without prior court approval.
Observing that courts can't be a 24x7 entertainment channel, the Supreme Court on Friday passed an interim order prohibiting the extraction, editing, dissemination, reposting, uploading or monetisation of audio and video recordings of judicial proceedings on social media and other digital platforms without prior permission from the concerned court.
A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohan passed the interim direction while hearing a public interest litigation filed by journalist Harshita Grover seeking guidelines to regulate the clipping, editing, dissemination and monetisation of audiovisual recordings of court proceedings.
"There shall be no extraction, modification, dissemination, posting, re-posting, uploading or monetisation of audio/video recordings of the judicial proceedings on social media or other digital platforms without the prior permission of the Registrar General of the concerned High Courts or the Secretary General of the Supreme Court," the Bench said.
According to a report in Live Law, the court, however, clarified that the interim order would not affect fair news reporting of judicial proceedings.
The Bench issued notice on the petition and impleaded all High Courts in the matter. It also directed the Union government to place before the court a proposal identifying the nodal ministries that could implement the reliefs sought in the plea.
The High Courts have also been asked to submit reports on the adoption of the Supreme Court's model livestreaming guidelines and explain the impact of continuous livestreaming of proceedings.
Notices were also issued to social media intermediaries, including Meta and X.
During the hearing, senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the petitioner, clarified that the plea was not against livestreaming of court proceedings but against the misuse of selectively edited clips circulating online.
"I personally don't see any problem with livestream," Singh submitted, adding that snippets of hearings were often taken out of context and went viral. Referring to a recent incident, he said a clip from proceedings before Justice Viswanathan had become viral, making "the judiciary a joke before the lay people".
Singh relied on the Supreme Court's Model Rules for Live-Streaming and Recording of Court Proceedings, which prohibit any unauthorised recording, sharing, reproduction, modification or republication of livestreamed proceedings without prior written approval of the court, and sought an interim order enforcing those provisions.
Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed that regulating digital data had emerged as "one of the biggest challenges" and suggested that livestreaming should become "an exception rather than a norm."
"Regulating data is one of the biggest challenges in digital space... so we should ensure limited access and therefore restrict livestream itself. Parties must expressly make a prayer that they want to see. It can't be a 24/7 entertainment channel by court," Justice Bagchi remarked, while expressing concern over virtual hearing links being shared indiscriminately.
"It can't be a 24x7 entertainment channel by the court," the bench observed, adding that there was a need to ensure limited access.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta supported the plea for interim protection and cautioned against the misuse of artificial intelligence to manipulate courtroom videos.
"Suppose your lordships are saying something to me and I am responding. There are AI tools. With the same lip movement, my and your lordships' words can be changed in our respective voices," Mehta submitted.
He also argued that selectively edited clips were often used to create misleading narratives about court proceedings.
The Chief Justice agreed that distorted reporting posed a growing challenge, saying he had personally experienced his remarks being misrepresented.
"In the print forum, I have already experienced. What I never said was thrust upon me by these people," CJI Kant observed, referring to media reports on an earlier plea concerning student protests.
The petition contends that while livestreaming was introduced to promote transparency and the principle of open justice, the absence of a regulatory framework has enabled courtroom recordings to be clipped, edited and circulated with misleading captions, sensational commentary and clickbait content, often for commercial gain.
Filed under Article 32 of the Constitution, the plea argues that isolated courtroom exchanges and oral observations are routinely taken out of context, exposing judges, lawyers and litigants to trolling, reputational harm and distorted public narratives.
It seeks guidelines governing the recording, clipping, redistribution and monetisation of audiovisual recordings while preserving the principles of open justice and fair reporting.
The petition also cites multiple instances of alleged misuse of judicial recordings, including controversies involving judges' remarks, and misleading social media content featuring courtroom exchanges.
The plea also highlights international practices such as the United Kingdom Supreme Court's copyright framework governing audiovisual recordings.

headline: Democracy, not rule by diktat: Anna Hazare after Dharmendra Pradhan quits
cluster_text: Democracy, not rule by diktat: Anna Hazare after Dharmendra Pradhan quits [SEP] Democracy, not rule by diktat: Anna Hazare after Dharmendra Pradhan quits
full_text:
Democracy, not rule by diktat: Anna Hazare after Dharmendra Pradhan quits
Anna Hazare urged peaceful agitation and dialogue as the Cockroach Janata Party ended its protest after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. He said public grievances should be resolved through democracy and not through violence.
Social activist Anna Hazare on Saturday said peaceful agitation, democracy and dialogue were the only ways to address public grievances, as the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) called off its agitation following the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
He stressed the importance of democracy and dialogue in resolving public grievances, saying, “It is democracy, not rule by diktat, and one should always follow the path of democracy.”
Speaking to reporters in Ahilyanagar, the 89-year-old activist recalled his own history of civil agitation and said lasting systemic change could be achieved through dialogue rather than confrontation.
“Any issue gets resolved through dialogue. Dialogue leads to solutions. Creating tension and going down the wrong path will not solve anything,” Hazare said.
Recalling his 22 hunger strikes, Hazare said he had never resorted to violence and credited peaceful agitation with helping bring about legislative changes.
“I did 22 fasts, never used violence, and because of that, 10 laws were enacted. Creating violence is not right. Whoever the person may be, one should never indulge in violence,” he said.
Hazare also stressed that governments must listen to citizens and prioritise public welfare. He said democratic avenues should always be used to resolve public grievances.
“One has to see what the public is saying. For the public's welfare, even if we have to step forward, there's no harm in it. But public interest must happen. Issues are never resolved by violence but by dialogue among people,” he said.
“Whatever happens through democracy happens. One should always follow the path of democracy,” Hazare added.
His remarks came amid political developments in the national capital following Pradhan's resignation. A CJP delegation held a third round of talks with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh at the Constitution Club of India.
Following the discussions, the CJP formally announced the withdrawal of its 37-day agitation at Jantar Mantar.
“Cockroach Janta Party declares that we withdraw the agitation in good faith, with the understanding that the agreed-upon terms will be executed within the agreed-upon timelines,” CJP Chief Spokesperson Saurav Das said.

headline: 21 is the new political age: Revanth Reddy seeks lower age to contest MLA, MP polls
cluster_text: 21 is the new political age: Revanth Reddy seeks lower age to contest MLA, MP polls [SEP] 21 is the new political age: Revanth Reddy seeks lower age to contest MLA, MP polls
full_text:
21 is the new political age: Revanth Reddy seeks lower age to contest MLA, MP polls
A Revanth Reddy said Telangana will move a resolution to lower the minimum age for contesting Assembly and Lok Sabha elections to 21. He presented it as a push for stronger youth representation and wider student participation in national politics.
In a major political pitch aimed at empowering India's youth, Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Saturday announced that his government would move a resolution in the State Assembly urging the Centre to reduce the minimum age to contest Assembly and Lok Sabha elections from 25 years to 21 years.
Addressing a massive Gen Z rally in Hyderabad, Revanth Reddy said the time had come to give young Indians a greater role in shaping the country's future. "If a 21-year-old can become an IAS officer, contest local body elections, and even serve the nation through the civil services, why can't they contest Assembly and Parliament elections?" he asked.
The Chief Minister said the Telangana government would convene a special session of the Assembly and Legislative Council in the first week of August to pass a resolution seeking the constitutional amendment. He added that Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge would pursue the issue in Parliament.
Making a strong case for lowering the age limit, Revanth Reddy cited former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's decision to reduce the voting age from 21 to 18 through the 61st Constitutional Amendment and PV Narasimha Rao's 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, which enabled 21-year-olds to contest local body elections. He also referred to countries such as Germany, the United Kingdom and Singapore, where younger leaders are allowed to contest elections at an earlier age.
The Chief Minister said Gen Z accounts for nearly 30 per cent of India's population but has less than one per cent representation in Parliament. "India's future lies in the hands of its youth. The country's legislatures must reflect that reality," he said.
Revanth Reddy also praised the nationwide Gen Z movement over the alleged NEET paper leak, claiming it had compelled the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. He demanded that the Centre withdraw cases filed against protesting students and provide compensation to the families of students who allegedly died by suicide in connection with the controversy.
Calling the movement a victory for India's youth rather than any political party, the Chief Minister urged young people to continue their fight for justice and greater representation. "This tsunami of youth must not stop here. The voice of Gen Z should be heard from Jantar Mantar to Parliament," he said.

cluster_text: Contractors to be blacklisted for substandard road restoration: Yogi Adityanath [SEP] Contractors to be blacklisted for substandard road restoration: Yogi Adityanath
full_text:
Contractors to be blacklisted for substandard road restoration: Yogi Adityanath
UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath warned of blacklisting contractors and filing FIRs if the restoration work of roads dug up for drinking water pipelines in Agra is found unsatisfactory. He also pushed for faster legal clearances and infrastructure planning across Agra and the Braj region.
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday directed officials to take a stern approach to the upkeep of civic amenities and warned that contractors could be blacklisted if work falls short. At a meeting with public representatives in Agra, he expressed displeasure over delays and poor-quality restoration of roads dug up for drinking water pipelines under the Jal Jeevan Mission.
He also reviewed development matters linked to Agra and the Mathura-Vrindavan region, asking officials to closely track court cases affecting the city, prepare plans to promote key industries, improve processes linked to Ayushman payments, and move proposals on transport and tourism infrastructure.
According to a government statement, Adityanath told Jal Nigam officials that merely making a dug-up road motorable was not enough. He said that if the work was found unsatisfactory, the contractors should be blacklisted and FIRs lodged against the officials concerned.
Referring to the recent Supreme Court permission to the Taj Trapezium Zone Authority to process about 400 pending applications for non-polluting MSMEs, he directed the divisional commissioner to monitor court rulings involving Agra so that the city’s development is not held up due to lack of legal advocacy.
Saying Agra has strong potential in leather products and defence manufacturing, the Chief Minister asked for a concrete plan to promote these sectors. He also said street vendors operating on footpaths should not be evicted and should instead be shifted to designated vending zones. He directed the Health Department to verify and speed up the settlement of payments related to Ayushman cards and empanelled hospitals.
Adityanath also chaired a meeting of the Uttar Pradesh Braj Tirth Vikas Parishad in Agra. He called for the early submission of a ropeway project proposal for Vrindavan and asked officials to send proposals for a combined road-rail project on the Mathura-Vrindavan rail route and for a land-pooling scheme to expand parking facilities.
Officials, in turn, presented a proposal for the construction of several key Master Plan roads in the Mathura-Vrindavan area. He also sought a government order on the Tirth-Mitra policy and asked for a proposal for 50 small electric buses.

5 of family arrested in UP over law student's suspected honour killing
According to a complaint by the law student's boyfriend, her family claimed she had died due to illness and cremated her before the matter could come to the notice of the authorities.
A 20-year-old law student was allegedly killed in Uttar Pradesh's Aligarh district by her family in a suspected case of honour killing after she refused to end her relationship with a young man, and five of her family members have now been arrested in connection with the death.
The case came to light after the woman's boyfriend, Harshit, approached the police on Friday with a written complaint alleging that her family had killed her, according to the police.
According to the complaint, the family claimed that the woman, Himanshi, had died due to illness and cremated her on Thursday night before the matter could come to the notice of the authorities.
The police launched a probe following the complaint and arrested five people by Friday night on charges of homicide. Those arrested include Himanshi's mother, her two brothers and two maternal uncles, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Neeraj Kumar said.
In his complaint, Harshit claimed he and Himanshi had been in contact for nearly one and a half years, and that the latter's family had consistently opposed their relationship as they were from different castes.
He alleged that both of them were repeatedly given death threats by Himanshi's family. A CCTV video related to the case has also surfaced.
The footage reportedly shows the moment when Himanshi ran away from her home and reached a shop where Harshit was already present. Reports suggest that the woman's family members arrived at the scene and thrashed the duo.
While demanding justice for Himanshi, Harshit also said that he fears for his own life now. Police said further investigation into the case is underway.

full_text:
Ayodhya donation theft: UP to propose 3-IPS panel for new SIT to Supreme Court
Uttar Pradesh is set to place the names of three senior IPS officers before the Supreme Court for a new SIT in the Ayodhya temple donation case. The move follows the court's insistence on a team that conducts the probe itself rather than merely supervising it.
The Uttar Pradesh government is set to submit a panel of three senior IPS officers before the Supreme Court on Monday for the constitution of a new Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe the alleged theft and misappropriation of donations at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya.
The matter is scheduled to come up for hearing before the apex court, which had earlier directed the state government to constitute an SIT headed by a senior IPS officer to ensure an independent and effective investigation into the alleged embezzlement of devotees' donations.
According to sources, the state government is likely to propose the names of Inspector General (IG), Lucknow Range, Kiran S, Deputy Inspector General (DIG), Ayodhya Range, Somen Verma, and Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Ayodhya, Gaurav Grover for the new SIT. The proposed team is expected to function under the leadership of IG Kiran S and submit its findings to the Supreme Court.
The proposed panel marks a change from the existing SIT. Earlier, the committee included Lucknow Divisional Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant and Special Secretary (Finance) Neel Ratan Kumar. Under the revised proposal, the two civil officers have been replaced by senior IPS officers in line with the Supreme Court's observations.
The Supreme Court, while hearing a batch of petitions on July 20 seeking a fair, impartial and time-bound investigation into the alleged embezzlement, had questioned whether the existing SIT was directly investigating the case.
Responding to the Bench, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Uttar Pradesh government, had informed the court that the investigation was being carried out by the Uttar Pradesh Police, while the SIT was only supervising the probe.
Expressing dissatisfaction with the arrangement, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant directed the state government to obtain instructions on constituting an SIT that would itself conduct the investigation. The Bench suggested that the team be headed by a senior IPS officer, such as the IG of the Lucknow Range, who was already a member of the existing SIT.
The matter is being heard by a bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohan in a batch of petitions seeking an independent probe into the alleged embezzlement of donations made by devotees at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple.

headline: Dharmendra Pradhan a small sacrifice for BJP's bigger goals?
cluster_text: Dharmendra Pradhan a small sacrifice for BJP's bigger goals? [SEP] Dharmendra Pradhan a small sacrifice for BJP's bigger goals?
full_text:
Dharmendra Pradhan a small sacrifice for BJP's bigger goals?
The BJP is a party which obsesses over the future. That a resignation would create precedence was one of the key reasons it didn't want Dharmendra Pradhan to go. But then, the BJP has bigger Parliament plans, and Pradhan was but a tiny sacrifice.
Hearts and messages are generally carved on the wooden desks of colleges. "Today's a gift, that's why it's called present" is one of the cheesier ones. The BJP didn't study in one of those small-town colleges. A big part of its education came from the streets of competitive post-Independent India, where survival was the primordial instinct, and tomorrow was always the concern.
Millions in India believe Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan should have gone long before the crowds swelled at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar seeking his head. There was the NEET-UG paper leak, followed soon after by the CBSE online marking scheme fiasco.
There was neither action nor communication from the party and the government as India's higher education looked like the crumbled blocks of Jenga on a table.
With the Opposition missing, the cockroaches turned up on the table. Sonam Wangchuk fed the fledgling movement with his hunger strike. But what they might have failed to achieve was done by Delhi Police and the RAF. The brutal use of force on July 20 on protesters, thousands of whom were minors, pushed the BJP into the proverbial cul-de-sac.
With 'what if tomorrow...' on its mind, the BJP tried to delay what was destiny. That Pradhan's resignation might create a precedence was one of the key reasons why the brass tried to save him.
However, the more the delay in packing off Pradhan, the more it presented itself as a rigid regime, showing no flexibility to accommodate people's demands.
With the monsoon session of Parliament about to begin, political activity in the capital intensified. Leaders from Opposition parties started streaming into Jantar Mantar to be seen with a fasting Wangchuk.
The monsoon session began on July 20 and the first week was a washout.
Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, protested both in the House and in front of the PM's house and got detained. The Opposition was in no mood to let Parliament function. It knew what the government was aiming for. The government knew what the Opposition was striving for.
Two senior ministers — JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh — succeeded in getting Wangchuk to end his fast, toning down his demand for Pradhan's resignation. But by then, the protest had become way bigger than Wangchuk or the Cockroach Janta Party. The fire had spread and it needed a sacrifice made.
No stringent laws or fast-track courts or portrait-mode videos would satiate the leaping flames. It needed Pradhan, who had become the face of the crumbled Jenga blocks.
The BJP now thought, and thought seriously about tomorrow. About the future. Precedence can be taken care of, and the bigger goals, thus, took precedence.
The crucial delimitation bill, sources have revealed, might be introduced in the monsoon session. Though it wasn't among the five bills listed by the government, reports suggest the landmark bill could be brought in the session that would continue till August 13.
The Bill is special, and in April, the Modi government convened a special session to tie it with the women's reservation bill and get it passed. It was defeated as the treasury couldn't muster the support of two-thirds majority.
That was the first time that a constitutional amendment bill moved by the Modi government had been defeated. But the political landscape has changed since April.
Recent defections, inner-party feuds, lack of Opposition cohesion and political realignments have given the government hope that it could try and get the delimitation bill passed.
After the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the NDA had 293 MPs, including the BJP's 240. Its tally rose to 318, mainly because 20 rebel Trinamool MPs aligned with the NDA and six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs merged with the Shinde Sena faction.
In the Rajya Sabha in mid-June 2024, the NDA had 101 members. The number has now increased to 152.
The growth wasn't a miracle. They have been managed shrewdly and painstakingly towards the one big delimitation goal. Other than the engineering, it needed Sharad Pawar and MK Stalin to be persuaded. No mean task.
Consequently, this monsoon session was going to be all about the BJP's guts, guile and the splintering of the Opposition, especially of the Congress. But the CJP agitation consumed every other issue. The Congress had seized the opportunity to derail the BJP's parliamentary agenda. The government couldn't have brought its agenda up as long as Jantar Mantar remained combustible. Pradhan thus became the offering.
So, it was a choice between prestige and Pradhan on one hand, and hard work and big goals on the other. So, the Modi government tapped out to save the situation, and fight a bigger fight, on another day.
The optics had already gone bad. Senior leaders Nadda and Singh negotiating with rookies Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, both seated with crossed arms, wasn't the best image for the veteran duo.
But the Modi government has been known, though rarely, to make a tactical retreat when it becomes an absolute necessity. The withdrawal of the three farm bills after the prolonged farmers' agitation is one such example.
That protest too, like the one at Jantar Mantar, was taking an altogether different shape. No government wants a protest to be hijacked and turned into an inferno that goes beyond its control.
The stakes in Parliament were already very high and Pradhan was a small sacrifice. Though everyone knows what parampara, pratishtha and anushasan mean for the party steeped in tradition and aiming for civilisational goals, what would remain a question is why the BJP let the issue fester. Why didn't the BJP, which is always planning for tomorrow, not sacrifice Pradhan yesterday itself? Why can't a party on the climb get rid of the dog Nietzsche named 'Ego'?

Government gave Gen Z content gold: Chetan Bhagat to India Today
Author Chetan Bhagat said the NEET paper leak protests have become India's first major Gen Z digital revolt. He said Instagram reels and viral videos of police action turned student anger into a nationwide movement.
Author Chetan Bhagat believes the nationwide students' protests over the NEET paper leak mark India's first major "Gen Z digital revolt", driven not just by anger over the examination system but also by the explosive power of Instagram reels, which transformed online outrage into a mass movement. The protests, led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), culminated in Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation on Saturday.
Speaking to India Today, Bhagat said the anger among students had existed for months, but it was the viral videos of police action against protesters that became the turning point.
"The anger was always there. The NEET paper leak issue was even an issue in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. What surprised everyone was the extent to which the protests spread," he said.
According to Bhagat, the biggest misconception was that Gen Z would remain confined to social media. "People felt this generation would never leave their phones. They are digital warriors. They would never come out on the streets. However, they did this time."
He argued that the police action inadvertently gave the movement its most powerful weapon. "The government gave them content gold, visuals of heavily armed policemen chasing and lathi-charging teenagers. Those images triggered a huge emotional response."
'INSTAGRAM BECAME A WEAPON OF PROTEST'
Bhagat said Instagram reels played a far greater role than platforms like X because of their ability to spread short, emotionally charged videos at lightning speed. "Instagram has become a powerful weapon of protest, bringing all these groups together," he said.
He further said the platform rewards dramatic visual content, and the images from the protests fit that format perfectly.
"Big cops hitting teenagers... they weren't demanding money or jobs. They were asking for fairness, and they were getting beaten up. That was bound to explode online," he said.
Bhagat predicted the movement would continue to gather momentum. "This weekend, wait and watch the level of participation. The exponential growth function is something people underestimate. It is all Instagram-driven."
Comparing the ongoing protests with the 2011 Anna Hazare anti-corruption movement, Bhagat said the biggest difference was the availability of cheap mobile internet and instant video sharing.
"You and I have probably seen the same videos within hours. That wasn't possible in 2011."
He said governments now need to react much faster in the social media era. "Every hour they delay, the movement spreads further. Governments have to act quickly and dramatically, not through lip service or tokenism."
Bhagat praised the young protesters for standing up for what they believe in. "It's very brave of you. You make us all proud. We were also young once, and it's nice to see the same spark in your generation," he said.

headline: CJP protest ends, what's next? Ashutosh Ranka, Neha Bora reveal plan to India Today
cluster_text: CJP protest ends, what's next? Ashutosh Ranka, Neha Bora reveal plan to India Today [SEP] CJP protest ends, what's next? Ashutosh Ranka, Neha Bora reveal plan to India Today
full_text:
CJP protest ends, what's next? Ashutosh Ranka, Neha Bora reveal plan to India Today
After Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, Ashutosh Ranka and Neha Bora said the protest leaders would first return home and rest. They said the movement would now press for accountability and structural reforms in education.
After nearly 50 days of protests, a 23-day hunger strike and weeks away from their families, the leaders of the movement that forced Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation have a surprisingly simple immediate plan: go home and sleep.
But the rest of their answer is more complicated.
“The only thing we have planned for now is to go home and sleep, meet our families,” said Ashutosh Ranka, spokesperson of the Cockroach Janta Party, after Pradhan's resignation.
Ranka said the core team had spent nearly two months away from their families and was now dealing with infections and fever after the prolonged protest.
But the break, he made clear, is not the end of the movement.
“Stay rest assured, the cockroaches are just getting started,” Ranka said.
The nearly 50-day protest may have achieved its immediate demand - Pradhan's resignation - but the leaders of the movement say they now want to push for accountability and structural reforms in India's education system.
“This has not ended. This is just getting started. We will not stop till the education system of this country is fixed, and that's a promise,” Ranka said.
He said the movement had already submitted a five-point demand charter to the government and that another round of discussions with ministers had been agreed for a month later.
“The idea is not agitation. The idea is to bring back accountability in the system. The idea is to push structural reforms in the system, and whatever it takes, we'll do,” Ranka said.
AISA president Neha Bora, who spent 23 days on hunger strike during the protest, also said the movement had achieved more than it had initially set out to do.
“We had set out to take Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, and instead what we also achieved, along with Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, was a young people, a young nation, that has learnt to fight its battles,” she said.
Bora said the movement had brought together anger over paper leaks, unemployment, the National Education Policy, the National Testing Agency and what she described as the wider “bulldozing” of India's education system.
“This is a country of unemployed people, where even if you have a degree, even if you complete your higher education, it is almost impossible for us to get a job,” she said.
The leaders also rejected the idea that the movement had ended with Pradhan's resignation or that the Education Minister was merely “collateral damage” in a wider anti-BJP campaign.
“I wouldn't make the mistake of calling Dharmendra Pradhan collateral damage,” Bora said.
Ranka described the protest as a movement for accountability rather than simply an anti-BJP agitation.
“It is a movement for accountability in the system, which has gone missing in the last few years in this country,” he said.
The next phase could also take the movement beyond street protests. Asked whether the Cockroach Janta Party could become a political party, Ranka did not rule it out.
“The only thing I've learnt in my short career in public life and politics is never say no. Never say no,” he said.
So, for now, the protesters are going home to sleep.
But if their own leaders are to be believed, the “cockroaches are just getting started.”

10 defining images that captured India's watershed Gen Z protests
A sequence of photographs traced the CJP's agitation over alleged NEET irregularities from street clashes to talks with the government. The images showed the protest's spread across cities and its culmination in Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.
A tear gas canister thrown back at police. Water cannons turning protesters into silhouettes. A hunger strike ending with a hospital shift. A woman standing defiantly in front of a police van. And, finally, celebrations at Jantar Mantar after the Education Minister's resignation.
For almost 50 days, the Cockroach Janta Party's agitation over alleged NEET irregularities produced a series of images that captured a protest moving from confrontation on the streets to negotiations with the government - and eventually, a political victory for its principal demand.
Here is the CJP agitation in pictures, from the first clashes and hunger strikes to the moment its protesters celebrated after Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned.
THE PROTEST THAT REACHED PARLIAMENT
A protester throws back a tear gas canister towards police as supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party march towards Parliament on the opening day of the Monsoon Session, demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged examination paper leaks, in New Delhi on July 20. The image captured one of the most intense moments of the agitation as protesters confronted security personnel during the march.
THIS MOVEMENT IS NOT JUST IN DELHI
A 27-year-old model, Rhiya Ahir, stands with her arms outstretched in front of a police van during a demonstration in Mumbai in solidarity with the CJP's agitation over alleged NEET irregularities on July 22. The protest reflected how the movement found support beyond the national capital.
WATER CANNONS USED AGAINST PROTESTERS
Police use a water cannon to disperse Students' Federation of India activists during a protest march demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination in Thiruvananthapuram on July 23.
SHE STOOD BETWEEN THE BATON AND THE PROTESTERS
As a police officer moves through a tightly packed crowd during the protest, a young woman reaches out to protect fellow demonstrators caught in the confrontation. With protesters pushing against the barricades and police trying to control the crowd, she appears to place herself between the officer and those around her - a striking moment from an agitation marked by escalating tensions on the streets.
SOLIDARITY AT JANTAR MANTAR
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk and his wife Gitanjali J Angmo attend a protest organised by the CJP at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on July 17. Wangchuk, who was on an indefinite hunger strike, also reiterated his demand for constitutional safeguards and greater protection for Ladakh.
A MOMENT OF TENSION
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacts after a woman threw an ink-like liquid on him as he began an indefinite hunger strike at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on July 18.
'HAM AAPKE BACHCHE NAHI HAIN'
A moment from the CJP agitation captures the anger and defiance that became a recurring feature of the protest, as demonstrators challenged the government's handling of alleged examination irregularities and demanded accountability.
THE MOMENT THE PROTEST TURNED
Protesters clash with security personnel at barricades during a march towards Parliament demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination and expressing support for climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, near Parliament House in New Delhi on July 20.
HUNGER STRIKE ENDS WITH A HOSPITAL SHIFT
Activist Sonam Wangchuk, who had been on an indefinite hunger strike for 21 days, waves as he is shifted to a hospital from Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on July 18. He later broke his fast on the 26th day at Gurgaon hospital.
CELEBRATIONS AFTER PRADHAN'S RESIGNATION
CJP spokespersons Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka celebrate with supporters at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on July 25, after Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and took responsibility for the NEET paper leak.
49 DAYS LATER, THE PROTESTERS HAD THEIR ANSWER
CJP supporters celebrate at Jantar Mantar after Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned over the NEET paper leak controversy, bringing the protest's principal demand to an end. After 49 days of agitation, slogans of anger gave way to cheers, raised fists and celebrations as protesters marked what they saw as a victory for their movement.

How global media covered CJP protests that led to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
As images of police action and thousands of young protesters flooded global headlines, the Cockroach Janta Party-led movement came to symbolise a wider debate on governance, youth aspirations and political accountability in India.
What began as a protest over irregularities in India’s education system, particularly the 2026 NEET-UG paper leak, quickly escalated into a major international story.
Images of baton charges, tear gas, candlelight marches and thousands of young protesters camping on Delhi’s streets travelled widely across global media. As the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) movement grew, international media increasingly covered it as a broader story about governance, youth aspirations and political accountability in India.

Here’s how some of the world’s biggest news organisations reported the protests.

"Protesters were scathing about how celebrities had commented on global tragedies or injustices but turned a blind eye to the grievances of people at home, even when their most devoted fanbase were being baton-charged and teargassed by the police," it said.

It reported that while the movement began with anger over alleged education irregularities, it soon expanded into broader concerns about unemployment, corruption and governance, reflecting wider public frustration.

Did CJP's 72-hour ultimatum force Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation?
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned after Centre ministers held multiple rounds of talks with the CJP. The student outfit then withdrew its agitation, saying its main demand had been met.
Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation on Saturday came after intense negotiations between the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), with the student outfit reportedly issuing a 72-hour ultimatum demanding his removal and threatening to revive its march to Parliament if the demand was not met.
According to sources, the ultimatum was delivered during the second round of talks on Friday between CJP leaders and Union ministers JP Nadda and Dr Jitendra Singh. During the meeting, the CJP maintained that Pradhan's resignation was its sole non-negotiable demand.
The student organisation reportedly told the ministers that if Pradhan did not step down within 72 hours, protesters would once again march towards Parliament and publicly announce the escalation of their agitation.
In response, Nadda and Jitendra Singh assured the CJP delegation that they would discuss the demand with the government. Sources said the two ministers subsequently briefed Union Home Minister Amit Shah on the outcome of the talks.
GOVT INITIATED BUREAUCRATIC MEASURES
Even as discussions continued, the government initiated steps to overhaul the National Testing Agency (NTA). Forty-seven NTA officials were relieved of their duties, while the process of recruiting personnel as part of the agency's restructuring was also set in motion.
However, despite these measures, the CJP remained firm that reforms alone would not suffice and insisted that Pradhan's resignation was essential for accountability.
Sources said Nadda and Jitendra Singh met Amit Shah once again on Saturday before a decision was taken. Shortly afterwards, Pradhan submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
3RD ROUND OF TALKS TAKES PLACE
Following the resignation, the two Union ministers held another round of talks with CJP representatives to finalise the remaining issues.
The Centre and the CJP later addressed a joint press conference, where the student outfit announced the withdrawal of its agitation after securing what it described as its principal demand. CJP leaders appealed to protesters gathered at Delhi's Jantar Mantar and supporters across the country to return home peacefully.
Pradhan's resignation came after weeks of nationwide protests over alleged examination irregularities and the NEET-UG controversy, marking one of the rare instances of a senior Union minister stepping down amid sustained public mobilisation.
The sequence of events has raised questions over whether the CJP's 72-hour ultimatum ultimately accelerated the government's decision to seek the minister's resignation.

full_text:
Dipke skips thanking Wangchuk, activist whose fast turned protest into movement
Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned and an elated CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke announced victory from the protest stage at Jantar Mantar. However, there was no mention of activist Sonam Wangchuk, whose 26-day fast turned the protest into a movement.
Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned and an elated CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke announced victory from the protest stage at Jantar Mantar. However, there was no mention of activist Sonam Wangchuk, whose 26-day fast turned the protest into a movement.
The announcement of victory on Saturday was made by CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke from the protest stage at New Delhi Jantar Mantar. Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan announced his resignation just minutes ahead. But missing from Dipke's speech, as he addressed the protesters, was the mention of activist Sonam Wangchuk.
Dipke emphasised that people should resist turning one person into a hero. He said he himself shouldn't be made a hero.
"I want to say something very important. Don't make me a hero because Dharmendra Pradhan resigned today. Don't make that mistake. The country has been ruined because we keep making one person a hero," said Dipke.
In his brief speech, Dipke said that Pradhan's resignation was "proof that if you people are not afraid, if you do not bow before this government, then we can make anyone resign. There's no need to be afraid. This is democracy."
Why the skipping of any mention of Sonam Wangchuk was deafening was because the activist from Ladakh had fasted for 26 days and had given the momentum to the protest.
Wangchuk is admitted in the ICU of Medanta hospital in Gurgaon, and he broke his fast just on Thursday night on the assurances and requests of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh.
After Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike, the decision became the subject of political debate and criticism from a section of people. As questions mounted over the circumstances in which he broke his fast, his wife, Gitanjali Angmo, defended him, urging critics to remember the personal cost of his sacrifice.
HOW SOMAN WANGCHUK TURNED THE CJP PROTEST INTO A MOVEMENT
The protests at Jantar Mantar began on June 6 as Dipke landed in India from Boston, the US. Other than a few aides like Saurabh Das, Ashutosh Ranka and the now-fired Vijeta Dahiya, there were no big names associated with it. Only Wangchuk, an eminent educationist, who had lent support to the youngsters.
India Today Digital reported from the ground from the very beginning and witnessed that the crowd was sparse initially. Seeing that the government was in no mood to relent, Wangchuk started an indefinite hunger strike on June 28.
As his fast continued into weeks, and he turned visibly weak, people grew concerned and interested in the protest. India Today Digital saw a remarkably higher footfall.
The government, worried over the repercussions, shifted Wangchuk to a hospital by force on July 18. He then shifted to Gurgaon's Medanta hospital.
The removal of Wangchuk became a focal point of the protest. His continued hunger strike from the hospital became the rallying point with people associated with the protest and lakhs of supporters changing their WhatsApp DP to "I support Sonam", with the activist's photo and tricolour in the background.
Though Wangchuk wasn't on the ground, his messages kept inspiring the protesters. Dipke and others spoke about him reverentially. It was Wangchuk who made a fervent appeal to people to make the CJP's march to Parliament on July 20 a success. He said he would "return as ghost" if the march didn't get enough participation.
However, the sentiment shifted entirely after July 20. As the protesters marched in large numbers, there was large-scale confrontation. Under attack from lumpen elements, the Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel resorted to the use of force.
What even Wangchuk couldn't achieve had been achieved by the Delhi Police and the RAF. Tens of thousands poured into Jantar Mantar seeing the videos of alleged brutality by the security personnel. The protest reached its peak.
On July 22, Wangchuk declared that he would end his hunger strike. That came after ministers Nadda and Singh met him in hospital and gave him assurances. Wangchuk also scaled down his demand for Pradhan's resignation. Wangchuk, the centre of the agitation, had been won over.
THE BACKLASH AFTER WANGCHUK ENDED HIS FAST
After Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike, the manner in which he did so triggered debates. Critics questioned his decision to break the fast after assurances from Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh. Many said he diluted his conditions as they didn't include Pradhan's resignation. Wangchuk's wife, Gitanjali Angmo, hit out sharply at the critics and appealed for compassion. She said people should remember the personal cost of his sacrifice.
But by then, no one was actually the centre of the protest now. Even the CJP leadership wasn't in full control. It was a mass of protesters with one single point of demand, which was the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.
On Friday evening, CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka was asked his opinion on Wangchuk resigning without demanding Pradhan's resignation by India Today journalist Rajdeep Sardesai.
"This is not just about the CJP or the protesting people at Jantar Mantar any more," Ranka told India Today TV. "There are protests happening all across the country... The people of this country want Pradhan gone." Ranka also said the agitation "has become bigger than CJP."
"We are so happy that Sir ended his fast... We have been requesting him to end his fast for a few days now because we are really, really concerned about his health." Ranka added, "He has ignited the entire country... People have really woken up because Sonam Wangchuk Sir was with this movement."
But by then, no one was actually the centre of the protest now. Even the CJP leadership wasn't in full control. It was a mass of protesters with one single point of demand – Dharmendra Pradhan must resign.
In multiple interviews, Dipke, Das and Ranka made that clear. The movement had become bigger than the CJP and Pradhan's issue had become non-negotiable.
The evident happened on Saturday, as Pradhan announced his resignation.
While the movement had become bigger than an individual and an outfit, Dipke's skipping of Wangchuk's mention in the victory speech was jarring. For, it was Wangchuk who gave credence and spirit of fighting to the youth movement.

headline: Rajnath Singh honours Kargil heroes in Ladakh on Operation Vijay anniversary
cluster_text: Rajnath Singh honours Kargil heroes in Ladakh on Operation Vijay anniversary [SEP] Rajnath Singh honours Kargil heroes in Ladakh on Operation Vijay anniversary
full_text:
Rajnath Singh honours Kargil heroes in Ladakh on Operation Vijay anniversary
At Dras, the Army held Shaurya Sandhya to honour soldiers killed in the 1999 Kargil war. The commemoration underscored Operation Vijay's legacy as families, veterans and top leaders paid tribute.
The Army on Saturday held a Shaurya Sandhya at the Kargil War Memorial in Dras to honour the Indian soldiers who died in the 1999 Kargil conflict, as part of a two-day commemoration marking the 27th anniversary of Operation Vijay. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh took part in the event and handed a ceremonial kalash (sacred metal pot) to some family members of the personnel who made the ultimate sacrifice in the war.
The programme began on the eve of Kargil Vijay Diwas and will conclude on Sunday with a wreath-laying ceremony and the flag-in of the Shaurya Vijay Yatra from the National War Memorial in Delhi to the Kargil War Memorial in Dras. Singh, who arrived in Dras on Saturday, will be the chief guest at the Shradhanjali Samaroh on Sunday.
Saturday evening's ceremony was attended by Ladakh Lieutenant Governor VK Saxena, Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth, General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Northern Command, Lieutenant General Pratik Sharma, other senior Army officers and several military veterans.
A band of the Ladakh Scouts played patriotic songs, including AR Rahman's "Maa Tujhe Salaam", after which guests lit candles near the obelisk of the main memorial. As night fell, hundreds of neatly placed stones in rows in the Veer Bhoomi cenotaph zone were illuminated.
Earlier in the day, the Army held several events to mark the anniversary of Operation Vijay, which falls on July 26. The two-day commemoration began with Yudh Sansmaran at the Lamochen viewpoint overlooking the Kargil battlefield. Officials said the occasion marks the victory in which Indian soldiers, braving snow-clad peaks and firing by Pakistani troops, reclaimed the heights of Kargil.
The event opened with a 33-minute video on the Kargil war and India's triumph under Operation Vijay, followed by a 17-minute commemorative clip honouring 40 Kargil bravehearts whose next of kin will be present. Major General Amit Prakash Singh, General Officer Commanding, Forever in Operations Division, senior Army officers, Kargil war veterans, Veer Naris and Veer Matas attended the programme.
Murti Devi Dahiya, whose son, Sep Ravinder of 4 Jat unit, died in the war, said she was overcome with emotion at the event. "When I see other soldiers in uniform, I feel they are like my sons too. And standing here watching the peaks we reclaimed in the Kargil war, I feel very proud of my son and his service to the nation," she told PTI.
In the afternoon, a Gauravmaya Sanskriti event was organised at Vishwanathan Stadium in Dras, with the General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Northern Command, in attendance. The cultural programme celebrated patriotism, India's cultural heritage, and the courage and professionalism of the Army.
It included a motorcycle display by the Shwet Ashw Motorcycle Riders, a display of India's combat drone capabilities, and the participation of robotic mules. The Army also hosted a Vijay Bhoj at the 16 Grenadiers Officers' Mess to mark the success of Operation Vijay.
The events are being held to commemorate India's victory in the battles fought on the icy heights of Kargil during the nearly three-month conflict and to pay homage to the fallen soldiers. Sunday's programme will also include the Shradhanjali Samaroh, where Singh and the Army chief will pay tribute in the presence of senior officers, Kargil war veterans, next of kin, civil dignitaries and serving soldiers.

headline: Longer jail terms, faster trials: Proposed key changes in anti-cheating law
cluster_text: Longer jail terms, faster trials: Proposed key changes in anti-cheating law [SEP] Longer jail terms, faster trials: Proposed key changes in anti-cheating law
full_text:
Longer jail terms, faster trials: Proposed key changes in anti-cheating law
The Centre will introduce the Public Examinations Amendment Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha on Monday. The move follows the NEET-UG paper leak row and seeks faster trials with tougher penalties.
The Union government is set to table the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha on Monday, July 27, as it seeks to strengthen the legal framework against examination-related fraud. The amendments are aimed at strengthening the 2024 law by introducing harsher punishments, ensuring time-bound investigations and trials, and creating special fast-track courts to ensure speedy justice.
The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 seeks to significantly strengthen India's legal framework against examination malpractices by introducing tougher penalties, faster investigations, and time-bound trials. The proposed amendments aim to improve accountability, deter organised examination-related fraud, and restore confidence in the country's public examination system.
WHY THE GOVERNMENT IS BRINGING AMENDMENT BILL
The amendment bill is being brought against the backdrop of the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, which sparked widespread protests by students across the country and intensified demands for tougher anti-cheating laws, greater transparency, and stronger accountability in the conduct of public examinations. The move comes just hours after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) called off its protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Saturday, saying the government had agreed to its principal demands and assured action on the issue.
As per the Lok Sabha's list of business, Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh is scheduled to introduce the legislation. Following its introduction, he is also expected to seek the House's approval to take up the Bill for discussion and passage.
Amid escalating protests over the alleged NEET paper leak and mounting political pressure, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday unveiled a series of measures aimed at tackling examination fraud, including the creation of fast-track courts to expedite trials in paper leak cases.
The announcement came as students continued demonstrations in Delhi, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, while the issue also dominated proceedings in Parliament. Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister on Saturday.
"We have decided to set up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks. Have directed the concerned authorities and officials to take all necessary steps in this regard," the Prime Minister said.
PM Modi stressed that safeguarding students' interests remained a key priority for his government and warned that any attempt to compromise the future of young aspirants would be dealt with firmly. He added that the fast-track courts were part of a broader strategy to strengthen the integrity of the country's examination system.
The announcement followed criticism of the government's handling of protests, particularly after police action against demonstrators marching towards Parliament on July 20.
Meanwhile, Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi intensified his attack on the government, alleging that there had been 152 examination paper leaks over the past decade without a single conviction. He argued that the recurring incidents had severely undermined India's education system and called for greater accountability.
WHAT CHANGES FROM THE 2024 LAW?
Against this backdrop, let us see how this amendment differs from the principal 2024 Act, which was enacted with the objective of bringing greater transparency, fairness, and credibility to the public examination system, inspiring confidence among candidates and effectively deterring persons, organised groups, and institutions from indulging in unfair means.
STRICTER PUNISHMENT FOR INDIVIDUALS AND ORGANISED CRIME FRAUD
One of the most significant changes proposed in the Bill is the enhancement of punishments for those found guilty of examination fraud. The proposed amendments significantly enhance penalties for both individual offenders and organised examination-related fraud.
For individuals found guilty of using unfair means in public examinations, the Bill proposes increasing the prison term to five to 10 years, up from the existing three to five years. It also seeks to raise the maximum fine from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 50 lakh, signalling a much tougher stance against examination malpractice.
The legislation also introduces stricter punishments for organised examination-related crimes. The minimum imprisonment for those involved in organised paper leak rackets or cheating networks has been increased from five years to seven years, while the minimum fine has been raised tenfold—from Rs 1 crore to Rs 10 crore. The enhanced penalties are aimed at deterring large-scale examination fraud and dismantling organised criminal networks involved in such offences.
TOUGHER ACTION AGAINST SERVICE PROVIDERS
The Bill also proposes stringent action against service providers—including agencies or organisations responsible for conducting examinations—if they are found complicit in examination malpractice. The maximum financial penalty for such entities has been increased from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore, while the period during which they can be barred from conducting examinations has been doubled from four years to eight years.
Corporate accountability has also been strengthened under the proposed legislation. Directors, senior management personnel, or any individual responsible for the affairs of a company found involved in examination fraud will face a minimum prison sentence of five years (the existing minimum is three years), along with fines of Rs 5 crore (the existing fine is Rs 1 crore). The provision aims to ensure that top executives cannot evade responsibility for organised malpractice carried out under their supervision.
SPECIAL TASK FORCE AND TIME-BOUND INVESTIGATIONS
To strengthen enforcement, the legislation empowers the Central Government to constitute a Special Task Force (STF) wherever necessary to investigate serious offences related to public examinations. The STF will be tasked with handling complex cases involving organised fraud, large-scale paper leaks, or other major examination-related crimes.
The amendment also introduces strict timelines for investigations. Police authorities, central investigating agencies, or the STF will be required to complete investigations into offences under the Act within two months, ensuring that cases are not delayed indefinitely.
SPECIAL FAST TRACK COURTS AND QUICKER TRIALS
To ensure speedy resolution of cases, the Bill empowers State governments and Union Territory administrations to designate any Court of Session as a Special Fast Track Court for the exclusive trial of offences under the Act. These dedicated courts will handle cases related to public examination fraud, enabling faster hearings and disposal of matters through a focused judicial process.
The Bill mandates day-to-day hearings in these Special Fast Track Courts, with trials expected to be completed within three months of the filing of the chargesheet. This provision is intended to deliver timely justice and strengthen public confidence in the examination system.
To support faster prosecution, States and Union Territories will appoint Special Public Prosecutors for these designated courts. These prosecutors will exclusively handle cases under the Act, enabling more focused and efficient legal proceedings.
FASTER DISPOSAL OF PENDING CASES
All pending cases under the Act will be transferred to the designated Special Fast Track Courts, which will be required to complete the trials within three months from the date of transfer. These courts will also be empowered to hear and decide connected offences arising from the same matter under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, or any other applicable laws.
The proposed amendments also streamline the appeals process. Appeals against judgments delivered by the Special Fast Track Courts will lie directly before a Division Bench of the High Court. The Bill provides that appeals should ordinarily be filed within 30 days, although courts may allow an extension of up to 90 days in exceptional circumstances. It also envisages that High Courts should endeavour to dispose of such appeals within three months, ensuring that legal proceedings are concluded without undue delay.

2024: 3–5 years jail | Rs 10 lakh fine
2026: 5–10 years jail | Rs 50 lakh fine
Organised Crime:
2024: Min 5 years jail | Rs 1 crore fine
2026: Min 7 years jail | Rs 10 crore fine
Service Providers:
2024: Rs 1 crore fine | 4-year ban
2026: Rs 5 crore fine | 8-year ban
Investigation Window:
2024: No deadline
2026: Mandatory 60 days
Trial Timeline:
2024: Regular court timelines
2026: Fast-track court (3-month trial limit)

cluster_text: Don't troll him: Assam CM defends minister whose daughter joined NEET protest [SEP] Don't troll him: Assam CM defends minister whose daughter joined NEET protest
full_text:
Don't troll him: Assam CM defends minister whose daughter joined NEET protest
Videos of Keshab Mahanta's daughter at a NEET protest drew a response from Himanta Biswa Sarma. The Chief Minister said adult children's actions should not be linked to their parents.
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Saturday defended Cabinet colleague Keshab Mahanta after videos of the minister's daughter participating in a protest over alleged NEET examination irregularities went viral, saying parents should not be judged by the political choices of their adult children.
The controversy erupted after Dibisa Mahanta, daughter of Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) leader and Assam Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Keshab Mahanta, was seen at a protest in Guwahati on Thursday demanding accountability over the alleged examination irregularities and the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Videos circulating on social media purportedly showed Dibisa raising slogans against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and calling for Pradhan's resignation. PTI reported that it could not independently verify the authenticity of the clips.
Responding to the controversy, Sarma said Keshab Mahanta should not be criticised or trolled because of his daughter's participation in the protest.
'DON'T ATTACK HIM FOR HIS DAUGHTER'
"I don't think we should attack or troll Keshab Mahanta for the protest by his daughter. She may not follow her father's political ideology," the Chief Minister said.
Drawing a parallel with his own family, Sarma added, "Tomorrow when my son practises law, he may defend someone whom I may not like."
He stressed that once children become adults, their actions and political beliefs should not be linked to those of their parents.
At the same time, Sarma said he did not agree with the slogans allegedly raised by Dibisa during the protest. "When I meet her next time, I will definitely talk to her about it and try to make her understand that what she said was not right," he said.
The protest in Guwahati was organised to highlight alleged irregularities in the NEET examination and to demand the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union Education Minister.
There was no immediate reaction from Keshab Mahanta over the controversy. According to PTI, attempts to contact the minister for comment were unsuccessful.

full_text:
Will live up to PM's expectations, says new Education Minister Pralhad Joshi
Union Minister and BJP MP Pralhad Joshi took additional charge of the Education Ministry after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned. He said he would work with humility amid NEET protest fallout.
Newly-appointed Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi on Saturday said he would discharge his responsibilities with “complete humility” and a strong sense of duty after being given additional charge of the ministry following Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation in the wake of students' protests over the NEET paper leak controversy.
President Droupadi Murmu accepted Pradhan’s resignation on Saturday, after which Prime Minister Narendra Modi assigned Joshi the additional portfolio.
Speaking after taking charge, Joshi said the Prime Minister had placed his trust in him by entrusting him with a “significant responsibility”. He thanked PM Narendra Modi for the opportunity and said he would work sincerely under his guidance to meet expectations in the Education Ministry.
“With full dedication, humility and honesty, I will work towards fulfilling this responsibility,” Joshi said.
The 63-year-old credited Pradhan with implementing the National Education Policy (NEP) and said several important initiatives had been undertaken in the education sector in recent years.
“In the last four to five years, Dharmendra Pradhan also implemented the National Education Policy, and several important initiatives were undertaken. The country has made significant progress in the new education system,” Joshi said.
He added that he would work to the best of his ability under the Prime Minister’s guidance and fulfil his responsibilities with dedication.
Joshi will retain his existing portfolios while also taking charge of the Education Ministry. The Lok Sabha MP from Karnataka’s Dharwad constituency currently serves as Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, as well as Minister for New and Renewable Energy.
Pradhan stepped down amid student protests over irregularities in the NEET examination. In a letter shared on X, he said he had submitted his resignation to PM Modi in the interest of students and to ensure that the protests were not exploited by “anti-national forces”.
“The situation that has emerged at Jantar Mantar and elsewhere in the country should not be exploited by anti-national forces. The unity of the country must remain intact. The future of every student in India should not get entangled in legal complications,” Pradhan said.
“Keeping these considerations in mind, I have sent my resignation to the Hon’ble Prime Minister,” he added.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) called off its 49-day agitation at Delhi's Jantar Mantar following the resignation of Pradhan and government assurances on the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters and organisers.
The decision was taken after three rounds of talks between a CJP delegation and government representatives, including Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh.
Announcing the withdrawal, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said the agitation was being called off in good faith, with the group expecting the government to implement the agreed terms within the promised timelines.

headline: Sarnath becomes India's 45th Unesco World Heritage Site, PM calls it a proud moment
cluster_text: Sarnath becomes India's 45th Unesco World Heritage Site, PM calls it a proud moment [SEP] Sarnath becomes India's 45th Unesco World Heritage Site, PM calls it a proud moment
full_text:
Sarnath becomes India's 45th Unesco World Heritage Site, PM calls it a proud moment
The ancient Buddhist site Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh has been inscribed on the Unesco World Heritage List, becoming India's 45th World Heritage Site during the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea.
India's ancient Buddhist site of Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh was on Saturday inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List during the 48th session of the Unesco World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea.
Unesco announced the decision in a post on X, saying, "New inscription on the Unesco World Heritage List: Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath, India."
The inscription makes Sarnath India's 45th site on the Unesco World Heritage List.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the recognition and described it as "a proud moment for every Indian."
"A proud moment for every Indian! Delighted that Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh has been inscribed on the Unesco World Heritage List," PM Modi said in a post on X.
The Prime Minister said Sarnath has a deep connection with Lord Buddha, whose timeless message of wisdom, compassion and harmony continues to inspire the world.
"This recognition celebrates India's profound civilisational and spiritual heritage. It will also inspire more people across the world to come to Sarnath and connect with the ideals of Lord Buddha," he said.
Located around 10 kilometres from Varanasi, Sarnath is one of the most significant pilgrimage sites for Buddhists across the world. It holds a unique place in history as the site where Gautam Buddha delivered his first sermon.
The decision to inscribe Sarnath on the World Heritage List was taken during the ongoing 48th session of the Unesco World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea.
In August 2025, Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat informed the Lok Sabha in a written reply that India had submitted a dossier titled "Ancient Buddhist Site, Sarnath" to the Unesco World Heritage Centre for the 2025-26 nomination cycle.
The World Heritage Committee is one of the two bodies that govern the Convention for the Protection of the World's Cultural and Natural Heritage.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah also welcomed the development, saying, "Our cultural pride soars even higher today as Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh has been included in the Unesco World Heritage List."
Calling it an endorsement of India's ancient heritage associated with Lord Buddha, Shah said the recognition would take the Buddha's luminous wisdom to more people and inspire them to embrace the ideals of peace and enlightenment for a better world.
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India's timeless civilisational heritage continues to receive global recognition.
"Sarnath's inscription on the Unesco World Heritage List is a proud moment for every Indian and a shining reflection of Uttar Pradesh's glorious spiritual and cultural legacy," he said, adding that Uttar Pradesh welcomes the world to experience this eternal heritage.

full_text:
Will build Agra museum dedicated to Chhatrapati Shivaji by year-end: Yogi Adityanath
UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said Agra's proposed museum will honour Chhatrapati Shivaji and not Aurangzeb. He made the announcement as he sharpened his attack on the Samajwadi Party, while tying heritage to development politics.
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has criticised the previous Samajwadi Party government over its plan to build a museum dedicated to Mughal emperor Aurangzeb in Agra, and said his government will instead complete a grand museum in the name of Chhatrapati Shivaji by the end of this year. He said public money would not be used for a museum named after “an invader”.
Speaking at a function where he inaugurated and laid the foundation for 53 development projects worth more than Rs 342 crore, Adityanath also said the government had approved the acquisition of the ‘kothi’ (residence) in Agra where Shivaji had stayed. He also spoke about infrastructure, industry, tourism and farmer-related measures in Agra, while attacking the Samajwadi Party and Congress over governance and law and order.
Addressing the gathering, Adityanath said, “In Agra, the city where Chhatrapati Shivaji displayed his valour, the Samajwadi Party government was building a Mughal museum. Public funds would not be used for a museum named after an invader; instead, a museum would be constructed in the name of India’s national heroes.” He said construction of the Shivaji museum would be completed by the end of this year.
He added, “We have also approved the acquisition of the ‘kothi’ in Agra where Chhatrapati Shivaji had stayed.”
Targeting the Samajwadi Party, Adityanath said it had remained focused on its own development.
“Public funds became a medium for the ‘Saifai Syndicate’ to engage in loot. Whether it was stealing job opportunities meant for the youth, misappropriating welfare schemes intended for the poor, or the sinful act of snatching away the prosperity of our farmers, the Samajwadi Party and before them, the Congress, committed these sins,” he said.
He said the impact of this was that the state’s youth faced an identity crisis, farmers were driven to suicide, and daughters and traders lived in insecurity. In an apparent jibe at former Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav, he said, “Only God save a state where its chief minister would wake up at 12 noon, get ready by 2 pm, head to the gym at 5 pm, and enjoy spending the time after 7 pm with his circle of friends.”
Adityanath said this was why a mafia figure had emerged in every district and every police station and tehsil had effectively gone into the hands of goons. “Anarchy, curfews, and the rule of criminals and the mafia once plagued the state. The picture of Uttar Pradesh you see today represents a system free from all that. Today, there are no curfews or riots. Everything is truly well here,” he said.
On Agra’s development, he said, “We have already taken steps to establish an international airport in Agra. It is now developing into a new centre not only for industrial activity in the Braj region, but also for tourism. Connectivity has improved significantly.” He said the Supreme Court had approved work that had earlier been halted because of the Taj Trapezium Zone.
On Thursday, the Supreme Court allowed the Taj Trapezium Zone Authority to process around 400 pending applications for setting up non-polluting Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises in the ecologically sensitive area around the Taj Mahal.
The court, however, said experts from the Central Empowered Committee and the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute must scrutinise each proposal. It said that if any objection arose, the application concerned would not be accepted without the leave of the court.
Adityanath said Agra was becoming not only a smart city but also a new model of a safe city. He said Peru’s International Potato Centre had to open a branch somewhere in India, and land was offered in Agra. “This will benefit our farmers: their produce will receive value addition, and with much higher prices, their incomes will increase. This will bring prosperity to their lives,” he said.
He said work on multi-level parking, an Integrated Command and Control Centre, and the modernisation of the city’s traffic system would now move ahead quickly. He added that farmers’ concerns had been resolved after they were raised by public representatives. He also said the government was working to give Petha global recognition under the “One District, One Product” and “One District, One Cuisine” schemes.
Adityanath said development works were also being carried forward at Bateshwar Dham, Kailash Temple, Guru Ka Tal, Geet Govind Vatika, the birthplace of Atal Bihari Vajpayee at Bateshwar, Fatehpur Sikri and Sauripur Jain Teerth.
He also announced that a working women’s hostel with capacity for 500 residents would be built in Agra in memory of Lokmata Ahilyabai Holkar, and said the state government had approved the project and released the budget.
He ended with a warning on safety, saying, “There will be no compromise on the safety of our daughters and traders. Anyone who attempts to breach their security has only two destinations: jail or hell.”

cluster_text: Tej Pratap Yadav arrested hours after joining student protest in Patna [SEP] Tej Pratap Yadav arrested hours after joining student protest in Patna
full_text:
Tej Pratap Yadav arrested hours after joining student protest in Patna
Jan Shakti Janata Dal chief Tej Pratap Yadav was arrested hours after joining a student protest in Patna, with police linking the action to alleged violence and arson during the Bihar bandh. He was later sent to 14 days judicial custody.
Jan Shakti Janata Dal (JSJD) chief Tej Pratap Yadav was arrested by Patna Police on Saturday evening, hours after being briefly detained and released during protests held as part of the Bihar bandh over the alleged NEET paper leak. He was later sent to 14 days' judicial custody.
Tej Pratap was at a shopping mall in Patna when a police team, led by the City Superintendent of Police (SP), arrived and took him into custody. He was escorted in the City SP's official vehicle amid the presence of a large contingent of police personnel.
While Patna Police is yet to issue an official statement detailing the charges, sources said the arrest is linked to incidents of vandalism and arson reported during the Bihar bandh earlier in the day.
TEJ PRATAP DETAINED FOR DEMONSTRATIONS
Earlier on Saturday, Tej Pratap had joined protesters at Ram Gulam Chowk near Gandhi Maidan, where demonstrations were held in support of demands for a fair investigation into the alleged NEET paper leak. He was detained during the protest but was later released.
However, according to sources, police subsequently reviewed CCTV footage from the protest site and allegedly found evidence suggesting that Tej Pratap had incited protesters during the demonstration.
Based on the fresh findings, police launched another operation and arrested him from the shopping mall on Saturday evening.
When police arrived at the mall, Tej Pratap's associates questioned why he was being taken away despite having already been released earlier in the day.
Police informed them that he would be transported in the City SP's vehicle rather than a police van.
Tej Pratap also asked officers who would bring his personal vehicle, to which they replied that it would be driven separately by police personnel.
BIHAR 'BANDH' FOR NEET PROTESTS
The Bihar bandh witnessed protests across several districts, with demonstrators demanding a transparent probe into the alleged NEET paper leak and strict action against those responsible for examination irregularities.
The agitation also led to incidents of road blockades, disruption of rail services and clashes with police in parts of the state.
Police are expected to formally disclose the charges against Tej Pratap after completing the legal process. Sources indicated that his alleged role in violence on Exhibition Road, including vandalism and arson, is central to the case.
