NEW DELHI: Opposition MPs took out a 'candlelight march' Thursday to the Gandhi Smriti in solidarity with the protesting students, two days after they held a dharna outside the PM's residence and were forcibly evacuated by police.
The MPs belonging to Congress, SP, TMC, Left parties, RJD, Shiv Sena and others met at Rahul Gandhi's residence. From there, they marched to the Gandhi Smriti holding their phone torches. The marchers included Rahul, K C Venugopal, Ramjilal Suman, Supriya Sule, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, N K Premachandran, John Brittas, Sandosh Kumar, Sudhakar Singh, Misa Bharti, Arvind Sawant, Saugata Roy and Mahua Moitra.
Rahul said, "We go to remember the students we lost - the children driven to take their own lives after the NEET paper leak. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
And we go to stand with the students who lie injured today - beaten for peacefully demanding justice and accountability. India's students are not alone. The entire opposition stands with them and their demands."
Congress's P Chidambaram said, "All roads are barricaded, and hundreds of policemen are mobilised to 'secure' the roads of Delhi. What is govt afraid of? Why this sense of panic?" Earlier, Congress rubbished PM Modi's statement assuring the protesting youth. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the students don't need platitudes after govt used pellet guns, shock batons and tear gas on them.

[SEP] Dharmendra Pradhan, who stepped down as Union education minister on Saturday after a five-year tenure, leaves behind an education system more standardised, digitally connected and centrally regulated than the one he inherited â but also questions over examination credibility, institutional autonomy, data privacy and the Centreâs capacity to implement reforms on such a large scale.
full_text:
NEW DELHI: 
Dharmendra Pradhan, who stepped down as Union education minister on Saturday after a five-year tenure, leaves behind an education system more standardised, digitally connected and centrally regulated than the one he inherited â but also questions over examination credibility, institutional autonomy, data privacy and the Centreâs capacity to implement reforms on such a large scale.
Pradhan, the longest-serving education minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs cabinet, held the portfolio from July 7, 2021, to July 25, 2026. Until 2024, he was also minister for skill development and entrepreneurship.
His tenure was less about announcing a new education policy â the National Education Policy had been approved in 2020 â and more about constructing the machinery required to put it into operation.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
The defining theme was standardisation and portability: common entrance examinations, transferable academic credits, permanent student identification numbers, comparable assessment standards and an attempted umbrella regulator for higher education.
The Common University Entrance Test, introduced in 2022, sought to replace differing Class XII board cut-offs with a common admission platform for central universities. 
It also dramatically expanded the role of the National Testing Agency, whose functioning and credibility later became one of the biggest challenges of Pradhanâs tenure.
The National Credit Framework, Academic Bank of Credits and four-year undergraduate programmes were designed to allow students to accumulate and transfer credits, pursue multidisciplinary courses and enter or leave programmes without losing their academic record.
APAAR, envisaged as a permanent academic identity for every student, sought to link school, university and skill qualifications through DigiLocker and the credit bank. While intended to ease mobility, it triggered concerns over consent and protection of childrenâs data.
In school education, the ministry released curriculum frameworks for the foundational stage and school education, operationalising the NEPâs 5+3+3+4 structure. PM SHRI was launched to upgrade more than 14,500 existing government schools as models of NEP implementation, while PARAKH was established to develop common assessment standards and bring greater comparability among school boards.
Other big-ticket measures included the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, One Nation One Subscription for access to research journals, PM-USHA funding for state universities, permission for foreign universities to open campuses in India and the establishment of IIT campuses abroad.
Pradhan also pushed Indian-language textbooks, multidisciplinary education, vocational integration and apprenticeship programmes, drawing on the overlap between his education and skill-development portfolios.
The proposed replacement of UGC, AICTE and NCTE with an umbrella regulatory architecture remained unfinished. Implementation also met resistance from some states over language, curriculum and centrally sponsored schemes.
Ultimately, the sharpest contradiction of the Pradhan years lay in national testing. Common examinations were meant to deliver fairness and uniformity, but paper leaks, cancellations and administrative failures raised doubts about whether centralisation had moved faster than institutional capacity.

full_text:
NEW DELHI: BJP leader Pralhad Joshi on Saturday was appointed as the new Union education minister, hours after 
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned.
Pradhan resigned taking moral responsibility for the NEET-UG paper leak controversy that triggered weeks of nationwide student protests. His resignation was accepted by President Droupadi Murmu.
A press release by Rashtrapati Bhavan read: "The President of India, as advised by the Prime Minister, has accepted the resignation of Shri Dharmendra Pradhan from the Union Council of Ministers, with immediate effect, under clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution of India. Further, as advised by the Prime Minister, the President has directed that Shri Pralhad Joshi, Cabinet Minister, be assigned the charge of the Ministry of Education, in addition to his existing portfolio.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
"
After being appointed as education minister Pralhad Joshi said he accepted the additional charge of the education ministry with 'a sense of duty and humility' and pledged to work under the guidance of PM Modi to further strengthen the country's education system.
"I accept this responsibility with a sense of duty and humility. I am thankful to the Prime Minister. In the last 12 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, many historic achievements have been made. 
In the last four to five years, Dharmendra Pradhan also implemented the National Education Policy, and several important initiatives were undertaken. The country has made significant progress in the new education system. Under the guidance of the Prime Minister, I will work to the best of my ability and fulfil my responsibilities with dedication," Joshi said.
Joshi, the Lok Sabha MP from Karnataka's Dharwad constituency also hold the portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution. A five-time MP, he has previously served as the Union minister for coal, mines and parliamentary affairs.
As the minister for new and renewable energy, Joshi has been leading the Centre's efforts to expand clean energy capacity, with a focus on achieving 500 GW of renewable and non-fossil fuel energy capacity by 2030 and net-zero emissions by 2070.
He has overseen key initiatives including the National Green Hydrogen Mission, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, PM-KUSUM scheme and offshore wind energy projects, while pushing for annual bids for 50 GW of renewable energy capacity and other policy measures to boost the sector.
His appointment comes at a crucial time as the education ministry implements sweeping reforms following the 
NEET-UG controversy, including the restructuring of the National Testing Agency (NTA), stricter anti-paper leak measures and a shift to computer-based testing for NEET from 2027.

Rahul Gandhi on Saturday congratulated the youth protesters after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan tendered his resignation amid protest across the country over NEET paper leak.
In a social media post on X, Rahul said that Pradhan's resignation is a huge step in rebuilding the education system
"Education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is a huge step in rebuilding our education system. It's a symbolic step because he was a symbol. But it is still a big step," the 
Congress leader said.
"And I want to congratulate every single student, every single youngster who came out on the streets and fought for democracy, fought for the future of this country and defended the Constitution.

I'm proud of you. Well done," he added.
Accusing the government of "attacking India" and destroying the constitution, Rahul also the called on the youngsters for getting rid of the "regime."
"It's also a signal to other parts of society. Farmers, laborers, poor people. Anybody who this regime is attacking and oppressing. There is wisdom and courage in standing up. Daro Mat. Let's get rid of this regime," Rahul said.
"This regime that is attacking India. Destroying our constitution, capturing all our institutions," he added.
Rahul also urged the government to fulfil the two remaining demands -- action against the police officials who allegedly assaulted protesting students during CJP's march to Parliament on July 20, and an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
"Let me remind the government. There is still two demands outstanding. The first one and most important one. Anybody who has raised a finger on our students, beaten them, shot at them. Has to be held accountable. People who've organised it, people who've implemented it. All have to be punished," Rahul said.
"And the final demand. That the Prime Minister of India. Out of respect for the students of India. Out of respect for the future of India. Has to apologise to the students who were brutalised and attacked. Thank you. Jai Hind," he added.

In his letter, Pradhan said, "For over four decades, I have dedicated myself to the cause of students, teachers, and educational reform. I have always believed that a robust, inclusive, and visionary education system forms the cornerstone of a strong nation."
"I deeply respect the aspirations, sentiments, and legitimate expectations of the country's youth. Realising the dreams of India's young generation has been a moral commitment in our political and social lives. I express my gratitude to the Honourable Prime Minister for the opportunity to serve the nation under his visionary leadership," he said.
This comes amid nationwide protests demanding strict action against the paper leak and exam irregularities, following Education Minister Pradhan's resignation, which he said was rooted in accountability.

Uttar Pradesh government has constituted a new 
Special Investigation Team (SIT) led by senior IPS officers to investigate the alleged embezzlement of devotees' offerings at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya.
The reconstituted team is headed by Inspector General Kiran S, with Deputy Inspector General Somen Verma and Ayodhya Senior Superintendent of Police Dr Gaurav Grover as members. It replaces the earlier SIT, which was headed by Lucknow Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant and included Special Secretary (Finance) Neel Ratan Kumar among its members.

Investigators probing the case earlier examined CCTV footage, donation registers, cash-handling records and financial documents, besides questioning temple staff. 
Their preliminary findings indicated suspected irregularities in the counting and deposit of donations.
The investigation led to the arrest of several accused, while police seized cash, vehicles, investment documents and other assets allegedly acquired using the misappropriated funds. Investigators also analysed bank transactions and other digital evidence to trace the alleged money trail.
With the new SIT now taking over the probe, the Uttar Pradesh government is expected to place its findings before the Supreme Court in a status report on July 27.

According to an order issued by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), Gangwar, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre, will succeed Vineet Joshi as Secretary of the Department of Higher Education.

On Friday, a high-level meeting between leaders of CJP and senior BJP leaders, including Union Health Minister JP Nadda and Union Minister Jitendra Singh, was held at the Constitution Club in New Delhi.

NEW DELHI: A special court in Bhopal on Saturday rejected the bail plea of retired judge Giribala Singh, an accused in the alleged dowry death of former model and actor Twisha Sharma, observing that the charges against her were "serious."
Giribala Singh, Twisha's mother-in-law, is accused in the case after the former model and actor was allegedly found hanging at her marital home in Bhopal on May 12.
The retired judge and her son, Samarth Singh, were later arrested on charges of dowry-related harassment, mental abuse and domestic violence. The 
Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is probing the case.
The bail application was initially listed before Special Judge Neelam Shukla, who recused herself from hearing the matter. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
The case was then transferred to Special Judge Ram Pratap Mishra, who reserved the order on Friday after hearing arguments from both sides.
Seeking bail on humanitarian grounds, the defence argued that Singh, an elderly woman with health issues, was not receiving adequate medical care in jail. It also submitted that her nearly 100-year-old mother depended on her for care.
The defence further contended that Singh had cooperated with the investigation, suffered a burglary at her residence while in custody, and received a regular salary and a war widow's pension, making the allegation of dowry demand implausible.
Opposing the plea, the CBI argued that Singh's gender alone could not justify bail, particularly when the deceased was also a woman. It pointed out that the Madhya Pradesh High Court had on May 27 quashed the anticipatory bail granted to her by a subordinate court in Bhopal.
The agency also alleged that Singh had refused to provide her voice sample during the investigation, attempted to influence the probe by contacting a CCTV technician and a salon operator linked to the case, and sent a private representative to obtain CCTV footage.
The CBI argued that her release could enable her to influence witnesses, tamper with evidence or hamper the ongoing investigation.
After hearing both sides, the special court rejected Singh's bail application.

full_text:
Nitish Kumar, 22, a student from Nawada, Bihar, first relied on over-the-counter medicines when he began experiencing symptoms of 
chikungunya in February last year. For almost a week, he believed it was an ordinary viral fever.
âI did not immediately go to a doctor. I bought some medicines from a pharmacy to treat the symptoms of what I thought was a viral fever and made some changes to my diet.â
Even after seeing a doctor, the mosquito-borne viral disease went undetected. âOne day, I noticed a sudden eruption of red spots on my body, and I suspected I was infected with chikungunya. I went to AIIMS Bhopal to see a doctor, but the doctor handed me a list of medicines prescribed for viral fever. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
Even the doctor could not diagnose it initially despite the rash.â
The 
World Health Organization (WHO) notes that chikungunya symptoms â abrupt fever, swelling, muscle pain, headache, nausea, fatigue â overlap with those of other infections, making misdiagnosis common. If the illness lacks severe joint pain, it may go unnoticed because symptoms in many infected individuals are mild.
This is hardly an outlier. The initial symptoms of most monsoon-related illnesses closely overlap with those of common viral fever. 
âThis is a typical situation observed during the rainy season. We come across many cases of patients who present with symptoms such as fever, sore throat, or general body weakness and are treated as viral infections. But after 2 to 3 days, if the high fever persists, body pains, or low platelets indicate influenza or dengue,â said Dr. M. J. Jayakanth, Consultant â Internal Medicine, SPARSH Hospital, Sarjapur Road, Bangalore.
For dengue, WHO says most people are asymptomatic, while symptomatic cases experience high fever, headache, body aches, nausea and rash. Malariaâs mild symptoms are similar: fever, chills and headache.
The monsoon brings relief from summer heat, especially in northern India, but also a hidden cost: a surge of infections. Pools of stagnant water left by heavy downpours become mosquito breeding grounds, fueling spread of vector-borne illnesses like malaria, dengue and chikungunya. Heavy rainfall and high humidity also allow airborne viruses, including influenza, to linger longer, and as people retreat indoors, close contact in poorly ventilated spaces facilitates transmission. Because many monsoon illnesses begin with fever and headache â symptoms associated with viral fever â delayed detection can allow them to worsen into life-threatening conditions.
Impact on newborns
Dr Manish Mittal, senior consultant paediatrician at Cocoon Hospital in Jaipur, says newborns and toddlers are more vulnerable during the monsoon because of immature immune systems. âThe combination of high humidity, pollution through dirty water, a moist environment, and mosquitoes increases their susceptibility to lung infections, diarrhoea, skin infections, and vector-borne diseases. Even a small infection may develop into something serious in infants.â
Delayed detection is common in children because they cannot always communicate symptoms clearly. âParents sometimes seek medical care only after dehydration, persistent fever, or unusual lethargy develops, which can delay timely diagnosis and treatment.â
Dr. Mittal recommends parents ensure hygiene at home: keep surroundings dry, use clean water, protect babies from mosquitoes, and continue breastfeeding if feasible. âIf the infant has fever, poor feeding, lethargy, vomiting, diarrhoea, low urine output, or difficulty breathing, prompt medical care is required.â
Why the risk is higher among children
Contribution of climate change
On the UNDP blog, Kathryn Johnson, a policy specialist in HIV and health for the UNDP regional office for Asia-Pacific, writes that changing rainfall patterns and rising temperatures increase the risk of vector-borne diseases in rapidly urbanising regions with weak health infrastructure. âWarmer climates extend the breeding seasons and geographical range of many vectors, while increased rainfall or poor water management in urban settings provides ideal conditions for their spread.â
This complicates diagnosis, as these diseases are no longer confined to the monsoon season.
Abhay Tripathi, 22, a journalism student at Central University of Odisha, says he contracted chikungunya last May in Bhopal, a month of high temperatures. Because it wasnât monsoon, he assumed it was ordinary fever. âI did not go to the doctor on the first day because, being a student living away from home, I thought it was just a fever. I took a paracetamol that I had in my room and rested for a day. But on the second day, the fever didn't break, and I noticed minor rashes on my hand. I got worried and decided to see a doctor.â
Government data show rising malaria cases in pre- and post-monsoon months. The National Centre for Vector-Borne Disease Controlâs monthly report records a slight rise in positive malaria cases in 2025 during pre-monsoon months compared with 2024. Mapped against the three-year average, the increase is significant, especially in months approaching peak summer.
Government data reflects rise in malaria cases during the pre-monsoon months
Dr. Jayakanth says climate change is not the sole contributor. Improved testing and surveillance have picked up cases that earlier went unreported. âUrban water storage, construction sites, poor drainage, and changing human movement patterns also create year-round breeding habitats.â
âSo, this trend is probably not due to a single factor; it reflects a combination of climate change, environmental changes, urbanisation, and better disease detection systems,â he adds.
Why diagnosis gets delayed
Gaps remain in diagnostic infrastructure and mechanisms, including low availability of rapid diagnostic tests in peripheral areas, delays in laboratory results, poor early screening, and limited healthcare infrastructure in both urban and rural areas. âMost primary hospitals do not have the infrastructure to conduct tests on-site, meaning that the samples will be taken to external laboratories, hence causing a delay,â he says.
Ultimately, this escalating public health challenge is more than a seasonal inconvenience. Climate change is reshaping environmental patterns and vector habitats, while access to advanced diagnostics remains unequal â a convergence that is intensifying the risk and reach of these illnesses.

Sonam Wangchuk - whose wide recognition helped expand the reach of Cockroach Janta Party's protest into uncomfortable territory for BJP - to break his hunger strike.

The breakthrough with Wangchuk became possible because of deft footwork, including behind-the-scenes moves by home minister Amit Shah, that saw ministers JP Nadda and 
Jitendra Singh overcoming the activist and bringing in local netas of Ladakh. Wangchuk's fears about violence and the risk of protests being overtaken - something that he articulated in the video-graphed conversation with the ministers - were helpful.
Official circles are hopeful that Wangchuk's appeal for peaceful protests and against any form of violence, besides govt's positive response to his demand for not registering criminal cases against peaceful protestors and suitable compensation to families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, will have a positive impact and may also help isolate "genuine" students from activists motivated by a dizzying array of motives - from partisan political considerations and gender fluidity to angst over Brahmanical patriarchy and Manuvad and Hindutva dominance.
Unlike Abhijeet Dipke-led CJP, Wangchuk has not insisted on Pradhan's resignation. Considering it as the hook that connected that segment of youth with the protest who are not overtly political and might have been even otherwise sympathetic to some of the causes of the party, Wangchuk nuancing his pitch for accountability for paper leaks and expanding it beyond the individual to the ministry should help a govt pitted against a determined and competitive push for the minister's scalp.
PM Modi was quick on X to wish the Ladakh activist - who was detained under NSA last year for his alleged role in violent protest in the UT - and that he regains the weight he lost in the fast.
CJP could not have been pleased with the turn of events, but it was careful not to express its annoyance. Dipke lauded Wangchuk's "extraordinary courage" but left no doubt that he would carry on with his protest until Pradhan was sacked.
The rift was evident after Wangchuk's wife Gitanjali Angmo wrote on X, "Before you rush to criticise Wangchuk, first pause to earn the ethos of fasting for 26 days for a cause larger than yourself. He lies in the ICU today, having lost 11 kg, including muscle mass, because he chose sacrifice over comfort... The least we can offer him is a day of compassion before burdening him with our own expectations and political calculations. Not everyone is qualified to judge a life of selfless service. One must first earn the moral stature to do so. Please. Have a heart."

Five-time Karnataka MP and Union minister Pralhad Joshi, who holds several other portfolios, has been given additional charge of education.

âDemocracy wins,â CJP said on X.
CJP spokesperson Saurav Das announced withdrawal of protests with immediate effect at a news conference, where both ministers wore a resigned look. Govt has also agreed to provide âhonourableâ compensation to families of NEET candidates who died by suicide and withdraw FIRs against protesting students in Delhi and other BJP-governed states, he added.
The two sides will again meet after four weeks to work on broader reforms in the exam system, CJP said.
In a two-page statement, Pradhan said he has quit so that âanti-national forces do not take advantage of the situationâ at Jantar Mantar and across the countryâ. It is not a matter of personal prestige, he said.
His statement was addressed to âmy young friendsâ, a nod to Gen Z, who have been the face of CJP-led protests, and left the all-powerful BJP searching for answers to their unconventional onslaught. A govt functionary said largescale participation of youth gave the campaign, which BJP initially saw as sponsored by AAP and Left-aligned groups, an emotive undercurrent, leaving them little choice but to retreat as the protest grew.
Why BJP chose to cut its losses
For a party which rarely makes any concession to rivals on their terms and exudes an air of bold strength rooted in popular endorsement in polls, BJPâs decision to bow to the student protest also reflects the pragmatism it has shown when confronted with street agitation â better to cut losses than let the pain fester into a more serious challenge.
In Nov 2021, Modi had announced withdrawal of farm laws in the face of over a yearlong protest by farmers, which was largely confined to Punjab and parts of Haryana and western UP but had remained stubborn. NEW DELHI: Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on Saturday tendered his resignation from the council of ministers amid the ongoing protests over the NEET paper leak.
In a letter addressed to his "young friends," Pradhan said that he has sent his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, considering the situation that has developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country.
He said he sent his resignation letter to PM Modi so that "anti-national forces do not take advantage of this situation". Pradhan added that the "unity of the country should be preserved ... not even a single student's future should get entangled in legal complications, and our children should devote their time to studies and focus on building their careers".
Read his full statement
My Young Friends,
I have been dedicated to students, teachers, and education reform for more than four decades. I have always believed that a strong, inclusive, and visionary education system is the very foundation of a strong nation.
I deeply respect the aspirations, emotions, and just expectations of the country's youth. Realizing the dreams of India's young generation has been a moral commitment of all of us in political and social life. I express my gratitude to the Hon'ble Prime Minister for the opportunity he gave me to serve the nation under his visionary leadership.
However, irregularities came to light in the NEET-UG examination held on 3 May 2026. The Government of India took immediate cognizance of this, handed over the investigation to the CBI, cancelled the examination, and announced a new date for the re-examination. Alongside this, it was decided that from next year the examination would be conducted in CBT (Computer-Based Test) mode.
During this period, our foremost priority was to ensure that the examination for more than 20 lakh (2 million) students was conducted smoothly. This was carried out under a "whole of government" approach. In this, along with the Government of India, the state governments â especially the district administrations â played an important role. With the cooperation of students and parents, this examination was completed on 21 June 2026.
From the very first day, I took responsibility and never turned away from this situation. My resolve was that we would not let any meritorious student's chances be ruined because of an examination mafia, and that no injustice would be done to any student.
The NEET-UG results declared on 16 July were satisfactory, with many meritorious students from poor backgrounds also achieving success.
However, during this time too, certain individuals occupying positions of responsibility tried to mislead students and create obstruction, which caused me deep anguish.
I have always been an unwavering believer in the strength of our democracy, and I have always held deep respect for the aspirations, dreams, and expectations of the youth. They are not only India's future, but also the bearers, builders, and architects of a new and developed India.
Watching the events of the last 10 days has saddened me. This is not a matter of personal reputation for me.
The youth power of India is the real strength of this country.
My resolve is that we will not let the country's youth get caught in a web of confusion.
Considering the situation that has developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country â that anti-national forces should not take advantage of this situation, that the unity of the country should be preserved, that not even a single student's future should get entangled in legal complications, and that our children should devote their time to studies and focus on building their careers â I have sent my resignation to the Hon'ble Prime Minister.
I express my heartfelt gratitude to the Hon'ble Prime Minister for his guidance, trust, and continuous support. I also express my gratitude to all my esteemed colleagues in the Council of Ministers, the officials and staff of the Ministry, and all those with whom I had the privilege of working. Service to the nation is the highest priority of my life, and I shall remain dedicated to it always.
By the blessings of Lord Sri Jagannath, I shall continue to dedicate myself in every possible way, in the future as well, to the fulfillment of the aspirations of Mother India, the people of Odisha, and the youth of the country."

She said students across the country had been demanding accountability over examination paper leaks and broader reforms in the education system, but alleged that the Centre had chosen repression over dialogue.
"The student protests are a natural consequence of these interrelated forces: today's bleak education landscape, which evokes only hopelessness, and the Modi government's trademark arrogance and unwillingness to be accountable or constructive," Gandhi wrote.

She further alleged that the government had weakened India's education system while acting with "utter impunity, supreme self-delusion, and abject insensitivity".
According to Gandhi, it was the moral, political and constitutional responsibility of every public representative to stand with students and protect their future.

NEW DELHI: The Centre has proposed sweeping changes to the anti-cheating law, seeking to speed up investigations and time-bound trials while introducing tougher punishment for those involved in paper leaks and examination malpractice.
Under the proposed Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, the central government to constitute a special task force (STF), wherever necessary, for investigation of offences under the Act.
Thereupon, investigations into offences under the Act will have to be completed within two months.
After that, within three months from the date of filing of the chargesheet, a time-bound appeal mechanism in the amendment requires the special fast track courts to conduct trials on a day-to-day basis and complete it.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
Appeals against judgments, sentences or orders passed by a special fast track court will lie before a two-judge bench of the high court, which will be required to dispose of such appeals within three months of their admission.
To facilitate this, the Bill empowers all state governments and Union Territory administrations to designate any Court of Session as a special fast track court for trying offences under the Act.
According to the Statement of Objects and Reasons, the amendment aims to strengthen the credibility of public examinations by ensuring speedy investigation, time-bound trials and stronger deterrence against paper leaks and organised examination malpractice.
Stricter penalities introduced 
For individuals found guilty of offences under the Act, the proposed punishment has been enhanced. The minimum imprisonment has been increased from three years to five years, while the maximum jail term has been raised from five years to 10 years. The maximum fine has also been increased from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 50 lakh.
The Bill also proposes stricter action against service providers involved in examination fraud. The maximum fine for such entities has been increased from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore, while the period during which they can be barred from conducting public examinations has been doubled from four years to eight years.
Directors, senior managers or other persons responsible for the conduct of the business of a service provider, if found to have connived in the offence, will face a minimum imprisonment of five years, compared with the existing minimum of three years. The proposed fine for such persons has also been increased from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore.
The amendment further enhances punishment for organised crime related to paper leaks. The minimum jail term has been increased from five years to seven years, while the proposed maximum fine has been raised from Rs 1 crore to Rs 10 crore.

full_text:
From satire to sit-in is the most popular, and perhaps the easiest, explanation for the student protest movement that culminated in the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. This explanation is empowering in its simplicity. But it is incomplete.
By now, everyone knows how the story goes. On May 15, 2026, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant likened unemployed youth turning to activism and social media to “cockroaches”, triggering widespread backlash. Seizing on the remark, Abhijeet Dipke, an Indian student in Boston, launched a satirical online platform for fellow “cockroaches”, transforming an insult into a rallying cry for disaffected youth. Within the first 24 hours, 50,000 people signed up. That number swelled to more than a million within five days, while the movement’s Instagram account surged past 22 million followers.
Yet behind the viral posts, soaring follower counts and colourful symbolism stood a trio: Abhijeet Dipke (30), Ashutosh Ranka (30) and Saurav Das (27), whose skills complemented one another. They come from different parts of the country, different social backgrounds and possess markedly different temperaments.
Those who have spent time around Jantar Mantar since the movement began describe Mr. Dipke as politically intuitive, though at times a touch emotional, and the beating heart of the movement. On July 18, after activist Sonam Wangchuk was removed from Jantar Mantar, it was Mr. Dipke who argued that the movement should escalate its demands. Instead of limiting itself to seeking Mr. Pradhan’s resignation, he proposed demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Mr. Dipke loves discussing A.R. Rahman’s music and reciting Shah Rukh Khan’s dialogues from Swades. He brought a sense of lightness to the protest, spending time in the evenings talking to the protesters, posing for pictures with them and cracking a joke every now and then.
Mr. Ranka, meanwhile, has been described as decisive, though at times authoritarian, and quicker to lose his temper than others. He remains the mind of the movement and its principal strategist. Mr. Das, the youngest of the three, is known as much for his affable demeanour as for his outreach skills, though colleagues say he can occasionally be indecisive.
If Mr. Ranka and Mr. Dipke rave about Shah Rukh Khan starrer Swades and Aamir Khan’s Rang De Basanti, Mr. Das represents the other end of the social spectrum where his favourite series is Modern Family — a mockumentary about a multigenerational family based out of Los Angeles.
Association with AAP
One obvious thread connecting the three is their association with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), a link none of them has sought to conceal. Both Mr. Dipke and Mr. Ranka have worked for the party, while Mr. Das’s proximity to former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal is hardly a secret.
Mr. Dipke was born in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (formerly Aurangabad), Maharashtra, into a Dalit family, though his caste identity largely remained in the background during the protest. “He is a student leader who is also a Dalit and not the other way round,” a leader associated with the 36-day protest said. One occasion on which he publicly asserted his caste identity came after ink was thrown at him at Jantar Mantar on July 18. His response was brief: “Blue is my colour. Jai Bhim.”
He studied journalism at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth in Pune before moving to the U.S. in 2023 to pursue a Master’s degree in Public Relations at Boston University. Mr. Dipke worked in political communications and was associated with the AAP social media team between 2020 and 2023, working closely with senior leader Manish Sisodia.
Mr. Ranka’s journey to the CJP was unlike that of most protest leaders. Born and raised in Jaipur, he studied Materials Science and Engineering at IIT-Kanpur, where he was elected president of the Students’ Gymkhana, an early indication of his interest in public life.
He served as a Delhi Assembly Fellow during 2019-20, working closely with the team of former Delhi Chief Minister and current Leader of Opposition Atishi during the pandemic, before pursuing a Master’s in Public Administration at the London School of Economics. He subsequently worked with McKinsey & Company and with Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, before gradually moving away from the worlds of consulting and international policy in favour of Indian public life.
Mr. Ranka also worked on the AAP campaign for the February 2025 Delhi Assembly election, focusing exclusively on the New Delhi constituency, where Mr. Kejriwal was the candidate. He was part of the team examining voter deletions and continued to publicly defend Mr. Kejriwal and the party even after the election. His most recent article as AAP’s “national spokesperson” was published on March 16.
Unlike many political organisers, Mr. Ranka has never hidden his ambitions. He has often expressed a desire to focus on Rajasthan politics. Following the 2025 Assembly election, he turned his attention to the State, running campaigns to protect a 100-acre forest near Jaipur. More recently, he gave Rajasthan Education Minister Madan Dilawar a three-month ultimatum to address issues faced by students at Rajasthan University, warning that the CJP would otherwise seek the vice-chancellor’s resignation.
Saurav Das, the movement’s young spokesman, became its public face. A journalist before he became a protest leader, he understood how newsrooms functioned, how narratives were shaped and, more important, how to keep a movement in the headlines.
Mr. Das spent part of his childhood in Puducherry and speaks a smattering of Tamil. He studied Journalism and Mass Communication at Amity University, Noida, graduating in 2019. He is best known for his detailed profile of former Chief Justice of India D.Y. Chandrachud for The Caravan, and has also written for Frontline and other publications.
‘The language of Gen Z’
Mr. Das is also the co-founder of Climate Action Front, an initiative focused on climate governance, sustainability and environmental policy. Alongside journalism, he has been working on his debut book, Complicit Silence: The Court’s Role in India’s Quiet Suffering, which examines the judiciary’s role in contemporary India through a series of case studies involving citizens seeking justice. Videos of Mr. Das dancing after Mr. Pradhan’s resignation also went viral, attracting admiration as well as criticism. Mr. Das defended the celebrations as “the language of Gen Z”, arguing that young people express political victories differently.
None of the three had ever led a protest of this scale before they laid siege to the government near the 18th century observatory, Jantar Mantar. Nor had the majority of the protesters who took to the streets of Delhi, in response to their call. For now, the three insist that the CJP will continue to function as a pressure group rather than a political party.

The tiger prowling in the forests of Eluru district reportedly killed a calf in Pandugudem village of Buttaigudem mandal. The animal also killed two cows in the forests at Mangapathidevipeta village in Kannapuram range two days ago.
Forest department officials said that the tiger attacked the cattle in Pandugudem village on Friday night and killed the calf.
A team of officials, including Chief Conservator of Forests (CCF) T. Asha Jyothi, Eluru District Forest Officer (DFO) P.V. Sandeep Reddy and Rajamahendravaram DFO Prabhakar Rao, visited the forests in Jangareddygudem and Buttaigudem.
“The tiger is moving through the reserve forest near Marlagudem village in Jangareddygudem range. An expert team from Wardha in Maharashtra is trying to trap the animal,” Jangareddygudem Forest Range Officer (FRO) Kumar Babu told The Hindu on Saturday.
Nearly 30 Forest department staff were involved in the operation to trap the animal. Officials and the expert team arranged traps and are monitoring the movements of the tiger through CCTVs, the FRO said.
“Villagers are living in constant fear due to the movement of the tiger that killed three cattle in the last three days. Residents have remained indoors for the last few days, and children are not going to schools in Koyyalagudem, Lakshmanudugudem, Pandugudem, Kangalavarigudem and other villages,” said Ch. Nageswara Rao, a villager.
“Agriculture work is in full swing in the villages as monsoon has started. However, farmers are hesitant to go to the fields due to fear of the tiger lurking in the forests,” said A. Surya Chandram, a farmer from Mangapathidevaipeta village.
“We request the villagers not to move alone during nights. Tom-tom has been arranged in Koyyalagudem, Buttaigudem, Kannapuram and other areas where tiger movement has been traced,” said Jangareddygudem Sub-DFO Venkata Subbaiah.
Meanwhile, heavy rains that have been lashing the forests for the last few days have been hampering the operation to trap the tiger, the officers said.

full_text:
On Monday, August 3, we will get a sense of the public mood in the country, or, to be specific, in Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) strongholds such as Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Bihar. Three Assembly seats, one in each of these States, held bypolls on July 30.
The one that all of us should watch closely is Bankipur in Bihar’s capital city, Patna. Bankipur is the heart of the heartland. The outcome in this seat will provide an indication of heartland politics in the aftermath of the student protests that recently rocked the country. The seat was vacated by Nitin Nabin, the BJP’s national president, and Jan Suraj leader Prashant Kishor is contesting from the constituency, testing his caste-free, anti-BJP politics in one of the party’s strongest forts.
No BJP candidate has ever lost from this seat. Mr. Nabin himself won it four consecutive times, most recently in 2025. It is an urban constituency with a demographic composition that has long made the BJP appear invincible. Yet the party has been compelled to deploy all its might in this by-election. Hundreds of party leaders from within and outside Bihar have camped there, mobilising every resource at their disposal.
Why is this seat so important for the BJP, and why will Monday’s (August 3) result be indicative of the party’s standing?
Bankipur is the first election after the BJP took over the Chief Minister’s post from Nitish Kumar. The party won the 2025 Assembly election with Mr. Kumar as its leader, and he continued to command a strong following among Other Backward Classes (OBC) voters within the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in the State. Bankipur will test how the BJP fares when it is fully in command, with Mr. Kumar removed from the political scene.
Bankipur has 3.79 lakh voters, of whom about 1.6 lakh are upper-caste Hindus, the core of BJP support in the Hindi heartland. There are around 40,000 Yadavs and roughly the same number of Muslims. Yadav and Muslim voters usually tend to support the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD), which has never been in contention for much more than a lakh votes here. There are around 50,000 Dalits. The anti-Yadav social polarisation that has been a defining feature of Bihar elections for several years has overwhelmingly worked in the BJP’s favour in this constituency.
Apart from that, Bankipur has also become a hotspot of Hindutva mobilisation. Mr. Nabin began organising large Ram Navami processions in the constituency, which observers estimate drew nearly a lakh participants last March. Muharram processions, in which Muslims gather in large numbers, have also long been a feature of the constituency. Though the two do not occur at the same time, there has been a sense of competitiveness between them, helping to keep communal divisions politically salient over the years.
Mr. Kishor’s candidacy and campaign have challenged this pattern. A Brahmin himself, Mr. Kishor has advanced a caste-free politics in the State, seeking votes on a development agenda. But identity politics still matters in Bihar. What became a concern for the BJP was that some caste arithmetic also appeared to shift in his favour. Since the RJD never stood a realistic chance in the constituency, and Mr. Kishor emerged as a viable alternative, a section of upper-caste voters appeared inclined towards him. Muslims found in him an attractive option, while non-Yadav OBCs seemed less enthusiastic about the NDA without Nitish Kumar. Given these factors, even a section of Yadav voters may have viewed Mr. Kishor as a credible choice.
All told, turnout was low, at 34.24%, representing a drop of more than seven percentage points from last year, and there were indications of remarkable social realignment.
Mr. Kishor told The Hindu on Saturday (August 1) that the State government had unleashed the police on polling day to suppress his voters. “The BJP knows that its communal politics is no longer working. So this time it tried to misuse the administration and the police. Still, they will get a shock on Monday.”
Regardless of who wins on Monday (August 3), there will be enough indicators to gauge the mood of the heartland. Patna University is located in Bankipur. Jayaprakash Narayan lived in the Kadam Kuan locality within the constituency. Gandhi Maidan, which has witnessed many turning points not only in Bihar’s politics but also in the political history of the country, is also in Bankipur.

The Union government has approved the advance release of its share of the State Disaster Response Fund of ₹2,117.85 crore to support seven flood-affected States during the ongoing monsoon season, an official statement said on Saturday (August 1, 2026).
Of the affected States, Himachal Pradesh, Odisha, and Nagaland have already received the first instalment of the Central share for the financial year 2026-27.
“To ensure timely availability of funds for relief operations, Union Home Minister Amit Shah has approved the advance release of the second instalment of the Central share of SDRF to Himachal Pradesh and Odisha,” the statement said.
Himachal Pradesh has been sanctioned ₹193.95 crore and Odisha is to get ₹500 crore as their second instalments.
The advance release of first instalments has been approved for Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Gujarat, and Maharashtra by relaxing documentary requirements under applicable guidelines, considering the urgent need for resources for relief measures, the statement said.
The assistance approved for Arunachal Pradesh amounts to ₹44.55 crore, for Assam ₹379.35 crore, for Gujarat ₹500 crore, and for Maharashtra ₹500 crore.
“With this approval, a total of ₹2,117.85 crore has been made available to the flood-affected States to strengthen their ongoing relief and response measures,” the statement said.
Inter-Ministerial Central Teams (IMCT) have already been deputed to Arunachal Pradesh and Assam to assess damages. Two IMCT visits have been undertaken in Assam in view of the severity of the flood situation there, it said, adding, “On request of the Government of Nagaland, an IMCT is being constituted for the state.” The statement further said the Centre has been continuously monitoring the flood situation in close coordination with the State governments since the onset of the monsoon.
“Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the government remains committed to extending all necessary assistance to states for effective relief, rescue and rehabilitation measures and will continue to monitor the situation closely,” it added.

“Migration meant hope. With the improved earnings he could build a house in his village. He thought he would save up enough for that shelter he wanted since losing his father at the age of four. But that wasn’t to be,” says Deepak’s maternal uncle Dilharan Sande. Deepak was among the two labourers from Chhattisgarh gunned down by terrorists in Kelam area of south Kashmir’s Kulgam district late on Friday evening. The other deceased was 28-year-old Bhupendra Baina from Chhuiya village of Sarangarh-Bilaigarh district.
While Deepak was born in his native village of Bundeli in Sakti district, his father’s untimely death led the family to move to his mother’s maternal village, Hardidih in Sakti. “There weren’t enough opportunities here, so he along with his family moved to Jammu last year and worked there in a brick kiln. Earlier this year, he went to Kashmir valley. Now, the devastating news of his death has come, the whole village is in mourning,” Mr. Sande told The Hindu over the phone from Hardidih.
In Chhuia village, Bhupendra’s younger sister Annu often breaks down as she tells presspersons that the only son of the deceased will never be able to see his father again. She said Bhupendra and his wife had left their four-year-old child in the care of the man’s grandmother and her. Their parents and brother are away working as labourers in Himachal Pradesh.
People in both the villages expressed disappointment that Bhupendra and Deepak were not cremated at their native places.
Meanwhile, Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai on Saturday announced an ex gratia assistance of ₹20 lakh for each of the families of the Chhattisgarh workers killed in the “cowardly terrorist attack in Kulgam”. Mr. Sai described the attack as an assault on humanity and the unity of the nation.
“The Chief Minister has directed the Chhattisgarh Government to depute a senior officer to Jammu & Kashmir immediately. The officer will coordinate with the bereaved families and the local administration to ensure that the last rites of the deceased are conducted in Jammu & Kashmir with full dignity and in accordance with all religious customs and protocols,” said a government official.

full_text:
The DMK on Saturday announced its decision not to participate in the verification of the electronic voting machines (EVMs) used in the Kolathur Assembly constituency, where party president M.K. Stalin had contested, alleging that the machines had not been properly protected.
“So far, we have verified eight EVMs, and found discrepancies in three of them. Since nearly 30% of the machines examined have shown problems, we have come to the conclusion that the election was not conducted fairly. We believe we can establish this scientifically and legally. We will approach either the Madras High Court or the Supreme Court,” senior advocate N.R. Elango, who represented Mr. Stalin during the verification process, told reporters.
He said the party had submitted a letter containing 19 questions to the District Election Officer and sought clarifications from the officials, including representatives of Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited, who were supervising the verification.
‘Address tags unused’
He alleged that when he went to examine the EVMs used in Polling Station No. 157, the address tags on the machines appeared to be new and unused.
“We examined three machines. Since there were 36 candidates in the Kolathur constituency, each polling station should have had one control unit and three ballot units, with a total of seven address tags. However, the address tags appeared to be new and did not contain the required details,” he said.
Explaining the alleged discrepancy, Mr. Elango said the address tags were ordinarily secured with amber seals.
“In the machines produced for verification, the amber seal was found only on the front side. Election officials have attributed this to human error, but we cannot accept that explanation. The ballot units are not used during counting; only the control unit is accessed. That means the control unit would have been opened during counting and sealed again. There should, therefore, have been two amber seals. We believe the EVMs were not properly protected. We will not participate in the procedure,” he said.

full_text:
J&K Cabinet Minister Javed Ahmed Rana, who holds the Forest, Ecology and Environment and Tribal Affairs portfolio, on Saturday (August 1, 2026) announced that the Tribal Affairs department would be the nodal agency to implement the Forest Rights Act (FRA) 2006, and warned against the issuance of eviction notices to forest dwellers without following the set procedure.
“No notices will be served by the J&K Forest Department to any member of forest dwellers, whether a Schedule Tribe or any other traditional forest dwellers living for decades. These dwellers will not be disturbed or evicted from the forest under occupation till the process of recognition and verification is complete,” said Mr. Rana.
The announcement comes months after the Lok Bhavan and the elected government were at loggerheads over the eviction drive in Jammu’s Sunjwan, Bathindi, Raika, and Sidhra areas in Jammu. The drive had triggered protests by BJP legislators, with the elected government accusing the Forest department of functioning under the directions of the Lok Bhavan.
Mr. Rana said the Tribal department, and not the Forest department will be the nodal department for implementing the FRA in J&K.
“A three-member Project Monitoring Units has been established. No one will be evicted till a set procedure is followed. All the deputy commissioners will speed up the pending cases under the FRA,” he said.
According to the 2011 Census, Jammu and Kashmir has a Scheduled Tribe population of 12.75 lakh, including 8.10 lakh in the Jammu division and 4.64 lakh in the Kashmir division.
The Government is pushing hard to implement the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (FRA) and has expedited the process of receiving, verifying and settling claims through the statutory three-tier mechanism.
An official circular said the Gram Sabha is the statutory authority responsible for initiating the process of determining the nature and extent of individual and community forest rights under the provisions of Section 6 of the Act.
“The Gram Sabha is mandated to receive, scrutinize and verify claims, prepare maps of the recommended claims and forward its recommendations to the Sub-Divisional Level Committee (SDLC) for further examination and decision,” an official spokesman said.
Separately, J&K Legislative Assembly Speaker Abdul Rahim Rather held a public outreach camp at Kanidajan in the Charar-i-Sharief Constituency. An official spokesman said a major concern was raised by the villagers pertaining to the alleged harassment caused by the eviction notices issued by the Forest Department and the obstruction of agricultural activities on lands, “which have been under their possession and cultivation for generations”.
“No one would be allowed to act in violation of the provisions of the FRA. The rights of all eligible beneficiaries under the Act would be protected in letter and spirit adding that no undue harassment of villagers would be tolerated,” said Mr. Rather.
The Speaker cautioned that no individual should attempt to misuse the Act as a pretext for fresh encroachments on forest land or government property. “The law must be implemented fairly and transparently while safeguarding the rights of genuine beneficiaries,” he added.

As the death toll in the Kulgam terror attack rose to two on Saturday (August 1, 2026), Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant-Governor, Manoj Sinha, asked security agencies “to conduct a comprehensive review of the Standard Operating Procedures (SoPs) established to protect labourers from outside in J&K”.
Targeting the Centre over its “failure to contain terrorism”, J&K Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary demanded a high-level probe into the killings, while questioning the Centre’s peace narrative.

Suspected terrorists, in a targeted killing, fired upon two non-local labourers from Chhattisgarh on Friday (July 31) evening in Kulgam’s Kellam area. The attackers managed to flee after the attack under the cover of darkness.
One labourer, identified as Deepak Ratray, 24, was declared dead in a hospital late Friday evening. Bopinder Kumar, 28, also from Chhattisgarh, died during treatment. Both the deceased, who worked as labourers at a brick kiln, were cremated in Kulgam on Saturday afternoon under tight security arrangements.
J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah described the incident as “dastardly” and announced ex gratia relief of ₹10 lakh each for the next of kin of the deceased from the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund. This will be in addition to immediate assistance of ₹6 lakh each to be provided by the district administration.
Mr. Sinha said the J&K administration and the entire nation stand with the families.
Valley on alert
The attack, which is the second targeted attack in two weeks, has the security apparatus on tenterhooks in Kashmir. Frisking and search of vehicles were intensified across the Valley, especially on the Amarnath Yatra routes of Pahalgam and Baltal. Meanwhile, Mr. Sinha handed over an appointment letter to the son of Head Constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi, who was killed in a similar attack on July 22, under the government’s compassionate appointment scheme.
The J&K L-G chaired a high-level security review meeting in Srinagar, which was attended by top security officials. A Lok Bhavan spokesperson said all the Deputy Commissioners and Senior Superintendents of Police (SSP) were directed by the L-G “to conduct a comprehensive review of the Standard Operating Procedures (SoPs) established to protect labourers from outside in J&K”.
The L-G directed the employers to provide insurance cover to non-local labourers and said their details should be registered with local police and district authorities. “We must intensify precise, high-impact anti-terror operations to neutralise the terrorists,” Mr. Sinha said.
‘Failed experiment’
Commenting on the sudden spurt in terror attacks, Mr. Choudhary said the region’s Statehood was ended, and Article 370 of the Constitution abrogated “on the promise that terrorism would be eradicated”. “Six years later, if innocent people are still being killed, the Centre must explain whether its experiment has failed,” Mr. Choudhary said.
J&K National Conference president, Dr. Farooq Abdullah, while condemning the attack, demanded a fair, transparent, and time-bound investigation to identify and punish the perpetrators of crime.
“It is difficult to ignore that whenever the demand for the restoration of Jammu and Kashmir’s Statehood gains momentum, such disturbing incidents occur. Why does this repeatedly happen? The people deserve credible answers,” said Mr. Abdullah.
Kashmir chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq said that Islam upholds the sanctity of every innocent human life and unequivocally condemns the killing of innocent persons.
“Targeting poor labourers who have come to earn an honest livelihood is completely contrary to the teachings of Islam and the values of humanity. The spilling of innocent blood only brings more pain and suffering,” said the Mirwaiz.
He said violence as a means should be shunned; instead, the policy of accommodation, dialogue and engagement is the way forward to make South Asia a more peaceful and better place for all its people.

full_text:
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar appears to have entered a politically challenging phase, with his leadership being tested simultaneously on multiple fronts — the Cauvery water-sharing issue, the long-pending expansion of the State Cabinet, the proposed Bidadi township project and the government’s drive to clear encroachments on footpaths.
The Chief Minister has increasingly found himself on the defensive. His appeal to his Tamil Nadu counterpart, C. Joseph Vijay, to postpone his proposed visit to Bengaluru in the wake of the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s (CWMA) direction on the release of water reflected the political sensitivity surrounding the inter-State river dispute.
Many visits to Delhi
The delay in the Cabinet expansion has emerged as perhaps the major political challenge before Mr. Shivakumar. Despite repeated visits to New Delhi, he has so far been unable to secure the Congress high command’s approval to fill the 20 vacant ministerial berths. His return from the national capital without a finalised list of new Ministers has fuelled speculation that the State leadership enjoys limited autonomy. Unlike his predecessor Siddaramaiah, who expanded his Cabinet to its full strength within days of assuming office, Mr. Shivakumar has had to wait for the party leadership’s clearance.
The Cauvery dispute presents a different set of political constraints. Any decision to release water to Tamil Nadu invites criticism from Kannada organisations, farmers and the Opposition, while disregarding the CWMA’s directions could expose the government to legal consequences. With little room for political manoeuvre, the government has struggled to strike a balance between protecting Karnataka’s interests and complying with statutory obligations. The BJP and the JD(S) have sought to portray the government as “weak” in defending the State’s interests. However, with copious rains on Saturday (August 1), the situation, at least for the time-being, seems to be easing.
Similarly, the proposed integrated township near Bidadi has exposed the tension between Bengaluru’s urban expansion and the concerns of farmers facing land acquisition. Although the government initially defended the project, sustained protests by farmers and Opposition parties compelled it to constitute a committee to examine its merits and demerits. While the move helped defuse immediate tensions, it also created the perception that the government had retreated from its original position under public pressure.
Footpath vs. livelihood
The government’s campaign to reclaim footpaths by removing encroachments, abandoned vehicles and other obstructions presents another political challenge. While the middle-class urban residents favour sanitised and more accessible public spaces, street vendors and small traders constitute an important political constituency. Any large-scale eviction without adequate rehabilitation risks generating political backlash, making the enforcement drive a delicate balancing act between urban governance and livelihood concerns.
None of these issues is likely to threaten Mr. Shivakumar’s leadership. However, they reinforce the perception that his government is spending considerable political capital on managing controversies and competing interests rather than advancing its governance agenda.

[SEP] The Karnataka High Court has ruled that a special provision in the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, which excludes certain estates of former royal families from the purview of being partitioned under the Act, remains valid despite abolition of privy purses and royal privileges more than five decades ago through the amendments to the Constitution of India.
full_text:
The Karnataka High Court has ruled that a special provision in the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, which excludes certain estates of former royal families from the purview of being partitioned under the Act, remains valid despite abolition of privy purses and royal privileges more than five decades ago through the amendments to the Constitution of India.
“Articles 291 (privy purse sums of rulers) and 362 (rights and privileges of rulers of Indian States) were only with respect to guarantees and assurances made by the Dominion of India with regard to payment of privy purse, personal rights, privileges, dignities and titles of erstwhile rulers of princely States of India and not with respect to their personal private properties and Gaddi, impartible estate,” the court said.
Justice M.G.S. Kamal passed the order while dismissing the petitions filed in 2015 by Chaduranga Kantharaj Urs, a grandson of Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar, who was the last ruler of the princely State of Mysore, and Venkatrao Y. Ghorpade and Gayatri Ghorpade, son and daughter, respectively, of Yeshwantrao Ghorpade, the erstwhile Maharaja of Sandur.
On Section 5(ii)
The petitioners had sought the deletion of Section 5(ii) from the statute book while contending that this provision has lost its relevance with the passage of time and due to the abolition of Articles 291 and 362. It has no nexus with the object which was initially sought to be achieved. Further, the very concept of Gaddi has lost its meaning and purport, the petitioners had claimed.
The petitions arose from the issues in the civil suits between members of the erstwhile Mysore and Sandur royal families over property partition as some family members, including Pramoda Devi Wadiyar, invoked Section 5(ii) to argue that certain estates inherited by a sole heir under pre-Independence agreements were impartible.
Rejecting these contentions of the petitioners, the court held that the deletion of Articles 291 and 362 and insertion of Article 363-A by the 26th amendment to the Constitution has no bearing on the validity or otherwise of Section 5(ii) of the Hindu Succession Act.
Section 5(ii) states that “provisions of the Act are not applicable to any estate which descends to a single heir by the terms of any covenant or agreement entered into by the ruler of any Indian State with the Government of India or by the terms of any enactment passed before the commencement of this Act”.
The court examined the merger agreements of the former States of Mysore and Sandur with the Government of India, and found that they separately dealt with three issues — privy purses, private properties and succession to the Gaddi. While the Constitution removed guarantees relating to privy purses and privileges through Article 363-A, it did not disturb arrangements concerning private properties or succession to the ceremonial throne, that is, the Gaddi.
Customary perspective
On relevance of Section 5(ii) of the Act, the court said that “determination of issue with regard to succession to private properties as well as to impartible estate is still a relevant subject. It may be that purport and object of Gaddi has lost its relevance but from the customary practical perspective it is still a relevant subject”.
Referring to the apex court’s verdicts, Justice Kamal made it clear that after the signing of the merger agreement and notification of certain properties as the personal private properties of rulers, only the perceived throne would devolve according to the rule of primogeniture, and not the personal private properties of the ruler.

The protest was part of a Statewide agitation by the AKSTU seeking a solution to service- and education-related issues faced by teachers.
Organised by the Thiruvananthapuram district committee of the AKSTU, the protest demanded that the Union and the State governments abandon moves to “weaken” the public education sector; implement the 12th Pay Revision Commission recommendations following the five-year model; withdrawal of contributory pension scheme; revise the teacher-student ratio according to birth rates to protect teachers’ jobs; improve basic infrastructure and academic environment in schools; find a permanent solution to service-related issues; find a solution to problems faced by teachers from pre-primary to higher secondary; and preventing closure of schools in the name of being uneconomic.
The protest was inaugurated by AKSTU State general secretary O.K. Jayakrishnan.
AKSTU district unit president Praveen S. presided. CPI State council member Pallichal Vijayan and AKSTU State unit vice-president S.S. Anoj were present.

Vinod, MLA, urged the government to include the construction of a new water tank in the Asian Development Bank (ADB)-funded project to address water scarcity.
The new tank at Thammanam was proposed following the partial collapse of the 1.35-crore-litre water tank, which had triggered a temporary drinking water crisis in the city.
In a social media post, the MLA called for fixing accountability on the French firm SUEZ, which is responsible for the operation and maintenance of the Kerala Water Authority’s (KWA) assets. He said the city’s drinking water problems could not be resolved by laying pipelines alone and stressed the need for a new water storage tank.
“If there is no other way to raise funds, the ADB loan should first be used to construct the water storage tank. The remaining loan amount can then be utilised for the other works, including the pipeline,” he said.
According to KWA sources,the design and proposal for the new water storage tank were submitted in November last year, but administrative approval is still pending.
“Once we receive administrative sanction, the remaining procedures will be straightforward. Since the tank is proposed to be constructed on KWA land, there will be no delay owing to land acquisition,” a KWA source said.
“The contract with the French firm was signed on the basis of data available in 2017. Since then, several ageing pipelines have been replaced and may no longer require replacement. The general consensus is that the savings from these works could be used to construct the new water storage tank,” the source added.
Another KWA source said the proposal for the new tank was awaiting approval as a funding source had yet to be identified. “The estimated cost of the proposed tank is less than ₹30 crore. It can be included under the ADB-funded project,” the source added.
A senior SUEZ functionary said the construction of water reservoirs did not form part of the firm’s contract with the KWA. “Since we took over the operation and maintenance of the system, the areas that have consistently faced water shortages include Pachalam, Vaduthala, Kaloor and parts of Karuvelippadi. However, the contract does not provide for the construction of a new water storage tank,” the official said.

Heavy rain triggered widespread disruption across the hilly regions of Kannur district on Saturday (August 1, 2026), damaging roads, inundating houses, forcing evacuations, and prompting the authorities to impose travel and tourism restrictions.
Eight families comprising 26 people were shifted to a relief camp after floodwaters entered houses at Peratta Thottipalam in Ulikkal grama panchayat. Fire and rescue services, assisted by residents, rescued those stranded in their homes and relocated 19 adults and seven children to the relief camp.
Two persons were reported missing in separate rain-related incidents. Hanifa, 40, of Kottamchuram in Manthana village, was swept away in the Kunhirapuzha at Peravur. In another incident, Rajesh, a swimming instructor from Thiruvananthapuram, was swept away while trying to rescue a person who was stranded on a river island at Meenthulli in Pullingome village. A search is on for the two missing persons.
Traffic ban imposed
Heavy rain damaged Boys Town-Palchuram road, disrupting traffic between Kannur and Wayanad. The District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) has imposed a night traffic ban on the route from 6 p.m. on Saturday to 6 a.m. on Sunday (August 2, 2026), owing to the risk of landslides.
A woman, Sumathi, stranded on a river island at Thuruth in Pullingome-Kozhichal, was rescued by Fire and Rescue Services personnel and residents.
Landslides and flash floods affected several parts of the district. Water submerged Mattara, Vattiyamthode and Vayathur bridges in Ulikkal panchayat, while the Aralam Butterfly Sanctuary was inundated. Rafting in the Kariyangode river was suspended due to strong currents.
Following a sudden rise in water level the Kariyangode river, five families living on a river island in Kozhichal were shifted to relatives’ house as a precautionary measure.
Pazhassi dam shutters raised
The Pazhassi dam shutters were raised after the reservoir level went up following heavy rainfall in the catchment area. Residents living along the banks of the river have been advised to remain alert.
The District Tourism Promotion Council temporarily closed tourist spots like waterfalls and parks attached to beaches, besides suspended rafting and kayaking activities. Vehicle entry to the Muzhappilangad beach has been banned, and the public has been advised to avoid visiting beaches owing to rough sea conditions.
District Collector P. Vishnuraj chaired two meetings of the DDMA to review the evolving situation. Officials were directed to keep emergency shelters ready, strengthen preparedness in landslide-and flood-prone areas, issue warning to people living near rivers and the coast.

full_text:
Heavy rain triggered flooding, isolated landslips, and widespread damage across Kozhikode district on Saturday (August 1, 2026), prompting the district administration to intensify rescue and relief measures. The Revenue department authorities opened eight relief camps, accommodating 214 people from 72 families evacuated from vulnerable areas.
Officials attached to the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) said no casualties or injuries were reported till Saturday evening. The relief camp members included 84 men, 72 women, and 58 children.
Vadakara taluk accounted for the largest number of evacuees, with 109 people from 33 families shifted to the relief camp at the Vilangad parish hall. In Thamarassery taluk, 95 people from 36 families were moved to four relief shelters. A family of three was provided shelter at a camp opened at Kumaranallur village in Kozhikode taluk.
Revenue officials said five houses were damaged in rain-related incidents across the district, while four others were found to be in a dangerous state. Several families residing in landslide-prone upland areas were relocated to safer places and relatives’ homes as a precautionary measure.
Fire and Rescue Services officials reported structural damage, landslips, and the collapse of retaining walls and protective structures in several rural areas. They said emergency squads had been deployed following instructions from the higher authorities to clear roadblocks and carry out evacuations from vulnerable locations.
The situation worsened in Engapuzha town and neighbouring areas after the Engapuzha river overflowed following incessant rain. More than 30 houses and several commercial establishments were affected by floodwaters. Traders reported losses after water entered shops, with many unable to move their goods to safer locations before the water level rose.
Officials said rising water levels in the Iruvazhinji river could lead to further evacuations. Flooding was reported from Kodenchery and Koodaranhi areas, where rescue teams were kept on standby. In a rain-induced landslip at Nirannapara near Kodenchery, nearly four acres of agricultural land were destroyed.
The DDMA imposed restrictions on traffic through the Thamarassery ghat road following safety concerns. District Collector M.S. Madhavikutty issued orders under Sections 30 and 34 of the Disaster Management Act, 2005, prohibiting the movement of heavy vehicles, multi-axle lorries, trailers, tourist transport vehicles, and non-essential private vehicles through the pass.
Joint inspections
In support of the safety measures, the Kozhikode Rural police have set up checkpoints at Adivaram, while rapid response teams equipped with earthmovers, chain saws, and rescue equipment were positioned along vulnerable stretches of the ghat road. Joint inspections were carried out by the Public Works department (PWD) and the Forest department.
Access to tourist and eco-tourism destinations, including Kakkayam and Kariyathumpara, has been restricted due to rising water levels. The Malabar River Festival organisers also postponed kayaking events scheduled for Saturday until clearance was obtained from the DDMA.
The Kerala State Electricity Board issued a safety advisory asking residents to stay away from snapped power cables and trees touching electric lines. The authorities urged people in vulnerable areas to remain vigilant and cooperate with evacuation measures.

Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan is in the firing line from the Opposition for using a helicopter hired by the State government primarily as an air ambulance and for other emergencies for an alleged personal visit to Kochi.
Mr. Satheesan reportedly flew aboard the helicopter from Golf Club in Thiruvananthapuram to Kochi on Friday to visit his father-in-law, who was undergoing treatment. However, inclement weather prevented the helicopter from landing, and it returned to Thiruvananthapuram. Reports suggest the journey was made later.
CPI(M) State committee member M.B. Rajesh slammed Mr. Satheesan for using the helicopter “for personal purposes, with prime-time actors in [his] lap remaining in silent mode”, in an oblique criticism of prime-time television anchors for not covering the issue. As Leader of the Opposition, Mr. Satheesan had criticised the then LDF government for its “extravagance” in hiring the helicopter.
Another State committee member of the CPI(M), V. Sivankutty, also mocked Mr. Satheesan’s flight as a ‘U-turn’ by the helicopter. Health Minister K. Muraleedharan defended the Chief Minister’s use of the chopper, saying modes of transport change with the times. He also contended that “nobody was criticised earlier for travelling by helicopter”.
However, social media was abuzz with criticism over the helicopter journey, with many users digging up old posts by Mr. Satheesan and other Congress leaders criticising the then State government and then Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan for hiring the helicopter. The Chief Minister’s Office did not respond to messages seeking clarification.
