'Abusing someone is not a crime'
The CJP founder also said that while abusive language may be objectionable, it does not amount to a criminal offence.
"And using abusive language is not a crime. Abusing someone is not a crime. If someone uses abusive language, it may be wrong, it may be inappropriate. You can counsel that person, you can tell them not to use abusive language. But why are cases being filed over it?" he said.
Dipke claimed that if abusive language alone were the basis for criminal prosecution, BJP leaders and the party's IT Cell would face the highest number of cases.
"If cases were to be filed for using abusive language, then the highest number of cases would be against the BJP IT Cell, because they are the ones who have hurled the most abusive language at women. And cases would also be filed against BJP leaders who have used such abusive language for years, even inside Parliament," he said.
CJP leaders back Dipke
Shortly after Dipke's remarks, CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka shared on X a video, seemingly, being the one referenced by the founder.
"FIR. FIR. FIR", Ranka wrote on X and demanded similar legal action. The clip purportedly showed Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath using abusive language.
Earlier in the day, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das criticised the FIR and called it a "misuse of criminal machinery."
"Profanity does not attract criminal case. 50% of Lok Sabha MPs have criminal cases against them, close to 100 MPs in the BJP. The Police can focus their energy towards them, not a 25-year old! Harassment of the young must STOP immediately!" Das wrote in a post on X.
He said that “using the criminal justice machinery to target and harass" protesters "through the police is absolutely unjustifiable.”
“Since when has using abusive language become a criminal offense in this country? People use such language in everyday life all the time,” Das told news agency ANI.
The police registered a zero FIR in Noida on Thursday, and later transferred it to the Parliament Street police station in New Delhi, which has jurisdiction over the case. A zero FIR can be filed at any police station, irrespective of where the alleged offence occurred.

Zee's Subhash Chandra, Punit Goenka fined by SEBI, barred from markets for one year
ZEEL has also been fined ₹3 million and barred from the securities market for two months.
Market regulator SEBI has cracked the whip on Zee Entertainment Enterprises (ZEEL) over securities law violations, with the company, Chief Executive Punit Goenka and Founder-Chairman Emeritus Subhash Chandra facing penalties totalling ₹14.8 million, news agency Reuters reported.
Goenka faces a fine of ₹5.8 million, while Chandra faces a penalty of ₹6 million after the SEBI's 150-page order issued naming Goenka, Chandra and ZEEL on Friday.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) also barred Goenka and Chandra from the securities market for one year.
ZEEL has also been fined ₹3 million and barred from the securities market for two months.
The trouble for the company stems from a SEBI investigation which found that the company had used its land in Hyderabad as security for loans taken by large shareholder-linked entities without proper approvals.
The market regulator found that ZEEL's property was deployed for the benefit of related entities and the arrangement was not disclosed to the company's board, audit committee, shareholders or investors.

SEBI in its order said that four entities of Essel Group had availed four separate loans aggregating to ₹726 crores from Indiabulls Housing Finance Limited (“IHFL”) on December 13, 2016.
“As on March 31, 2019, Essel Home held the entire share capital of each of the four borrowing entities. Though the ownership of Essel Home was held through multiple corporate layers, the investigation traced its ultimate ownership and control to Ms. Sushila Goenka, Noticee No.2 and Essel International Limited,” SEBI said.

SEBI noted that a listed company's assets are held in trust for all shareholders and cannot be used to benefit promoter-controlled entities without proper approvals and governance safeguards. IMD ने केरल के 12 जिलों के लिए ऑरेंज अलर्ट भी जारी किया है, तो वहीं दिल्ली में शनिवार रात को बारिश हुई. गुजरात के कई जिलों में तो बाढ़ का अलर्ट जारी किया गया है.
केरल की बात करें तो मौसम विज्ञान विभाग (IMD) ने केरल के 12 जिलों के लिए ऑरेंज अलर्ट जारी किया है. भारी बारिश के 6 लोगों की मौत हो गई. वहीं 6 लोग लापता बताए जा रहे हैं. केरल में हालात इतने बुरे हैं कि 65 राहत कैंपों में 1,400 से ज़्यादा लोगों को रखा गया है. प्रशासन द्वारा लोगों को हर संभव मदद दी जा रही है. IMD ने शनिवार और रविवार के लिए राज्य के 12 जिलों में ऑरेंज अलर्ट जारी किया है. पथानामथिट्टा, अलाप्पुझा, कोट्टायम, इडुक्की, एर्नाकुलम, त्रिशूर, पलक्कड़, मलप्पुरम, कोझिकोड, वायनाड, कन्नूर और कासरगोड जैसे जिले इसमें शामिल हैं.
भारी बारिश को देखते हुए त्रावणकोर देवस्वोम बोर्ड और पथानामथिट्टा ज़िला प्रशासन ने 2 और 3 अगस्त को 'निरापुथरी' त्योहार के लिए सबरीमाला जाने की योजना बना रहे श्रद्धालुओं को सलाह दी है कि वे भारी बारिश, पंपा नदी में बाढ़ और भूस्खलन के खतरे को देखते हुए अपनी यात्रा करें. मौजूदा मौसम की स्थिति को देखते हुए अलर्ट जारी किया गया है.
यह भी पढ़ें: बाढ़ प्रभावित सात राज्यों को केंद्र की मदद, एडवांस में जारी किए ₹2,117 करोड़
राष्ट्रीय राजधानी दिल्ली के मौसम की बात करें तो शनिवार रात को राजधानी के कई हिस्सों में बारिश हुई. IMD के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक रविवार को दिल्ली के कुछ हिस्सों में हल्की बारिश हो सकती है.
IMD ने आगामी कुछ दिनों के लिए दिल्ली में हल्की बारिश की संभावना जताई है.
गुजरात में भी भारी बारिश से हाल बेहाल है. कई जिलों के लिए रेड और ऑरेंज अलर्ट जारी किया गया है. प्रशासन पूरी तरह मुस्तैद है. कई जिलों में अधिकारियों की छुट्टियां रद्द कर दी गई हैं. वहीं भारी बारिश को देखते हुए स्कूल, कॉलेज और आंगनवाड़ी केंद्रों में छुट्टियां कर दी गई हैं. NDRF और SDRF जलमग्न वाले इलाकों में फंसे लोगों को बचाने में लगे हैं. IMD ने रविवार के लिए अहमदाबाद, सुरेंद्रनगर, राजकोट, भावनगर, मोरबी और बोटाद ज़िलों में भारी बारिश का रेड अलर्ट जारी किया है.

headline: DKS Cabinet likely to be finalised, but Karnataka delay among rarest in history
cluster_text: DKS Cabinet likely to be finalised, but Karnataka delay among rarest in history [SEP] DKS Cabinet likely to be finalised, but Karnataka delay among rarest in history
full_text:
DKS Cabinet likely to be finalised, but Karnataka delay among rarest in history
Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar and senior Congress leaders from the state met the party high command in Delhi to discuss the long-pending issue of Cabinet expansion. The delay is among the lengthiest for a state government operating with an incomplete cabinet in recent years.
Nearly two months after DK Shivakumar took the oath as Karnataka Chief Minister on June 3, the full expansion of his Council of Ministers remains pending, with reports indicating the list could be finalised over the weekend, around August 2, and swearing-in possibly early next week.
DKS and other state leaders met the Congress top leadership at party president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in New Delhi on Thursday to discuss the expansion of the Cabinet.
Shivakumar was sworn in at Lok Bhavan along with Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara and 12 other ministers, a first batch of 13 ministers in total with him, for a 14-member team initially. Karnataka's constitutional limit is 34 ministers including the CM, so roughly 20 berths remain vacant.
Portfolio allocation for the first group happened quickly, but further expansion has been delayed by high-command consultations in Delhi over regional, caste, community, gender and generational balance, competing factional lists (involving Shivakumar and predecessor Siddaramaiah), and other political priorities.
By July 31, this amounts to about 58 days since the initial swearing-in.
Recent reports have pointed to finalisation of names by around August 2, with induction targeted for August 3 or shortly after, ahead of the monsoon session, which begins on August 13.
This is longer than some recent Karnataka precedents but does not set a new national record for the time a state government has operated with a minimal or incomplete cabinet after a CM's induction.
Indian states have seen several extended periods of limited cabinets, often one- or two-member core teams handling all departments, while leadership negotiated equations, high-command clearances, or other factors.
OTHER STATES HAVE SEEN A LONGER DELAY IN CABINET APPOINTMENT
One of the longest such instances in recent years came in Telangana, where K Chandrasekhar Rao (KCR) was sworn in as Chief Minister on December 13, 2018, along with only one other minister, Mohammed Mahmood Ali.
The council remained a two-member affair for over two months before 10 more ministers were inducted on February 19, 2019, creating a gap of around 66–68 days. The delay, attributed to administrative reorganisation and political considerations, also drew criticism from the Opposition over governance.
Maharashtra has also witnessed similar delays on multiple occasions.
After the Shiv Sena split in 2022, Eknath Shinde and Deputy Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis ran the government as the only two members of the council for nearly 40 days before the cabinet was expanded on August 9. Three years earlier, the Uddhav Thackeray-led Maha Vikas Aghadi government functioned with just a seven-member cabinet for about 40 days after taking office in November 2019, as alliance partners negotiated the distribution of portfolios.
Karnataka itself has experienced a comparable, though shorter, phase. After the collapse of the JD(S)-Congress coalition in 2019, BS Yediyurappa was sworn in as Chief Minister on July 26 and headed a one-man cabinet for 25 days before inducting 17 ministers on August 20. During this period, he even chaired cabinet meetings alone while the BJP worked through caste and regional representation and awaited the party high command's approval.
Similar, though less prolonged, episodes have unfolded elsewhere.
In Himachal Pradesh, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu and his deputy operated with a two-member council for about four weeks after taking office in December 2022 before the first cabinet expansion in January 2023.
Delays of several weeks have also been seen in Puducherry, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and other states, particularly where coalition negotiations or consultations with party leadership have prolonged the process of balancing regional, caste and political representation.
Against this backdrop, Karnataka's current delay — of around 58 days since the initial swearing-in — stands out as one of the longer recent examples, though it remains shorter than Telangana's 2018-19 record. The Constitution does not prescribe a deadline for completing cabinet formation, but prolonged delays have often sparked criticism over governance.

In Himachal Pradesh, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu and his deputy operated with a two-member council for about four weeks after taking office in December 2022 before the first cabinet expansion in January 2023.
Delays of several weeks have also been seen in Puducherry, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and other states, particularly where coalition negotiations or consultations with party leadership have prolonged the process of balancing regional, caste and political representation.

headline: CAPF officers move Supreme Court against new law over stalled promotions
cluster_text: CAPF officers move Supreme Court against new law over stalled promotions [SEP] CAPF officers move Supreme Court against new law over stalled promotions
full_text:
CAPF officers move Supreme Court against new law over stalled promotions
Around 3,000 CAPF cadre officers have moved the Supreme Court against parts of the new CAPFs Act. They say the law defies the court's earlier ruling and prolongs promotion stagnation.
A group of paramilitary officers has moved the Supreme Court against certain provisions of the newly enacted CAPFs (General Administration) Act, saying the law will continue to restrict their career progression, official sources said on Saturday. The matter has been listed for hearing in the first week of August, according to court documents.
Officers and their legal representatives told PTI that a batch of writ petitions has been filed by about 3,000 cadre officers from the CRPF, BSF, ITBP, CISF and SSB. They said the petitions were filed under Article 32 of the Constitution, which allows citizens to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of their Fundamental Rights.
The petitioners said they were "forced" to approach the Supreme Court because they felt justice was not served by the new Act and the directions in the Supreme Court's May 2025 verdict were not implemented. "We feel that the latest Act will not resolve the huge stagnation and career progression of CAPF cadre officers," they said. The petitioners include gallantry medal winners and a few women officers.
The officers have sought a declaration that Sections 3 and 4 of the CAPF (General Administration) Act, 2026 are "ultra vires" the Constitution. They have also asked that the Union government be directed to give "full effect" to the Supreme Court's May 2025 judgment.
On May 23 last year, the Supreme Court said deputation of Indian Police Service officers up to the rank of Inspector General in the CAPFs should be "progressively reduced" over two years to create more opportunities for cadre officers, whose delayed promotions can "adversely" affect morale. The top court had also rejected a review petition filed by the Centre against that order.
The Union government later brought the CAPFs (General Administration) Bill in Parliament, which was notified as an Act in April. Section 3 of the Act deals with regulation of recruitment and service conditions in the CAPFs, while Section 4 covers the central government's power to amend schedules. The officers are also understood to have sought that posts in the Additional Director General rank in the CAPFs should be opened to cadre officers of the respective forces on the basis of prescribed eligibility, instead of being filled only through deputation from the IPS.
The government has said the Act aims to create a unified legal framework for service conditions across the CAPFs, replacing separate service rule systems for cadre officers and officers on deputation from the IPS. Under the new Act, 50 per cent of posts at the Inspector General level, 67 per cent at the Additional Director General rank, and 100 per cent of posts at the Special Director General and Director General ranks are reserved for IPS officers.
The issue affects the career progression of about 13,000 CAPF cadre officers, whose first promotion is delayed by as much as 15 to 16 years in the worst cases, while an IPS officer gets four promotions in the same period. Retired IPS officers have said in newspaper editorials that, as members of an all-India service, their deputation to the CAPFs was "vital" and "essential" for smooth coordination with state police forces. The CAPFs function under the Union home ministry and handle law and order duties, internal security work such as border guarding, counter-terror operations and anti-insurgency tasks, as well as election duties.
The petitions before the Supreme Court centre on whether the new law addresses long-standing concerns over stalled promotions in the CAPFs, with the petitioners seeking implementation of the court's earlier ruling and a wider role for cadre officers in senior ranks.

headline: Supreme Court judge's 'ant' remark during discussion on judicial transparency
cluster_text: Supreme Court judge's 'ant' remark during discussion on judicial transparency [SEP] Supreme Court judge's 'ant' remark during discussion on judicial transparency
full_text:
Supreme Court judge's 'ant' remark during discussion on judicial transparency
Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said that not giving reasons for judicial appointments did a disservice to outstanding judges whose work and achievements deserved to be in the public domain.
Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan has called for greater transparency in the collegium system, arguing that withholding reasons for judicial appointments not only denies deserving judges due recognition but could also allow individuals who make "wholly unconstitutional" remarks to enter the judiciary.
Speaking during a panel discussion to mark the launch of the Judicial Transparency Index by the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy, Justice Bhuyan said the collegium should explain the reasons behind its recommendations and questioned why judicial appointments should be insulated from informed public debate.
"By withholding reasons, we also create space for individuals to enter the judiciary who may later describe groups of people as 'ants' and make other remarks that are wholly unconstitutional and contrary to the values of the Constitution," he said during the panel discussion.
Justice Bhuyan said that not giving reasons for judicial appointments did a disservice to outstanding judges whose work and achievements deserved to be in the public domain.
He argued that greater disclosure and discussion around appointments could help prevent the elevation of individuals whose views may be at odds with constitutional values.
"To prevent the elevation of such individuals, there should be discussion. There should be reasons explaining what happened. What harm is caused if there is informed public debate on such decisions?" Justice Bhuyan said.
'NEED GREATER TRANSPARENCY IN APPOINTMENTS'
Separately, in his address to the gathering, Justice Bhuyan made a broader case for greater transparency in the process of appointing and transferring judges.
He pointed out that deliberations over the elevation and transfer of judges remain confidential, reasons for rejecting or deferring recommendations are rarely disclosed in full, and the criteria applied by the collegium are not codified in any publicly accessible document.
Justice Bhuyan also drew attention to what he described as a recent shift in Supreme Court collegium statements.
"I have seen that the last three statements of the Supreme Court collegium do not contain any reason at all for recommending elevation as opposed to the earlier statements where each of the recommendations were supported by some reason," he said.
Justice Bhuyan described this as a "reflexive gap", pointing to the contrast between a judiciary that has embraced greater openness in its adjudicative role and one that remains more guarded about its own institutional processes.
"Deliberations over the elevation and transfer of judges remain confidential; reasons for rejecting or deferring a recommendation are rarely disclosed in full; and the criteria applied are not codified in any publicly accessible instrument comparable to the Memorandum of Procedure's own limited disclosure," he said.
Justice Bhuyan also raised the broader question of accountability within the judiciary.
"Every legal system that claims to administer justice rather than merely dispense power must answer an old and uncomfortable question: who watches the watchmen?" he said.
WHY THE COLLEGIUM SYSTEM HAS BEEN CONTROVERSIAL
The Supreme Court collegium system remains one of the most debated aspects of India's judiciary.
Under the system, the Chief Justice of India and a group of senior Supreme Court judges recommend appointments and transfers in the higher judiciary. The government can seek reconsideration of a recommendation, but its role in the process is limited.
Critics have long argued that the collegium lacks transparency, with little public information available on why particular candidates are selected, rejected or deferred. Questions have also been raised over the absence of clearly codified and publicly accessible criteria governing appointments.
The judiciary, however, has consistently defended the system as necessary to protect judicial independence and insulate appointments from executive interference.
The issue has also repeatedly led to friction between the judiciary and the government. Parliament sought to replace the collegium with the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC), but the Supreme Court struck down the law in 2015, holding that it undermined judicial independence.
Former Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud had also defended the collegium system in 2024, saying efforts were being made to improve transparency in the appointment process.
In an interview with PTI, he said it was easy to criticise the system, but maintained that the collegium made every effort to ensure that the required process of consultation was followed before a judge was appointed.

CBI case against Anil Ambani, Reliance Capital over Rs 1,816 crore EPFO loss
The CBI has filed an FIR against Reliance Capital and former chairman Anil Ambani over alleged EPFO losses.
The CBI has registered an FIR against Reliance Capital Limited (RCL) and its former chairman Anil D Ambani over allegations that the company caused a loss of Rs 1,816.22 crore to the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).
The case follows a complaint dated July 21 from the Union Ministry of Labour and Employment, which alleged cheating, criminal conspiracy and wrongful loss to the EPFO. Ambani has denied any wrongdoing through his spokesperson.
According to the complaint, now part of the CBI FIR, RCL issued secured non-convertible debentures during 2013 and 2014. The complaint said investments totalling Rs 2,500 crore were made by portfolio managers on behalf of the EPFO in these debentures, with maturity in 2023 and 2024.
The complaint alleged, "The present complaint is being lodged on behalf of EPFO through its authorised officer pursuant to the approval of the competent authority in relation to the substantial loss suffered by the EPFO arising out of its investment in the secured Non-Convertible Debentures issued by Reliance Capital Limited and the subsequently discovered material indicating fraudulent conduct connected with such investment."
It said the Ministry of Labour and Employment sent the complaint after being informed by the Enforcement Directorate that it had found documentary evidence and that a transaction audit by BDO India LLP showed, prima facie, a number of fraudulent transactions by RCL and those in charge of its management between December 7, 2019, and December 6, 2021.
The complaint further alleged, "In addition, during an earlier period as well, various fraudulent transactions have been found which also led to ultimate failure of RCL as a consequence of siphoning off of money of RCL." It said the ED probe prima facie pointed to a series of transactions involving irregular lending, diversion of funds, impairment of security and other acts by RCL that require investigation.
The complaint added, "If established upon investigation, such conduct may have materially contributed to the financial deterioration of RCL, its inability to honour its obligation towards Debenture Holders, and the consequent loss of Rs 1,816.22 crore suffered by EPFO."
Responding to the complaint, Ambani's spokesperson said, "The FIR registered by the CBI pertains to Reliance Capital Limited. Mr. Ambani served as a Non-Executive Director/Chairman of the Board of Reliance Capital Limited from 2005 until November 2021, when the Reserve Bank of India superseded the Board of Directors of the company and appointed an administrator." The spokesperson added, "Anil Ambani denies any wrongdoing, whatsoever, and reserves all rights available to him in law."

full_text:
Antilia case: NIA court frames charges against Sachin Vaze, Pradeep Sharma, others
A special NIA court in Mumbai has framed charges against 10 accused in the Antilia bomb scare and Mansukh Hiran murder case. The trial will test allegations of terror staging, extortion and a deep police-linked cover-up.
A special NIA court in Mumbai on Saturday framed charges against 10 people, including former policemen Sachin Vaze and Pradeep Sharma, in the 2021 Antilia bomb scare and businessman Mansukh Hiran murder case. The accused will face trial under the Indian Penal Code for murder, extortion, destruction of evidence and criminal conspiracy, along with relevant provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and the Explosive Substances Act.
Special National Investigation Agency court judge Chakor Baviskar framed the charges after the accused pleaded not guilty. Besides Vaze and Sharma, the other accused are Riyazuddin Kazi, Sunil Mane, Vinayak Shinde, Anand Jadhav, Satish Tirupati Mothkuri, Manish Vasantbhai Soni, Naresh Gaur and Santosh Shelar. Kazi, Mane and Shinde are also former policemen.
The prosecution has accused all 10 of forming a "terrorist gang" and entering into a criminal conspiracy between February and March 2021. An SUV containing explosives was found near billionaire industrialist Mukesh Ambani's south Mumbai residence, Antilia, on February 25, 2021. Businessman Mansukh Hiran, who had claimed that the SUV had been stolen from him, was found dead in a creek in neighbouring Thane on March 5, 2021. A few days later, Vaze, once known as an "encounter specialist" police officer, was arrested in the case.
According to the NIA, the accused allegedly posted a message on the Telegram channel "Jaishish-Ul-Hind" carrying the threat, "Agle baar connect ho kar ayega" (next time the bomb's wires will be connected), to create the impression that a terrorist organisation was involved. In draft charges filed earlier, the agency identified Vaze as the mastermind and alleged that his motive was to terrorise wealthy individuals and extort money to meet a Rs 100-crore monthly target allegedly set by a high-ranking political figure, while also trying to regain his "lost glory" as a "super cop".
The NIA also alleged that Vaze conspired with the other accused to eliminate Hiran because he refused to take the blame for the explosives and was seen as a "weak link" who could expose the conspiracy. Sharma, another former "encounter specialist" officer of Mumbai Police, allegedly played a key role in the plot to abduct and kill Hiran. The agency claimed he was involved in procuring SIM cards and had directed Shelar, Jadhav, Mothkuri and Soni to dump Hiran's body into the Thane creek.
To cover up the crime, the accused allegedly destroyed key evidence, including digital video recorders, CCTV footage and the victim's mobile phone. The draft charges also said the operation was partly funded through extortion. According to the prosecution, the conspirators used benami SIM cards and unregistered mobile phones to hide their identities, while the policemen among them created fake alibis by staging midnight raids and preparing nil panchnamas to show they were on duty away from the crime scenes.
While Sharma, Kazi, Gaur and Mane are out on bail, Vaze and the remaining five accused continue to be in judicial custody. The case centres on the explosives-laden SUV found near Antilia, Hiran's killing days later, and the NIA's allegations of conspiracy, extortion and a cover-up involving all 10 accused.

headline: Army, Rajasthan Police bust fake uniform racket, 1,000m cloth seized

full_text:
Army, Rajasthan Police bust fake uniform racket, 1,000m cloth seized
Army intelligence units and Rajasthan Police uncovered an alleged fake military cloth supply network in Sriganganagar. Officials said the unauthorised fabric poses a security risk because it can aid impersonation.
A joint operation by Indian Army intelligence units and Rajasthan Police has uncovered an alleged counterfeit military uniform supply network in Rajasthan's Sriganganagar district, leading to the seizure of nearly 1,000 metres of unauthorised Army-pattern combat cloth from multiple shops.
The operation stemmed from a June seizure of counterfeit combat cloth in Bareilly, which investigators traced back to a manufacturing source in Sriganganagar. Following the lead, Indian Army intelligence personnel conducted a discreet investigation that identified a local firm as a key link in the supply chain allegedly distributing fake Army-pattern combat fabric across the region.
According to officials, the firm was suspected of supplying counterfeit military-pattern cloth to vendors in Sriganganagar town as well as markets in Lalgarh Jattan, Suratgarh and nearby areas.
LEAD FROM BAREILLY SEIZURE TRIGGERED PROBE
After gathering evidence, Army intelligence units shared an interim investigation report with Rajasthan Police in mid-July. Based on the findings, a coordinated operation was launched on July 30, with police and security personnel carrying out searches at multiple shops across the district.
The raids resulted in the recovery of around 1,000 metres of unauthorised new-pattern combat cloth resembling material used for military uniforms.
SECURITY RISK DUE TO POTENTIAL IMPERSONATION
Officials said the unauthorised possession, sale or use of military-pattern combat fabric is a punishable offence. Such counterfeit material poses a significant security threat as it can be used to impersonate armed forces personnel and facilitate unlawful activities.
Investigators are now probing the extent of the supply network and whether the counterfeit cloth was being distributed beyond Rajasthan to other parts of the country.

full_text:
How did Abhijeet Dipke's father fund US education? RTI activist seeks probe
RTI activist Amit Tiwari questioned the status of the Cockroach Janta Party and whether it could receive funds while operating under the name of a political party.
A Surat-based Right to Information (RTI) activist has sought a probe into the finances of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke's father, questioning how the retired Maharashtra government employee funded his son's education abroad.
The activist, Amit Tiwari, has also written to the Election Commission of India and tax authorities seeking scrutiny of the Rs 1 crore legal defence fund announced by senior advocate and Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal for CJP protesters facing police cases.
Tiwari sought an examination of the financial status of Dipke's father, Bhagwanrao Dipke, citing his status as a retired government employee and his son's higher education abroad.
Separately, Tiwari questioned the status of the CJP and whether it could receive funds while operating under the name of a political party.
"The Cockroach Janta Party is an unregistered entity but is operating as a political party. If Rs 1 crore has been pledged to it as a legal defence fund, then the EC should verify whether the CJP is registered with it under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951," Tiwari said.
"If not registered, then its operation under the name of a political party and collection/receipt of funds may require examination," he added.
Tiwari also approached the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs, asking it to examine whether GST would apply to Sibal's proposed contribution to the legal defence fund.
Sibal had on Monday announced a Rs 1 crore contribution to a fund set up by the CJP to provide legal assistance to protesters arrested by Delhi Police during the agitation over the NEET paper leak controversy.

Delhi High Court transfers six judges to newly set up exclusive NIA courts
The Delhi High Court has transferred 151 judicial officers and posted 13 judges to newly created special courts at Rouse Avenue. The move shifts all NIA trials from Patiala House and reshuffles several high-profile judicial assignments.
The Delhi High Court on Saturday transferred 151 judicial officers across the capital, including 13 judges who will take charge of newly established Special Exclusive Courts for National Investigation Agency (NIA), Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) and Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act cases at the Rouse Avenue Court Complex.
According to the High Court's transfer order, six judges—Anu Grover Baliga, Vikas Dhull, Prashant Sharma, Amit Bansal, Kiran Bansal and Pulastya Pramachala—have been posted as Special Exclusive NIA judges. They will assume charge from August 4.
The newly constructed NIA courtrooms at Rouse Avenue are scheduled to be inaugurated on Monday, marking the shift of all NIA trials from Patiala House Courts to the new judicial complex.
In addition to the NIA courts, dedicated MCOCA and NDPS courts have also been established at Rouse Avenue. Four judges—Sandeep Yadav, Anuradha Shukla, Devendra Kumar Sharma and Bhupinder Singh—have been posted as Special Exclusive NDPS judges, while Gaurav Rao, Gagandeep Singh and Surbhi Sharma Vats have been appointed as Special Exclusive MCOCA judges.
CHANGES IN JUDICIAL ASSIGNMENTS
The restructuring also brings changes to several high-profile judicial assignments.
Additional Sessions Judge Prashant Sharma, who has been hearing NIA cases involving Hafiz Saeed, leaders of the Popular Front of India (PFI), and cases related to Ukrainian and US nationals, will now continue as a Special Exclusive NIA judge at Rouse Avenue.

A woman found dead by a roadside in Uttar Pradesh's Hamirpur appeared to be the victim of a road accident. But within 48 hours, the case took a chilling turn. VICTIM'S BODY FOUND BY THE ROADSIDE
The case began on the night of July 29, when farmers returning after guarding their fields spotted a woman's body by the roadside in Hamirpur district.
Police reached the spot, collected evidence and sent the body for a post-mortem examination. At first, the circumstances suggested that she may have been killed in a road accident.
But police did not immediately know who she was.
A bank account slip recovered during the investigation provided the first major lead, helping police identify the woman as 32-year-old Reeta.
Following a complaint by her father, Sarvesh Kumar Gupta, police registered a murder case and began investigating how she had ended up dead by the roadside.
HUSBAND REPORTS HER MISSING, THEN IDENTIFIES BODY
Even as police were trying to establish what had happened to Reeta, her husband had approached Sumerpur police station to report her missing.
Later, when news emerged that an unidentified woman's body had been recovered, Amar also turned up to identify it.
Police now allege that both actions were part of an attempt to distance himself from his wife's death and create the impression that he knew nothing about what had happened to her.
That version, however, began to unravel as investigators examined evidence from the scene and turned to technical surveillance.
Within 48 hours, police said what initially appeared to be an accidental death had emerged as an alleged premeditated murder.

As investigators dug deeper, attention turned to Reeta's marriage and the couple's financial circumstances.
Reeta had married Amar around two-and-a-half years ago. According to her family, it was her second marriage, while Amar had reportedly been married twice earlier.
After her first husband died, Reeta began working in Kanpur, where she met Amar. The two fell in love and later married.
Investigators allege that financial troubles eventually became central to a conspiracy to kill her.
According to police, questioning of the accused revealed that they owed a substantial amount of money to Pushpendra Soni alias Sahil.
Police alleged that an insurance policy was then taken out on Reeta and a plan was drawn up to kill her, make her death appear accidental and claim Rs 44 lakh in insurance money.
Investigators claimed the accused had even decided how the payout would be divided. Amar was allegedly to receive Rs 15 lakh, while the remaining amount would be shared among the others.

Police said Amar took Reeta to an arterial road near Paudhiya as part of the alleged plan, where his associates were waiting in a car.
Investigators allege that the car was first used to hit Reeta, causing her to fall into a roadside ditch.
The accused then allegedly pulled her out, placed her on the road and drove the car over her again, killing her.
They then fled, leaving the body at the scene in an attempt to make the killing appear to be a road accident, police said.
Amar subsequently reported his wife missing and later identified her body, actions that investigators allege were intended to deflect suspicion.
48 HOURS LATER, PLOT UNRAVELS
The investigation eventually turned towards Amar and the other accused.
Police said evidence collected from the scene, technical analysis, surveillance data and questioning of the accused exposed inconsistencies in the accident theory and helped them reconstruct the alleged conspiracy.
Police arrested Amar and three others identified as Amit Gupta alias Ram, Pushpendra Soni alias Sahil and Abhay Singh alias Golu.

headline: Honeytrap gang posing as cops, journalists busted in UP; 2 arrested
cluster_text: Honeytrap gang posing as cops, journalists busted in UP; 2 arrested [SEP] Honeytrap gang posing as cops, journalists busted in UP; 2 arrested
full_text:
Honeytrap gang posing as cops, journalists busted in UP; 2 arrested
Two accused have been arrested, while a search is underway to arrest two more members of the five-member gang.
A gang that allegedly impersonated police personnel, senior police officers and journalists to run a honeytrap-based extortion racket has been busted in Uttar Pradesh's Meerut, police said on Saturday.
Two accused have been arrested, while a search is underway to arrest two more members of the five-member gang.
The case came to the fore after a resident named Neeraj Pal alleged that he was lured into a honeytrap through a fake female profile, threatened with fabricated criminal charges and forced to transfer money.
Social media posts also claimed that the gang had been running a fake police outpost. However, police have rejected the claim, saying the accused operated from a rented office and not a police station.
VICTIM LURED THROUGH FAKE WOMAN PROFILE, FORCED TO PAY MONEY
According to police, the accused, Shashank Sharma, Rahul Pal and Akash, posed as a woman online and struck up a conversation with Neeraj. Over time, they established an intimate rapport and exchanged photographs with him.
After gaining his trust, they asked Neeraj to meet the woman in person. However, when he reached the designated location, two men approached him instead and demanded money to facilitate the meeting.
The accused then identified themselves as police personnel and journalists, threatened Neeraj with legal action and demanded Rs 2 lakh to settle the matter. They also forced him to transfer Rs 10,000 through Google Pay.
As per the complaint, they also recorded videos of Neeraj and further used them for deepfake purposes to blackmail him.
Following the incident, Neeraj approached the local police and lodged a complaint. Acting on the complaint, a special team constituted on the directions of the Senior Superintendent of Police launched an investigation and arrested Rahul Pal and Akash. Police said efforts are underway to trace the remaining accused.
During the investigation, the accused told investigators that they followed the same modus operandi for other targets. They identified targets through Instagram by creating fake female profiles, called them for a meeting, and then threatened them by impersonating fake police personnel and journalists.
FAKE POLICE EQUIPMENT, WALKIE-TALKIES, AND DOCUMENTS SEIZED
Police recovered a handful of items used by the accused to impersonate law enforcement officials and lend credibility to their operation.
The seized articles include a Maruti Alto car without a registration plate, a separate number plate, two mobile phones, a telephone set, a laptop, a tablet, a calculator, walkie-talkies, a PhonePe receiver box, a baton, a beat book, official-looking seals, nameplates, complaint applications, files and several other documents.
Police suspect these materials were used to convince people that they were dealing with genuine police officials before extorting money from them.
POLICE DENY REPORTS OF FAKE OUTPOST
Addressing speculation surrounding the case, senior cop Vinayak Gopal Bhonsle said the accused were not operating a fake police outpost.
"There was no fake police chowki. It was an office with 'Karyalaya' written outside it. Claims circulating on social media that a fake police outpost was being run are incorrect," he said.
Bhonsle said police registered an FIR immediately after receiving Neeraj Pal's complaint regarding the forced transfer of Rs 10,000.
"The accused created fake female identities to honeytrap people. Neeraj was called to their office, where he realised there was no woman. They recorded videos to blackmail him using fabricated allegations and demanded Rs 2 lakh. Two accused have been arrested, while two others remain absconding. They will be arrested soon," the officer said.
Police said the investigation is continuing to identify other possible survivors and determine whether the gang was involved in similar cases elsewhere in the region.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bhogapuram airport inauguration drew open backing from NDA allies in Andhra Pradesh. Their speeches framed the event as a public endorsement of his leadership after recent protests.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Andhra Pradesh on Saturday to inaugurate the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram turned into a strong show of support from his NDA allies, with Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan publicly praising his leadership and appealing for continued public backing.
The event marked Modi's first visit to Andhra Pradesh after the recent CJP protests and GenZ demonstrations that spread across Delhi and several other cities.
PAWAN KALYAN REFERS TO JANTAR MANTAR PROTESTS
Addressing the gathering in Telugu, Jana Sena Party chief Pawan Kalyan referred to the protests at Jantar Mantar, saying criticism directed at the Prime Minister had deeply affected him.
"PM Modi is leading India for a third term. So many people spoke harshly about him at Jantar Mantar. It brought tears to my eyes," Kalyan said.
Questioning the criticism, he said Modi had dedicated his life to the nation and continued to shoulder his responsibilities without taking leave. Kalyan also said the Prime Minister faced challenges both from outside and within the country, adding that any criticism of Modi was, in his view, criticism of him as well.
As Kalyan spoke, Naidu was seen explaining parts of the speech to the Prime Minister. After the address, Modi smiled and shook hands with the Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister.
NAIDU URGES SUPPORT FOR PM MODI
Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu devoted a significant portion of his speech to praising the Prime Minister, repeatedly leading the audience in chants of "Modi, Modi" and "Thank you."
Appealing for continued support, Naidu said, "Protect PM Modi's leadership."
Without directly referring to the recent protests, he said critics should recognise the Prime Minister's contribution over the past 25 years, first as Gujarat Chief Minister and later as Prime Minister.
"Without Narendra Modi, we cannot imagine Viksit Bharat by 2047," Naidu said, adding that India could become the world's number one country under Modi's leadership.

Smriti Irani said the Centre answered the NEET paper leak protests with legislation, a task force and direct outreach by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She said the response showed engagement with students while drawing a line against violence during dissent.
Senior BJP leader and former Union Education Minister Smriti Irani has dismissed claims that the NEET paper leak protests exposed a widening disconnect between Generation Z (GenZ) and the Narendra Modi government. She asserted that the Centre responded swiftly through legislation, dialogue and direct communication by the Prime Minister.
In an exclusive interview with India Today, Irani said the passage of the anti-paper leak legislation in Parliament, coupled with Prime Minister Modi's recent appeal to students through an Instagram video, demonstrated that the government was responsive to the concerns of young people rather than indifferent to them.
'NO DISCONNECT BETWEEN GENZ AND GOVT'
Asked whether the student-led protests reflected a growing gap between the youth and the government, Irani rejected the premise, arguing that the government's response proved otherwise.
She said Parliament had passed the anti-paper leak Bill after extensive deliberations and described the Prime Minister's message to protesting students as evidence of constructive engagement.
"It is a great insult to Parliament when you say the issue has merely been papered over," she said, adding that the government had acted proactively by setting up a task force, passing the legislation and directly communicating with young citizens.
Irani also accused sections of the media of disproportionately focusing on the Jantar Mantar protests while ignoring similar student movements elsewhere, particularly in Jharkhand.
DEFENDS EDUCATION REFORMS, ANTI-PAPER LEAK BILL
Responding to concerns over whether previous reform committees had yielded tangible results, Irani said the new legislation "speaks for itself" and argued that examination-related challenges had existed long before the Modi government came to power.
Drawing on her tenure as Education Minister, she said the National Education Policy was framed after one of the most extensive consultation exercises in independent India's history.
According to her, the government consulted more than 2.25 lakh village education councils, district education officers, state education ministers, parent-teacher associations and student bodies before finalising the policy.
She also defended the composition of the newly constituted task force on examination reforms, saying it reflected the Prime Minister's willingness to involve experts and individuals across political and ideological lines rather than limiting participation to supporters of the government.

The Centre has announced changes to NEET-PG 2026, including wider test city options, earlier city allotment and more time per question. The measures add tighter security checks and a single-shift format to make the exam fairer and more convenient.
In a series of changes for the NEET-PG to be held later this year, the Centre will expand the choice of test locations, give candidates more time to plan travel to their examination cities, and give them more time per question in the test.
The reforms are aimed at making the process more convenient for National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test for Postgraduate (NEET-PG) candidates, according to the Union health ministry.
"The end-to-end question paper preparation and delivery process has been further reinforced through multiple layers of encryption, secure offline preparation, time-bound finalisation of the question paper shortly before the examination, and controlled digital decryption only at the scheduled commencement of the test," the ministry said in a statement.
The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) has also operationalised a dedicated email address for reporting impersonation, touting and other unfair practices while issuing regular advisories to candidates to promote awareness and vigilance.
The ministry said that to strengthen the integrity of the examination process, Aadhaar-based authentication has been introduced during both the application process and on the examination day. Iris-based biometric verification will be used wherever fingerprint authentication is unsuccessful, it said.
Under the revised system, candidates will indicate three state preferences for their examination centre, with their correspondence state being the mandatory first preference, enabling allotment of centres closer to their place of residence, the ministry said.
Earlier, exam cities were allotted on a first come, first-served basis prompting candidates to rush to submit their applications as soon as the registration window opened, a source explained. Those who delayed often found all nearby centres filled, forcing them to travel to other states to appear for the exam.
In another key change, candidates will be informed of their allotted test city nearly three weeks before the August 30 examination, giving them more time to plan travel and accommodation, the ministry said.
The NBEMS has also rationalised the examination pattern to 180 questions to be answered in 210 minutes, allowing candidates more time per question while retaining the overall duration of the test, it said.
The exam previously had 200 multiple choice questions with a maximum score of 800 marks.
The source said that recently, the exam had been conducted in two shifts due to emergencies or postponements but the 2026 edition will be held in a single shift to ensure uniformity in the difficulty level and assessment of candidates.
Earlier, candidates often faced stress as the final venue and location details were released very close to the test date, leaving minimal time to book travel or accommodation, the official added.
Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda on Saturday reviewed the preparedness for NEET-PG 2026 and directed all agencies to ensure the examination is conducted in a smooth, secure, transparent and technology-enabled manner. He assessed the readiness of NBEMS, technology partners and other stakeholders and stressed that every effort must be made to ensure a fair and candidate-friendly examination.
A total of 2,73,183 candidates have registered for NEET-PG 2026, an increase of over 12.5 per cent compared to last year. The examination will be conducted in a single shift across around 340 cities and more than 1,300 examination centres.
Comprehensive security arrangements have been put in place for the examination, including advance sealing and verification of examination centres, CCTV surveillance, biometric authentication, candidate frisking, deployment of signal jammers, dynamic comput, live monitoring through central and regional command centres, and real-time supervision by independent observers and appraisers.

BJP leader Shehzad Poonawalla on Saturday took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi's critics, saying the Prime Minister had "failed" to become a dictator, and contrasted PM Modi's response to the recent NEET protest controversy with what he called the Congress's and opposition-ruled states' record on dissent. His remarks came just a day after he updated his X account and dropped "BJP national spokesperson" from his bio.
In a video posted on X, Poonawalla said he was "totally disappointed" with PM Modi, adding sarcastically, "Twelve years have passed, and he is a failure. He doesn't even know how to become a proper dictator."
The remark came a day after Prime Minister Modi released a video message urging people to forgive the students who had allegedly used abusive language against him and his late mother during the NEET protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
Instead of behaving like a dictator, Poonawalla said, PM Modi had appealed to society, the police and everyone else to forgive the students.
"Last night he released a video and, regarding the children who used abusive language against constitutional authorities and his late mother, he said, 'They are mischievous children, forgive them.' He appealed to society, to the police and to everyone to forgive them," Poonawalla said.
The BJP leader then targeted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, saying, "Rahul Gandhi is a descendant of Indira Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru. Learn from them what a real dictatorship is, what a real Emergency is, Modi ji."
He alleged that while the Modi government had withdrawn cases against student protesters after accepting their demands, Congress governments were registering cases over social media posts and protests.
Referring to recent incidents, Poonawalla claimed that cases had been registered in Kerala against Instagram users for allegedly insulting Rahul Gandhi. He also referred to police action in Karnataka over a poster and against a rap artist.
Poonawalla went on to invoke the Congress's political history, alleging that it was Jawaharlal Nehru who curtailed freedom of speech and that Indira Gandhi imposed the Emergency, jailed opposition leaders and suppressed dissent.
He also referred to the Assam movement, the Navnirman movement and the Anna Hazare-led anti-corruption agitation, alleging that thousands of protesters had been jailed during those periods.
Addressing PM Modi again, Poonawalla said, "Today, the children are using abusive language and you're saying, 'They are kids, mistakes happen. We should help them get to the right path.' But Rahul ji, like a real dictator, is getting cases filed over an Instagram post."
He ended his remarks with another jibe at the Prime Minister's critics: "Modi ji, it has been 12 years. You are unable to become a dictator. You have dashed the hopes of all these Left liberals. You have failed."

In a late-night video on Friday, Prime Minister Modi said it pained him that even his late mother had been subjected to "filthy abuses" during the NEET protests, but urged society not to punish the students.
Calling them "misguided children", Modi appealed to people to forgive them and help them "learn from their mistakes".
"The children are ours. It is our responsibility to show them the correct path," the Prime Minister said, adding that dragging them to court or publicly shaming them would not solve the problem.
The remarks came days after the 36-day agitation led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) ended following the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and the government's acceptance of the protesters' key demands.
The protests over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination had drawn nationwide support from opposition parties, many of whose leaders repeatedly accused the Modi government of acting in a "dictatorial" manner over the police crackdown on demonstrators. A brief commotion broke out at a cultural programme in Kolkata on Saturday after exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen invited Bengali poet Joy Goswami to join her on stage. Protests from a section of the audience briefly interrupted her address during an event marking her return to the city after nearly two decades.
As Goswami got up from his seat and began walking towards the dais, loud shouting erupted from part of the audience, forcing him to turn back and sit down. The disruption paused the programme for several minutes before Nasreen appealed for calm and resumed her speech.

When he responded, the auditorium reverberated with slogans and loud voices. Organisers repeatedly appealed to the audience to remain calm, but the commotion continued for some time. Nasreen then broke her silence and said, "Shall I speak? Then please calm down and take your seats," after which order was restored.

The reaction came despite Goswami having publicly expressed regret in the past over Nasreen's long exile, saying he considered himself "guilty" for not doing enough when she was forced to leave Kolkata in 2007 amid violent protests over her writings.
Many in the audience, however, appeared unwilling to see him share the stage with Nasreen during what was billed as her symbolic homecoming.
The programme was held hours after Suvendu Adhikari accorded Nasreen a civic reception at a hall in the state secretariat complex. It marked her first visit to Kolkata in 19 years. In her speech, Nasreen said her return was like coming back to "a part of life" she had left behind. She said her homecoming showed that "injustice can be long but cannot be permanent", and expressed hope that one day no writer would be forced into exile for exercising the right to free expression.
Nasreen had left Kolkata in November 2007 after violent protests over her presence in the city. She was first moved to Jaipur and later to New Delhi under central security before eventually leaving India. I am back: Taslima Nasrin renews free speech call in first public appearance
Taslima Nasrin returned to Kolkata for her first public address in the city since 2007. She used the occasion to defend free speech, secularism and equal rights while reflecting on exile.
Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasrin returned to Kolkata after a gap of 19 years on Friday, describing the moment as the recovery of "a chapter of my lost life" while delivering a forceful defence of free speech, secularism, women's rights and the right to criticise religious ideologies.
The event, attended by West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, marked Nasrin's first public address in Kolkata since leaving the city in 2007. During her speech, she thanked Adhikari and the West Bengal government for ensuring her security, while stressing that her gratitude should not be mistaken for political allegiance.
Speaking at a public event in Kolkata, Nasrin reflected on decades of exile from both Bangladesh and West Bengal, saying her return was more than a personal milestone. She called it a reminder that "closed doors do not remain closed forever" and said the day represented a victory of free thought over fear and censorship.
"I have not just returned to a city. I have returned to a chapter of my lost life," she said, adding that she was overwhelmed by the welcome she received after nearly two decades away from Kolkata.
Nasrin thanked Secular Mission chairman Osman Gani Mallick for inviting her to the city and expressed gratitude to Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari for facilitating her return and ensuring her security.
"I have not come here to speak for any political party. I have come to speak for equal rights of women, human rights, secularism, rationality, free thought and freedom of speech," she said.
RECALLING YEARS OF EXILE
The author recounted how she was forced to leave Bangladesh on August 8, 1994, after facing threats over her writings, and later had to leave Kolkata in 2007 despite not being convicted of any crime.
Describing exile as both a personal and political experience, she said the state had failed to protect writers from extremist threats.
"The state removed me from the country, but it could not remove the country from within me," she said, describing the Bengali language as her "portable homeland."
Nasrin recalled discovering Kolkata through literature, radio broadcasts and correspondence long before she first visited the city. She said poetry and literature had connected the two Bengals even when political borders divided them.
She also spoke about finding a home in Kolkata during her years in exile before being forced to leave in 2007 following threats from fundamentalist groups.
'FREEDOM OF SPEECH BELONGS TO EVERYONE'
A major part of Nasrin's address focused on freedom of expression and the dangers of governments yielding to threats from extremist groups.
She argued that exiling writers does not create lasting peace but instead strengthens those who seek to silence dissent.
"In a civilised society, the answer to one argument is another argument, the answer to a book is another book," she said, urging people to challenge ideas through debate rather than violence or censorship.
Nasrin said freedom of speech must extend even to unpopular opinions, arguing that the strength of a democracy is reflected in how safely dissenting voices can express themselves.
She also expressed hope that writers would one day no longer require police protection simply to attend events or publish their work.
CRITICISM OF RELIGIOUS FUNDAMENTALISM
Nasrin reiterated her long-held criticism of religious fundamentalism, saying she opposed all forms of extremism but had spoken most extensively about Islamic fundamentalism because it was the ideology she had experienced firsthand.
She rejected the suggestion that criticism of Islam amounted to hatred of Muslims, arguing that people deserve protection while ideologies should remain open to scrutiny.
According to Nasrin, reform within Muslim societies requires open discussion on issues including women's rights, freedom of belief and equal citizenship.
She also criticised governments that, in her view, prioritise religious pressure over constitutional rights and warned that compromising with threats only emboldens extremists.
CALLS FOR EQUALITY AND SECULARISM
The author devoted a significant portion of her speech to advocating equal rights for women and a secular state.
She argued that no religious law should deny women equality and called for legal systems to be guided by constitutional values rather than religious identity.
Nasrin also supported the idea of a common civil code based on human rights and gender equality rather than the principles of any particular religion.
She maintained that true secularism requires separating religion from state institutions, politics and education while ensuring equal rights for believers and non-believers alike.
HOPE DESPITE EXILE
Despite recalling decades of persecution, threats and displacement, Nasrin said she remained optimistic about the future.
She expressed hope that Bangladesh would one day separate religion from the state, guarantee equal rights for women and minorities, and allow writers and free thinkers to express themselves without fear.
Concluding her address, Nasrin became emotional as she reflected on returning to Kolkata after nearly two decades.
"No one can give me back those 19 years," she said. "But today's opening of the door proves that injustice can last a long time, but it is not eternal."
Calling her return a victory for freedom of speech, free thought and the affection of ordinary people, she ended with a message of gratitude to the city she once considered home.
"Today, you did not just bring me back to Kolkata," she said. "You brought me back to my lost life."

"I have not come here to speak for any political party. I have come to speak for equal rights of women, human rights, secularism, rationality, free thought and freedom of speech," she said.
RECALLING YEARS OF EXILE
The author recounted how she was forced to leave Bangladesh on August 8, 1994, after facing threats over her writings, and later had to leave Kolkata in 2007 despite not being convicted of any crime.
Describing exile as both a personal and political experience, she said the state had failed to protect writers from extremist threats.
"The state removed me from the country, but it could not remove the country from within me," she said, describing the Bengali language as her "portable homeland."
Nasrin recalled discovering Kolkata through literature, radio broadcasts and correspondence long before she first visited the city. She said poetry and literature had connected the two Bengals even when political borders divided them.
She also spoke about finding a home in Kolkata during her years in exile before being forced to leave in 2007 following threats from fundamentalist groups.
'FREEDOM OF SPEECH BELONGS TO EVERYONE'
A major part of Nasrin's address focused on freedom of expression and the dangers of governments yielding to threats from extremist groups.
She argued that exiling writers does not create lasting peace but instead strengthens those who seek to silence dissent.
"In a civilised society, the answer to one argument is another argument, the answer to a book is another book," she said, urging people to challenge ideas through debate rather than violence or censorship.
Nasrin said freedom of speech must extend even to unpopular opinions, arguing that the strength of a democracy is reflected in how safely dissenting voices can express themselves.
She also expressed hope that writers would one day no longer require police protection simply to attend events or publish their work.
CRITICISM OF RELIGIOUS FUNDAMENTALISM
Nasrin reiterated her long-held criticism of religious fundamentalism, saying she opposed all forms of extremism but had spoken most extensively about Islamic fundamentalism because it was the ideology she had experienced firsthand.
She rejected the suggestion that criticism of Islam amounted to hatred of Muslims, arguing that people deserve protection while ideologies should remain open to scrutiny.
According to Nasrin, reform within Muslim societies requires open discussion on issues including women's rights, freedom of belief and equal citizenship.
She also criticised governments that, in her view, prioritise religious pressure over constitutional rights and warned that compromising with threats only emboldens extremists.
CALLS FOR EQUALITY AND SECULARISM
The author devoted a significant portion of her speech to advocating equal rights for women and a secular state.
She argued that no religious law should deny women equality and called for legal systems to be guided by constitutional values rather than religious identity.
Nasrin also supported the idea of a common civil code based on human rights and gender equality rather than the principles of any particular religion.
She maintained that true secularism requires separating religion from state institutions, politics and education while ensuring equal rights for believers and non-believers alike.
HOPE DESPITE EXILE
Despite recalling decades of persecution, threats and displacement, Nasrin said she remained optimistic about the future.
She expressed hope that Bangladesh would one day separate religion from the state, guarantee equal rights for women and minorities, and allow writers and free thinkers to express themselves without fear.
Concluding her address, Nasrin became emotional as she reflected on returning to Kolkata after nearly two decades.
"No one can give me back those 19 years," she said. "But today's opening of the door proves that injustice can last a long time, but it is not eternal."
Calling her return a victory for freedom of speech, free thought and the affection of ordinary people, she ended with a message of gratitude to the city she once considered home.
"Today, you did not just bring me back to Kolkata," she said. "You brought me back to my lost life."

Unable to eliminate extortion despite being in power: Bengal BJP chief's admission
BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya said West Bengal could reverse the flight of capital only if partisan politics was kept out of business, and announced that the government would soon hold consultations before finalising a new industrial policy.
The BJP has not yet been able to eliminate extortion in West Bengal despite coming to power in the state, the party's state president Samik Bhattacharya said on Saturday, while admitting that a section within his own party was showing the same tendencies.
He said the government had been in office for only two months and that not everything had changed with the change in power.
Bhattacharya also warned party workers, supporters and newly inducted leaders against hurling eggs at opposition leaders, saying such acts could rebound on those now indulging in them. He said Bengal could reverse the flight of capital only if partisan politics was kept out of business, and announced that the government would soon hold consultations before finalising a new industrial policy.
Addressing the 'Udyami Samagam' event at the IIT Kharagpur Research Park in Rajarhat on the outskirts of Kolkata, Bhattacharya said, "Our government has come to power only two months ago. We have not been able to solve all problems. If I say on behalf of my party that we have been able to eradicate extortion from everywhere, then I will be making a false claim. There are deviations. People had become accustomed to passing through a system of making easy money through syndicates. Not everything has changed with the change in state power."
He added, "Some joined the ruling party within four hours, others had dormant wishes that have now surfaced. We are trying to control such tendencies within the party. Our CM Suvendu Adhikari is also trying to apply strict brakes on such tendencies." Bhattacharya said a section of workers in the party was trying to enter every sector, from education and health to business, with political flags.
Stressing the need to clean up the business environment, he said Bengal was at a point where it could move away from its difficult industrial past.
"We must keep partisan politics out of this system. We have become residents of a political society in West Bengal. We need freedom from it. Till such time Bengal is able to come out of the culture of infiltration of politics in every sphere of life, no government can bring about its effective change and attract investment," he said.
"We are making an earnest effort to build a government for West Bengal and not a BJP government," he added.
Bhattacharya said the party had achieved only partial success. "We haven't been able to provide you with an error-free atmosphere, but we have largely been able to deliver an investment climate that is fear-free. To set up a company, you can now buy your own brick, cement and sand. If someone approaches you, use the phone. He will either leave your premises or find himself inside lock up," he said.
Calling the BJP government in Bengal one that had "stepped into its adolescence", he said the business community should point out mistakes directly and protest if needed. "No system can function or be made to live for long by quashing protests. All autocracies across the world inevitably fall. If someone from our side sports a body language of having 207 MLAs and hits the road, then the consequence will be disastrous," he said.
He added, "The unwarranted egg-therapy we see now can turn on its head and start falling on the other side as well. All, including those in my party, must understand that. Those Sanatanis who have suddenly found a place in our party and are harbouring aspirations for influence and advantage must also remain careful because the trajectory of those eggs can change in no time."
Referring to the government's move to scrap the Urban Land Ceiling Act to unlock developable land and attract large-scale industrial and real estate investment, Bhattacharya said the next step would be wider consultation. "
Within the next few weeks, the government will sit in a meeting with the investors in this state, those who have set up start-ups, professors in different universities and our industrialists before drawing up our new industrial policy," he said.
Bhattacharya said the government was trying to curb extortionary practices, keep politics out of commerce and build conditions for investment, while also warning his own party against excesses.

Tamil Nadu tightens civic spending rules amid fund crunch in Chennai
The fresh directive by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply (MAWS) Department comes after the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) reported a severe financial crunch, with nearly Rs 2,000 crore in pending bills and a fiscal deficit of Rs 1,970 crore as of March 2026.
The Tamil Nadu government has tightened financial controls over urban local bodies, making government approval mandatory for projects worth over Rs 10 crore and barring officials from splitting large works into smaller packages to bypass the requirement.
The fresh directive by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply (MAWS) Department comes after the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) reported a severe financial crunch, with nearly Rs 2,000 crore in pending bills and a fiscal deficit of Rs 1,970 crore as of March 2026.
The move follows the state government's finding that civic officials had, in some instances, taken up projects without the required approval, including by splitting large infrastructure works into smaller packages to keep them below the threshold for mandatory government clearance.
"All projects exceeding Rs 10 crore require mandatory Tamil Nadu government approval. Officials have been artificially splitting them into multiple projects to keep the value below Rs 10 crore and execute them using the local body's funds. We will put an end to this practice," senior MAWS Department officials told India Today.
SALARIES, PENSIONS TO GET PRIORITY
The directive also lays down a clear order of financial priorities for urban local bodies before they sanction new projects.
Civic bodies have been instructed to first meet essential financial commitments, including salaries, pensions and provident fund contributions, before allocating money for fresh works.
The move is aimed at preventing corporations and other urban local bodies from committing funds to new infrastructure projects when they do not have sufficient resources to meet existing liabilities.
The fresh directive replaces guidelines issued in 2021 under the previous DMK government and modifies the financial approval limits governing projects undertaken by urban local bodies.
FUND CRUNCH IN CHENNAI
The tighter controls come against the backdrop of mounting financial stress at the Greater Chennai Corporation.
Several civic officials recently told India Today that the GCC had accumulated nearly Rs 2,000 crore in pending bills and recorded an overall fiscal deficit of Rs 1,970 crore by the end of March 2026.
Officials estimate that another Rs 1,500 crore in liabilities could accrue during 2026-27, potentially taking the Corporation's pending commitments to around Rs 3,500 crore.
A senior GCC official had acknowledged the extent of the problem, saying, "Because of the major financial crunch, the overall deficit has surged to Rs 1,970 crore by the end of March 2026. Nearly Rs 2,000 crore bills are pending in the GCC as of today."
The Corporation attributed the crunch primarily to spending on civic infrastructure, recurring maintenance commitments and big-ticket projects undertaken using its own funds.
"The fund crunch is mainly due to works undertaken in civic infrastructure, maintenance commitments and taking up big-ticket projects using our own funds," the GCC said in a financial note shared with India Today.
FUND CRUNCH SPARKS POLITICAL PROTEST
The financial strain has also taken a political turn, with DMK councillors staging a protest over the alleged withholding of funds meant for ward-level development works.
The councillors alleged that the Corporation had failed to release Rs 60 lakh allocated to each councillor for development works, delaying projects and affecting civic services across several wards.
Amid the financial crunch, the GCC has stepped up efforts to boost its own revenues.
The Corporation's Revenue Department conducted an intensive property tax collection drive in July, collecting Rs 158 crore compared with Rs 61 crore during the corresponding period in July 2025.
Despite the jump in collections, officials have acknowledged that outstanding bills, infrastructure spending and recurring maintenance commitments continue to put considerable pressure on the Corporation's finances.

New Delhi: One of the Bharatiya Janata Party’s most visible faces on social media and TV channels, Shehzad Poonawalla on Friday removed all reference to the BJP from his X bio, triggering speculation about his resignation from the party.
However, there has been no official confirmation of the BJP spokesperson quitting the party. Poonawalla didn’t respond to calls and messages from ThePrint.
His updated bio now reads, “Religion, Islam, Culture, Hindu, ideology-Bhartiya, Author: GST ki Yatra; Lifelong follower of PM Narendra Modi.”
Poonawalla also shared a screenshot of the revised bio on X. In his updated bio, Poonawalla describes himself as a “lifelong follower” of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
However, his current bio on Instagram still mentions “BJP Spokesperson”.
Poonawalla had joined the BJP after he quit the Congress in December 2017.
The change in his bio has raised eyebrows as he had hinted a few days back that the time had come to move on from active politics.
On Friday, he reposted videos of interviews in which he had made those remarks.
— Shehzad Jai Hind (@Shehzad_Ind) July 30, 2026
— Shehzad Jai Hind (@Shehzad_Ind) July 30, 2026
A lawyer by training, Poonawalla grabbed headlines in 2017 when he termed the Congress presidential election process as rigged and claimed it was rigged in favour of Rahul Gandhi to elevate him to the post of party president. He had quit the party following this controversy.
ThePrint had reported that at the time of his quitting, he alleged that Congress leaders treated him very shabbily despite his repeated attempts to get in touch with Rahul’s office before his public outburst.
PM Modi used his claims to hit out at the Congress and the rival party’s presidential elections.
Shehzad is the brother of political analyst Tehseen Poonawalla, and they had a very public split, when Shehzad openly criticized the Congress leadership’s internal elections, which led to Tehseen distancing himself from him.
The BJP spokesperson is from Pune and comes from a well-off Aga Khan Muslim family. He started working for the Congress in 2008. Poonawalla studied law and interned with Congress leader Suresh Kalmadi before joining the All India Congress Committee (AICC) as a volunteer. After completing his course in 2008, he interned with the Congress’ media research team in Delhi.
He had been the vice-president of the Pune wing of the National Students Union of India and also worked in the AICC’s media cell. After quitting the Congress, he joined the BJP wherein he was first given responsibility at the state level and was later elevated to the position of the national spokesperson.
