Congress MP Amarinder Singh Raja Warring addresses the gathering during the launch of the 'Har Booth Mazboot' campaign
NEW DELHI: Congress' internal rift in Punjab showed no signs of easing on Saturday after supporters of former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi disrupted two party programmes by raising slogans in his favour, prompting AICC general secretary in charge of Punjab Bhupesh Baghel to warn that anyone indulging in indiscipline would be expelled from the party.The slogan shouting took place during the Congress' 'Har Booth, Congress Mazboot' programmes in Patiala and Sangrur, where Baghel, Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring and several senior leaders were present.Despite the disruption, Baghel reiterated that the Congress high command would decide the party's chief ministerial face only after the Punjab Assembly elections, due early next year.
Channi supporters disrupt Congress meetings
The disruption began in Patiala soon after Warring started addressing party workers. Channi's supporters raised slogans including "Charanjit Singh Channi Zindabad", "Channi Teri Soch Te Pehra Deyange Thok Ke" and "Channi Liyao, Punjab Bachao", briefly bringing the programme to a halt.
A visibly upset Warring repeatedly appealed to workers to maintain discipline and allow the meeting to continue but the slogan shouting persisted for some time before proceedings resumed.Senior Congress leaders, including Baghel, MP Amar Singh and Brahm Mohindra, witnessed the developments while other leaders attempted to calm the workers.
Similar scenes unfolded later in Sangrur, where another group of Channi supporters raised slogans in favour of the former chief minister and against Baghel. Tensions escalated after some of Channi's supporters clashed verbally with other Congress workers.
One supporter demanded that the Jalandhar MP be declared the Congress' chief ministerial face, claiming it reflected the wishes of party workers.However, Warring dismissed suggestions that Channi had orchestrated the protests."Channi did not send these people. He is our crown," Warring said in Sangrur, while alleging that the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) had sent people to disrupt the Congress programme.
Baghel says CM face will be decided after polls
Addressing party workers, Baghel urged leaders to remain united and focus on defeating the ruling AAP, the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal instead of engaging in internal rivalries.He made it clear that the Congress leadership, including party president Mallikarjun Kharge and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, would decide the chief ministerial candidate and ministers only after the Assembly elections."Smaller differences are part of every party which can be sorted out for the bigger battle that the Congress has to fight against AAP, BJP and Akalis," Baghel said.He expressed confidence that the Congress would emerge stronger in the Assembly elections because everyone shared the common objective of bringing the party back to power in Punjab.Baghel also underlined the importance of strengthening the party at the booth level, saying a strong grassroots organisation would be key to electoral success.
Warning on indiscipline
Later, speaking to reporters in Patiala, Baghel issued a stern warning against indiscipline."Whosoever indulges in indiscipline will be shown the door from the party irrespective of the position one holds," he said, citing the earlier expulsion of Navjot Kaur Sidhu as an example.
When asked whether the party would initiate action against Channi, Baghel responded by asking what mistake the former chief minister had committed.Warring, meanwhile, announced that former MLA Madan Lal Jalalpur had been suspended for remarks against senior Congress leaders.Rejecting reports that some leaders had stayed away from district committee meetings, Baghel said all leaders had been informed about the programmes and were participating as their schedules permitted.
Warring stresses organisation over individuals
In his address, Warring stressed that no leader, regardless of popularity, could win elections without a strong organisational structure.He cited the example of late Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala, saying that despite his immense popularity, he lost the 2022 Assembly election by over 60,000 votes because of inadequate booth-level management.Warring also said his only wish was to see a Congress chief minister and ministers taking oath after the next Assembly elections, adding that he would be happy to watch the swearing-in ceremony from the audience.He described senior leaders including Channi, Partap Singh Bajwa, Rajinder Kaur Bhattal and Brahm Mohindra as more experienced and capable than himself, and assured workers that all senior leaders would soon be seen sharing one platform ahead of the polls.
The latest developments indicate continuing factionalism within the Punjab Congress despite repeated assurances from the party leadership that organisational unity is being strengthened ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.Baghel is currently touring the poll-bound state as part of the 'Har Booth, Congress Mazboot' campaign, meeting district and block-level leaders after launching the initiative in Fatehgarh Sahib and Mohali on Friday.Baghel had earlier dismissed reports of factionalism, claiming that the media and a few individuals were creating a perception of infighting.However, discontent within the state unit has continued since the Congress retained Amarinder Singh Raja Warring as Punjab Congress president while appointing Channi as chairman of the campaign committee.A section of leaders led by Channi and Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa had opposed Warring's continuation as state chief and sought his removal.

NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday announced that all pending applications for citizenship under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) in the state would be disposed of within the next six months, asserting that the law was enacted to grant citizenship and not to take it away.Speaking at a CAA citizenship certificate distribution programme in New Town, where around 300 members of the Matua community from North 24 Parganas district received citizenship certificates, Adhikari alleged that the previous Trinamool Congress (TMC) government had spread misinformation about the law for "political gains"."The CAA is meant to grant citizenship, not to take away anyone's citizenship," Adhikari said, as quoted by news agency PTI.He urged all eligible applicants to come forward and apply under the Act, saying more citizenship certificates would be issued in the coming months.
Nearly 24,000 citizenship certificates issued so far
Presenting the state's progress in implementing the CAA, Adhikari said 23,956 citizenship certificates had been issued so far, including 5,966 certificates over the past 11 weeks since the BJP government assumed office.According to him, the state has received 2,30,605 applications under the CAA.
He said Nadia district has recorded the highest number of beneficiaries with 10,191 citizenship certificates, followed by North 24 Parganas with 8,930 certificates.Adhikari also said that, following discussions with the Union home secretary, the process of delegating legal and administrative powers to district magistrates for the speedy disposal of CAA applications is expected to begin within a month."Following discussions with the Union home secretary, the process of delegating legal and administrative powers to district magistrates for the speedy disposal of CAA applications is expected to begin within a month," he said.He noted that district magistrates in Gujarat and Rajasthan already exercise such powers.
'CAA was never meant to target anyone'
The chief minister reiterated that the Citizenship (Amendment) Act was introduced to grant Indian citizenship to eligible refugees and not to deprive anyone of their rights.The CAA, passed by Parliament in 2019, provides a pathway to Indian citizenship for Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians who fled religious persecution in Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan and entered India on or before December 31, 2014.Recalling the BJP's promise on citizenship, Adhikari said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had assured members of the Matua community before the 2019 Lok Sabha elections that eligible refugees from Bangladesh would receive Indian citizenship.He said the rules under the Act were eventually notified on March 6, 2024, after implementation was delayed due to the Covid-19 pandemic.
TMC accused of spreading confusion over CAA
Targeting the previous TMC government, Adhikari alleged that it deliberately equated the CAA with the National Register of Citizens (NRC), creating confusion among people, particularly Muslims."The previous government projected the CAA as the NRC and misled the people, particularly the Muslim community. False propaganda was spread claiming that applying under the CAA would result in the loss of jobs, ration benefits or the Lakshmir Bhandar financial assistance scheme," he alleged.He claimed that government property had been vandalised during protests triggered by such misinformation and said, "Today, the truth has come out, and even MLAs from the opposition have attended this government programme voluntarily."
Government to assist beneficiaries
Adhikari said the state government would take steps to help eligible CAA beneficiaries who continue to face legal proceedings or remain in jail because of documentation-related issues by facilitating their release on bail.He added that the state police had been instructed to ensure that no eligible applicant faced harassment in matters related to the CAA.The state government will also facilitate the inclusion of beneficiaries' names in electoral rolls after citizenship is granted and ensure that eligible applicants receive Scheduled Caste certificates in a time-bound manner.One of the beneficiaries, a woman refugee originally from Bagerhat in Bangladesh, thanked the government after receiving her citizenship certificate."I lived in Bagerhat in Bangladesh and came to India in 2006. I had been living in fear for so many years. I thank the Prime Minister and the chief minister," she said, as cited by PTI.
The announcement comes as West Bengal began the self-enumeration phase of the country's 16th Census.Adhikari had said the Census exercise and illegal immigration were separate issues, while distinguishing between illegal immigrants and refugees covered under the CAA.He had maintained that refugees eligible under the CAA would be protected, while illegal immigrants would not be entitled to government welfare benefits.He also said the Census would help create a permanent database for delivering government welfare schemes more efficiently.

NEW DELHI: National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah on Saturday questioned the timing of the terrorist attack on two migrant labourers in Kulgam, asking why such incidents occur whenever his party demands the restoration of statehood for Jammu and Kashmir.The NC had staged a protest in Delhi on July 20, demanding the restoration of statehood for Jammu and Kashmir.âI regret it. We do not even know who killed them or how they were killed. There should be an investigation, a fair probe to identify those responsible,â Abdullah told reporters in north Kashmir's Baramulla district, according to PTI.

Why do they travel so far? Because, perhaps, there is no employment for them back home. They find work here in Kashmir, yet they are being gunned down like this. I have no words to condemn this incident," Mufti said in Srinagar."I believe there is a lapse in security somewhere. I request that the local government should provide compensation to these victims, in addition to whatever compensation their home state provides. A proper investigation must be conducted... The government needs to examine where the lapses are occurringâhow militants managed to come in and kill two unarmed individuals despite the presence of the Army, CRPF and police," she added.

A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Vipul M Pancholi quashed the order of Rajasthan High Court which had held that a wife cannot be denied interim maintenance during pendency of the husbandâs application
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday ruled that a wife cannot be granted interim maintenance if an allegation of adultery is made against her which, at first glance, looks true.A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Vipul M Pancholi quashed the order of the Rajasthan High Court which had held that a wife cannot be denied interim maintenance during pendency of the husbandâs application under Section 125(4) of the Criminal Procedure Code relating to adultery. It allowed the plea of a husband who approached the court through lawyer Prabhjit Jauhar against the orders of a trial court and HC rejecting his plea to examine allegations of adultery before granting interim maintenance.âIt is obvious that when a case is sought to be proved by circumstantial evidence, it requires a detailed study of the circumstances presented. The evidence furnished in support thereof, including verification, particularly when the evidence in question is electronic, etc. These procedures are bound to take time. Since the stipulation in Section 125 (4) is that if adultery is proved, the wife would neither be entitled to interim nor final maintenance, we are of the view that if a husband files an application under Section 125(4) and is, at the first instance, able to establish the charge through evidence ex facie, then only, there can be said to be a bar to interim maintenance,â the bench said.
It added that the trial court and HC clearly fell into error to hold that it was only at the stage of final adjudication that such a question could be decided. âThis view would render otiose what has been provided in the statute,â it said.Section 125(4) says that no wife shall be entitled to receive an allowance for maintenance or interim maintenance and expenses of proceedings, as the case may be, from her husband if she is living in adultery, or if, without any sufficient reason, she refuses to live with her husband, or if they are living separately by mutual consent.
âIf the application for maintenance is to be denied at the interim stage itself, the party having filed the application under Section 125(4) must present clear and cogent evidence that would ex-facie establish adultery on the part of the claimant for maintenance,â the bench said.Noting that the husband in the case has placed a large number of photographs and 92 videos to substantiate his allegation against the wife, the court said they were perhaps procured from a private detective and expressed the need to frame a law to regulate the sector as there was an increasing reliance on private investigators to gather information.âWe believe that regulation and accountability are equally important in the sphere of private investigation,â it said

full_text:
The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) has recently decided that the criteria for bidders to procure medical supplies for the three major hospitals here.
The TTD governs the administration of the Sri Balaji Institute of Surgery, Research, and Rehabilitation for the Disabled (BIRRD), the Sri Venkateswara Institute of Medical Sciences (SVIMS), and the Sri Padmavathi Children’s Heart Centre (SPCHC), all located in Tirupati, and offers exclusive, specialised medical care.
While reviewing the tender process, the TTD authorities found that the existing eligibility for procurement of medicines, injections, medical and surgical consumables, in terms of the minimum annual turnover for manufacturers, authorised distributors and importers has been on the higher side. The authorities also found the criterion to be restrictive, due to which the number of participants from eligible bidders remained “limited”, thus affecting competition and efficiency.
Revised cap
The committee was reconstituted to review the criteria met on July 3 under the Chairmanship of the BIRRD Director. The committee unanimously recommended revising the eligibility criteria for the minimum average annual turnover, currently capped at ₹100 crore, to ₹25 crore for the procurement of medicines and injections, and ₹15 crore for surgical and medical consumables for the laboratories and blood bank.
The panel recommended to the TTD trust board to continue the multi-vendor procurement system, which enables procurement from the willing L2 and L3 bidders at the rates quoted by and approved for the L1 bidder. This system provides relief to the TTD in case of a supply failure by the L1. The committee’s proposals were approved by the TTD’s trust board at its meeting held on July 14.

Members of the Indian diaspora in China raised concerns over abusive anti-India content on Chinese social media, declining work visas for professionals, and restrictions on employment for spouses at the Indian Embassy’s first Open House in recent years.

Indian Ambassador Vikram Doraiswami, accompanied by Counsellor (Consular, Education and Community Affairs) Nitinjeet Singh and Counsellor (Visa) Ramesh Singh, interacted with members of the diaspora on a range of issues.

Mr. Doraiswami, who assumed charge in May and has stepped up engagements with Chinese officials as part of efforts to improve bilateral ties, said the embassy would further simplify the documentation required for Chinese nationals applying for Indian visas from next week to facilitate greater travel to India.
Responding to concerns over negative and abusive content on Chinese social media, he said the Chinese government is also concerned about the rise in such content and is taking steps to address the issue.
On its part, the embassy is countering misinformation by disseminating fact-based information through its social media handles, Mr. Doraiswami said.
The ambassador also said the embassy planned to organise more cultural events, building on the huge response to annual programmes such as the Vasant Mela, to showcase India’s diverse culture and cuisine.
The mission is also working to establish a mechanism with legal professionals to assist Indians facing work-related issues, he said.
To improve consular services for the Indian diaspora, the embassy plans to hold Open House interactions periodically to address their concerns, Mr. Doraiswami said.

During the verification process, bank officials allegedly detected 10 counterfeit ₹500 notes in the cash remittance.

full_text:
Stand-up comedian Kunal Kamra has cancelled his scheduled shows from Monday to Thursday at a venue in Whitefield and shifted them to another venue in Koramangala.
The development comes after a Hindutva outfit, Hindu Rashtra Samanvaya Samiti, petitioned the Whitefield police, demanding that Mr. Kamra should not be permitted to perform.
They had contended that Mr. Kamra had disrespected Hindu deities.
A senior police official from the Whitefield Division told The Hindu that Mr. Kamra and the organisers of the shows visited the Whitefield Police Station on Sunday and informed that they had decided to cancel the shows. The decision, they said, was taken as the event had become controversial. No law and order incident was reported in connection with the scheduled performance.
Taking to social media platform X, Mr. Kamra on Sunday announced: “Shows for Monday - Tuesday - Wednesday - Thursday shifted to Underground Comedy Club in Koramangala.”
He further said that amount would be refunded to those who had already booked tickets for the Whitefield shows and requested them to book shows at the Koramangala venue afresh.
On Saturday, responding to the Hindutva activists objecting to his shows in Whitefield, Mr. Kamra gave an open invite on X that he would be at the Whitefield Police Station on Sunday to seek permission to perform and any objectors were free to join him to debate on “comedy and culture”. He later said only senior journalist Aakar Patel turned up.
Meanwhile, Mohan Gowda, spokesperson, Hindu Janajagruti Samiti, said that Mr. Kamra shifted the shows after facing strong opposition and appealed to the Koramangala police not to allow him to perform in their jurisdiction.
Sources in the government said that the shows would be not stopped.

However, Kannada Chaluvali leader Vatal Nagaraj, who is leading the protest, said the bandh will be held as planned.
At an all-party meeting, the Chief Minister said Karnataka is carefully assessing the Cauvery situation, including the petition of the DMK in the Supreme Court. A limited quantity of water is being released from the reservoirs in the light of rain, he said.
The meeting had been convened to address the concerns over the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA)’s directive to the State to abide by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee’s order to release 3,500 cubic metres daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days. The order set off protests in parts of Karnataka.
“(Four) reservoirs in the Cauvery basin are cumulatively receiving about 68,000 cusecs of water. Our dams were not full since there was no rain. There has been some rain (now) and the situation has become slightly better. Kabini (reservoir) is full,” he told presspersons here after the all-party meeting.
The data shared by the Water Resources Department shows that Karnataka was releasing water at the rate of 25,000 cusecs from the Kabini reservoir and 1,819 cusecs from the Krishna Raja Sagar on Sunday to Tamil Nadu.
The Chief Minister said: “We are releasing a limited quantity of water through canals only to fill lakes and tanks meant for drinking water purposes, and not for irrigation.”
‘Mekedatu is the solution’
Reiterating that the proposed Mekedatu project on the Cauvery is the long-term solution to the problems faced by both the States, he said, “Karnataka will respect the law and orders of the Supreme Court while protecting the State’s interest.”
On the petition filed by the DMK in the Supreme Court, Mr. Shivakumar said: “We are closely watching the situation. Individual petitions of political parties and organisations are treated differently. We have to utilise our experience and be careful.” He also said that a legal and technical team would fight the State’s case.
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joesph Vijay has agreed to postpone his visit to Bengaluru to discuss the Cauvery issue on the request of the Karnataka government, he said. “Mr. Vijay intended to hold talks, but the meeting has been deferred. I requested from him that we meet later when a cordial atmosphere prevails. I do not want anyone shouting slogans against my friends. We should respect each other. We have to live together and work together. Ultimately, India is one,” said the Karnataka Chief Minister.
Asked if he would be able to convince Mr. Vijay of the situation, he said: “We will make him understand (the situation) and he will understand. Though he is new to politics, he is courageous. Whatever our political differences may be, he wanted to come to Karnataka.”

When the government is standing with you and nature is also with you, bandh is of no use. It will affect our schools and businesses. Ultimately, it will not help us. We are committed to farmers’ welfare and bound to protect the State's interest,” the Chief Minister said. “They [Opposition leaders] have pledged their support to the Government and have provided valuable suggestions. We will take the suggestions that will be discussed with the legal team before moving forward.”
However, in Mysuru, former MLA Vatal Nagaraj said the bandh had not been called on one issue. “More than 2,000 Kannada organisations have extended support to the bandh. Educational institutions, film chambers and hotel industries, among others, have extended support. There is no question of withdrawing the bandh.”

The water level in the KRS and Kabini reservoirs in the Cauvery basin continued to rise on Sunday as the dams recorded heavy inflows following widespread rainfall in their catchment areas.
While the water level in the KRS reservoir was inching towards the 100-ft. mark, reaching 98.8 ft. against its Full Reservoir Level of 124.8 ft. on Sunday evening, the reservoir was receiving an inflow of 31,583 cusecs. The Kabini reservoir, meanwhile, had almost reached its maximum level.
According to a bulletin issued by the authorities, the water level in the Kabini reservoir stood at 2,282.43 ft. (above mean sea level) against its maximum level of 2,284 ft., with an inflow of 27,217 cusecs on Sunday.
Discharge from Kabini
The authorities were releasing 25,000 cusecs of water into the river through the four crest gates of the Kabini dam on Sunday. About 2,000 cusecs of water is being released into the canal system, the bulletin said.
The increased discharge from the reservoir submerged a low-level bridge near the dam while cutting off connectivity to a few villages in the vicinity.
The Irrigation Department had issued a flood warning on Saturday, advising residents of low-lying areas downstream of the river to take precautionary measures in view of the increased discharge from the dam.
Meanwhile, the rainfall in Kodagu district, the catchment area of the KRS reservoir, which had received heavy showers on Friday and Saturday, showed signs of easing on Sunday.
However, with the Cauvery in spate, the road connecting Karigodu and Chikkanahalli villages in Ammathi hobli of Virajpet taluk was submerged. The authorities cautioned the public against using the road and advised them to take alternative routes.
The water level at the Triveni Sangama in Bhagamandala also rose, the authorities said.
The water level in the Harangi reservoir stood at 2,856.72 ft. (above mean sea level) against its maximum level of 2,859 ft., with an inflow of 10,440 cusecs. The authorities had reduced the discharge from the reservoir from 14,470 cusecs at 8 a.m. to 9,500 cusecs at 8 p.m. on Sunday.

full_text:
Some confusion during the police constable recruitment examination at Sharadamba PU College in Tikota, Vijayapura district, led to a protests by several aspirants. They alleged irregularities in the distribution of question papers and OMR sheets. Many candidates walked out of the examination centre and demanded that the test be conducted again.
Candidates alleged that the question papers, scheduled to be distributed at 10.30 a.m., were handed over nearly 30 minutes late. They also claimed that there was a mismatch between the serial numbers on the question papers and OMR sheets. According to the aspirants, the distribution process varied across classrooms, with some receiving question papers before OMR sheets and others facing the opposite situation, leading to widespread confusion.
Following the disruption, candidates boycotted the examination and staged a protest outside the centre, raising slogans against the Karnataka government. Some aspirants broke down in tears, saying it was their final opportunity to appear for the recruitment exam after preparing for the past two to three years. They urged the government and the Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) to conduct a re-examination, claiming that the confusion had put their futures at risk.
Vijayapura Deputy Commissioner Anandh K., Superintendent of Police Laxman Nimbargi and other officials visited the examination centre to assess the situation. While some candidates continued writing the examination, many others refused to return and reiterated their demand for a fresh test.
Responding to the allegations, Dr. Anandh said Sharadamba PU College was one of the 61 examination centres in the district and that the examination was conducted as per the KEA’s Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). He clarified that there is no requirement for the serial numbers on the question paper and OMR sheet to match, and candidates only needed to correctly mention the question paper version code and their registration number on the OMR sheet.
The Deputy Commissioner said that similar confusion was reported at a few other examination centres, but most candidates resumed writing the examination after supervisors explained the procedure. He added that candidates who walked out carrying question papers and OMR sheets had violated KEA rules and were therefore not allowed to re-enter the examination hall. Around 115 candidates appeared for the examination at the Tikota centre.

A 35-year-old school teacher, whose family had earlier suffered substantial financial losses in cyberfraud, has once again fallen victim to online scamsters, losing ₹45 lakh in a fake investment scheme while attempting to recover her family’s financial losses.
According to a complaint lodged with the East CEN Police, the teacher, a resident of Kamaraj Road, stated that her husband had previously been cheated in cyberfraud, leaving the family under heavy debt. To repay the earlier losses, they had availed a gold loan and were searching for investment opportunities that promised better returns.
In November 2025, the couple came across an online investment application through social media. The operators of the application assured them of exceptionally high returns. Believing the claims, the couple obtained additional personal loans and transferred money from the husband’s bank account to various beneficiary accounts specified by the fraudsters.
Between November 2025 and February 20, 2026, they allegedly transferred ₹45,00,000. When they later attempted to withdraw their investment and promised profits, they found themselves unable to access the application, while all contact numbers of the operators had been switched off or blocked.
Realising that they had been cheated, they registered a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. However, the complainant stated that due to mental stress and work pressure, she could not approach the police immediately to lodge a formal complaint.
Based on her complaint, the police registered a case on Friday and initiated a probe to identify the fraudsters, trace the money trail, and take appropriate legal action.
Further investigation is under way.
The case serves as a reminder that cybercriminals often target victims with promises of unrealistic returns, and even individuals who have previously experienced online fraud can become victims again when attempting to recover earlier financial losses, a senior cybercrime investigator said.

“The main innovation is the preparation of the material itself. It is a multifunctional catalyst that combines acidic and redox (reduction-oxidation) properties in a single material, making it more efficient than conventional catalysts,” he said.
According to the researchers, conventional catalysts generally perform only one function, limiting their efficiency. The newly developed catalyst integrates multiple functions enabling chemical reactions to proceed more effectively while improving access to active sites within the material.
The technology is expected to find future applications in the petroleum and petrochemical industries, particularly in the production of cleaner fuels, fuel additives, polymers and other value-added chemicals. Prof. Sakthivel said the research had so far focused on developing and patenting the catalyst material, and commercial fuel production using the technology was yet to begin.

full_text:
Though Wayanad has witnessed heavy rain over the past few days, cumulative southwest monsoon rainfall in the hill district remains around 50% below normal after the first two months of the season.
Data released by the Hume Weather Lab of the Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology shows that Wayanad received only 802 mm of average rainfall between June 1 and July 31, against the India Meteorological department (IMD) normal of 1,600 mm for the period.
This year, the onset of the southwest monsoon was delayed, a phenomenon experts attributed to the combined influence of global climate change and the El Niño phenomenon.
“The recent spell of heavy rain has, however, brought some relief. Between July 27 and 31 (five days), Wayanad recorded 199 mm of rainfall, accounting for nearly 25% of the total rainfall received during the past two months. The prevailing wet spell is expected to continue until August 4,” said C.K. Vishnudas, executive director of the Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology.
Rainfall distribution across the district has remained highly uneven. Lakkidi recorded the highest rainfall at 2,548 mm, while Muthanga received the least at just 228 mm. After being on tenterhooks for the past 24 hours, Pathanamthitta finally got some respite on Sunday as floodwaters began receding from several inundated areas, offering relief to thousands affected by the deluge. However, the Upper Kuttanad region continued to bear the brunt of the rain fury, with rising waters forcing more evacuations and disrupting normal life.
Water levels in major rivers, including the Pamba, Achankovil and Manimala rivers, started receding as residents in the upper reaches began returning home. In Ranni, one of the worst-affected areas in the district, the flood situation improved considerably, allowing residents and traders to begin the recovery process. Shop owners were seen removing water-damaged goods from their establishments, with traders estimating losses running into several crores of rupees.
The floodwaters in Aranmula also began to recede, while authorities continued to urge people living in vulnerable areas to remain vigilant. The storage position in major reservoirs remained comfortable, with the live storage level in the Pamba reservoir at 35.47% and the Kakki dam at 44.11%.
However, as water receded from the upper reaches, the runoff entered the low-lying Upper Kuttanad region, inundating several houses and triggering a large-scale evacuation drive. Water levels continued to rise through the day in parts of the region, even as more people were shifted to relief camps.
Floodwaters from the Pamba and Manimala rivers spilled onto the Thiruvalla–Ambalappuzha State Highway around 1 a.m., inundating roads, houses, commercial establishments and places of worship. The Nedumpram stretch, which is prone to flooding during intense rain spells, witnessed major disruption to traffic movement.
KSRTC suspended services through the waterlogged stretch at Nedumpram. Buses from the Alappuzha, Edathua and Haripad depots operated only up to Chakkulathukavu Junction, while services from Thiruvalla were curtailed at Vaikkathillam Bridge.
Traffic on the Thiruvalla–Ambalappuzha State Highway came to a standstill after nearly 1.5 km of the road, from Padarattilpadi to NC Junction at Nedumpram, was submerged.
As of Sunday evening, the district had 95 relief camps sheltering 3,568 people. Thiruvalla taluk, which includes parts of the Upper Kuttanad region, accounted for the highest number of camps at 47. A detailed assessment is under way to ascertain the extent of damage to houses and property. Authorities have also issued orders to clear flood debris. Preliminary estimates indicate that one house was completely damaged, while 42 houses suffered partial damage.
In view of the continuing heavy rain and flooding, District Collector A. Nizamudeen declared a holiday for all educational institutions in Pathanamthitta, from anganwadis to professional colleges, as well as tuition centres, on Monday. The holiday will not apply to scheduled public and university examinations.
The Travancore Devaswom Board has also issued an advisory urging Sabarimala pilgrims to exercise extreme caution, considering the prevailing weather conditions.

Sugathan, who was arrested under the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (KAAPA) and is currently lodged at the high-security correctional facility at Viyyur Central Prison in Thrissur.
The letter, dated July 20, 2026 and signed by an Under Secretary on behalf of the Additional Chief Secretary, was sent to Mr. Sugathan in response to his request for an escort parole to take part in the council meeting on Friday (July 31). However, it is not right for any official to add to the report we had signed on. In case such additions are made, it has to come back to us. However, in this case, the report went to the Home department after the official made the addition. Such conduct cannot be allowed. On Monday, we will take decisive action on this,” said Mr. Shaji.
Earlier, Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala had also expressed dissatisfaction at the letter, dated July 20, 2026, which was signed by an Under Secretary on behalf of the Additional Chief Secretary, Home department. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] State secretariat said in a statement on Sunday that the Chief Minister, who also heads the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority, should not stand aside and delegate responsibility to Ministers.
“The primary duty of an administrator is to protect the lives and property of the people. Not fulfilling that can only be seen as a defiant attitude towards the public. Pathanamthitta and Idukki districts, which received the most rainfall, had only an orange alert until Saturday morning. The fact that many areas were under water by the time the red alert was announced is evidence of mismanagement. No steps were taken to relocate people to safe places and evacuate them from danger-prone areas,” said the CPI(M).
The CPI(M) alleged that the Coastal Police arrived 13 hours late to rescue the fishermen whose boat capsized near Muthalapozhi in Thiruvananthapuram. The State rented the helicopter to use it for disaster-relief activities and in times of need. The then Leader of the Opposition who criticised the LDF government when it rented the helicopter and called it wasteful expenditure is now using it for private purposes,” said the CPI(M).
Don’t politicise: MLA
Congress MLA C. Noushad Ali of Ponnani said such issues should not be politicised to target the Chief Minister during times of disaster. “Shouldn’t the Chief Minister go anywhere or have food during the rainy season? Contrasting Mr. Satheesan’s conduct during the flood with that of Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan during his term as the Chief Minister, the CPI(M) said Mr. Vijayan and his office had stayed vigilant round-the-clock, coordinating rescue efforts.

Through this, it was possible to give confidence to the people and also make them alert,” said the CPI(M).
‘No warnings’

Traders did not even get time to secure the goods in their shops. The negligence in the relief camps is also worrying. The government agencies themselves have admitted that there was a lapse in food distribution. Due to the lack of coordination by the officials, volunteers, local people and political activists had to prepare and distribute the food. The government should also examine the lapses and prevent them from recurring,” said Mr. Vijayan.

The death toll in rainfall-related incidents in Kerala rose to 11 by Sunday, even as more than 7,600 people were evacuated to relief camps across the State, the State government said.
Rain lashed most districts in Kerala on Sunday as well, although the intensity had come down when compared to Saturday, enabling government agencies to step up relief operations. Four people have died so far in Malappuram district, two each in Thiruvananthapuram, Alappuzha and Idukki and one in Kozhikode, Revenue Minister A.P. Anilkumar said in a Sunday evening update on rescue and relief operations. Search operations also continued on Sunday for people who have been reported missing in various districts.
Populated regions, including towns in central Kerala, remained heavily waterlogged, disrupting normal life and causing heavy damage to property. Across Kerala, 7,674 people have been temporarily resettled in 273 camps. Mr. Anilkumar said the camps have been provided drinking water, food and medical facilities. Steps are being taken to prevent the spread of epidemics. Pathanamthitta district has the highest number of camps (75), followed by Kottayam (64), Kozhikode (36), Wayanad (28), Kannur (18), Alappuzha (14), Idukki (13), Ernakulam (7) and Thrissur and Kasaragod (6 each). Thirty houses have been destroyed in the rain havoc so far while 293 have been reported damaged. All districts except Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam were on orange alert on Sunday.
Holiday in 10 districts
Rescue and relief operations are progressing under the National and State Disaster Response Forces, the Fire and Rescue Services and the State Police. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has placed all 14 districts on yellow alert for isolated heavy rainfall on Monday. As a precaution, holiday has been declared for educational institutions in the districts of Kasaragod, Kannur, Kozhikode, Malappuram, Palakkad, Wayanad, Thrissur, Idukki, Kottayam and Pathanamthitta. In Alappuzha district, Monday will be a holiday for schools doubling as relief camps and for all educational institutions in Chengannur and Kuttanad taluks. In Ernakulam district, Monday will be a holiday in Kothamangalam and Muvattupuzha taluks.
The IMD has not issued heavy rainfall alerts for Tuesday and Wednesday, but northern districts are likely to receive isolated heavy rainfall by Thursday.
Curb on tourism
The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) has directed the District Tourism Promotion Councils to regulate tourism-related activities linked to waterfalls and waterbodies and tourist spots along the high ranges.
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, in a Facebook post on Sunday, asked the people, especially residents of high ranges, to remain alert. Sanitation works have been launched in regions where the floodwaters have receded, he said. He assured the public of all support from the government machinery in tackling the crisis.
Meanwhile, the CPI(M) State secretariat accused the UDF government of lapses in evacuating people from the vulnerable areas of the State. The CPI(M) urged Mr. Satheesan to “comprehend the gravity of the situation and perform his duty to help the people.” The State secretariat also urged all party units to actively assist the people by becoming part of the relief operations.

Professor M.K. Sanoo had never believed that continuous rule by a political front would be dangerous, Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan said here on Sunday (August 2, 2026) in a veiled attack on cultural figures who had warned against the Left Democratic Front (LDF) retaining power in the State. He added that Sanoo was someone who never attempted to enhance his image by tarnishing the Left front.
He was inaugurating a commemorative meeting on the first death anniversary of the renowned Malayalam literary critic, orator, and former MLA, organised by the Prof. M.K. Sanoo Master Samskarika Kendram.
“One may receive applause and greater public acceptance if one criticises the Left from within the fold. Sanoo Master was well aware of his position in people’s minds and knew that he did not have to resort to such fake methods to improve his public image. Those who lacked such self-awareness had to adopt other stances,” Mr. Vijayan said.
In what sounded like a veiled criticism of former Kerala Sahitya Akademi president K. Satchidanandan, Mr. Vijayan recalled how gracefully Sanoo had occupied the same position during an earlier tenure of the LDF. Mr. Satchidanandan’s comments cautioning against a prolonged, continuous rule by the LDF had sparked a major political controversy ahead of the Assembly elections.
Earlier in the day, Mr. Vijayan presented the maiden ‘Sanoo Sammanam’, instituted by the Samskarika Kendram, to Malayalam literary stalwart M. Leelavathy at her home in Thrikkakara. Receiving the lifetime achievement award, which carries ₹1 lakh, a statuette and a certificate, Ms. Leelavathy said she had mixed feelings about the honour. “I’m deeply pained to receive the award instituted in the name of a long-time colleague in his absence. At the same time, I’m glad to receive it as a blessing from him, considering the deep friendship we shared,” she said. Ms. Leelavathy announced that she would donate the cash award to Kanivu Pain and Palliative Care. The Sanoo Sammanam Yuvaprathibha Puraskaram was presented to historian Vinil Paul at the event. Writer N.S. Madhavan chaired the meeting.
CPI(M) leaders P. Rajeeve, C.N. Mohanan, S. Sharma, C.M. Dinesh Mani, S. Sathish and M. Anilkumar, writers Sunil P. Elayidom and Thanooja Bhattathiri, and journalist R. Rajagopal were among those who spoke.

Heavy rain continued to batter Kannur and Kasaragod districts on Sunday (August 2, 2026), inundating low-lying areas, triggering landslips, disrupting road traffic and forcing hundreds of people to evacuate to relief camps.
In Kannur, heavy rain affected 32 villages. One person died, two people, including a rescue volunteer, went missing after being swept away by swollen rivers, and one person was injured. The deceased was identified as Rareesh of Kalashparambath.
Four landslips were reported and 47 houses sustained partial damage. According to the district administration, 905 people were staying in 18 relief camps, while Iritty taluk remained the worst affected. A major landslip at Chekuthan Thodu near Palchuram in Kottiyoor blocked the road after huge boulders fell onto the carriageway.
Several areas remained cut off after bridges were submerged. Floodwaters entered houses in Peratta, Pulittattu and Aralam, forcing dozens of families into relief camps. The Palappura bridge at Murukunnu, the Vattiyamthodu bridge, the Manikkadavu Chappath bridge and several other crossings were submerged. Compound walls and houses were damaged in Thalassery, Panappuzha and other places due to landslips and heavy rain.
Amid the threat of further landslides, District Collector P. Vishnuraj ordered the closure of the Boys Town-Palchuram road connecting Kannur and Wayanad. Traffic was diverted at Kottiyoor and Boys Town.
Meanwhile, CPI(M) Kannur district secretary K.K. Ragesh urged the State government to step up emergency intervention in the rain-hit high-range areas of the district.
He claimed that rescue operations in many areas were being carried out largely by local residents and youth organisations, and alleged that Fire and Rescue Services personnel had yet to reach some of the affected areas. He also called for the immediate restoration of damaged roads and snapped power lines.
In Kasaragod
In Kasaragod, heavy rain continued to cause widespread disruption, though no deaths or missing persons were reported. Two landslips were reported at Thayyeni in Pallavayal village and Kattamkavala in Maloth village, while four houses sustained partial damage at Kurinji in Panthady village, Ujjampady in Delampady village, and in Padre and Bayar villages.
As a precaution, the district administration shifted residents from vulnerable areas to safer locations. Six relief camps were sheltering 325 people, including 132 men, 143 women and 50 children.
The district administrations urged the public to remain vigilant, avoid vulnerable areas and strictly follow official advisories as heavy rain and the threat of landslides persisted.
In Wayanad
Though Wayanad heaved a sigh of relief as the heavy downpour eased on Sunday, many parts of the district were yet to fully recover from the continuous showers of the past few days.
Authorities opened more relief camps and shifted people from flood- and landslide-prone areas of the district. As of Sunday evening, 1,328 people from 414 families had been moved to 28 camps. Of the total, 15 camps were functioning in Vythiri taluk, 10 in Mananthavady and three in Sultan Bathery.
Meanwhile, in view of the prevailing situation, District Collector D.R. Meghashree declared a holiday for all educational institutions in the district on Monday (August 3).

full_text:
As relief and rehabilitation efforts continue across flood-ravaged Pathanamthitta, the focus is rapidly shifting from rescue to accountability, with allegations of administrative lapses and poor disaster management dominating the political discourse.
The sharpest criticism came from CPI(M) Pathanamthitta district secretary Raju Abraham, who described the deluge as a `government-sponsored flood’. He accused the authorities of failing to issue timely red alerts and opening dam shutters without adequate public warning, and demanded compensation for all those who suffered losses.
“The authorities neither issued a proper red alert nor gave advance warning before opening the dam shutters. The lack of timely information from both the government and weather monitoring agencies caused widespread anxiety among the public and resulted in losses worth crores,” he alleged.
According to Mr.Abraham,the Moozhiyar and Kariyarkayam dams were opened at 1 a.m. Under the existing protocol, the authorities are required to inform elected representatives, local self-government institutions and the Public Relations Department before releasing water. Public announcements through loudspeakers should also have been made to alert residents. However, the government failed to follow any of these procedures. Had even a public announcement been made, people would have had time to move their belongings to safety and take the necessary precautions, he pointed out.
He also claimed that DYFI volunteers had to undertake cleaning operations because the official response was delayed.
Questions have also been raised over the government’s preparedness and the coordination of relief operations. Residents and public representatives alleged that relief camps lacked basic facilities, flood-hit areas did not receive adequate support and coordination among various departments remained patchy at a time when swift action was crucial.
Taking a serious note of the situation, Aranmula MLA, Abin Varkey urged the government to extend additional assistance to the constituency, saying it was among the worst-hit regions and required greater support. Ranni MLA, Pazhakulam Madhu likened the aftermath of the floods to `a battlefield after the battle’ and said local teams were doing their best with the limited resources at their disposal while appealing for more government assistance. Complaints also surfaced over inadequate facilities at a relief camp in Aranmula.
Even in Ranni, where post-flood cleaning operations were being coordinated under the leadership of the MLA, residents alleged that official support remained inadequate and inter-departmental coordination continued to be poor.
Responding to the criticism, Revenue Minister A.P. Anil Kumar said the government would step up rehabilitation efforts and improve facilities in the coming days. District in-charge Minister P.C. Vishnunath also remained in the district to oversee the relief and rehabilitation work in the flood-affected areas.

Worli MLA and Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray has written to Maharashtra Director General of Police (DGP) Sadanand Date seeking clarity over the first information reports (FIRs) registered against protesting students.
Mr. Thackeray said that the Home Department had said on July 31 that it had decided to withdraw, in accordance with the prescribed legal procedure, the criminal cases/FIRs registered against students, youth, and other individuals who participated in protests held at various places across Maharashtra in support of the demonstration at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi.
“We are continuously being contacted by many students, parents, lawyers, and citizens across the State. There is confusion regarding how the decision will be directly implemented. Many students are still receiving police notices; investigation is underway in some cases; and in many cases, crimes are pending in the court,” Mr. Thackeray wrote in the letter on Saturday (August 1, 2026).
He asked if the benefit that Home Department of the State offered extended to all cases; if police stations would pursue suo motu charges; if the students would have to independently file applications in the court; and if a standard operating procedure had been issued to the police to make sure the cases were withdrawn.
“It is essential that the government’s decision does not remain merely on paper but is implemented uniformly and effectively throughout the State. Students who exercised their democratic right to protest should not suffer unnecessary adverse consequences in their academic, professional, or social lives on account of criminal proceedings,” he emphasised.

The Bombay High Court, on Friday (July 31, 2026), refused to grant urgent bail to Ramesh Mhatre, the corporator accused of assaulting a doctor at a municipal hospital in Dombivli. Mhatre is a member of the Shiv Sena, led by Chief Minister Eknath Shinde.
A division bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Dhuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad made the decision after considering the stage of the police investigation. The court noted that the original complainant, Dr. Vaibhav Salunkhe, has not yet conducted the identification parade to confirm the identity of the accused. Additionally, the police are required to record statements from more witnesses and collect further evidence.
The court has directed the state government to provide protection to the victim, Dr. Salunkhe, and other witnesses involved in the case. The bench clarified that the bail application will be heard next on August 6.
In court, Senior Counsel Aabad Ponda, representing Mhatre, argued for bail. He stated that since his client is currently in custody, there is no possibility of pressuring the victim or witnesses. He also submitted that the investigation is largely complete. Ponda informed the court that Mhatre is willing to stay outside Maharashtra for four to six weeks, if necessary, to prevent any influence on the ongoing inquiry. He requested the court grant bail during the remaining investigation period.
Opposing the bail plea, Senior Counsel S.U. Kamdar, representing the Dodian Medical Association, made a strong case against the relief. Kamdar argued that Mhatre’s actions have created a sense of fear among doctors at the municipal hospital. He further alleged that the accused has a history of securing acquittals in multiple cases by pressuring witnesses. Kamdar also claimed that attempts to exert pressure on the complainant and witnesses are still ongoing.
Meanwhile, Advocate General Milind Sathe, appearing for the State Government, provided the court with the current status of the investigation. He stated that a Deputy Commissioner of Police is now leading the probe following a court order. The investigation has so far recorded statements from 26 individuals. Sathe informed the bench that critical procedures, including recording additional witness statements, collecting voice samples of the accused, and sending the victim’s video evidence for forensic analysis, will be completed in the next two weeks. He also gave an assurance that the identification parade for Dr. Salunkhe will be conducted under police security.

A court has granted bail to five accused in the sexual harassment and forcible conversion case at the Nashik unit of IT major TCS, observing that the chargesheet has been filed and the investigation was practically complete.
Additional Sessions Judge Amit Vinayak Kharkar allowed the pleas of Raza Rafiq Memon, Asif Aftab Ansari, Shahrukh Hussain Shaukat Qureshi, Shafi Bhikan Shaikh and Tausif Bilal Attar on July 30. They were granted bail in connection with multiple FIRs registered at the Mumbai Naka police station in Nashik.
The court also said there was no serious apprehension that the accused would threaten witnesses or tamper with evidence if released.
According to the prosecution, the accused and the victim worked at TCS in Nashik.
The police have alleged that Raza Rafiq Memon made sexually coloured remarks, touched the victim inappropriately, demanded sexual favours, and belittled her religion while glorifying his own. The other accused allegedly supported his actions, it added.
Toxic work environment
The prosecution opposed the bail, saying the accused took undue advantage of the victim's poor financial condition, which forced her to endure a toxic work environment.
However, the defence, represented by advocate Rahul Kasliwal, claimed the alleged remarks, even if taken at face value, were “light hearted banter” in the office.
The court, after hearing both sides, acknowledged that the accused have been behind bars for over three months.
“The chargesheet is filed. Investigation is practically completed. There is no serious apprehension that the accused, if released on bail, would threaten the prosecution witnesses or tamper with the evidence,” the court said.
Conditional bail
The court, while allowing their pleas, imposed several conditions, including visiting the police station every Saturday between 11 a.m. and 4 p.m. until the trial concludes.
They have been prohibited from entering the workplace and residential vicinity of the informant, contacting the informant and witnesses, or any individual associated with the case.
The SIT is probing a total of nine cases registered in connection with the alleged exploitation, attempted forceful conversion, hurting religious sentiments, molestation and mental harassment of female employees at the TCS unit.
TCS has clarified that it has adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards harassment and coercion of any form for a long time, and the employees allegedly involved in sexual harassment at the Nashik office have been suspended.

The internal rift in the Punjab Congress refuses to abate despite efforts by the top party leadership, with supporters of former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi sloganeering at party programmes attended by Bhupesh Baghel, the AICC general secretary in-charge for the State, for the second consecutive day on Sunday (August 2, 2026).
Mr. Channi’s supporters raised slogans at an event in Barnala on Sunday (August 2, 2026). Pro-Channi slogans had disrupted the "Har Booth Congress Mazboot" programmes in Patiala and Sangrur on Saturday (August 1, 2026).
Mr. Baghel, however, said it was time for the Congressmen in Punjab to remain united and fight "the big battle" against the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which were "two sides of the same coin".
At the Barnala event on Sunday (August 2, 2026), a group of partymen started raising slogans in favour of Mr. Channi, briefly interrupting the programme. Punjab Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring urged them to let the meeting continue. "No nara (slogan)," he told them.
Barnala MLA Kuldip Singh Kala Dhillon got down from the stage in a bid to calm down the Channi supporters.
Without naming anyone, Mr. Dhillon said, "In this State, there are five to seven leaders who speak in Delhi and make up their own stories. Sitting at Indira Bhawan in Delhi, they speak about strengthening the Congress. Then they come back and start undermining others (in the State). We need to remain cautious of these people."
Former Minister Razia Sultana called upon the party high command to take strict action against all those who were indulging in indiscipline and damaging the party. She warned that if timely action was not taken, the party could suffer major damage. "Nip the evil in the bud," Ms. Sultana remarked.
The Punjab Congress has been struggling with factionalism, despite repeated assertions by the party leadership that efforts are underway to strengthen organisational unity ahead of the 2027 Punjab elections.
The infighting came to the fore when the Congress leadership on July 1 announced its decision to retain Mr. Warring as the State unit chief, and appointed Jalandhar MP Channi as the chairperson of its campaign committee.
During his address in Barnala, Mr. Baghel said, "The Congress is the only party in the country with internal democracy and takes decisions with consensus. Nobody knows how presidents and conveners are appointed in parties like the BJP and the AAP.”
Mr. Baghel, who is currently on a tour of the poll-bound State, said Punjab would lead the way for Congress's victory at the national level.
"We need to get rid of the BJP government at the Centre and the AAP government in Punjab," he said, adding, "We will start with Punjab. We will throw away the corrupt and incompetent government and bring a people-friendly government instead."
Mr. Warring called upon party workers to come together with discipline and dedication. “No election can be won without making the party strong at the grassroots,” he said.
Mr. Warring pointed out that in 2022, sitting and former Chief Ministers lost elections mainly because the Congress did not focus on micro-management at the grassroots level, despite having done a great job between 2017 and 2022.
Exhorting the party workers, he said that just the way they broke AAP's Barnala citadel in the 2024 bypolls, they should next target to bring down Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's forte in Sangrur.

A 57-year-old man from Kanniyakumari was arrested by Tirupattur Town police on Sunday for stealing cash and mobile phones from a series of shops near the bus terminus in town.
The arrested person was identified as R. Vijayakumar. He has criminal cases against him at Kanniyakumari, Puducherry, Madurai, Cuddalore, and Pudukottai police stations. Initial inquiry revealed that victim G. Santhosh, a resident of Rajapalayam village near Tirupattur town, was running a mobile phone outlet near a bus terminus in town.
The police said that on July 28 when Santhosh opened his shop, he found more than 30 high-end mobile phones and cash ₹50,000 missing. He checked CCTV camera footage that was fixed at the entrance of the outlet and found suspect Vijayakumar in the shop the previous night.
Investigation revealed that suspect Vijayakumar had burgled at least 10 shops in town, including a mechanic outlet, grocery shop and a wholesale rice shop on the same day. The police analysed CCTV camera footage on the route. On being informed, a special police team reached the bus terminus and arrested Vijayakumar. He was arrested and lodged at sub-jail in Tirupattur town. A probe is under way.

full_text:
Water released from the Kabini Dam in Karnataka is expected to reach the Tamil Nadu boundary on Monday (August 3, 2026) and flow into the Mettur Dam by Monday night or Tuesday (August 4), according to Water Resources Department (WRD) officials.
Following heavy rainfall over the past few days in Karnataka, the Karnataka government began releasing Cauvery water from the Kabini Dam on Saturday (August 1). Officials had initially expected the water to reach Tamil Nadu by Sunday (August 2) evening. However, the flow has been delayed as the water is moving slowly through the Cauvery riverbed.
WRD officials at the Mettur Dam said water was first released from the Kabini Dam at 500 cusecs on Saturday (August 1) morning. The discharge was gradually increased to 5,000 cusecs in the afternoon before reaching 25,000 cusecs by Saturday night. They attributed the delay to the dry riverbed, which has absorbed a significant amount of the released water, slowing its downstream movement. As a result, the water is now expected to reach the Mettur Dam on Monday (August 3) night or Tuesday.
“We expect the present discharge of 25,000 cusecs to continue for the next few days. If the Mettur Dam receives 25,000 cusecs of inflow for an entire day, the water level will rise by about four feet. Once the reservoir level crosses 90 feet, the government will decide on releasing water from the dam for delta irrigation,” WRD officials said.
Officials said Tamil Nadu is likely to receive a substantial quantity of Cauvery water only after the Krishna Raja Sagar (KRS) Dam fills up. The dam is yet to reach capacity. At present, the reservoir holds around 20 tmc ft of water against its storage capacity of 49.45 tmc ft.
“If the current spell of rain continues, the KRS Dam is expected to reach capacity within the next 10 days. Thereafter, surplus water from Karnataka is expected to flow into the Mettur Dam,” the officials added.
On Sunday (August 2), the water level at the Mettur Dam stood at 73.33 feet against its full reservoir level of 120 feet. The storage stood at 35.63 tmc ft, compared with the dam’s capacity of 93.47 tmc ft. Inflow into the reservoir increased to 47 cusecs from 42 cusecs, while the discharge for drinking water purposes into the Cauvery river was maintained at 1,500 cusecs.

Southern Railway has dropped departmental action contemplated against motorman K. Karunakaran, who flagged a major safety issue between Ambattur and Avadi railway stations here on March 5, 2026, and rewarded him for the good work, sources in the zonal headquarters said.
The motorman’s name was also recommended for an award at the Railway Board level. On the day of the incident, Mr. Karunakaran stopped his train, despite the signal giving clearance to proceed, after seeing two other trains parked on the same track. He photographed the scene and alerted his superior officers about the safety issue.
The signal failure was rectified and normal train services resumed. Investigators held the motorman “blameworthy” for exceeding the permissible speed limit. The All India Loco Running Staff Association had represented to the railway authorities to drop action against Mr. Karunakaran as he had done his best in the dynamic situation.
A multi-departmental inquiry, comprising senior railway officers drawn from different departments, confirmed the signal failure. Further inquiry revealed that the particular automatic signal (S192) had failed multiple times but was reset by a local signal department technician without following the standard operating procedure. A few other automatic signals had also failed in recent times but were reset with no investigation conducted to analyse the root cause.
The inquiry committee gave a set of recommendations on the safety front. The railway officers who examined the sequence of events, circumstances that led to the incident, and technical evidence called for launching a safety drive in Chennai Division. They said the Station Masters should be counselled about the rule position in resetting the multi-section digital axle counter (MASDAC) while restoring signal failures. Since the failure buzzer that alerted the Station Master of signal failures was found disconnected on March 5, 2026, the committee wanted the authorities concerned to check and ensure the functioning of the same.
To avoid opening of the relay room randomly by the signal technicians for resetting, a double lock arrangement was recommended for access control. The diagnostic panels in MSDAC huts should be made failsafe, the report said.
The Chennai Division accepted the recommendations and directed the departments concerned to take necessary action, the sources said. There was no response from the Southern Railway spokesperson to questions sent by The Hindu on the inquiry committee’s recommendations and the reward given to the whistleblower motorman.

The Tamil Nadu government has decided to implement the Singapengal Entrepreneurship Credit Scheme by restructuring and broadening the scope of lending through cooperatives to include youth and marginalised sections of society as beneficiaries, apart from members of self-help groups (SHGs), to promote entrepreneurship.

Instructions were also issued to ensure at least 30% of loans across all categories were extended to new members. Officials were directed to take steps to fully achieve the loan targets for SHGs and review loan applications received by cooperative banks and societies, including pending and rejected ones. The allocation for the new scheme is likely to be announced in the upcoming Budget.
In the run-up to the 2026 Assembly election, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) had promised to launch the Singapengal Empowerment Scheme, under which SHGs would be supported by facilitating the repayment of their existing loans and providing interest-free financial assistance of up to ₹5 lakh to enhance their productivity and sustainability. The party also promised that SHGs transitioning into registered micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) would receive an annual grant of ₹5 lakh as a 100% subsidy to support their growth and expansion.

Exiled Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasrin on Sunday (August 2, 2026) called for all countries of the Indian subcontinent to implement a Uniform Civil Code (UCC), arguing that this was needed to protect women from discrimination.
“Uniform Civil Code is a must. This is the first step for any civilised society,” Ms. Nasrin said, interacting with journalists in Kolkata. The Bengali writer said that she has been fighting for the UCC for the past 40 years and added that “if women come under religious laws, there is discrimination and persecution”. Delivering a speech in Kolkata on Saturday (August 1), she had said that India, Bangladesh, and Pakistan should have a uniform law for all their citizens.
“Due to religious laws, women are suffering. Hindus are being tortured in Bangladesh. During the Yunus regime, Hindus were tortured even more. In many madrasas and mosques, hatred is being taught against Hindus. Now we have Jamaat-e-Islami as an Opposition party. It is against women’s equality, and they want Sharia rule,” she said, reflecting on the situation in her home country.
The author’s remarks come at a time when the West Bengal government has announced plans to implement UCC in the State and has set up a committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge to look into the provisions of a draft UCC Bill.
Return to Kolkata
Ms. Nasrin arrived in Kolkata on July 31, almost 19 years after she was forced to leave the city due to violent protests by a mob upset with her writings during the Left Front government. Prior to this, she was exiled from Bangladesh in 1994.
Her return to Kolkata was celebrated by West Bengal’s first BJP government, even as she shared the stage with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. Asked for her view on different governments in the State, she said, “One government had forced me out, another did not allow me to return, and one government has helped me to return,” she said.
‘Some madrasas produce jihadis’
Ms. Nasrin also came down hard against madrasas, saying that some of these “religious schools produce jihadis”. “In my opinion, madrasas should not exist. Not in all cases, but in some, it is seen that jihadis are being produced in madrasas,” the writer said. Alleging that “child abuse is going on there, rapes are happening, and imams and madrasa teachers are being held,” she opined that “there is no need for madrasas to exist.”
“No one does anything after passing out of madrasas. They beg, survive on charity. Madrasas should go, and secular schools should come up instead,” Ms. Nasrin said.
Freedom of speech
The Bengali writer also expressed anguish over an incident during Saturday’s (August 1) event, where the crowd prevented Bengali poet Joy Goswami from addressing the gathering. The poet is considered to be close to the Trinamool Congress regime. Ms. Nasrin had called Mr. Goswami to take his seat on the stage when the people gathered started shouting.
“Not only was Mr. Goswami insulted, but I was also insulted because I had invited him,” she said. “In my speech, I spoke about freedom of expression. Everyone should be allowed to speak. It is not right to stop anyone from expressing their views,” she said.

The Congress has strongly criticised the police case registered against protester Ruchika Singh for allegedly making objectionable remarks at Jantar Mantar on July 23, 2026. Social media has erupted with pleas from users asking YouTube India to restore the account of Mohammad Irfan, a resident of a Delhi slum, whose channel gained a substantial following overnight before being taken down by the video-hosting platform.
While YouTube has not yet issued any official clarification, attempts to access Mr. Irfan’s page, Main Irfan, display a message stating that “this account has been terminated for violating Google’s Terms of Service”.
Mr. Irfan went viral for reciting the Preamble to the Constitution during the recent Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar.
He spoke about the hardships faced by workers in the unorganised sector and the need for accessible education, healthcare, and democratic rights.
On July 28, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, met him and said Mr. Irfan’s outlook reflected the strength and promise of India’s youth.
After his YouTube channel was taken down, Mr. Irfan took to X, saying the termination was “some kind of mistake” and urging the platform to rectify it.
“My channel was completely new, and I have honestly followed all of YouTube’s guidelines,” Mr. Irfan said in his post on X. “People really liked my content, which is why my subscribers increased. It seems like there was a mistake by your automatic system. Please review my channel again and restore it.”
Mr. Irfan’s channel found a vocal supporter in veteran journalist Ajit Anjum, who posted several times on X in support of the page while it was active, and after it was taken down.
“A young man named Mohammad Irfan, who lives in a slum in Delhi, started his YouTube channel just yesterday with our support,” Mr. Anjum posted on X on Sunday (August 2, 2026). “From yesterday evening until this morning, his channel gained more than 70,000 subscribers.”
“Suddenly this morning, his YouTube channel was terminated,” he added. “How did a working-class young man manage to gain so many subscribers in such a short time? That in itself is an extraordinary achievement. So why did YouTube terminate his channel so abruptly?,” the post said.
Several other social media users also posted in support of Mr. Irfan’s page, saying that the content and the channel were genuine, and that its termination was the result of a mistake by Google-owned YouTube’s automated systems. They urged the platform to rectify the issue.

Four people have been detained in connection with a rape and murder of a 15-year-old girl who was found dead at her home near National Highway-6 in Assam’s Hailakandi district on Saturday night, police said.
Senior superintendent of police (SSP), Hailakandi, Amitab Sinha, said Hailakandi police registered a case, however denied from sharing any details and detained four persons for interrogation. Sexual assault accusations are yet to be medically ascertained, police said.
“The family members are claiming it [rape], but we are waiting for the post-mortem report to draw any conclusions. We are investigating the matter thoroughly, and four persons are currently being questioned,” Sinha said.
The incident took place in the Aloichora area under Katlichera police station at 11pm on Saturday. The victim’s family said they were attending a feast at a nearby relative’s house at the time.
“It’s a neighbourhood where many members of the same extended family live together, and her family members were not far away when the incident happened,” SSP said.
“She was there at the feast too, but after an argument with a cousin, she left for home at 10.30pm. We thought we’d bring some food for her later, but when we reached home around an hour later, it was a horrible scene,” her mother said.
She said her body was found lying on the floor, almost unrecognisable.
“It was horrible; how can a human treat another human, a little girl, in such a brutal manner,” she said, while demanding capital punishment for the accused.
The victim’s sister alleged that the attackers used utensils and other objects to mutilate the body after the assault.
“Her face was smashed, her head was bludgeoned with a heavy object, and some rod-like object was inserted into her private parts,” she said. “They are not humans, even calling them animals would be wrong. They don’t deserve to live. I appeal to the police to shoot them, or they should be hanged,” she said.
Police said they received the information around 12.30am, and recovered the body on Sunday morning following protests by family members and neighbours. Locals in Aloichora blocked NH-6 on Sunday morning in protest against the alleged rape and murder, initially refusing to hand over the body to the police.
“If a 15-16-year-old girl is not safe in her own house, what kind of society have we become? There must be exemplary punishment so that nobody dares repeat such heinous acts,” one of the protesters said.
Local MLA Milon Das later intervened, helping police transport the body to SMCH for the post-mortem. Das met with the family members and assured them that the culprits would be arrested immediately.
“The body has been sent to Silchar Medical College and Hospital (SMCH) for a post-mortem, and we are investigating the matter further,” confirmed the additional superintendent of police (Crime), Hailakandi, Shamirdapar Baruah.

Chennai, PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss on Sunday asserted that if the proposed Mekedatu reservoir had been constructed, Tamil Nadu would not have received even the current inflows from Karnataka's Kabini reservoir.
Urging the Tamil Nadu government to firmly oppose Karnataka's attempts to implement the project, the PMK leader, in a statement, called for a unified action plan involving all political parties and farmers' associations.
Claiming that Karnataka's water releases over the past two days had been erratic, he said, "On Saturday, the discharge from the Kabini reservoir into the Cauvery was increased to 25,000 cusecs. It was drastically reduced to 10,000 cusecs on Sunday morning before being revised to 14,958 cusecs as inflows rose to 28,009 cusecs."
"This unpredictable pattern clearly demonstrates that Karnataka has no intention of releasing Tamil Nadu's lawful share of water. Instead, it is using the Cauvery, which flows through Tamil Nadu, merely as a flood drainage channel to flush out surplus water," Anbumani alleged.
Highlighting the current storage levels, the former union health minister said the four major reservoirs in Karnataka collectively held 74.05 TMC of water, amounting to 64 per cent of their combined capacity of 114.57 TMC.
He claimed that, with Karnataka owing Tamil Nadu 40 TMC of water by the end of July, it could easily release water from the nearly full Harangi, Hemavathi and Kabini reservoirs.
"Instead, Karnataka is diverting a major portion of the water released from Harangi to the Krishna Raja Sagara reservoir to fill it up," he alleged, adding, "While the inflow into Harangi stands at 10,430 cusecs, 14,470 cusecs is being released towards KRS."
He claimed that Hemavathi was expected to reach its full capacity within a week and that its surplus water would also be stored in the KRS reservoir, reflecting Karnataka's continued refusal to release Tamil Nadu's due share of water.
Explaining why the proposed Mekedatu project posed a serious threat, Anbumani said the reservoir would be located downstream of Karnataka's four major reservoirs, close to the Tamil Nadu border.
"If the project is implemented, even the surplus water currently flowing from the Kabini, Harangi and Hemavathi reservoirs through the KRS dam would be impounded at Mekedatu," he claimed.
"Under such circumstances, it would become virtually impossible for any water to reach Tamil Nadu," he claimed.
He urged the State government to maintain its firm opposition to the project, consult all political parties and farmers' organisations, and formulate a clear and decisive action plan to safeguard Tamil Nadu's rights over the Cauvery waters.
Tamil Nadu has been opposed to Karnataka's move to construct the balancing reservoir at Mekedatu in that state, claiming it would affect its interests.
