Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is set to make her first open appearance before the media in India, nearly two years after her government was ousted amid a mass student-led uprising in Bangladesh. The event will be hosted virtually by the Foreign Correspondents' Club of South Asia (FCC South Asia) in New Delhi, where Hasina is expected to speak about her future plans and her proposed return to Bangladesh.
The interaction will take place on August 5, 2026, from 6 PM to 7:30 PM at the Sir Mark Tully Auditorium on Mathura Road in New Delhi, with live streaming on the club's social media platforms.
FIRST MAJOR APPEARANCE SINCE OUSTER
The event coincides with the second anniversary of the collapse of Hasina's 15-year rule. On August 5, 2024, student-led demonstrations against a controversial quota system evolved into a nationwide anti-government movement that forced Hasina from office. She left Bangladesh for India after protesters stormed and vandalised official buildings in Dhaka, bringing an abrupt end to her nearly 16-year rule.
Since arriving in India, Hasina has stayed away from public events and formal media interactions. Her upcoming address is expected to be her most significant public appearance since leaving office.
PROMINENT BANGLADESHI FIGURES TO JOIN EVENT
The invitation lists several Bangladeshi political leaders, diplomats and public figures who are expected to participate in the programme alongside Hasina.
Among them are Sajeeb Wazed Joy, Hasina's son and former ICT adviser to the Bangladesh prime minister; Mohibul Hasan Chowdhury Nowfel, Bangladesh's former education minister; and Mahammad Ali Siddique, general secretary of Bangladesh Human Rights Watch.
The panel also includes former Bangladesh cricketer and ex-member of Parliament Shakib Al Hasan; former diplomat and security analyst Aminul Hoque Polash; political and counterterrorism analyst Abu Obaidha Arin; and Shah Md Bakhtiar, director of Bangladesh Human Rights Watch USA.
The event will be chaired by Dr. Waiel Awwad, president of FCC South Asia and the International Association of Press Clubs (IAPC).
Bangladesh's political landscape has changed significantly since Hasina's ouster. The interim administration led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus ended after the February 2026 general election, paving the way for a Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP)-led government under Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. The new administration has continued legal proceedings against several leaders of the former Awami League government, while the party's political activities remain banned under the country's anti-terrorism law pending court proceedings.

Taslima Nasreen draws parallels between CJP protests and 2024 Bangladesh unrest
Days after the CJP protests in Delhi, Taslima Nasreen said the events in Bangladesh in 2024 and afterwards should serve as a warning for India.
Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday drew parallels between the recent protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi and the student-led movement that led to the ouster of former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in 2024, saying people should learn from what followed in her home country.
Speaking at a press conference in Kolkata, a day after her felicitation ceremony was briefly disrupted, Nasreen said the events in Bangladesh should serve as a warning.
"I felt what is happening here is similar to what happened in Bangladesh during the July student movement. People were fooled. The result in Bangladesh has not been good. Jihadis have taken over power there," she said.
Bangladesh witnessed months of student-led protests in 2024 over a controversial job quota system. The demonstrations soon turned into a wider anti-government movement that culminated in Sheikh Hasina leaving the country after weeks of violence. Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus later took charge of an interim government. Since then, Bangladesh has seen political uncertainty, while minority groups, including Hindus, have repeatedly raised concerns over attacks on their community.
Nasreen claimed the condition of Hindus had worsened under the interim government.
"Hindus faced torture during the Hasina government too, but there are more atrocities under the Yunus government," she alleged, attributing the situation to a lack of education and the growing influence of religious institutions.
Calling for secular reforms, Nasreen said religion should be kept separate from the state. She criticised the madrasa education system, alleging that it promoted communal thinking, and said Bangladesh should instead focus on secular education.
She also reiterated her support for a Uniform Civil Code, saying there should be "one law for everyone" in India, Bangladesh and Pakistan to ensure equal rights, particularly for women.
Nasreen also expressed support for jailed Hindu monk Chinmoy Krishna Das, saying she and several others had protested against his imprisonment.
Asked about the opposition in Bangladesh, she said it would have been better if the Awami League had remained the principal opposition instead of Jamaat-e-Islami. She opposed any move to ban the Awami League and said former prime minister Sheikh Hasina should be allowed to return to Bangladesh despite her criticism of some of the former government's policies.
The author also spoke about the disruption during her felicitation at Kolkata's Rabindra Sadan on Saturday, where noted Bengali poet Joy Goswami was prevented from addressing the audience after protests from a section of those present.
"I felt bad. It was not only Joy Goswami's humiliation but also mine because I had invited him. Political ideologies can differ, but everyone has the right to express their views," she said, adding that she planned to visit the poet at his residence.
On the political response she has received over the years, Nasreen said, "One government barred me, one government expelled me, and one government invited me," in an apparent reference to the Left Front, the Trinamool Congress and the BJP.
She also thanked West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari for assuring her security during her visit to Kolkata.
Expressing hope for better ties between India and Bangladesh, Nasreen said India had played a key role in Bangladesh's liberation in 1971 and that relations between the two neighbours should remain friendly.

headline: Taslima Nasreen backs UCC, says India, Bangladesh, Pakistan need it
cluster_text: Taslima Nasreen backs UCC, says India, Bangladesh, Pakistan need it [SEP] Taslima Nasreen backs UCC, says India, Bangladesh, Pakistan need it
full_text:
Taslima Nasreen backs UCC, says India, Bangladesh, Pakistan need it
Taslima Nasreen backed a Uniform Civil Code during her return visit to Kolkata. She said equal laws are essential for women's rights and defended free expression after a felicitation disruption.
Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday strongly backed the implementation of a Uniform Civil Code in India, saying such a law was essential to remove discrimination, especially against women. She said Bangladesh and Pakistan also needed a Uniform Civil Code, and argued that there should be equal laws for everyone.
Speaking to reporters in Kolkata during her first visit to the city in nearly 19 years, Nasreen also expressed anguish over a disruption at her felicitation ceremony a day earlier, when poet Joy Goswami was forced to leave the stage amid objections from a section of the audience. She said the incident went against the principle of freedom of expression, which Kolkata had long stood for.
"I have been fighting for the UCC for the past 40 years. This is much needed in any civilised country. Bangladesh, Pakistan and India need a Uniform Civil Code. There should be equal laws for everyone. Women face a great deal of discrimination, and much of it can be removed through a UCC. It is essential," Nasreen said.
Her remarks came as the West Bengal government has constituted a high-level committee to examine a draft Uniform Civil Code for the state. A government notification said the panel was formed in view of the "wide ramifications and voluminous nature" of the proposed legislation and would undertake a comprehensive examination of the draft Bill before any further steps are taken.
Referring to Bangladesh, the 63-year-old writer said equality was the cornerstone of civilisation, but many women continued to face discrimination. "In Bangladesh, Hindu women do not have equal rights. They cannot inherit their father's property. If Hindu women are to enjoy freedom and equal rights, a Uniform Civil Code is necessary," she said.
Nasreen was felicitated at a state government programme at Rabindra Sadan on Saturday after returning to Kolkata for the first time since 2007, when protests over the publication of her book Dwikhandito forced the then Left Front government to move her out of the city. She had left Bangladesh in 1994 after receiving death threats from radical groups over her writings and views on religion.
Recalling the disruption at Saturday's event, Nasreen said she felt "insulted" after Goswami was prevented from speaking. "Not only was Joy insulted, but I was also insulted because I had invited him," she said. The controversy erupted after she invited Goswami onto the stage and asked him to address the gathering, but loud objections from a section of the audience forced him to step down without speaking.
"In my speech, I had spoken about freedom of expression. Everyone should be allowed to speak. It is not right to stop anyone from expressing their views," she said. Questioning the conduct of those who objected, she added, "Those who appreciated my speech were the ones who did not allow him to come on the stage. Didn't they also question me? It is contradictory. When someone speaks about freedom of expression, people support it, but when a poet is invited to speak, they do not want to hear him. That is not right." She said she would visit Goswami at his residence, adding, "I have not got the opportunity to speak to Joy (after the incident), but I will pay him a visit today or tomorrow."
Nasreen said she hoped such an incident would not happen again in her favourite city. "Kolkata is a city of progressives. People here believe in freedom of speech and the right to express one's views. People's political ideologies may differ, but everyone must be given the space to express one's opinions," she said.
Asked to compare the Left Front, the Trinamool Congress and the present BJP government in West Bengal, Nasreen praised the BJP-led dispensation for allowing her to visit Kolkata.
"There is, of course, a difference between the three governments. One government expelled me, another did not allow me to return, while the third has allowed me to come. Instead of focusing on those differences, I think we should celebrate the fact that I have been able to come back. I am very happy that I could return. I want to believe that this government believes in the right to freedom of expression and freedom of speech," she said.
Nasreen said she had been invited to Kolkata by an organisation called Secular Mission and that the state government later provided her security cover and facilitated her visit to West Bengal. On Saturday, she had said her return after 19 years showed that "injustice can be long but cannot be permanent", while maintaining that her fight had always been for women's rights and freedom of expression, and not for or against any political party.
When asked whether she wanted to return to Kolkata permanently, Nasreen said she had not yet "give it thought" but wanted to come back for the Kolkata Book Fair next year. "I surely want to come to Kolkata Book Fair. The Bengal chief minister has promised me security. So, I will definitely try to come. I will," she said. Stressing again that her views were independent of politics, she added, "I travel to many states. If I visit Kerala, does that make me part of that state's politics? Certainly not. I remain independent. Any government that provides me security is only discharging its responsibility. That has nothing to do with politics."
Nasreen's visit to Kolkata combined a renewed call for a Uniform Civil Code with a strong defence of equal rights and free speech, even as she spoke about her difficult history with the city and her wish to return again for the Book Fair.

full_text:
26,000 schools shut in UP to deny education to PDA children: Akhilesh Yadav
Akhilesh Yadav alleged the Uttar Pradesh government shut over 26,000 primary schools since 2017. He said the issue reflects discrimination in education and will be raised in the Assembly.
Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday alleged that the Uttar Pradesh government has shut more than 26,000 government primary schools since coming to power in 2017, and claimed that the move was aimed at denying education to children from PDA communities, which he described as Backwards, Dalits and Minorities.
Addressing a press conference at the party headquarters in Lucknow, Yadav said the Samajwadi Party would raise the issue during the Monsoon Session of the Assembly, which begins on Monday. He also said party MLAs would target the government on education, paper leaks, law and order, and alleged corruption.
Yadav said official data showed that Uttar Pradesh had 1,13,938 government primary schools until March 2017, when the BJP came to power, and claimed that more than 26,000 of them have been closed since then.
He said the highest number of closures was in Lakhimpur Kheri, where 758 schools were shut, followed by Sitapur with 650 and Prayagraj with 638. In Gorakhpur, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's home district, around 500 primary schools were closed, he said.
Saying that most students in government primary schools belong to Other Backward Classes and Scheduled Castes, Yadav alleged that the BJP did not want children from PDA communities to get education.
He said enrolment in these schools had fallen from 1.17 crore students in 2017 to around 89 lakh in 2026, and added that of these 89 lakh students, about 25 lakh belong to OBC, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe categories.
He also said the number of teachers in these schools had come down from around 4 lakh in 2017 to 3.40 lakh at present, while nearly 81,000 teaching posts remained vacant. Yadav alleged that the government was reducing teaching posts because it did not want to provide permanent government jobs, as regular recruitment would require budget allocations and implementation of reservation policies.
Yadav said the closure of government primary schools had hurt girls' education, with the number of girls studying in these schools falling from 61.57 lakh in March 2017 to around 45 lakh now.
He also claimed that thousands of government schools still lacked basic infrastructure, saying around 7,000 schools had no electricity, about 2,300 had no toilets for girls, 576 had no drinking water facilities and nearly 23,000 had no provision for computer education.
Yadav said the Samajwadi Party would press the government in the Assembly over school closures, falling enrolment, teacher vacancies and poor facilities in primary schools.

West Bengal to fine builders for dumping materials on roads from September 1
Agnimitra Paul announced fines from September 1 for anyone storing construction materials on public roads. The warning broadens West Bengal's civic discipline drive to vacant plots, parking violations and footpath encroachment.
West Bengal Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Minister Agnimitra Paul said on Sunday that people who leave construction materials such as sand, bricks and stones on public roads while building houses will face penalties from September 1. She said roads cannot be used to store such materials and property owners must keep them within their premises.
Paul also said owners of vacant plots would be responsible for keeping their land clean, and warned of strict action against illegal parking. She urged hawkers not to occupy entire footpaths, but said no eviction drive against them would be carried out until the end of the Durga Puja festivities.
Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of a programme at the Siliguri Municipal Corporation, Paul said, “People cannot leave stones, sand and bricks on the road while constructing houses. We will impose fines. Roads are not anyone's private property.”
She said landowners cannot leave vacant plots overgrown with bushes or clogged with drains and waterbodies for years, as such conditions could contribute to mosquito breeding and increase the risk of diseases such as dengue.
Maintaining vacant land, like maintaining one's house and its surroundings, is the responsibility of the owner, she said. Reiterating the government's recent measures to improve civic discipline, Paul said vehicles must be parked only in designated parking spaces and reminded people that the state government is introducing a dedicated parking app.
Those parking cars or motorcycles on footpaths would also face hefty fines, she added. Paul also urged hawkers occupying entire footpaths to move back and leave adequate space for pedestrians.
In summary, Paul announced fines from September 1 for keeping construction materials on public roads, said vacant plot owners would have to keep their land clean, warned of action against illegal parking and asked hawkers to leave space on footpaths, while saying no eviction drive against them would be carried out until the end of the Durga Puja festivities.

[SEP] Kolar: Only 11,831 mango growers have benefitted this year under the Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) and the Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS)..As many as 771 farmers, despite registering to sell their mango produce, did not sell it. As a result, the government could not procure 11,500 metric tonnes of Totapuri mangoes, leaving nearly Rs seven crore of the allocated assistance unutilised..Owing to a sharp crash in mango price, the government had earmarked Rs 58.45 crore to procure 1.30 lakh metric tonnes of Totapuri mangoes through the APMC. Of 12,602 farmers who registered to sell under the scheme, 771 did not complete the sale. .Mango price crash pushes growers into distress in Karnataka.Consequently, only 11,831 growers, who sold 1,18,500 metric tonnes, received benefits amounting to Rs 51.85 crore. The payment is already being credited to the farmers' bank accounts..Kolar district produces nearly 5.20 lakh tonnes of Totapuri mangoes annually. However, thousands of growers from KGF, Mulabagilu and other taluks could not register under the scheme and suffered heavy loss. While some left their produce to rot in orchards, others were forced to sell mangoes at throwaway price of Rs two – Rs three per kg, which did not even cover transportation cost. Frustrated by the loss, several farmers reportedly chopped down their mango trees.."The registration process was conducted for only three to four days before it was abruptly closed. As a result, nearly 50% of the district's mango growers were deprived of the support price," said District Mango Growers' Association President Neelatur Chinnappa Reddy..The Central government, through an order issued on June 26, fixed the procurement limit at 1.30 lakh metric tonnes of Totapuri mangoes. Registration began on June 27 across Kolar, Chikkaballapur, and Bengaluru rural districts. However, by the time 12,602 farmers had registered their produce, the procurement ceiling had already been exhausted. Registration was therefore stopped on June 30, leaving many more farmers without an opportunity to register..Although the farmers staged protests on the national highway and in front of the deputy commissioner's office, demanding that registration be extended, their demand was not accepted..Responding to farmers' appeals, State Cooperation Department principal secretary wrote to the secretary, Union Ministry of Agriculture on July 2, requesting that the procurement limit be increased from 1.30 lakh metric tonnes to 5.20 lakh metric tonnes. However, there was no response from the Centre..Under the PDPS, the farmers were eligible for Rs 4,370 per tonne of mangoes. The scheme limited assistance to 40 quintals per acre, with a maximum of 200 quintals for five acres. July 27 was the last date for submitting sale bills.."I sold 17 tonnes of mangoes under the PDPS and received nearly Rs 75,000. This year, the payment has been made much faster," said T V Ramesh, a mango grower from Totli village in Kolar taluk..In jiffy Only 1,18,500 metric tonnes of Totapuri mangoes were procured against the sanctioned limit of 1.30 lakh metric tonnes Growers from KGF and Mulabagilu largely missed out the support price due to the early closure of registration July 27 was the last date for submission of sale bills under the scheme.M Manjunath, Mango Development Board Assistant Director, said "The payment is being credited to the accounts of farmers who sold mangoes under the PDPS. So far Rs 49.67 crore has been disbursed and the remaining payments will be completed by Monday.".Neelatur Chinnappa Reddy, District Mango Growers' Association President, said "The government discriminated against mango growers. Registration was closed too quickly and many farmers could not even register to sell their produce.".Registered but did not sell A total of 771 farmers who had registered to sell Totapuri mangoes under the MIS and PDPS did not ultimately sell their produce. However the quantity of mangoes they had registered was counted within the government's 1.30 lakh-tonne procurement ceiling. Since the registration process closed immediately after the limit was reached many other eligible growers were denied registration. Had these farmers been given an opportunity they could have sold their produce under the scheme. As a result nearly Rs seven crore allocated by the government remained unutilised.

NEW DELHI: Around 158 cases related to alleged recruitment examination irregularities are pending trial in courts across the country despite the completion of investigations, with some cases dating back more than two decades, PTI reported.The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), which probed these matters, has decided to approach high courts seeking the transfer of pending cases to fast-track courts being set up in several states to handle cases under the new anti-paper leak law.The agency will inform the high courts that it would provide dedicated special prosecutors and make all possible resources available to ensure the earliest possible conclusion of the trials.Government officials attributed the delays to the transfer of investigating officers, prosecutors, and even presiding judges.
Which state accounts for how many cases
Delhi accounted for 25 alleged irregularity cases registered since 2000. These include the AIIMS PG recruitment examination case of 2010-11, the Delhi University Medical and Dental Entrance Examination case of 2011, CAT (Common Admission Test) irregularities of 2004, the SSC (Staff Selection Commission) recruitment case of 2013, and teachers' recruitment cases.
Bihar has five pending cases, including three linked to the alleged NEET 2024 paper leak, besides irregularities in the PMT (Pre-Medical Test) examinations of 2003 and 2011.In Himachal Pradesh, the 2022 constable recruitment case is among three cases awaiting the start of trial. Jammu and Kashmir also has three pending cases, including alleged irregularities in junior engineer and constable recruitment.Similarly, five cases are awaiting trial in Jharkhand, five in Karnataka, three in Maharashtra â including two related to NEET 2024 â eight in Rajasthan, 14 in Tamil Nadu, and 10 each in West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh.
New anti-paper leak law
The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026, recently passed by Parliament, provides for every state and Union territory to designate a sessions court as a special fast-track court in consultation with the chief justice of the concerned high court.
The law mandates that these fast-track courts hear cases on a day-to-day basis without unnecessary adjournments, with trials to be completed within three months of the filing of the charge sheet. It also provides for the transfer of cases already pending before other courts to these newly designated special fast-track courts, where they are to be concluded within three months of transfer.Every state and Union territory will also appoint dedicated special public prosecutors to represent these cases.The legislation was enacted in the wake of the recent student protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, which culminated with the resignation of the-then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET (UG) paper leak in May. Protesters had also called for wider reforms in the country's examination system, following which the government constituted a high-powered task force, headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, to recommend reforms.

Taslima Nasreen draws parallel between Bangladesh and Delhi student protest
NEW DELHI: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday said the student movement that led to the ouster of Sheikh Hasinaâs government had âfooled usâ, drawing a parallel between the protests in Bangladesh and the recent student demonstrations in Delhi.Speaking to reporters in Kolkata two days after returning to the city for the first time since 2007, the acclaimed writer acknowledged that she had not followed the Delhi protest closely, but added that a short video clip from the agitation âreminded me of the July 2024 studentsâ movement in Bangladesh.â"That student movement in Bangladesh fooled us. Because we thought the students wanted to abolish the quota system. Sheikh Hasina had also agreed to their demands, but ultimately the government fell. Later, we found that jihadis (Islamic fundamentalists) were behind that movement. The fallout has not been good for Bangladesh. Jihadis have taken over power there," she told reporters.Nasreen, who left Bangladesh in 1994 following threats from Islamic radicals over her work, further stated that the developments in her home country had âreinforcedâ her concerns about the consequences of such movements.
The 63-year-old author added that the 2024 Bangladesh protests should âtherefore serve as a lesson.âNasreenâs remarks came ahead of the second anniversary of Sheikh Hasinaâs resignation on August 5. The former prime minister has been living in exile in New Delhi.
The Awami League government was replaced by an interim administration led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus three days after Sheikh Hasinaâs ouster.In February this year, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) secured a sweeping victory in a landmark parliamentary election, paving the way for party chairperson Tarique Rahman to become the new prime minister.The protests in Delhi were held demanding the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET (UG) paper leak issue and seeking broader examination reforms. After more than five weeks of an indefinite sit-in led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in the national capital, Pradhan resigned on July 25, bringing the agitation to an end.(With PTI inputs)

The Centre has approved Rs 379.35 crore under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) for Assamâs flood response
Assam continued to grapple with the aftermath of devastating floods on Sunday, with the death toll remaining at 82 and nearly 1.78 lakh people still affected across seven districts. Although floodwaters have begun to recede in some areas, thousands remain displaced, agricultural land is submerged, and the state government has intensified relief, rehabilitation and long-term mitigation efforts.According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), the flood situation has improved slightly, with the number of affected people declining from over 1.92 lakh to 1.78 lakh. However, 349 villages across Golaghat, Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat, Bajali, Dhemaji and Sonitpur districts remain affected.
Charaideo is the worst-hit district, with more than 75,000 people affected, followed by over 58,000 in Sivasagar. Nearly 15,060 hectares of crop area remain submerged, while thousands of livestock have been affected or washed away.
Relief and rescue under way
A total of 44 relief camps are currently sheltering around 15,000 displaced people, while another 17 relief distribution centres are providing assistance to more than 5,500 residents.
The state government has directed district administrations to expedite the identification of affected families so that financial assistance can begin from August 3.
Villagers rescue over 1,000 people in Sivasagar
One of the most remarkable rescue stories emerged from the Nepali Khuti area in Sivasagar district, where local villagers used six country-made boats to rescue more than 1,000 people from five villages after floodwaters rose rapidly on July 19.Residents said families were trapped on rooftops, elevated platforms and trees as water levels surged. The volunteer rescuers continued operations through the night despite having little food or water, ferrying stranded villagers to safer areas.
CM reviews flood-hit districts and compensation plans
Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma began a tour of the worst-hit districts on Sunday to oversee relief operations and prepare for a comprehensive damage assessment exercise scheduled to begin on August 9.The government has also directed officials to ensure uninterrupted distribution of relief kits, assess damage to educational institutions before schools reopen on August 10, and prepare restoration plans for damaged Namghars (Vaishnavite prayer centres).
IIT-Guwahati to be engaged for Brahmaputra erosion solution
During his visit to erosion-hit areas of Dibrugarh district, including Chabua, Balijan, Pukhurijan, Dinjan and Rahmoria, Sarma announced that the state government will engage experts from IIT-Guwahati to develop a long-term solution to the Brahmaputra riverâs erosion problem.Calling riverbank erosion one of Assamâs biggest geographical challenges, the chief minister said the state loses valuable land every year and that modern technology would be used to strengthen vulnerable riverbanks. The proposed IIT initiative will complement the governmentâs planned Rs 90 crore erosion mitigation project.
Agriculture rehabilitation begins
Agriculture minister Pijush Hazarika visited Charaideo district on Sunday to review post-flood rehabilitation measures and launched community paddy nurseries and seedling distribution programmes for flood-affected farmers.The government said quality seedlings and other assistance would be provided to ensure cultivation resumes without delay during the current agricultural season.
Aid pours in from NGOs, celebrities and political organisations
Support for flood-hit communities has continued to grow across Assam.Actor Randeep Hooda joined a relief drive organised by Global Sikhs in Sivasagar district, distributing essential supplies and serving food through langar for affected families. He warned that prolonged waterlogging and mud-filled homes could trigger disease outbreaks and urged people across the country to contribute to relief efforts.The Lok Janshakti Party (Ramvilas) has also launched a large-scale relief operation in Sivasagar, distributing food and essential supplies and announcing plans to feed up to 15,000 people daily for 10 days, along with setting up medical camps.
The Centre has approved Rs 379.35 crore under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) for Assamâs flood response. Sarma thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah for extending assistance and for deploying Inter-Ministerial Central Teams to support relief and rehabilitation planning.Reliance Foundation has also contributed Rs 21 crore to the Chief Ministerâs Relief Fund for flood relief and rehabilitation efforts.While water levels have started falling in parts of the state, the crisis is far from over. Thousands remain displaced, farmland continues to lie under water, and many families face the difficult task of rebuilding homes and livelihoods. NEW DELHI: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday criticised the ban on former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasinaâs Awami League party, calling it a "move against democracyâ and expressing uncertainty over Hasinaâs return to the country.âNo political party should be banned. The manner in which Sheikh Hasina was forced to leave the country is questionable. It was not right to ban the Awami League. It was a move against democracy. I want the ban to be lifted as soon as possible,â Nasreen told reporters at a press conference in Kolkata.
Sheikh Hasina has been living in Delhi since August 5, 2024, after resigning as prime minister following weeks of student-led protests. The interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, which took charge after the fall of the Awami League administration, banned the party in May 2025 under anti-terrorism laws.
Meanwhile, Nasreen alleged that several Awami League workers had been tortured and killed during Sheikh Hasinaâs exile and expressed uncertainty over whether the former prime minister would be able to return to Bangladesh.âMany Awami League workers were tortured and murdered. Sheikh Hasina wants to return, but I do not know whether that will be possible.
But no one wants me to go back,â she said.Nasreen also criticised Jamaat-e-Islami, now Bangladesh's principal opposition party, accusing it of opposing womenâs equality and seeking the imposition of Sharia law.âNow we have Jamaat-e-Islami as an opposition party. It is against womenâs equality, and they want Sharia rule. If that happens, no minority will survive. Bangladesh is moving towards darkness. No one is trying to civilise Bangladesh. The government is only trying to remain in power,â she added.The 63-year-old author further claimed that âhatred against Hindusâ was being spread in some madrasas and mosques in Bangladesh.âIn many madrasas and mosques, hatred is being taught against Hindus,â Nasreen remarked.
Nasreen backs Uniform Civil Code, calls it necessary for women's equality
Turning to the issue of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), Nasreen said she had been advocating for such a law for the past 40 years and described it as essential in any âcivilised countryâ.âI have been fighting for the UCC for the past 40 years. This is much needed in any civilised country,â she remarked.She claimed that religious laws continued to affect womenâs rights in Bangladesh, alleging that Hindu women in the country lacked adequate legal protections, including the right to divorce.âIn Bangladesh, Hindu girls have no rights; they do not even have the right to divorce. Due to religious laws, women are suffering. Hindus are being tortured in Bangladesh. During the Yunus regime, Hindus were tortured even more,â she alleged.In July, the BJP-led West Bengal government constituted a nine-member expert committee headed by retired Supreme Court judge Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai to examine and finalise a draft UCC for the state. The state government plans to introduce the legislation during the upcoming August Assembly session.
Nasreen, who has lived in exile since 1994, when she was forced to leave Bangladesh due to the threat from Islamic radicals over her work, returned to Kolkata nearly two decades. She was forced to leave the city in 2007 following protests over her writings and memoir Dwikhandito (Split into Two), published in 2003.(With ANI inputs)

Can BJP crack Punjab? Inside its strategy to challenge AAP and Congress in 2027
Priyanka Mukherjee / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 02, 2026, 19:46 IST

Rahul Gandhi, PM Modi, Arvind Kejriwal
NEW DELHI: When it comes to BJPâs election playbook, there is always a method to the madness. Punjab, which votes early next year, appears to be following the same script.Sample these headlines:
PM Modi to visit Punjab on February 1
7 AAP MPs from Punjab merge with BJP
BJP appoints Kewal Singh Dhillon as Punjab unit president
Ravneet Singh Bittu resigns from Union Council of Ministers
PM Modi inaugurates, lays foundation stone of several projects in Punjab
Corruption is rampant in Punjab: PM Modi targets AAP government
All these headlines, when looked at in isolation, appear to be one-off political developments separated in time. But one look at them together in the context of a wider long-term objective, they appear not just connected but also planned with a purpose. This is a perfect example of the BJP election playbook in action.
The BJP, which over the years played second fiddle to the Akalis in Punjab, contested the 2022 elections alone after snapping ties with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD). However, it could win only 2 seats with a vote share of 6.6%. Even the 2024 Lok Sabha elections were a huge disappointment. The BJP polled 18.65% of votes but could not win any seat. However, the BJP appears determined not to let the past numbers dictate its future strategy. And that explains the aggression with which the party has gone for the kill in Punjab.Punjab, which over the years alternated between the Congress and the Akalis, broke the duopoly in 2022 when it overwhelmingly voted for Arvind Kejriwalâs AAP.
And that perhaps gives BJP its biggest hope as it marshals its resources. Now, letâs analyze all these headlines as a part of one story to understand how the BJP is gearing up to add another state to its ever-expanding kitty.
The Ravidassia outreach
When Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Punjab on February 1 this year, the BJPâs election playbook was already in action. The visit was part of a well thought-out and planned outreach that could increase the partyâs base and presence in the state. The occasion was the 649th Birth Anniversary of Sant Guru Ravidas Ji. The Ravidassia community form an important electoral bloc of Punjabâs Scheduled Caste population, especially in the Doaba region. A slew of announcements were made, including renaming of Adampur Airport after Guru Ravidas and the launch of the Shri Guru Ravidas Ji Maharaj Express between Jalandhar and Varanasi. It was the start of a planned outreach. That outreach has continued with the Punjab BJP launching the statewide implementation of the 'Samrasta Sankalp Abhiyan' from July 29, the auspicious occasion of Guru Purnima, to commemorate the 650th birth anniversary year of Guru Ravidas Maharaj. Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon said the nationwide campaign will continue till February 20 (Magha Purnima) under the guidance of the BJP national leadership and aims to spread Guru Ravidas's timeless message of equality, dignity, social harmony and social justice across Punjab.
Targeted political acquisition
The BJP, enriched by its experience from victories in states like West Bengal and Odisha, perhaps knows the importance of organisational strength in winning states. So in Punjab, after breaking its alliance with the Akalis, the BJP has been on an overdrive to build a strong local leadership. After the 2022 elections, several prominent Congress leaders had joined the BJP. And now in the run up to the 2027 electoral battle, seven AAP members of Rajya Sabha from the state are already a part of the party. And this acquisition includes Raghav Chaddha, once the most trusted associate of AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal. Chadha has a good understanding of the electoral thinking of AAP that rules Punjab now and can help the BJP capitalise on its weaknesses. As the elections approach, we could see Raghav Chaddha play a greater role in crafting and implementing BJPâs Punjab campaign.
The âDhillonâ signal
When the BJP replaced one Congress export Sunil Jakhar with another Kewal Singh Dhillon as its state chief, the change was aimed to send across a message. Dhillon, who is a seasoned politician and a prominent industrialist, became the first Jat Sikh to head the BJP in the state. The purpose was clear: outreach among Sikh voters to help increase the acceptability of the party after its Akali alliance ended. The BJP would hope that Dhillon could help the party expand its rural footprint. Besides Dhillon's political base is in Barnala, which falls in the Sangrur-Malwa region. This region is considered a stronghold of Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann and the Aam Aadmi Party.
Ravneet Singh Bittu and Punjab focus
Ravneet Singh Bittu, who joined the BJP in March 2024 ahead of the general elections after ending his long association with the Congress, seems to have an important role in the saffron partyâs blueprint for Punjab. During the 2024 campaign, Bittu was projected as an important Sikh face for the BJP by none other than Amit Shah. For those who remember, the entire BJP had rallied in support of Bittu after Rahul Gandhi had referred to him as âtraitorâ. The BJP made Bittu a minister in the Modi government and a member of Rajya Sabha despite his Lok Sabha election loss from Ludhiana in 2024 to showcase his importance. But after his RS tenure ended in June this year, he quit as minister amid hints that he will play a key role in BJPâs Punjab plans. According to reports, in June, Bittu had expressed his desire to work for Punjab in the Vidhan Sabha after spending nearly 17 years in Parliament. Bittu had then said that the BJP made him the minister even though he had lost the 2024 parliamentary elections."People of Punjab are fed up (with other parties). People are very much aware of development and progress taking place in other (BJP-ruled) states and they want prosperity in Punjab as well," Bittu had then said.Ravneet Singh Bittu is the grandson of former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, who was assassinated in 1995. During his political career in the Congress, he was elected MP thrice and also served as the grand-old-party's leader in the Lok Sabha and as its whip in the Lower House.
PM Modiâs 'double-engine' promise
When Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Punjab for the second time on July 17, his focus was on development, youth and farmers. He pitched the BJPâs 'double-engine' model, arguing that a government of the same party at the Centre and in the state could bring investment, jobs and faster growth to Punjab.âOnly the BJP can bring real change in Punjab. Only the BJP will make Punjab developed. Only the BJP will make Punjab self-reliant,â PM Modi said, adding that the state needed new investment, employment opportunities and greater global reach for products made in Punjab.He also accused the AAP government of stalling development and merely rebranding central schemes. Citing BJP-ruled Delhi and Haryana, Modi argued that Punjab too needed a 'double-engine' government, while claiming that farmers in the state were being denied the support available elsewhere.
Rivals under fire
And while one part of PM Modiâs Punjab campaign was outreach, the other part was his fierce attack on the rivals in the state. Targeting the AAP government in Punjab over law and order and several other issues, PM Modi dubbed the ruling dispensation as a "Kattar Beiman" which neither has clean intentions, nor honesty.PM Modi then targeted the Congress, which has been in news more for factionalism than poll readiness. Taking a dig at infighting in the state unit over the chief minister's chair, the PM said "They are not fighting for people, they are fighting among themselves."Also under attack was the SAD, the BJPâs former ally. Taking a dig at the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the Prime Minister said it is not concerned about the welfare of the public as it is caught up with its own affairs.And finally, while the studentsâ protests against the NEET-UG paper leak forced Centre on the backfoot, the BJP is now using the same ammunition to target the Bhagwant Mann government over alleged paper leaks in Punjab.
Can BJP upset the AAP-Congress applecart in Punjab?
The BJP clearly has a plan for Punjab. It is bringing in leaders, strengthening its state organisation, reaching out to new social groups and sharpening its attack on both the AAP and the Congress. In the coming months, this push is likely to become more visible through political outreach, policy announcements and an aggressive campaign around governance, development and law and order.
But activity alone does not guarantee electoral success. The BJP may have increased its vote share and political visibility, but it still has to expand beyond its traditional urban base, build trust in rural Punjab and convert imported leaders into an effective ground organisation.So, can it upset the AAP-Congress contest? It is still too early to say. The BJP will leave no stone unturned to make Punjab the 23rd state in its kitty. The real test will be whether its carefully assembled strategy can finally translate into seats.

She also cares deeply about stories around womenâs rights and social change, while two very opinionated dogs make sure she never truly switches off.

NEW DELHI: Hundreds of students continued their protest in Ranchi on Sunday for the fifth consecutive day over alleged irregularities in the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) examination, the JSSC-CGL and other recruitment tests. The demonstrators are seeking a CBI probe into recruitment examinations, cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test and reforms in the stateâs recruitment agencies.The protestors escalated their agitation with a torchlight procession and threatened to march to the Jharkhand Assembly if the state government does not address their demands.The students, who are holding an indefinite sit-in at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, marched to Albert Ekka Chowk on Sunday evening, raising slogans against the JMM-led alliance government and demanding an impartial investigation into the alleged irregularities in the JPSC and JSSC examinations.They warned that if the government failed to respond in the coming days, they would march to the Jharkhand Assembly and stage a gherao.âWe have been holding protests, but no government officials approached us to listen to our concerns on these issues. This clearly shows the insensitivity of this JMM-led alliance government towards the thousands of students and youths of the state,â the protesters alleged.The demonstration began on July 29 and has since drawn support from students across Jharkhand, many of whom say years of preparation for competitive examinations are being undermined by repeated allegations of paper leaks and irregularities.
At the protest site, students continued raising slogans such as âOrder CBI probe in JPSCâ, âLong live Students Unityâ and âShame on Hemant Sorenâ.âPaper leaks in JPSC have happened several times. This time, OMR sheets of candidates have been leaked. Chief Minister Hemant Soren has ordered a CID probe, but we are not satisfied,â JPSC aspirant Rahul Kumar Kranti said.He alleged that previous investigations into the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission CGL paper leak had not resulted in action and claimed that the latest probe could also be âcovered upâ after a few months.âWe have completely lost faith in the ongoing CID probe. We demand a CBI probe into all recruitment examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC over the past seven years. We also demand the chief ministerâs resignation on moral grounds,â Kranti said.The protesters are demanding cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test held on April 19 and an independent investigation by central agencies, including the CBI and the Enforcement Directorate, into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC. They are also seeking the introduction of a fifth option of ânot attemptedâ in OMR sheets.For many of the young demonstrators, the protest has become a struggle over fairness and opportunity rather than merely an examination dispute.âThe careers of thousands of students and aspirants are at stake due to corruption in both agencies. Most of us come from farmersâ families. We only want fair opportunities based on merit,â said Ankit Kumar from Giridih district.Sneha, a tribal student from Ranchi, said protesters wanted strict punishment for those involved in the alleged irregularities and cancellation of the 14th JPSC examination.âI have been preparing for competitive examinations since 2023. But if an equal and fair chance is not given, how can I get a job? I urge CM Soren to listen to our demands,â she said.
Archana Kumari from Palamu said the students would continue their agitation until the government addressed their demands and fixed accountability for the alleged irregularities.Despite days of protest, students said they were determined to continue their sit-in, with volunteers and supporters from different parts of the country helping sustain the demonstration.âThe state government is still in a sleeping mode. We are getting support from across the country. People from various cities are sending food items to the protest site. We are thankful to those helping us continue our protest,â said Shyam Bihari Gupta, a student from Balumath in Latehar district.

The answer may lie not just in exercise and diet, but also in a trip to the theatre, museum or even the cinema.A new study by Japanese researchers has found that older adults who engage more frequently in cultural activities tend to have a lower physiological ageâa measure of how well the body's organs and systems are functioningâthan their actual age, suggesting cultural engagement may be an overlooked tool for healthy ageing.Researchers from the Institute of Science Tokyo analysed 4,207 observations from 1,899 adults aged 50 years and above in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. Participants who more frequently visited cinemas, museums, art galleries, theatres, concerts or the opera had lower physiological age. Every one-point increase in cultural engagement score was associated with a 0.085-year reduction in physiological age, even after adjusting for income, health status, employment, smoking, physical activity and other factors. The association persisted in a four-year follow-up analysis. Physiological age, estimated using 10 markers including blood pressure, lung function, grip strength, walking speed, BMI, haemoglobin, cholesterol and blood sugar, is considered a better predictor of disease and mortality than chronological age.The researchers said cultural engagement may promote healthy ageing by strengthening social connections, reducing loneliness and stress, improving mental well-being and encouraging healthier lifestyles.

Judge leading fast-track paper leak court transferred by Delhi HC
NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has transferred Special Judge Anu Grover Baliga, who was appointed last month to head the designated fast-track court for paper leak cases, as part of a reshuffle involving 138 judicial officers.Judge Baliga was appointed after the Delhi High Court, on July 23, designated a special court to hear criminal cases related to paper leaks and other unfair practices in public examinations, as cited by PTI.
Baliga had spent just over a week at the designated paper leak court after assuming charge on July 25. Special Judge Ajay Gupta, who had earlier been hearing paper leak cases, including the NEET matter, will replace her.According to the Delhi High Court's transfer order issued on Saturday, Judge Baliga has been posted to a special court constituted under the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Act to hear terrorism-related cases.The High Court also appointed Special Judges Vikas Dhull, Prashant Sharma, Pulastya Pramachala, Kiran Bansal and Amit Bansal to NIA courts dealing with terror cases.Prime Minister Narendra Modi had announced the setting up of fast-track courts to ensure the swift disposal of cases related to paper leaks.
Following the announcement, a designated fast-track court was established at Delhi's Rouse Avenue Courts to hear cases under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, and other related offences. All such cases were ordered to be transferred to the designated court.
The court held its first hearing in the NEET paper leak case on July 27, but the proceedings were adjourned at the request of the defence counsel. The matter was then listed for Monday for consideration of the CBI's chargesheet and the bail pleas of two accused.On May 12, the National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (Undergraduate), or NEET-UG, conducted on May 3 for medical admissions following allegations of a paper leak. A re-examination was subsequently held on June 21.

Indiaâs envoy to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra said Pakistan had eroded the foundation of the Indus Waters Treaty over the past five decades. He added that Islamabad had âdismantledâ the goodwill and friendship that underpinned the 1960 agreement, and that New Delhiâs decision to keep the treaty in abeyance merely acknowledged that reality.As reported by US' Newsweek magazine, Kwatra said the treatyâs preamble reflected a commitment made 'in a spirit of goodwill and friendship', but Pakistanâs conduct had weakened that foundation over half a century.
âIt is worth remembering that the treaty's preamble declares it was concluded âin a spirit of goodwill and friendshipâ. Pakistan spent half a century dismantling that goodwill and friendship. The abeyance merely acknowledges what Pakistan's conduct had already destroyed,â Kwatra said.His remarks came after Pakistan recently hosted a conference protesting Indiaâs decision to keep the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance on April 23 last year, a day after Pakistan-trained terrorists killed 26 people in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir.The IWT, signed by India and Pakistan in 1960, divided the waters of the six rivers of the Indus basin between the two countries. India was given control over the eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej which account for about 20 per cent of the basinâs water, while Pakistan received rights over the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab carrying around 80 per cent.
âThat asymmetry stifled development for decades in Indian regions that could have benefited from better water rights. India honoured the treaty anyway,â Kwatra said according to Newsweek.The envoy said Pakistanâs approach towards India had been marked by wars, hostility and cross-border terrorism, citing the 1965, 1971 and 1999 conflicts along with major terror attacks, including the 2001 Parliament attack, the 2008 Mumbai attacks, the 2016 Uri and Pathankot attacks, the 2019 Pulwama attack and the 2025 Pahalgam attack.Kwatra also said that if Pakistan sincerely wanted Indiaâs cooperation on bilateral issues, it must first dismantle the terror infrastructure it has built over the years.On implementation of the treaty, Kwatra alleged that Pakistan had repeatedly delayed Indian projects and opposed efforts to revisit the agreement in view of changing technology and requirements.âPakistan also consistently blocked India's initiatives to renegotiate the treaty in light of six decades of technological change, which would have let India develop its hydropower potential,â Kwatra added.âBit by bit, Pakistan eroded India's faith that it could exercise its rights under the treaty, or hope for a better one suited to today's realities,â he said.Responding to calls for India and Pakistan to resume talks, Kwatra said past initiatives had failed to address core concerns.
âPrime Minister Narendra Modi has clearly voiced Indiaâs stand today: âTerror and talks cannot go together... Terror and trade cannot go together... Water and blood cannot flow together',â Kwatra said.Kwatra also said Pakistan should focus on improving its own water management instead of blaming India for its challenges."The Government of Pakistan would do better to fix its dismal water productivity, than to stage conferences blaming India and issuing threats,â he said, adding, âThe habit of pinning every domestic failure on India has grown old."

With over three years of experience, she focuses on national and global developments, conflict, diplomacy and their impact on India. Her work combines breaking news with in-depth analysis, offering readers context and clarity on the stories shaping the world.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday launched the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan', calling on the country's youth to stay physically and mentally fit and remain away from drug abuse.He said achieving the goal of a developed India requires a healthy, confident and drug-free younger generation. During his address, PM Modi also highlighed how the drugs affect one's family and career.Launching the campaign through video conferencing, PM Modi said the initiative is not only for individuals, families and society but also for the nation. He added that the next 100 Sundays would represent 100 strong steps towards a drug-free India.
"Next 100 Sundays will mark 100 strong steps towards drug-free India," he said.PM Modi also warned that drug trafficking was part of a larger strategy by hostile forces to weaken India and called for greater public vigilance. "Hurting India's interests by supplying drugs part of enemy nations' terror plan," he said.
"Today, all countrymen have come together for a great and important resolve. The campaign we are witnessing is meant for individuals, families and society, but above all, it is for the nation. The campaign, 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat', clearly reflects this resolve. As the country moves towards the goal of a developed India, it is essential that our youth remain physically and mentally healthy and stay away from drugs and other such harmful substances."
"The campaign we are witnessing today is for the individual, the family, and society; above all, it is for the nation. The very name of this movementâthe 'Drug-Free Youth' initiative under the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan â clarifies its resolve. As the nation sets its sights on becoming a Viksit Bharat, it is essential that our youth be healthy in body and mind, brimming with self-confidence, and forever free from the deadly habit of drugs. This is the objective of the campaign... This campaign was launched last year as a pilot project from Kashi... Over 125 spiritual organizations have joined us today for the welfare of crores of our fellow citizens."
"By being addiction-free, you need to protect your potential. You need to be aware that drugs get you high for a short time, but take your career and family to a new low/bottom.
From Varanasi to nationwide campaign
"As the MP from Kashi, I am happy that this campaign was launched last year from the sacred land of Kashi as a pilot project. Along with scientific clarity, it also carries spiritual energy. Social organisations and NGOs have joined this initiative for the welfare of crores of Indians. Together, they have prepared a roadmap through the Kashi Declaration. Today, we are witnessing how the welfare-oriented idea that emerged from Kashi has become a national project. From today, the Nasha Mukt Yuva campaign is being launched across the country."
"The 'Nasha Mukta Yuva Abhiyaan' is launching across the country today... There is immense power in collective action, and today, driven by that very strength, this campaign is set to touch the heart of every young person. Lakhs of youths across the nation took a pledge to stay free from drugs... The pledge taken today will continue to move forward steadily over the next hundred weeks."
"Drug use disturbs focus, takes you away from dreams. If a youth gets addicted to drugs, his aspirations take a hit, family gets shattered."
Govt's anti-drug drive and national campaign
"Today, the government stands firmly with the youth in the campaign against drugs. Strict action is being taken in the country against drug traffickers and drug abuse; there have been many times more arrests compared to before, and drugs worth thousands of crores of rupees have been seized. This shows how tough our government is against drugs."
"Today, thousands of students from schools, colleges and universities are connected online to this programme. Even lakhs of volunteers of MY Bharat are also connected. The NSS jawans too have joined us. People from different sectors, institutions and backgrounds--more than 1 crore youths are together today. I congratulate all of you for this big movement."
Youth key to Viksit Bharat, drugs part of enemy agenda
"You are India's Amrit Peedhi. You will shape your lives over the next 20-25 years, and you will lead the country to the goal of a Viksit Bharat in 2047, and you will be at the helm. You will be the ones to reap its full benefits."
"The country needs your energy, your imagination, and your talent, so staying drug-free is crucial for the country and for your own lives."
"When a young person falls prey to drug addiction, it is not just that individual who loses; a dream is lost. Hostile nations conspire and leave no stone unturned to drag our youth into the trap of addiction. Profiting from the supply of drugs while aiming to destroy a country like ours is part of their terror-driven agenda."
Parents, teachers and society must lead the fight
"We must always keep this in mind: if any child from our home has become a victim of addiction, do not hide it under the guise of social prestige. Seek help from whoever is needed."
"Make efforts to free your child from addiction with medical help."
"We should also foster a culture of open communication with children in the family, so that you can hold their hand before they get caught in such a whirlpool."
"Along with teaching the courses, please also discuss the dangers of drugs with the students. Launch a movement against addiction on your campus. Your efforts can bring big results."
"The support of society, the power of yoga and meditation--these strengthen our inner resolve against addiction. And today, we also have facilities like rehabilitation centres to help quit drugs." "I appeal to all of you that you are all the leaders of this great movement. You have further strengthened my belief that the youth of India is so aware, so sensible, and so serious about their duties."
The 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan' aims to encourage young people to stay away from substance abuse and become ambassadors of positive social change in their communities.
The launch marks the beginning of a 100-week nationwide Jan Bhagidari campaign, under which awareness programmes will be organised every Sunday across the country.Activities will include sports events, walkathons, meditation sessions, cultural programmes, street plays, discussions, art competitions and community engagement initiatives.The campaign brings together educational institutions, youth organisations, civil society groups, industry bodies and more than 125 spiritual organisations to build a collective movement against substance abuse.Youth from over 10,000 locations across the country are participating through schools, colleges, universities, MY Bharat volunteers, NSS volunteers, youth clubs, NGOs and industry associations.

headline: Educated but unemployed: Inside India's broken jobs market and why the 'cockroaches' are fed up

Educated but unemployed: Inside India's broken jobs market and why the 'cockroaches' are fed up
Kanchan Yadav / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 02, 2026, 21:05 IST
