Bankipur Bypoll Result: Low turnout, high stakes - 26 candidates await verdict
The Bankipur Assembly by-election, held on July 30, recorded a voter turnout of 34.30 per cent, marking a drop of more than seven percentage points from the 41.45 per cent polling recorded during the last Assembly election. A total of 26 candidates are in the fray, with the outcome expected to determine whether the BJP retains its long-held stronghold or faces an upset in one of Bihar's most closely watched bypolls.
Bankipur By-Election Result: Prashant Kishor accuses Patna SSP of influencing polls
Hours before the counting of votes in the high-stakes Bankipur Assembly by-election, Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor has accused the Patna Police of attempting to influence the election. In a press conference late Sunday night, he claimed campaign workers were illegally detained, voters were intimidated, and announced that his party would approach the Election Commission and the Supreme Court over the alleged irregularities.
Displaying a notice issued by the Patna Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Kishor said the administration had detained people who had come from outside to campaign on the grounds that they could create a law-and-order problem. He also presented some of the detained individuals before the media.
Questioning the police action, he asked, "How can a person sleeping at home violate Section 144?" He further alleged that police personnel openly moved around Ward No. 22, threatening residents and preventing them from exercising their franchise.
Launching a sharp attack on the Patna SSP, Kishor called him "unprofessional" and referred to the officer's earlier handling of the death of a NEET aspirant, claiming the same officer had prematurely declared it a suicide.
Calling the alleged actions of the administration a "naked dance", Kishor accused the SSP of using the uniform to influence the election. "If the Patna SSP wants to enter politics, he should resign from service," he said.
Kishor said his party would file a formal complaint with the Election Commission within the next two days and, if necessary, move the Supreme Court.
Projecting confidence ahead of the results, the Jan Suraaj chief also claimed that the BJP would lose the by-election by such a wide margin that it would "forget the saying that it can field even a cat or a dog and still win the election."

full_text:
Probe PM CARES Fund, Modi ji will forgive you: CJP takes swipe at RTI activist
The Cockroach Janta Party has attacked an RTI activist who sought probes into founder Abhijeet Dipke's family finances and the outfit's funding. The exchange has sharpened questions over the group's legal status, donations and a Rs 1 crore legal aid fund.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has hit back at an RTI activist who sought an investigation into the finances of founder Abhijeet Dipke's family and the party's funding, accusing him of selectively targeting a private individual.
Reacting to the complaints filed by the Surat-based RTI activist Amit Tiwari, CJP spokesperson Vaishnavi Gaur said, "Those filing RTIs over a private individual's education expenses should also look at the PM CARES Fund. Modi ji will forgive you, don't worry."
Her remarks came after Tiwari on August 1 said he had filed complaints with the Election Commission of India (ECI), the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), and the Maharashtra government.
He has sought a probe into the finances of Dipke's father, Bhagwanrao Dipke, a retired Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC) junior engineer.
The activist questioned how a government employee earning around Rs 60,000-65,000 per month could allegedly afford to send his children to the US for higher education, and urged the Maharashtra government to investigate whether the case involved disproportionate assets.
While questioning the legal status of the CJP, saying that it is functioning like a political party without being registered, Tiwari urged the ECI to examine whether the outfit can legally accept donations despite not being a registered political party.
In a separate complaint to the CBIC, Tiwari sought the imposition of 18 per cent GST on the Rs 1 crore legal defence fund announced by veteran Congress leader Kapil Sibal for CJP protesters.
He further accused CJP leaders of crossing the line during the NEET paper leak agitation by allegedly using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, his late mother, and India's foreign relations, saying those remarks were also part of his complaint.
The controversy stems from Sibal's announcement on July 27 of a Rs 1 crore legal aid fund to support CJP protesters facing police cases following the nationwide agitation.
As questions over the outfit's funding and legal status intensified, the CJP dismissed the complaints as politically motivated.

Congress suspends disqualified ex-MLA ahead of Datia by-poll counting
Former MLA Rajendra Bharti, who was disqualified from the Madhya Pradesh Assembly in April after his conviction in a cheating case, said the action did not affect him and that he would show his strength in the next state polls.
The Congress on Sunday night suspended former Madhya Pradesh MLA Rajendra Bharti from the party's primary membership, hours before counting of votes for the July 30 Datia Assembly by-polls was set to begin.
Bharti, who was disqualified from the Assembly in April after his conviction in a cheating case, said the action did not affect him and that he would show his strength in the next assembly elections.
He also said the decision was wrong and that the public would respond to it in the 2028 Madhya Pradesh Assembly polls.
Bharti had represented the Datia seat before his disqualification. A Delhi court had sentenced him to three years' imprisonment in the cheating case in April, which led to the termination of his Assembly membership.
The by-poll was held on July 30, with 71.44 per cent voting, and the result is to be declared today.
Speaking to reporters, Bharti alleged that the entire episode was a 'conspiracy' by senior BJP leader Narottam Mishra. He also alleged that Congress candidate Ghanshyam Singh had contested the election in collusion with Mishra.
Bharti said his struggle had always been against Mishra and would continue.
Bharti had defeated Mishra by more than 7,700 votes in the 2023 Assembly elections. The Congress fielded Singh in the by-poll, while BJP's Ashutosh Tiwari was among 19 other candidates in the fray.

full_text:
After PM's forgiveness, Delhi Police drops case against minor who abused him
Delhi Police have decided not to pursue a case against the 15-year-old girl seen abusing Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a viral protest video, citing her age, apology, and appeals for leniency. The decision also follows PM Modi's public statement that he had forgiven the "misguided children."
The Delhi Police will not go ahead with the FIR filed against the minor girl seen in a viral video using expletives against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the Cockroach Janta Party's protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar last month.
The decision comes despite a Zero FIR being lodged by Noida Police. The accused later issued an apology video, claiming she is 15 years old and alleging that she made the remarks under the influence of others at the protest site.
In the video released earlier this week, the girl said, “I am only 15 years old. Whatever I did was not worthy of forgiveness. I have said a lot of bad things. This is my first and last mistake. I apologise to the entire country. I am so ashamed. I can't even look at myself. Please forgive me.”
As appeals for leniency gained traction on social media, PM Modi last Friday said that he had forgiven the “misguided children” who had abused him. In an Instagram reel, he said, “Punishing them and dragging them through courts and harassing them will not change the circumstances. I want to forgive them. I request society also to accept what I am saying.”
The girl's mother had also appealed to the Prime Minister to ask the authorities to withdraw the FIR. She said, “PM Modi has shown greatness by forgiving a daughter of the country who had used such dirty words. I thank him with folded hands. Today is her new birth. The prime minister has given her jeevandaan (a new life).”
“I request Prime Minister Narendra Modi, please revoke the FIR filed against her under the wrong name and age... Now she is under your supervision,” she said.
The mother also urged the Prime Minister to ban social media access for minors. “My humble request to PM Modi is that Instagram and Facebook should be stopped for children under 18. They should be allowed to study only. They should not be allowed to protest sites. These children can be easily taken advantage of. They don't know anything about the world,” she said. The case had drawn attention after the video went viral, but Delhi Police have now decided not to proceed against the minor.
STUDENTS PROTEST AT JANTAR MANTAR
The youth-led CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi ended on July 25 after days of mobilisation over the large-scale leaking of papers for competitive examinations. Thousands of student activists took part in the protest, which drew support from innovator-activist Sonam Wangchuk, who joined the agitation during his 26-day hunger strike.
The demonstrations intensified over the course of the protest, with police standoffs and a major march to Parliament on July 20 becoming key developments in the agitation. The protest also led to the resignation of then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The CJP later announced the end of the protest after the government accepted its main demands, including education reforms to improve transparency and accountability in competitive examinations.
The agitation at Jantar Mantar was centred on public anger over the paper leaks in competitive examinations. Student activists gathered in large numbers to press for action, while Wangchuk's participation during his hunger strike added to the visibility of the protest. As the demonstrations grew, confrontations with the police and the march towards Parliament marked a major phase of the campaign.
With the government agreeing to the core demands raised by the protesters, the CJP formally concluded the agitation on July 25. The protest had focused on examination paper leaks, demands for reforms in the education system, and calls for stronger transparency and accountability in the conduct of competitive examinations.

Madhya Pradesh woman strangles nephew-lover with dupatta over marriage pressure
The incident came to light on July 31 after Satyaprakash Gupta was found unconscious in a Maruti Suzuki S-Presso in Madhya Pradesh's Singrauli district.
A woman in Madhya Pradesh has been arrested for allegedly murdering her nephew, with whom she was in a relationship for two years. As per police sources, the woman, identified as Priya Gupta, strangled the victim with a scarf and left his body inside a car after being pressurised for marriage for a prolonged time.
The incident came to light on July 31 after Satyaprakash Gupta was found unconscious in the driver's seat of a Maruti Suzuki S-Presso in Singrauli district. His brother, Rahul Gupta alias Sanjay, alerted police after spotting him inside the vehicle.
The victim was taken to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
Following the murder, the local police registered a complaint, sent the body for a post-mortem, and launched an investigation shortly after. They visited the site and collected evidence for the investigation.
As part of the probe, the police soon discovered Satyaprakash’s link to Priya, his aunt and the widow of late Sunil Gupta. They found out that the two had been in a relationship and the victim was allegedly pressurising her for marriage. The proposals often led to severe disputes between the two.
According to the police, the two met on the day of the murder and had an argument which escalated further. As a result, Priya strangled Satyaprakash to death.
POLICE CRACK THE CASE WITH THE HELP OF CCTV
While investigating, the police found the CCTV footage on the day of the crime, which helped them crack the case.
It showed that Priya was taking Satyaprakash to his parked car around midnight. She later called the victim’s brother and informed him that Satyaprakash was inside the vehicle to divert suspicion after the murder.
Based on the evidence collected, police arrested Priya Gupta and registered a case at Morwa police station under Crime No. 420/26 under Sections 103(1) and 238(A) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). She was later produced before a court, while further investigation into the case is underway.

Pappu Yadav attack row: Accused denies knife charge, says will face probe
Happy Sharma denied carrying a knife during the scuffle at Pappu Yadav's Delhi press conference and said he would cooperate with police. The clash, triggered after a shoe was allegedly thrown, has led to rival allegations of assault and conspiracy.
Hours after Independent MP Pappu Yadav alleged that a man had tried to kill him with a knife during a press conference in Delhi, the accused denied carrying any weapon and said he would appear before police for questioning.
Speaking to India Today TV, Happy Sharma said he and co-accused Sumit had been searched by police stationed outside Yadav's residence before being allowed inside and that no weapons were found on them.
The incident took place during a press conference at Yadav's residence, where a shoe was allegedly thrown at the MP, triggering a scuffle between his supporters and the two men. Sumit, a resident of Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr, was overpowered at the scene and handed over to police.
Police said Yadav's supporters also handed them a knife along with Sumit. Investigators are trying to determine where the weapon came from and whether it was carried by either of the accused.
SHARMA'S VERSION
"We did not go there carrying knives. Police were present outside the MP's house, and we were thoroughly checked. A press conference was underway, and everything was recorded on camera," Sharma said.
He said he and Sumit had gone to Yadav's residence only to question him over remarks concerning Sanatan Dharma and Hindus.
"We only went to ask the MP why he was insulting Sanatan and Hindus. He was placing the saffron flag and Lord Ram's image on the ground. We told him that this should not be done," he said.
Sharma alleged that Yadav's supporters assaulted them after they raised the issue.
"As soon as we said this, his supporters beat us badly," he claimed.
He said he did not know who had thrown the shoe. Sharma also claimed that a group of sadhus had been protesting outside Yadav's residence before he arrived but were removed by police.
Asked whether he would cooperate with the investigation, Sharma said, "I will appear before the police."
YADAV ALLEGES ATTEMPT TO KILL HIM
In a post on X, Yadav shared purported photographs of Sharma with Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and the Deputy Chief Minister and demanded an investigation into his alleged political links.
"This man, who is seen with the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister, carried out a murderous attack on me. Prime Minister and Home Minister, please tell me: who hired him to kill me?" Yadav said.
The MP alleged that Sharma had come to kill him with a knife and claimed a wider conspiracy was behind the incident.
"Every day, some religious figures are saying, 'Burn him, we will give Rs 51 lakh.' Everyone is saying, 'Kill him.' There was a conspiracy to kill me," he said.
SUPPORTER CLAIMS KNIFE WAS DRAWN
Sources said the protest was linked to Yadav's earlier remarks on the alleged theft of donations meant for the Ram Temple.
Sumit reportedly told police that he was angry over what he considered Yadav's insult to Hindu saints.
One of Yadav's supporters alleged that an accused had pulled out a knife before being restrained.
"The moment he pulled out a knife, we acted together and overpowered him. Had we not restrained him, it is possible that Pappu-ji might not have been with us today," the supporter said.
Yadav's media convenor, who said he was injured in the scuffle, accused Delhi Police of failing to protect the MP despite prior warnings.

FIR not withdrawn despite apology: Mother of girl who abused PM seeks protection
Days after the 15-year-old apologised for using derogatory language against PM Modi, her mother said that the FIR against her has not been withdrawn despite her being a minor. If Prime Minister Modi has forgiven her, then the police should also close the matter and withdraw the FIR, the girl's mother said.
The mother of the 15-year-old girl whose video abusing Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar went viral has appealed for the FIR against her daughter to be withdrawn, saying the teenager has realised her mistake and is deeply ashamed.
She said that the FIR against the teenager, who had used extremely derogatory language against the Prime Minister, has not been withdrawn even though PM Modi had said that the "misguided children" should be forgiven and guided on the right path.
Speaking to India Today, the woman said her daughter should not have used abusive language against elders and apologised on her behalf to the entire country.
"My daughter made a mistake. She should not have abused people older than her. On behalf of my daughter, I apologise to the entire country. The most important thing for me is that today she realises her mistake and there is shame in her eyes," she said.
The mother said young people have every right to protest and raise their voices through demonstrations, social media or YouTube, but should avoid using abusive language. "Protests are a separate issue. Children should raise their voice, but they should not abuse elders. That is wrong," she said.
According to her, the girl had left home on July 23 saying she was going shopping ahead of her birthday on August 1. The family only learnt about the incident after relatives sent them the viral video.
The woman claimed the family has been forced to move from place to place after the video surfaced, alleging they have received no security or assistance from the authorities.
"We cannot step outside without covering our faces. Vehicles keep circling our neighbourhood. We have already left our previous residence and are constantly changing locations. We have received no protection and are struggling even for food," she alleged.
She further claimed that despite it becoming known that the girl is a minor, the FIR against her has not been withdrawn.
"No government help or protection has been provided. Even the FIR against my daughter has not been withdrawn. If it has been established that she is a minor, why is the FIR still there?" she asked.
Referring to the girl's public apology, the mother said, "If Prime Minister Modi has forgiven her, then the police should also close the matter and withdraw the FIR."
She also denied having links with any political party, saying the family's only demand is protection. "We are ordinary people. We don't understand politics or big political issues. We just want protection. The police has not contacted me regarding our safety," she said.
The mother said teenagers are easily influenced by their surroundings and social media, adding that her daughter got carried away by the atmosphere at the protest.
"Children between 12 and 18 are at a sensitive age. They have Instagram, Facebook and many other platforms. Sometimes, in the heat of the moment, they don't realise what they are saying because everyone around them is doing the same. Later, they understand what they have done," she said.
She reiterated that what mattered most to her was that her daughter now regrets her actions and understands that she spoke disrespectfully about someone much older than her.
The controversy began after a video of the girl making abusive remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest at Jantar Mantar went viral on social media. A Zero FIR was subsequently registered on July 29 at the Expressway police station in Uttar Pradesh's Gautam Buddh Nagar on the complaint of a Ghaziabad resident.
The girl later released a video apologising with folded hands, claiming she was 15 years old and had been influenced by others at the protest. She said she deeply regretted her remarks and appealed for forgiveness, calling it the "first and last mistake" of her life.
Based on the complaint, the case was registered under Sections 352 (intentional insult to provoke breach of peace), 353(1) (statements conducing to public mischief) and 356(1) (defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. A Zero FIR allows a complaint to be registered at any police station regardless of jurisdiction before being transferred to the appropriate police station for investigation.
Meanwhile, Delhi Police said that they have not registered an FIRn in connection with the incident and that no fresh case will be filed by it.

Wildlife panel clears Madhya Pradesh rail project using 200 hectares in tiger corridor
The wildlife board has given in-principle clearance to a third railway line through the Satpura-Melghat tiger corridor. The nod remains tied to scientific assessment and final design of mitigation structures for animal movement.
The Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (SC-NBWL) has given in-principle clearance to a railway line project that will use more than 200 hectares of forest land within a tiger corridor between the Satpura Tiger Reserve in Madhya Pradesh and the Melghat Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra.
The apex wildlife body recommended the project subject to several conditions, including the adoption of mitigation measures based on a scientific study by the State Forest Research Institute in Jabalpur. It has also said its site inspection committee must revisit the area after examining the study and other relevant data.
According to the project’s wildlife conservation management report, the proposed railway line will affect the Satpura-Melghat tiger corridor at two locations as well as the eco-sensitive zone in the ecologically significant Satpura-Pench-Melghat landscape.
The report said the corridor is a crucial stretch for maintaining forest contiguity in Satpura and for the sustenance of tigers in Central India. “It helps in maintaining biodiversity, allows tiger population to interbreed, permit movement of all animals and plants across a larger landscape and provide access to larger habitats, enable species to cross hostile areas, increase their range and colonise new sites,” the report said.
The report also flagged possible impacts on wildlife. It said the railway line may restrict, inhibit or prevent the movement of species because of a combination of traffic noise, train movement, pollution and human activity. It also warned of a possible rise in human-animal conflict due to increased human presence and shrinking habitat. “Railways may disrupt the normal home range of wild animals, forcing them to explore new areas, where they may come into conflict with human beings,” the report said.
The project involves the Central Railway building a third railway line from Jujharpur in Betul district to Chichonda in Narmadapuram district in Madhya Pradesh.
A committee set up by the SC-NBWL inspected the site in March this year. The minutes of an SC-NBWL meeting held on July 9 showed that the committee found that while the railway department had proposed several wildlife overpasses to reduce the project’s impact, their detailed engineering designs were still not complete.
It also noted that a comprehensive scientific assessment of the project’s likely impact and suitable landscape-level mitigation measures had not been completed at the time of inspection.
While recommending the project for clearance, the SC-NBWL said all mitigation measures must follow the scientific study report from the State Forest Research Institute, Jabalpur. It added, “Upon receipt and examination of the scientific study and other relevant data, the site inspection committee shall revisit the project area and submit definitive recommendations regarding the location, dimensions, design, and connectivity of the wildlife mitigation structures.”
In sum, the wildlife body has backed the railway project in principle, but tied its recommendation to further scientific assessment and final decisions on the design and connectivity of wildlife mitigation structures in the Satpura-Melghat corridor.

Why Dharmendra Pradhan's homecoming has set the cat among pigeons in Odisha
Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as a Union minister and a hero's welcome in Bhubaneswar have reignited speculation over his next political move. Will one of the most formidable leaders of the BJP become the CM? Experts suggest that the road ahead depends on several factors.
A resignation in New Delhi has resulted in the politics in Odisha hotting up. While it was watching the fast-paced developments in neighbouring West Bengal, the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union Education Minister and him receiving a hero's welcome have sparked speculation over the BJP heavyweight's next political move.
For the uninitiated, Dharmendra Pradhan, who's the Lok Sabha MP from Sambalpur, is credited for building the party's organisational muscles in Odisha. He commands the loyalty of a large number of MLAs and ministers, and is an alternative power centre in the state.
While the BJP projected Pradhan's Odisha homecoming as a show of strength, political observers in Bhubaneswar see it as the start of speculation about the leader's next role in the state where he built the saffron party from scratch. The reception at Bhubaneswar airport, attended by several Odisha ministers and MLAs, made many ask if the BJP was planning to assign the top job in the state to him. Just the buzz that Pradhan could be positioned for the CM's role has unnerved some in Odisha's political circles, say experts.
The circumstances of Pradhan's resignation in New Delhi and the political mood in Odisha, however, make these speculations far from straightforward. Two Odisha-based political observers and an insider in the BJP's political circle in Odisha say, while Pradhan remains one of the BJP's most formidable leaders in the state, the road ahead would be based on calculations of the party high-command. However, they see him as a rightful claimant to the CM's post.
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister after the CJP-led agitation over alleged examination irregularities demanded he quit from the post on the grounds of accountability. Pradhan's return to the east-coastal state has ignited speculation over whether the saffron party is scripting a role change for the leader who's been part of the Narendra Modi Cabinet since 2014. Though Pradhan has resigned as a Union minister, he continues to be the Sambalpur MP.
A Bhubaneswar-based journalist, who spoke to India Today Digital on condition of anonymity, says speculation about Pradhan's return to state politics has unsettled internal equations and "set the cat among the pigeons". We'll get into the explanation of why the journalist said so. But before that, let's first have a look at how Pradhan's resignation has gone down with people in Odisha.
A HERO'S WELCOME, BUT ALSO AN IMAGE RESET FOR PRADHAN?
Bhubaneswar-based senior journalist and political commentator Rajaram Satpathy says the optics of Pradhan's welcome at the Bhubaneswar airport were significant and noteworthy.
"Having relinquished his post as Union education minister in the face of fierce agitation over the NEET-UG question paper leak, Dharmendra Pradhan came home Tuesday [July 28] for the first time as an MP. There was, however, a good crowd at the airport to welcome him. The scene was reminiscent of the welcome NDA MPs gave him outside Parliament recently. Five of 16 ministers of the Mohan Charan Majhi-led government and 21 party MLAs were on hand to receive him," Satpathy tells India Today Digital.
Satpathy also says that he believes the reception carried a political message. "Observers view the heroic welcome accorded to Pradhan as a desperate image make-over bid to sustain him in politics in the days ahead," explains Satpathy.
Despite the setback, Satpathy argues that Pradhan's stature within the BJP remains significant.
"Close to the BJP top brass in New Delhi, Pradhan is rated an influential national Odia leader after [former Odisha chief ministers] Biju Patnaik and Harekrushna Mahatab. He is also credited with building the BJP's state unit almost from scratch to what it is today," says Satpathy.
However, he says Pradhan's resignation has altered some public perceptions in Odisha.

full_text:
New Delhi: More than half of the overall respondents of the latest snap poll by CVoter were not satisfied with Modi government’s handling of the paper leaks issue, the polling agency said in a statement Sunday. This number was 40 percent among NDA voters.
The polling agency added that PM Narendra Modi Modi continues to command a 12-percentage point lead over Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi when it comes to ‘most popular youth leader among Indians’. It went further to add that opinion remains sharply divided over CJP’s demand for withdrawal of all FIRs against protesters.
The survey findings and projections are based on CVoter Snap Poll CATI (Computer Assisted Telephone Interviewing) interviews conducted among 18+ adults nationwide (BARC-HSM) between 29 and 30 July. The sample spread of 1,349 respondents is spread across all districts covering all states, said CVoter. According to the polling agency, the data is weighted to the known demographic profile as per the census and final ECI results.
“Though still far behind (Modi), Rahul Gandhi is gaining as the most popular youth leader,” read the statement by CVoter, adding that “anti-incumbency among the youth is a serious issue” and that while a “majority of Indians want proper investigations into alleged police brutality; a majority also (wants) police action against those who indulged in violence and were offensively abusive”.
The statement went on to add, “Overall, the paper leak and the CJP protests have inflicted political damage to the NDA government. But they are not the main challenge. The real challenge is the frustration of the youth whose rising aspirations are hitting a roadblock of limited opportunities.”
Protests spearheaded by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over his handling of the NEET-UG (2026) paper leak last week forced the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The government also announced fast-track courts to deal with paper leak cases and steered an amendment to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, through both houses of Parliament, which proposes harsher punishment for those found using or facilitating unfair means.

58% NDA supporters want police brutality probed
According to the latest CVoter snap poll, 12 percent of respondents said they saw CJP being the voice of the youth and almost 50 percent said they would support the movement on other issues as well in the future.
As many as 31.7 percent of the respondents said stricter laws against paper leaks should have been the top priority for the government, followed by 27 percent who said it should have been Pradhan’s resignation, and 17 percent who said formation of an expert panel should have been top priority.
Were they satisfied with the discussion in Parliament on paper leaks? According to the polling agency, 35 percent of respondents were satisfied and 39 percent weren’t.
Opinion was sharply divided, however, on CJP’s demand for withdrawal of all FIRs against students who took part in demonstrations held across the country.
“On the face of it, a larger proportion of respondents (35.5 percent) want all FIRs to be withdrawn while less than one fourth say withdraw FIRs against only peaceful protestors. Significantly, more than one third of the respondents say investigative agencies should probe all FIRs first before arriving at a decision,” said CVoter.
However, 62.7 percent of respondents were of the opinion that allegations of police brutality during the protests must be investigated. “Interestingly, even almost 58 percent of those who support the NDA want a proper investigation,” the polling agency said.
At the same time, 54.2 percent of respondents want the police to act against protesters who used abusive language and uploaded objectionable content on social media. Among INDIA bloc supporters, 45 percent back police action in this regard.
For 27.6 percent of respondents, student anger over paper leaks was the trigger that earned the CJP its support. “Close to 50 percent of the respondents say they will support (CJP for other causes too) while less than 30 percent say they won’t. Almost 38 percent of NDA voters say they will support future CJP protests and movements,” CVoter said.

[SEP] New Delhi: Challenged by BJP MPs to authenticate his claim that the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh supported the Emergency, Congress MP Jairam Ramesh has submitted to the Rajya Sabha Chairperson three letters written in 1975 by then Sangh chief Balasaheb Deoras—which, he claims, vindicate his stand.
full_text:
New Delhi: Challenged by BJP MPs to authenticate his claim that the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh supported the Emergency, Congress MP Jairam Ramesh has submitted to the Rajya Sabha Chairperson three letters written in 1975 by then Sangh chief Balasaheb Deoras—which, he claims, vindicate his stand.
“…The ban on RSS may be lifted and the RSS and its volunteers may participate in the development of plans which are being implemented in all the spheres in the country,” reads an appeal made by Deoras in one of the letters.
Ramesh has submitted three letters by Deoras—two to then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and one to Acharya Vinoba Bhave.
Deoras had appealed to Gandhi to lift the ban on RSS. He had also congratulated Gandhi after the Supreme Court had upheld the validity of her 1971 election, writing: “Let me congratulate you as five judges of the Supreme Court have declared the validity of your election.”
The letters indicate that the tone and tenor of the correspondence was accommodative towards the government. Deoras had repeatedly appealed for the ban on RSS to be lifted, for its jailed volunteers to be released, and for the organisation to be allowed to contribute to government programmes.
The RSS was banned after Emergency was declared in 1975 as the Indira Gandhi government accused the organisation of opposing it and threatening law and order. The RSS had supported the Jayaprakash (JP) movement, which had called for nationwide protests and demanded Gandhi’s resignation after she was found guilty of electoral malpractice by the Allahabad High Court—a ruling that was later overturned by the Supreme Court.
Congress has cited the letters to argue that they reflect an accommodative approach by RSS leadership towards the Indira Gandhi government. The BJP and the RSS have, however, maintained that the letters were written to seek the release of jailed volunteers and the withdrawal of the ban on the organisation, rather than as an endorsement of the Emergency itself.
Ramesh, Congress general secretary (communications), Friday submitted to Rajya Sabha Chairman Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan what he described as “authenticated historical documents” after BJP MPs challenged him to substantiate his assertion that the then RSS chief had written to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in “support” of the Emergency.
In a covering letter dated 31 July, Ramesh wrote that the issue had arisen during an exchange in the House the previous evening. “Yesterday evening I had made a response to a statement made by the Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs. BJP MPs challenged me to authenticate my assertion that the RSS Chief had written to Indira Gandhi in support of the Emergency. I attach herewith my authentication for the records—2 letters to Indira Gandhi and 1 letter to Acharya Vinoba Bhave.”
The documents include authenticated extracts from Five Headed Monster: A Factual Narrative of the Genesis of Janata Party, a 1978 book by Brahm Dutt reproducing three letters attributed to Deoras during the Emergency. The pages attached by Ramesh carry his signature certifying them as authenticated copies.
The first letter, dated 22 August 1975, was written from Yerwada Central Jail after RSS’s ban. Referring to Indira Gandhi’s Independence Day address, Deoras had described it as “suitable for the occasion and well balanced”. Defending the RSS against the allegations levelled, he had written, “The work of RSS lies extended to every nook and corner of the whole of India, it is necessary to properly utilise such power of the Sangh for the upliftment of our country.”
He had also appealed for the ban on the RSS to be lifted and written that if Gandhi thought it proper, “my meeting with you will be a source of pleasure to me.”
In the second letter, dated 10 November 1975, Deoras had congratulated Gandhi after the Supreme Court had upheld the validity of her election. He had again appealed for withdrawal of the ban on RSS, seeking to distance the organisation from the Jayaprakash Narayan movement, and saying that the Sangh had “no connection with these movements”.
The third letter, addressed to Acharya Vinoba Bhave, urged him to remove the prime minister’s “wrong impression” of the RSS, so that “the ban on RSS may be lifted and the RSS and its volunteers may participate in the development of plans which are being implemented in all the spheres in the country”.
(Edited by Mannat Chugh)

full_text:
New Delhi: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge criticised the decision to replace the Indian hockey team’s traditional blue jersey with a saffron-coloured kit for the upcoming FIH Hockey World Cup, alleging that the move reflected an attempt to impose a political ideology on national sporting symbols.
The controversy erupted after Hockey India unveiled a new saffron primary jersey for the men’s and women’s teams. The federation has said that the redesign was meant to improve player visibility against blue synthetic turfs and that saffron was chosen as one of the colours of the Indian tricolour.
But this has raised questions over the decision and has drawn criticism from opposition leaders and some former players such as Olympic gold medal-winning captain Vasudevan Baskaran and former India captain Viren Rasquinha.
In a post made in Hindi on X, Kharge said the issue was “not merely a sporting decision” but one that was linked to the emotions of millions of Indians and the country’s sporting tradition. He added that Indian teams have long been recognised as the “Men in Blue”, “The Blues” and the “Blue Tigers”, calling the blue jersey a legacy of Indian sport.

Questioning the rationale behind the move, the Congress president wrote, “Today it is difficult to understand why there was a need to change this historic identity.”
“The question is not about any colour, but about the decision-making process, transparency and respect for public sentiment,” he said. Kharge elaborated that his objection was not with the colour saffron itself. “Saffron, white and green are all colours of our national flag and are also represented with equal respect in the Indian National Congress flag.”
The Congress chief also accused the Bharatiya Janata Party-Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (BJP-RSS) ideological ecosystem of attempting to leave its mark on national institutions and symbols. “It is unfortunate that those whose ideological tradition had no contribution to the freedom movement are today in a hurry to leave their ideological imprint on every national symbol and every public institution.”
“History knows that the RSS had fiercely opposed the Tricolour and Sardar Patel had also warned them.”
Kharge also claimed that the jersey issue was part of a larger pattern of changes to public institutions and symbols.
“From road pavements to Parliament staff uniforms, from the Doordarshan logo and now the players’ jerseys — all without broad public consensus,” he wrote. Calling for the decision to be reversed, he said, “National symbols, sports and players should not be made instruments of narrow political experiments.”
He urged the government to “immediately reconsider this decision” and asked why Hockey India’s Executive Board was not consulted before the decision to change the jersey colour was changed. The federation has denied any political motive behind the change. The issue has sparked a wider political debate, with the Congress accusing the government of attempting to reshape national sporting symbols.

[SEP] New Delhi: When the 2025 Delhi Assembly elections were announced, all the contesting parties knew that the key to power in the National Capital rested with its women voters. And so, all parties rushed to woo them, with promises of monthly cash benefits, free bus rides and dedicated pension schemes.
full_text:
New Delhi: When the 2025 Delhi Assembly elections were announced, all the contesting parties knew that the key to power in the National Capital rested with its women voters. And so, all parties rushed to woo them, with promises of monthly cash benefits, free bus rides and dedicated pension schemes.
Over 1.5 years later, the BJP government in Delhi is set to roll out one such promise, but with the quintessential ‘conditions apply’.
The Delhi Lakshmi Yojana, which offers a monthly assistance of Rs 2,500 to women from Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), is a series of eligibility and disqualification hoops, and even guidelines on how this money should be used. The benefit, which is expected to reach about 17 lakh women, according to officials, will cover women between 21 and 60 years of age whose family income is up to Rs 2.5 lakh per annum, and has been living in Delhi for at least 10 years.
But a woman who has more than three children, or who pays income tax or files GST returns, or whose family owns a four-wheeler, or whose family consumes more than 2,400 units of electricity, or who has a criminal record will not be eligible.
Those applying will also have to submit an endorsement letter from the MP or MLA of their constituency. Every application will go through a four-stage verification process.
And once a woman does succeed in jumping through all of these hoops to qualify for the scheme, she is still not entitled to receive the money directly in her bank account. Instead, she is given two ways to receive the benefit— she can either choose to have the entire sum of Rs 2,500 invested in a Recurring Deposit (RD) or Fixed Deposit (FD), or receive Rs 1,000 through a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) wallet and have the remaining Rs 1,500 deposited into an RD or an FD account.
And if she picks the second option, she still doesn’t get to choose what she would spend this money on. The CBDC wallet comes with its own list of goods and services that the money cannot be used for—including alcoholic beverages, tobacco products, and lottery tickets.
The destiny of election-linked freebies goes through a similar lifecycle in most states—a broad, open-ended announcement right before the elections to woo voters, a harsh reality check owing to financial constraints once the party actually comes to power, a realisation that the promise in its entirety may be unsustainable, and then a scheme that is just a faint shadow of the promise that birthed it.
In Maharashtra as well, in a bid to retain power, the BJP-led ruling Mahayuti promised cash handouts of Rs 1,500 to women under the Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana in 2024. To bolster its commitment, over 2.3 crore beneficiaries received monthly installments of the Rs 1,500 payout for months before the polls.
However, since then, the number of beneficiaries under the scheme has fallen from to 1.66 crore, with around 81 lakh registered beneficiaries being removed from the scheme following an e-KYC verification drive, citing non-eligibility. Ineligible beneficiaries included over-age women, vehicle owners, government employees and even 14,000 men.
Similarly, the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana, a Bihar government initiative, was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi a month before the polls in November 2025, to transfer R. 10,000 each into the bank accounts of 75 lakh women across Bihar.
The scheme promised the “possibility” of additional financial support of up to Rs 2 lakh in subsequent phases. But these installments haven’t reached the women so far.
Then Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar had announced in January that action to release the second installment under the scheme had been initiated, but Opposition in the state has alleged that the state’s coffers are empty and the installments haven’t come through.
While the schemes are often credited by analysts and even parties themselves for bringing them into power, their implementation is often a far cry from the promises that are made during elections, no matter the party in question— whether it is the Mahayuti government in Maharashtra, the BJP government in Delhi and Haryana, the Aam Aadmi Party government in Punjab, or the Congress government in Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh.
For a state government, the implementation of broad-based election promises also often turns out to be a double edged sword. For instance, non-implementation of its promise of Rs 1,000 for women continued to harm the AAP government’s credibility not just in Punjab but even in Delhi.
But implementation of the five promised guarantees in Karnataka led to then Deputy Chief Minister DK Shivakumar admitting that the state did not have funds for development. The guarantee schemes also had a direct impact on development in the state, with a 2025 Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) report saying that they reduced capital expenditure towards infrastructure by around Rs 5,229 crore in 2023-24.
Madan Sabnavis, Chief Economist at CARE Ratings, explains that whenever elections are being held, there is always a tendency for these policies to be spoken about, but at the end of the day, all governments have to function according to the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) rules and the fiscal space available to them.
“I think we have to take (such announcements) with a pinch of salt because these are only announcements which are made. Finally, at the end of the day, if you see what is delivered, it’s all based on what can be accommodated given the budgetary numbers. States have to go according to their fiscal deficit ratios,” he explains.
A tale of two states: Delhi & Punjab
When the Aam Aadmi Party threw its hat in the ring for the Punjab Legislative Assembly elections in 2022, it emerged as a major alternative to the Congress, the Shiromany Akali Dal and the BJP in the state. And one of their five guarantees was a monthly allowance of Rs 1,000 to women aged 18 years or above.
However, what followed over the next four years was a prolonged wait that may also have hurt Arvind Kejriwal’s campaign in the 2025 Delhi Assembly elections, which the AAP lost to the BJP.
While the AAP government never openly blamed financial constraints for the delay in implementation of the promise, the state’s economy has often been a cause of concern. Its revenue deficit, when adjusted for inflation, increased five-fold from Rs 544 crore in 1990-91 to Rs 24,588 crore in 2022-23, and its debt-to-GSDP ratio has remained between 45 percent and 47 percent in the recent estimates.
It is projected to be 45.1 per cent in the state’s 2026-27 budget—the highest among large states.
It was only on 1 July, with just months to go before the next Punjab elections, that the government rolled out the ‘Mawan Dhiyan Satkar Yojna’ to provide financial assistance of Rs 1,000 per month to general category women, and Rs 1,500 per month to women belonging to the Scheduled Castes. A dedicated budgetary outlay of Rs 9,300 crore was earmarked for the scheme for FY 2026-27. Meanwhile, Punjab’s outstanding debt is projected to approach the Rs 4.50 lakh-crore mark during FY 2026-27.
The scheme was announced in the 2026-27 budget, which Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema called “Saari Guarantiyan Puri Karan Wala Budget” (a budget to fulfil all guarantees), saying that 97 percent of all adult women in Punjab will be eligible under the scheme.
The money has initially been transferred in the bank accounts of nearly 36 lakh women, releasing three monthly installments together. And those who have registered themselves but haven’t got the money yet have been assured that they would receive the installment on 1 August.
Karnataka’s conundrum
While Punjab’s promise remained on paper for 4 of its 5-year term, the opposite is happening in Karnataka. The government is implementing its promises, but has been criticised for doing so at the cost of development.
For the Congress party, the June 2023 victory in Karnataka was historic. It was a comeback of sorts for the party that has been on a downward spiral across states since 2014, when it lost power at the Centre to the BJP. The party not just won 135 seats, it did so with the largest vote share seen in Karnataka since 1989.
However, two months after the victory, the state government came under fire from the Opposition when deputy chief minister DK Shivakumar made a statement that it did not have funds for development as it had budgeted Rs 40,000 crore for implementing the five election gurantees—free electricity of up to 200 units per month, free 10 kg rice per month, free bus rides for women, Rs 2,000 per month per woman head of a family, and Rs 2,000 monthly stipend to unemployed graduates and diploma-holders.
In February this year, DK Shivakumar reportedly admitted that the guarantees were a “burden” on the state exchequer, but that they will continue. However, he hinted at some pruning in the list, saying many people were drawing benefits in the name of ‘dead people’.
Last month, he declared that the beneficiaries have to submit fresh applications to continue to avail of the benefits, in another bid to streamline the beneficiaries.
Meanwhile, the spending on these schemes is estimated to be Rs 51,034 crore—14 percent of the state’s total expenditure—in 2025-26, and Rs 51,286 crore in 2026-27, which is 12 percent of the total expenditure, excluding debt repayment.
According to a 2025 report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on the state’s finances for 2023-24, the five guarantee schemes accounted for 15 percent of the revenue expenditure for 2023-24.
The schemes also contributed to a 12.54 percent increase in expenditure from the previous year, resulting in a revenue deficit of Rs 9,271 crore.
The state’s fiscal deficit increased from Rs 46,623 crore in 2022-23 to Rs 65,522 crore in 2023-24. The report said that in order to finance the guarantee schemes and the deficits arising due to them, the state availed net market borrowing of Rs 63,000 crore— Rs 37,000 crore more than the previous year’s net borrowings.
The report made another revelation: the guarantee schemes also reduced the capital expenditure towards infrastructure by around Rs 5,229 crore when compared with the previous year.
A transactional democracy
According to experts, the fate of election-linked freebies reflects both the ground realities of implementing welfare schemes and the increasingly transactional nature of Indian democracy.
Sabnavis says that as a social welfare programs, which, he says, are loosely called ‘freebies’, several governments have been announcing financial schemes for women.
“Now they are supposedly cleaning up the sheets, and lots of women have been excluded. So the overall cost of the programme itself has come down. If you’re looking at it from the practical way of doing it, there’s always a limited space which is there for governments to provide for these social welfare programmes, especially when they are cash transfers,” he explains.
Sabnavis says that if a scheme is linked to employment or education, like midday meals, they are usually carried out, while cash transfers are usually cut down.
“Once you’re in power, you become responsible because you have to be responsible because of the constraints you have. There’s a fixed amount of revenue you earn, and a fixed amount of borrowing. Interest, subsidies, pension, salaries have to be paid. They do whatever is possible with what gets left over. So, they cut back on expenditure from the scheme, or keep renaming things, or divert funds from some other scheme,” he explains.

According to political analyst Prof Chandrachur Singh, a professor of political science at Delhi University, political parties no longer treat their voters as citizens, but as consumers.
“And voters know this. Indian voters are very conscious of their right to vote, but the fact of the matter is that they do not look to vote for empowerment. They know that whosoever comes to power, it’s not going to lead to a massive change in their day to day life. So whatever they can get at that point in time is good enough,” he explains.
Consumers also have short-term memory, Singh asserts. “There used to be a generation of consumers of my father’s generation who were very much attached to any object that they would purchase. Remember the pen that we used to value, now you use the pen and then throw it because you don’t have any attachment with it. I think that is an analogy I will use to describe what’s happening right now.”
Diluting ‘sankalp’
In September 2024, weeks before the Haryana Assembly elections, BJP National President JP Nadda released the ‘Sankalp Patra’ for the polls in Rohtak with much fanfare. This document promised that “all women in Haryana” will receive Rs 2,100 per month.
Last year in September, the Nayab Saini government notified the ‘Deen Dayal Lado Lakshmi Yojana 2025’, stipulating a benefit of Rs 2,100 per month for every eligible woman.
However, the notification considerably reduced the ambit of the scheme, and subsequent notifications shortened it further— by January, only 10 lakhs of 80 lakh potential beneficiaries had registered for the scheme.
When the scheme was announced, it included only women who are 23 years and older, from families with a verified yearly income of not exceeding Rs 1 lakh per year, and with a 15-year residency condition.
It excluded women who are in receipt of any of the 10 social security financial assistance schemes listed in the scheme, or who is receiving any other financial assistance from any government or local/statutory body, owned and controlled by the government, or if she is an income tax payee, among other things.
In January this year, the cabinet approved another watering down of the scheme, splitting the Rs 2,100 monthly benefit, and locking half in a state-operated deposit account. This amount accumulated in the deposit account will be paid to the beneficiaries on maturity, and the tenure of the deposit will be decided by the government, although it cannot exceed five years.
But the additional eligibility criteria has slightly expanded the ambit of the scheme, making those women eligible whose children study in government schools and score more than 80 percent in their Class 10 or 12 board exams or achieve grade-level competency under NIPUN Bharat Mission in classes 1 to 4, or mothers who successfully rehabilitate their children from severe or moderate acute malnutrition.
For such women, the annual income cap is fixed at Rs 1.8 lakh compared to the Rs 1 lakh cap applicable to other beneficiaries.
A new-year gift
In the neighbouring Himachal Pradesh, the Congress party had promised to hike the number of free units of electricity to 300, and provide Rs 1,500 per month for all women between 18 to 60 years, before coming to power in the state in 2022.
A month before this promise by the Congress, the then BJP government in the State had launched the ‘125 Units of Free Electricity’ scheme, claiming that over 14 lakh electricity consumers were now getting zero electricity bills.
The Congress won the election. And instead of a hike, the new government had to by 2024 rationalise even the 125 units free scheme, excluding tax-paying consumers from it and restricting its application to ‘one family one meter’.
Citing severe financial crunch, Industries Minister Harshwardhan Chauhan had told the media that while the BJP government launched the scheme, the burden was borne by the Congress government.
“Rs 900 cr were spent on this scheme in 2022-23. This escalated to Rs 1,000 cr in 2023-24,” he was quoted as saying in 2024. On 1 January 2025, Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu’s new year’s gift to his state came in the form of relinquishment of the subsidy on all five power connections registered in his name. Simultaneously, he urged affluent citizens in the state to also relinquish their subsidies.
In the budget this year, with Assembly elections scheduled for late next year, the government finally announced that it would provide 300 units of free electricity per month, but only to “one lakh poorest families” in the state, under the Mukhya Mantri Apna Sukhi Parivar Yojana. The “sisters” of these 1 lakh families will also be provided Rs 1,500 per month, by expanding the ‘Indira Gandhi Pyari Behna Sukh Samman Nidhi Yojana’ in a phased manner.
As per news reports, 1.16 lakh families have been identified for the scheme. For other domestic consumers, the state government provides a subsidy of Rs 1.72 per unit in the 125-300 units consumption bracket, lowering their pay from the actual tariff of Rs 5.89 per unit. Those consuming up to 125 units per month will continue to receive a zero-bill, for up to two electricity meters per household.

full_text:
New Delhi: In 1990, the All India Students’ Association (AISA) was founded as the student wing of the CPI(ML) Liberation, opposing what it called the Congress’ “anti-people” economic policies and neoliberal reforms.
Today, some of the organisation’s most successful student leaders have ended up working for the very party AISA was created to fight—aiding and advising senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, writing speeches for his sister and politician Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, managing the party’s election campaign and running its social media operations.
It is one of the more striking political journeys to emerge from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) where the AISA long won elections.
Since 1990, AISA has won the JNU Students’ Union (JNUSU) presidency 14 times through 13 leaders. While some of its leaders remained with the CPI(ML) Liberation, many exchanged campus activism for classrooms as professors and researchers. Some became political consultants and at least three eventually crossed over to the Congress.
The renewed spotlight on AISA comes after its current president, Neha Bora, ended a 23-day hunger strike during the Cockroach Janata Party-led student protests in New Delhi last month.
Her speeches against Brahminism, the RSS and BJP, along with her participation in activist Sonam Wangchuk’s hunger strike, have made her one of the country’s most recognisable student leaders. But Bora is only the latest face of an organisation that has shaped JNU politics for more than three decades.
Here’s a look at what AISA’s former JNUSU presidents did after graduating from university.
Chandrashekhar Prasad (President 1994-95 & 1995-96)
Few AISA leaders are remembered as fondly as Chandrashekhar Prasad, better known as Chandu. He first served as JNUSU vice-president in 1993-94 before being elected president for two consecutive terms. A gifted speaker, Chandu played a key role in establishing AISA as one of the strongest political forces on the JNU campus.
He was known for speaking out against communal politics, supporting the Mandal Commission, and arguing that student politics should stay connected to the struggles of workers, farmers and other marginalised communities beyond the university.
After leaving JNU, Chandu returned to his home state of Bihar and became a full-time organiser with CPI(ML) Liberation. Based in Siwan, he worked with landless labourers and Dalit communities, taking on feudal interests and the region’s powerful criminal-politician nexus.
On 31 March, 1997, while addressing a public meeting, he was shot dead in broad daylight along with two others. His killing triggered protests across universities, and in 2012, a special CBI court sentenced three of the gunmen to life imprisonment. While the CPI(ML) Liberation has continued to link his killing with late RJD strongman and gangster Mohammad Shahabuddin, the probe couldn’t establish so.
Today, Chandrashekhar Prasad remains one of AISA’s most iconic figures and is widely remembered as a symbol of Left student activism.
Mona Das (President 2004-05 & 2005-06)
One of the few AISA leaders to win the JNUSU presidency twice, Mona Das represented a generation of student leaders who combined campus activism with scholarship. During her tenure, she focused on public education, democratic student participation and gender equality while helping consolidate AISA’s influence on campus.
Rather than entering electoral politics after leaving JNU, Das chose academia. She currently teaches political science at Delhi University’s Satyawati College and continues to write and teach on questions of democracy, constitutional values and gender. Unlike several of her contemporaries, she has largely stayed away from active party politics and maintains a relatively low public profile.
Sandeep Singh (President 2007-08)
Few former AISA leaders have travelled as far politically as Sandip Singh and that too in mainstream politics. Originally from Uttar Pradesh’s Pratapgarh district, he first became active in student politics at Allahabad University before joining JNU.
After leaving JNU, Singh gradually moved away from the Left and joined the Congress ecosystem. During the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, he worked closely with Rahul Gandhi, helping draft speeches and advising on campaign strategy and alliance politics. He later became part of Priyanka Gandhi Vadra’s core team. He now appears to have been sidelined but enjoyed proximity with the Congress high command for several years and elections.
Today, Singh describes himself as a political consultant, researcher and Union Public Service Commission faculty member while continuing to work in political communication. He also reportedly brought in former JNUSU president Akbar Chaudhary to the party later.
Sucheta De (President 2011-12)
Sucheta De became JNUSU president when campus elections resumed after several years, leading AISA back to the forefront of student politics. She focused on democratic student representation, accessible education and opposition to the growing privatisation of higher education.
Unlike several former presidents, De stayed firmly within the Left movement after leaving campus. She is now a central committee member of the CPI(ML) Liberation and continues to play an active role in organisational work, civil liberties campaigns and democratic rights movements across the country. She was seen actively supporting the CJP as well.
Akbar Chaudhary (President 2013-14)
Akbar Chaudhary’s career took him from campus politics into election management. After his time at JNU, he joined political strategist Prashant Kishor’s team and worked on major election campaigns, including those in Bihar and West Bengal.
He later established his own consultancy, Matrix Intelligence, which has handled several political campaigns, including the Congress’ during the 2022 Himachal Pradesh assembly election and 2023 Chhattisgarh assembly election.
Alongside political consulting, he has also taught at Aligarh Muslim University. In 2016, JNU’s Gender Sensitisation Committee Against Sexual Harassment cleared him of harassment charges made against him two years earlier.
Ashutosh Kumar Yadav (President 2014-15)
Ashutosh Kumar Yadav chose a quieter path after leaving student politics. Following his presidency, he completed his doctoral research at JNU before joining Lalit Narayan Mithila University in Darbhanga as an assistant professor of political science.
Today, his work is centred on teaching and academic research rather than active politics, making him one of several former JNUSU leaders who transitioned into higher education instead of electoral life.
Mohit Kumar Pandey (President 2016-17)
Mohit Kumar Pandey also moved from Left student politics into the Congress. After leaving JNU, he worked closely with Priyanka Gandhi Vadra’s political team in Uttar Pradesh before heading the Uttar Pradesh Congress’s social media operations.
His work has since expanded into political communication, campaign strategy, digital outreach and public policy. Like Sandeep Singh, Pandey is among former Left student leaders who eventually shifted to the Congress despite AISA’s longstanding ideological opposition to Congress-era economic reforms.
Geeta Kumari (President 2017-18)
Geeta Kumari remained closely associated with academia after completing her tenure as JNUSU president. She continues her doctoral research at JNU’s Centre of Spanish, Portuguese, Italian and Latin American Studies, where she works on literature, visual culture and Latin American studies. Alongside her research, she writes literary reviews for independent publications and continues to speak on issues relating to public universities, campus democracy and higher education.
N. Sai Balaji (President 2018-19)
N. Sai Balaji has combined academics with continued political engagement. Since 2024, he has been teaching political science while researching international relations, climate negotiations, trade and environmental politics. He continues to remain associated with AISA and frequently participates in discussions surrounding higher education, democratic rights and public policy.
Dhananjay (President 2023-24)
Dhananjay marked AISA’s return to the JNUSU presidency after several years. During his tenure, he raised issues including fellowship delays, hostel shortages and funding for public universities. After leaving office, he entered active electoral politics with the CPI(ML) Liberation and unsuccessfully contested the Bihar assembly election last year from Bhorey in Gopalganj. Alongside his political work, he continues pursuing a PhD in theatre and performance studies at JNU while campaigning on unemployment, migration and education.
Nitish Kumar Yadav (President 2024-25)
Nitish Kumar Yadav continues as a doctoral scholar at JNU’s Centre for Political Studies, where his research examines caste and the judiciary. His presidency coincided with increasing confrontation between students and the university administration.
In February 2026, JNU rusticated him for two semesters and barred him from entering the campus after protests against biometric attendance and facial recognition systems. The disciplinary action drew criticism from several student organisations and became one of the biggest campus controversies of the year. Nitish is seen at anti-government protests as of now and has contested his rustication.
Aditi Mishra (President 2025-26)
Aditi Mishra became JNUSU president in 2025, extending AISA’s electoral success. Her campaign focused on affordable education, fellowships, hostel shortages and student welfare. She has since emerged as one of the country’s most recognisable student leaders, grabbing attention for her speeches on caste, higher education and opposing government policies.
(Edited by Nida Fatima Siddiqui)

[SEP] Bengaluru: Even as Bengaluru's real estate market continues to witness robust demand, approvals for key proposals such as development plans, change of land use (CLU), building plans as well as occupancy certificates, have virtually come to a standstill at the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) and the Urban Development Department (UDD), leaving the sector in a limbo. .Industry insiders say the issue is widespread and not confined to a handful of developers. .While building plan approvals and occupancy certificates are processed by the GBA, CLU applications require clearance from the UDD. Builders claimed delays have been reported both at the GBA and the UDD levels, possibly indicating lack of work allocations. .Real estate push? Families in Bengaluru may lose 45% land for partition.In contrast, the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) and the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority (BMRDA), which also process a significant number of real estate projects, continue to clear applications without major delays. .What's more, the backlog has not just affected the developers but also delayed project completions and the issuance of occupancy certificates (OCs). An occupancy certificate is essential for obtaining an e-khata and, eventually, for handing over the property to the buyer. .While some officials cite the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls as the reason, builders believe the delays are also linked to the recent changes in the government. ."The town planning department is accepting applications from builders, but not processing them. There has effectively been a freeze for the past two months. The delay is affecting us badly. Some of our projects are on hold, and there is no clarity on when approvals will come," a builder said, adding that homebuyers have been repeatedly following up as developers are unable to hand over occupancy certificates on time. .Several builders said that although the real estate market had witnessed a sharp rise in sales, approvals had slowed considerably.."There is utter confusion among town planning officials," another builder said. "From khata-related matters to building plan approvals, there are hundreds of pending issues. Earlier, applications were handled through a central office. Now, the responsibility has been split among five corporations and each appears to be following a different process." .Builders said the problems that began after the formation of the GBA, which assumed planning powers earlier vested with the BDA, have worsened in recent months. ."The BDA continues to function smoothly because it is familiar with the approval system, though approvals often come at a cost. The BMRDA is also functioning efficiently and at a much faster pace. In comparison, the GBA has been slow," a well-known builder said. .With airport plan, 'Kanakapura Bande' as CM, real-estate buzz grows in South Bengaluru.B N Girish, GBA's Additional Director of Town Planning, said the issue could be limited to a few projects. "If applicants have not submitted the required no-objection certificates (NOCs) or if there are deficiencies in their applications, approvals will naturally be delayed. It could be specific to certain cases," he said. .However, one of the builders quoted earlier rejected that explanation, saying the problem is widespread and has already been taken up with the Confederation of Real Estate Developers' Associations of India (CREDAI). "We are told no meeting on approving CLUs has been held in the last two months. There is also a freeze on other town planning matters.".A developer said "There is utter confusion among town planning officials. Earlier applications were handled through a central office. Now the responsibility has been split among five corporations and each appears to be following a different process."

NEW DELHI: Improving court infrastructure and integration of technology in the justice delivery system with an outlay of more than Rs 9,800 crore since 2011 have had little impact on disposal of cases pending for several decades. More than 10,000 cases are pending in the Supreme Court for over 10 years â including 558 pending for over 20 years, and 26 cases for 30 years. In the 25 high courts across the country, over 80,000 cases are pending for over three decades.In a written response to a question in Parliament last week, law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal put the onus of disposal of cases on the judiciary, which has not fixed a time frame for their disposal.He further said: âTimely disposal of cases in courts depends on several factors which, inter-alia, include availability of adequate number of judges and judicial officers, supporting court staff and physical infrastructure, complexity of facts involved, nature of evidence, cooperation of stakeholders viz bar, investigation agencies, witnesses, litigants and proper application of rules and procedures.
âWhile the apex court has been prompt in appointing judges against vacancies, the situation in 25 high courts and subordinate courts is not the same. The HCs currently have 341 vacancies of judges against a sanctioned strength of 1,122. The subordinate courts have 7,311 vacancies against an approved strength of 30,868 judges.
The law minister blamed the respective HC collegiums for not following the timeline prescribed for initiating recommendation for appointments of judges for the HCs, the primary reason behind large vacancies. The HC collegium comprises the chief justice and two senior-most judges of the high court. For the SC, the recommendation for the appointment of judges is initiated by the Chief Justice of India.âArrears Committees have been set up in all 25 high courts and the district courts to clear cases pending for more than five years. The govt has also enacted the New Criminal Laws 2023, Negotiable Instruments (Amendment) Act, 2018, Commercial Courts (Amendment) Act, 2018, Specific Relief (Amendment) Act, 2018 with a view to reduce pendency,â Meghwal said.

full_text:
BJP is hopeful that DMK's bubbling anger with Congress will help its bid to win over the party's support for its key legislative measures, especially delimitation, in Parliament
NEW DELHI: DMK Sunday mounted a furious pushback against Rahul Gandhi's describing any support to govt's widely speculated move to revive the bill to increase Lok Sabha's strength, coupled with delimitation of constituencies, as a betrayal of Tamil Nadu amid buzz in political circles that the regional party may come around to backing the measure.A day after Rahul, during his visit to Tamil Nadu, said any party supporting the constitution amendment bill in Parliament will be a 21st century Ettappan, a historical figure reviled for treachery, senior DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran came out with a blistering retort. "These are the people who traded our trust in them for mere ministerial berths," he said, lashing out at "poisonous snakes" which sell trust to "buy" power, a reference to Congress's decision to snap ties with DMK and TVK.Maran's strongly worded rejoinder captured the lingering sense of betrayal within the Dravidian party over Congress's swift embrace of its rival after the national party went to the poll as DMK's ally and was fully backed by the latter on all key issues, including Rahul's leadership, in national politics through its years in office.BJP is hopeful that DMK's bubbling anger with Congress will help its bid to win over the party's support for its key legislative measures, especially delimitation, in Parliament, even though govt has so far not taken any official step to revive the bill that was defeated by a united Opposition in the last session.
DMK has anyway indicated its openness over the issue, saying it will take a call after studying the bill and insisting that the proposed law should not harm south India's interests.Rahul's comments are also a nod to the acknowledgement in Opposition camp of the possibility of DMK revising its stand on a bill which, opposition parties have alleged, will allow BJP-led governing alliance to reconfigure constituencies to its advantage for the 2029 Lok Sabha poll.
Targeting Rahul, Maran added, "Those who come to Tamil Nadu and stay silent about Cauvery rights are traitors. Those who only talk about irregularities in the exam, rather than insisting on completely abolishing NEET are traitors. Those who condemn BJP's horse-trading but ignore TVK's disgusting horse-trading are merely continuing that betrayal."

full_text:
NEW DELHI: For the first time since the Covid pandemic, fatalities on national highways (NHs) declined last year, even as overall road deaths rose in India. Govt data submitted in Lok Sabha last week shows that deaths on NHs, including Centre-run expressways, fell by 4.1% to 62,122 in 2025 from 64,772 in 2024.
Among states and UTs, 20 recorded a decline in fatalities on NHs while 15 reported an increase. Lakshadweep, with no national highways, was the only one to record âzero NH fatalitiesâ since 2022. 
Data shows UP registered the steepest decline in NH deaths, with fatalities dropping from 9,560 in 2024 to 7,573 in 2025. Madhya Pradesh also reported a significant reduction, from 4,644 to 3,610, along with Punjab, which logged a sharp fall from 1,562 to 1,022 during the same period. 
States that witnessed a rise in NH fatalities include Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat.

NEW DELHI: High drama unfolded at the New Delhi address of Independent MP Pappu Yadav Sunday after a man allegedly threw a slipper at him and another allegedly brandished a knife when he was holding a news conference.The accused, identified by sources as Sumit and Happy Sharma, are from Bulandshahr in UP. Police have detained Sumit (34), and are probing Happyâs role. They are verifying if Happy was the one who threw a slipper at the MP, and if Sumit, who runs a hardware shop, brandished a knife at the event.The attack is believed to be linked to Yadavâs recent skit outside Parliament over the alleged donation theft at the Ayodhya Ram temple. On July 31, Opposition MPs staged a skit outside Parliament to protest on the issue, during which Yadav, dressed as a priest, was seen putting donation money in his pocket. MP Bansuri Swaraj complained to police Saturday on the matter.Sundayâs videos show someone throwing a slipper at Yadav. Moments later, chaos erupts and chairs fly as supporters rush to overpower the men, and police step in. Members of Yadavâs team displayed before reporters the slipper and a knife which, they alleged, were used in the attack.
Yadav alleged that it was a planned attempt on his life. âWhen the knife was drawn to attack, our supporters and associates tried to restrain the assailant. I stepped forward and positioned myself between the attacker and Pappu Yadav, and I was beaten severely as a result,â Zaid, MP Yadavâs media convener, claimed.
Happy told reporters that the duo was ânot carrying a knife or any other weapon. We were allowed inside only after a security check.â Police, however, have found a knife in Sumit's possession. Advocate Kanishk Arora, of Yadavâs legal team, said the MP had received death threats in the past several days, including videos on social media announcing cash rewards for killing him and threatening his family. âWe had informed Delhi Police about the threats and sought enhanced security ahead of Sundayâs news conference. However, only three police personnel were deployed,â Arora said.
