NEW DELHI: After a paper leak exposed weak links in Indiaâs biggest entrance examination, National Testing Agency (NTA) is moving to put its premises, confidential records and examination material under round-the-clock watch. The agency has floated a tender estimated at Rs 7.5 crore to hire a security firm for its headquarters at Minto Road, regional office in Okhla and other notified locations.Issued on July 25, the tender is part of a procurement exercise covering security, housekeeping and examination-grade printing. Together, the bids signal an attempt to tighten controls across the examination chain â from printing and storage to access control and protection of digital infrastructure. The security contract will initially run for two years and may be extended twice by a year each. Bids can be submitted until 3 pm on Aug 17. The printing-services tender closes on Aug 20.The selected agency will watch over NTA employees, visitors, premises, confidential examination material, server rooms, strong rooms, warehouses, record rooms and other sensitive facilities. It will regulate entry and exit, verify staff and visitors, maintain logs and ensure that âonly authorised persons enter restricted areasâ.
The security apparatus will include door-frame and hand-held metal detectors, GPS-enabled guard patrol tracking, biometric attendance and digital incident-reporting systems.NTA has moved away from choosing a bidder mainly on cost basis. Citing the âsensitive nature of NTAâs examination ecosystem and confidentiality requirementsâ, it has adopted the quality-and-cost based selection model. Technical capability will carry 70% weightage and the financial bid 30%. Only agencies securing at least 70 marks in the technical assessment will reach the financial round.Bidders must have at least five yearsâ experience in professional security, an average annual turnover of Rs 10 crore in past three financial years and must have done prior work at high-security establishments such as central govt institutions, examination agencies, universities, airports, hospitals or metro systems.
Bidders for NTA tender will have to deposit 15 lakh as earnest moneyThe contract value excludes GST. Bidders must deposit Rs 15 lakh as earnest money, while the successful agency will furnish performance security equal to 5% of the contract value.Confidentiality is mandatory. The service provider and its personnel must protect information relating to examination material, security arrangements and IT systems even after the contract ends.The tender has been floated amid efforts to rebuild public confidence after the NEET controversy and have a foolproof system in place against paper leaks. The exercise suggests that NTA is treating security as a process in which every access point can become a vulnerability.

NEW DELHI: Punjab govt's stiff resistance to attorney general R Venkataramani's proposal for amicable implementation of a 15-year-old Supreme Court decree settling Bhakra Nangal and Beas power dues since 1966 in favour of Himachal Pradesh made SC observe, "The state has a habit of defying decrees and old habits die hard."Venkataramani told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that he had extensive consultations with Punjab, Haryana, Himachal and Union ministry of power after getting the records examined by CAG for independent determination of the historical capital cost liability."...a mutually workable settlement framework has been evolved. It envisages a cashless settlement, wherein the respective claims and liabilities are proposed to be adjusted through in-kind settlement of energy arrears and set-off of capital cost liability, thereby obviating the need for any direct financial transaction between the states," the AG said.Senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Balbir Singh, appearing for Himachal and Haryana, respectively, said they were agreeable with the AG's settlement proposal for implementation of the decree, which was passed by the SC in 2011 on an original suit filed by Himachal 30 years ago seeking settlement of assets on division of Punjab in 1966.For Punjab, senior advocate Nidhesh Gupta said the state had key concerns over workability of the AG's proposal and said the state would stand to lose substantially.
Given the fact that it is a 15-year-old decree passed on a 30-year-old original suit seeking resolution of a 60-year-old inter-state dispute, the bench said, "Your state has a habit of defying decrees...""There is a decree in Himachal's favour. When we order implement, it will be with interest from 2011. We will not allow them to be deprived of the fruits of the decree. If you settle, it is well and good. Otherwise, be ready for consequences." It posted the matter for hearing on Aug 12.In its July 30 order, the bench said, "While the states of Himachal and Haryana have graciously agreed in principle to the proposal, the state of Punjab has raised objections thereto. In the interest of justice, two weeks time is granted to Punjab to reconsider and clarify its stand."The AG's proposal had said, "Punjab and Haryana will provide 13,066 MU of energy arrears to HP at 871 MU per annum over 15 lean seasons (Oct-March), in the inter-se ratio of 58:42 (Bhakra Nangal project) and 60:40 (Beas projects). HP to pay BBMB-determined charges for the year in which each tranche is received."HP's liability (7.19% of composite Punjab) towards the capital cost of Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects - being the unreimbursed share of loan servicing by Punjab and Haryana since 1966-67 - be assessed at Rs 420.7 crore (Punjab: Rs 249.2 crore; Haryana: Rs 171.5 crore). The capital cost liability could be considered to set off against part of HP's energy arrear receivables.
At the rate of Rs 3.85 per unit, the units to be offset is approximately 1093 MUs."SC on Sept 27, 2011 (Justices R V Raveendran and A K Patnaik) had decreed the suit in favour of HP by ruling, "The state is entitled to 7.19% of the power of the composite state of Punjab from the Bhakra Nangal project with effect from Nov 1, 1966, and from Beas project with effect from the dates of production in Unit I and Unit II."

NEW DELHI: Drugs can give a momentary high but family and professional lives will hit a low, PM Modi told youth in a warning against substance abuse on Sunday, and exhorted families not to hide any addiction in the name of social prestige but reach out to experts and cultivate a culture of frank communication with kids.Launching âNasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyanâ (campaign for drug-free youth for developed India), Modi called for rejecting stigma on the issue. âYouth who come out fighting addiction are not weak; they are real warriors,â he said. Give drug survivors a second chance, respect them: PM ModiPM Modi said society should instead respect those who overcome their drug addiction. âThey are real warriors whose incredible courage is their true identity,â he said in a virtual address, with a host of chief ministers, governors, spiritual figures and a large number of youngsters joining the event from across the country.As the nation has set the goal of âViksit Bharatâ, it is imperative that the countryâs youth remain physically and mentally fit, steering clear of destructive habits like drugs, he said, stressing the importance of support system offered by the society besides the help from yoga and meditation.He said, âEven if a youth has mistakenly fallen into the trap of addiction, it absolutely does not mean that all doors are closed for them.â

Visakhapatnam district has completed arrangements for the Andhra Pradesh Teacher Eligibility Test (AP TET-2026), scheduled to be conducted in the computer-based test (CBT) mode from August 5 to 16. Reviewing the preparations with officials on Monday, District In-charge Collector Gobbilla Vidyadhari directed all departments to work in coordination to ensure the smooth conduct of the examinations.
According to an official release, 21,522 candidates will appear at eight examination centres in the district. The examinations will be held in two sessions daily, from 9.30 a.m. to noon and from 2.30 p.m. to 5 p.m. Candidates have been advised to reach their centres at least an hour before the examination and strictly follow the instructions in their hall tickets. The district administration has arranged 100 scribes for candidates with special needs.
Police have been directed to provide adequate security, while Section 144 will be enforced around examination centres. APSRTC has been asked to operate special buses for candidates, and officials have been instructed to ensure uninterrupted power supply and deploy medical teams with first-aid facilities at every examination centre.

Eight players, four each in the boys’ and girls’ categories, were selected to represent Andhra Pradesh at the National Under-19 Chess Championship to be held in October after emerging successful in the State-Level Under-19 Chess Championship that concluded in Visakhapatnam. The tournament was organised by the Visakha Chess Association and Aditya Chess Academy under the aegis of the Andhra Chess Association.
According to the organisers, 240 players from across the State participated in the two-day championship. The selection process was overseen by Andhra Chess Association president Adusumilli Suresh, secretary Jagadish, vice-president Venkateswara Rao and the tournament director.
In the boys’ section, Alluri Bhaskara Ratna Shanmukha Reddy of East Godavari secured first place, followed by Gnana Sai Santhosh of Kakinada, Majji Ram Charan Tej of East Godavari and Jayaprakash Vanam of Kakinada. In the girls’ section, Sharvani Cheedipalli of NTR district finished first, while Sravya Sri Bhimarasetti of Anakapalle, Himisha of Visakhapatnam and Gorli Naina of Visakhapatnam completed the top four. The eight players qualified to represent the State at the National championship.
The championship was inaugurated by Assistant Commissioner of Police Lakshmana Murthy and Sri Viswa Educational Institutions directors Siva Ganesh and Sivaji, who made the ceremonial first move.
The valedictory function was attended by Andhra Chess Association CEO Neelima Balli, All Visakha Association president Rangala Babu Rao, Anakapalle district secretary Amalakantha Srinivasa Rao, representatives of Aditya Chess Academy, and officials of Sri Viswa Educational Institutions, among others.

The Alluri Sitarama Raju district administration on Monday initiated the process of nominating representatives from tribal organisations to a proposed High-Power Committee that the State government has decided to constitute on tribal issues.
At a district-level meeting held at the Collectorate, representatives of tribal organisations proposed the names of retired IAS officer Baburao Naidu and legal adviser Kobba Srinivas for inclusion in the committee. District Collector T. Nishanthi asked the representatives to arrive at a consensus and submit the names of the remaining three nominees by Tuesday.
The proposed committee follows a decision taken at an earlier meeting chaired by Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha and Tribal Welfare Minister Gummadi Sandhya Rani. It is proposed to comprise IAS officers, legal experts and representatives of tribal organisations.
The meeting was attended by Joint Collector Tirumani Sripooja, Project Officer, Integrated Tribal Development Agency (ITDA), Aditya Varma, Additional Superintendent of Police Shruthi, and representatives of tribal organisations and employees’ unions.
Addressing the participants, Ms. Nishanthi appealed to tribal organisation leaders to present their grievances and demands through peaceful and democratic means and refrain from protests on public roads that could inconvenience the public. Representatives of the organisations assured the administration that they would pursue their demands through peaceful and democratic means and cooperate in constructive dialogue with the government.

The death toll in Assam floods increased to 87 with two more fatalities reported while over 1.28 lakh people in seven districts remained affected by the deluge, according to an official bulletin on Monday (August 3, 2026).
The Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), in its report, said both the deaths were reported from the worst-hit Sivasagar district.
The seven districts still reeling under flood were Charaideo, Sivasagar, Dhemaji, Golaghat, Biswanath, Jorhat, and Lakhimpur, where 380 villages and 14,230.148 hectares of crop area remained inundated.
With the latest report of deaths, the toll in this year's floods has risen to 87. Of the 1,28,071 people affected by the deluge, 55,200 were in Sivsagar, 34,050 in Charaideo and 20,209 in Jorhat.
On Sunday (August 2), five districts had more than 1.35 lakh flood-hit people.
The administration was operating 38 relief camps, sheltering 11,066 displaced people. Another 17 relief distribution centres were also functional.
The Dhansiri river continued to flow above the danger level at Numaligarh in Golaghat district.

full_text:
Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor scripted a major political upset in Bihar by defeating the Bharatiya Janata Party candidate in the Bankipur Assembly byelection, a constituency represented for five consecutive terms by the BJP’s national president Nitin Nabin. The BJP retained Manjalpur in Gujarat while the Congress held on to Madhya Pradesh’s Datia in other Assembly byelections.
Mr. Kishor dedicated the victory to the people of Bankipur and appealed to the BJP’s central leadership to change the Chief Minister of Bihar. The Bankipur Assembly seat had fallen vacant after Mr. Nabin vacated the seat upon his election to the Rajya Sabha and elevation as BJP chief.
The political strategist-turned-politician clinched victory over BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by a margin of 19,324 votes. He bagged 64,151 votes while Mr. Sinha finished with 44,827 votes. Rashtriya Janata Dal nominee Rekha Kumari secured the third position with 14,273 votes. A total of 25 candidates contested the election, with 646 voters choosing the NOTA option.
In the 2025 Assembly election, Mr. Nabin had defeated Ms. Kumari by a margin of 51,936 votes. He had secured 98,299 votes while Ms. Kumari polled 46,363 votes. The JSP’s Vandana Kumari had received 7,717 votes.
Prashant Kishor: From election backrooms to Bihar Assembly
Throughout the 32 rounds of counting on Monday, Mr. Kishor, contesting an election for the first time, remained ahead in every round and held on to his lead until the final tally. Celebrations broke out at the JSP office in Patliputra Colony after the 10th round, when Mr. Kishor had established a lead of over 6,000 votes.
A JSP worker, celebrating the victory while dancing to Bhojpuri songs, said: “Bankipur is just a trailer; the whole of Bihar is still to come.”
After the 22nd round of counting, when Mr. Kishor was leading by a margin of around 13,000 votes, he and his wife Jahanvi Das walked to the counting centre at A.N. College to join the party workers and supporters in celebrations.
“The people have not only elected an MLA, but the people of Bankipur have given a message to the central leadership of the BJP to replace Samrat Choudhary with a better person. I expect that the BJP leadership will seriously think about it,” Mr. Kishor said.
He added that the time had come for Prime Minister Narendra Modi to not only care about the people of Gujarat but also pay attention to the people of Bihar.
“My only concern is that the young people of Bihar need to go to other States in search of jobs. Migration from Bihar should be stopped,” he said.
Read updates from the vote counting for Manjalpur Assembly bypoll in Gujarat
The Bihar Chief Minister congratulated Mr. Kishor on his victory on his X handle. “In the grand festival of democracy, the people have chosen Jan Suraaj in the Bankipur Assembly by-election. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to Prashant Kishor ji on his victory, while respecting the people’s decision,” said Mr. Choudhary.
In his statement, Bihar BJP State president Sanjay Saraogi said, “The Bharatiya Janata Party humbly accepts the mandate of the Bankipur by-election and respects the decision of the people. In a democratic process, the verdict of the people is above everything! We will seriously analyse why we did not secure the votes; we will identify our shortcomings and work diligently to rectify them.”
He added, “Unlike Opposition parties, we do not blame constitutional institutions, EVMs, or the Election Commission for our defeat. The Bharatiya Janata Party has complete faith in democracy and constitutional systems, and believes in addressing its shortcomings through introspection and review.”
BJP wins in Manjalpur
In Gujarat, the BJP retained the Manjalpur Assembly seat in Vadodara district, with its candidate Satish Govindbhai Patel defeating Congress nominee and former Minister Bhikhabhai Rabari by 30,630 votes. According to the Election Commission, Mr. Patel secured 55,481 votes against Mr. Rabari’s 24,851 after 20 rounds of counting at Bhavan’s School in Makarpura. The byelection, necessitated by the death of senior BJP MLA and former Minister Yogesh Patel, recorded a voter turnout of 37.5%.
With the victory, the BJP’s strength in the 182-member Gujarat Assembly has increased to 162 seats, while the Congress has 12 MLAs.
The Congress defended Madhya Pradesh’s Datia Assembly constituency, with its candidate Ghanshyam Singh winning against BJP’s Ashutosh Tiwari by 6,016 votes. Mr. Singh, a member of Datia’s erstwhile royal family, polled 66,757 votes against Mr. Tiwari’s 60,741. Mr. Tiwari was picked to contest the bypoll over former State Home Minister Narottam Mishra. Aazad Samaj Party candidate Damodar Yadav ‘Mandal’ finished third with 22,527 votes.

full_text:
The Supreme Court directed the Union government on Monday (August 3, 2026) to provide pedestrians broad, clearly-marked footpaths exclusively for their use.
A Bench headed by Justice P.S. Narasimha said the right to a clean and broad footpath was a fundamental right the state could afford to everyone without any big investment.
Comment | Reclaiming footpaths for people
“Wherever there is a road, there should be space for walkers. Make sure these spaces are not encroached upon,” Justice Narasimha addressed Additional Solicitor-General K.M. Nataraj, appearing for the Union government, before posting the case after a fortnight.
‘Right to walk’
On June 19, 2026, the apex court had declared the right to walk on demarcated and well-maintained footpaths a fundamental right. The court had prioritised movement through walking over motorised locomotion.
“If a road exists, there must then be a duty to ensure that a footpath is demarcated and maintained for the walkers. This is an enforceable duty. The fundamental right to walk on demarcated footpaths shall override the privilege of a motorised vehicle,” Justice Narasimha, who had authored the judgment, held.
The judgment had come in a case about a five-year-old boy, who was crushed to death by a truck while walking to the neighbourhood school with his father.
Justice Narasimha had observed that walking safely and carefree along wide footpaths, without danger lurking at every turn, was the most basic of rights.
It is the “simplest of the simple human activity, inextricably connected to life”, the apex court had said.

full_text:
The Gujarat government has ordered the withdrawal of all criminal cases registered against students, youth and other participants in protests over the alleged NEET-UG examination paper leak, directing the police not to pursue any legal or penal action against those who took part in the demonstrations.
In a communication dated July 31, the State Home Department wrote to Director General of Police G.S. Malik, instructing that all FIRs and criminal cases registered in connection with the protests be withdrawn immediately. The Department also directed the police not to initiate any adverse legal action against students, youth or any other persons who participated in the agitations across Gujarat.
The order follows the Supreme Court’s July 28 judgment, in which it restrained police from taking coercive action against minor student protesters. Referring to the apex court’s ruling, the Home Department said the State should ensure that no punitive action is taken against those who participated in the demonstrations.
On Monday (August 3, 2026), the Supreme Court further clarified that the expression “criminal antecedents” used in its July 28 order referred only to persons involved in grave and heinous offences. The court said States were free to close or withdraw FIRs against the remaining students in accordance with the law.
Student-led protests had been organised in Ahmedabad and several other cities in Gujarat in solidarity with demonstrations at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi over alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination. Protesters demanded greater accountability in the conduct of the examination and called for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
The agitation at Jantar Mantar drew support from students and youth organisations across several States, including Gujarat. Demonstrations were held in Ahmedabad and other parts of the State, where participants raised concerns over the integrity of the national medical entrance examination and sought action against those responsible for the alleged paper leak.
The protests were called off on July 25 after Mr. Pradhan resigned and the Union government accepted the remaining demands of the CJP.
The Gujarat Home Department’s communication, however, did not specify the number of FIRs or criminal cases that would be withdrawn pursuant to the decision.

In a face-off between the ruling party and Opposition MPs on Monday at the meeting of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology, where Meta representatives were summoned in the backdrop of the recent students’ protests, the BJP members, led by panel chairperson Nishikant Dubey, demanded an apology from Meta chief Mark Zuckerberg for restricting Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Facebook post, while the Opposition pushed back, arguing that democracy should not be regulated in the name of regulating technology.
Instagram played a crucial role in the protest, acting both as the platform airing discontent and as a tool to mobilise protesters. The BJP has criticised many of the reels shared by the protesters as “distasteful”, a concern that was also shared by PM Modi.
Mr. Dubey warned that the social media company could face action if accountability was not fixed. It is learnt that he has asked Meta to provide a complete audit trail of the post, from “report to restoration”. The restriction, Mr. Dubey reportedly said in his opening remarks at the meeting, underscored the need for greater oversight of Meta’s content moderation processes, automated systems and recommendation algorithms.
The Opposition pushed back against this line of questioning by Mr. Dubey and other BJP MPs, arguing that content moderation decisions on social media platforms should not be subject to political influence. While raising their own concerns about Meta, particularly on issues of privacy and compliance with Indian laws, they maintained that criticism of the government could not be equated with anti-national content.
Congress MP Shafi Parambil is learnt to have told the meeting that “technology should be regulated, not democracy”, while emphasising that dissent could not be criminalised.
Mr. Dubey alleged that the incident reflected a pattern of conduct by Meta and questioned the company’s handling of content on its platforms.
‘Intent to destabilise country’
“This is not the first time Meta has done such a thing. In January, Meta chief Mark Zuckerberg had said that PM Modi lost the 2024 election. Ms. Shanthegouda’s petition against the election of M.K. Pranaesh had led to his disqualification from Chikkamagalur Local Authorities constituency, which he won against her in the Legislative Council in 2022. Though she was scheduled to take oath as MLC at 12.30 p.m. on Monday, it did not take place since the Council’s Secretariat did not receive the election certification from the Chikkamagalur Deputy Commissioner. Eventually, 19 legislators took oath through 20 names had been released.
Party sources said that opposition to her induction into the Cabinet came from Mr. Siddaramaiah on the grounds of caste and regional combination. “With her induction to the Cabinet, it was felt that there would be three Kurubas — Yathindra Siddaramaiah and Byrathi Suresh besides her, and all from South Karnataka region. He had favoured Basavaraj Shivannanavar from Byadagi. The vacancy is likely to be filled soon with a representation for women,” sources said.
Sources said that a couple of legislators who were inducted into the Cabinet in the evening had their names included only on Monday morning as hectic lobbying continued till late on Sunday.

full_text:
The High Court of Karnataka has said two children, both majors, will have to recover from their father the ₹25 lakh compensation, awarded by a tribunal for their mother’s death in a road accident, as the father’s negligence in driving the motorcycle had caused her death.
Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar passed the order while rejecting the appeals filed by the children seeking directions to the insurance company to pay the compensation to them as was awarded by the tribunal and recover the amount from their father, who owned the two-wheeler which was insured.
The tribunal, which had awarded compensation of ₹25 lakh with 6% interest to the children, had exonerated the insurance company from the liability while holding that the vehicle owner — the father of the claimant-children — must pay the compensation.
Upholding the tribunal’s order, the court noted that the accident occurred owing to the rash and negligent driving by the father. The chargesheet confirmed that he was not holding a valid driving licence at the time of the accident, with offences registered under Sections 279 and 304(A) of the Indian Penal Code.
The court ruled that the “pay and recover” principle cannot be applied in the presence case as the claimants’ own family member is the offender, as he had breached the term of the policy by driving the insured motorcycle without a valid driving licence.
Under the “pay and recover” principle, the insurance company must first pay the compensation amount to an innocent third-party accident victim. Then, the insurance company has the legal right to recover that same money from the vehicle owner or driver who had breached the conditions of the insurance policy.
Since the owner of the vehicle is the father of the claimants, the order of “pay and recovery” could not be applied and hence the tribunal has rightly exonerated the insurer from payment of compensation and asking the claimants to recover the compensation from the owner of the vehicle.

full_text:
As the State continues to face the threat of flooding amid intense monsoon rains, the social media accounts of District Collectors are being inundated with demands to declare holidays for educational institutions. The public comments, a mix of genuine requests, sarcasm and criticism, appear to exert considerable pressure on the decision-making officers, prompting some of them to call out this online behaviour.
District Collectors across the State have faced intense criticism on social media in the past few days, either for not declaring holidays in view of heavy rain or for allegedly delaying the announcements.
“Better late than never,” one user commented after Ernakulam District Collector G. Priyanka announced on Sunday night (August 2) a holiday for educational institutions in the Kothamangalam and Muvattupuzha taluks for Monday (August 3). However, many users in the comments section criticised the decision and demanded a holiday across the district. “Seriously, madam? Do you know the situation in Aluva?” another user asked. By 11.30 p.m., the Collector had declared a holiday for the entire district, drawing another round of criticism over the delay. Similar comments, some harsh in tone, were also seen on the social media accounts of other District Collectors.
Amid the debate, Kozhikode District Collector Madhavikutty M.S. shared a detailed note on social media explaining the challenges involved in deciding whether schools should be closed.
She pointed out that although a school holiday is almost certain when the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issues a red alert, there are no fixed rules for orange or yellow alerts. Such decisions, she explained, are based not only on weather forecasts but also on local assessments of waterlogging, landslide threats, river water levels and road conditions, as well as reports from tahsildars, village officers, Revenue Divisional Officers and local bodies.
Warning against decisions driven by public pressure, Ms. Madhavikutty said opinions expressed on social media were often formed without access to the detailed field reports and Automatic Weather Station (AWS) data available to the administration. “Such public pressure should not influence the decision-making process,” she wrote, clarifying that she was expressing her personal views.
The Collector also highlighted the consequences of unnecessary holidays, noting that students lose valuable academic time while many parents, particularly daily-wage earners, suffer a loss of income. She further pointed out that a significant number of drowning incidents involving children during the monsoon occur on days when schools remain closed, as children may venture near rivers, ponds and flooded areas without adequate supervision.
Another District Collector, on condition of anonymity, said Ms. Madhavikutty’s remarks echoed the sentiments of several Collectors. “The unnecessary online backlash is quite stressful. It also gets abusive sometimes,” the officer said, admitting that Collectors often feel pressured to declare holidays even when their reasoning suggest otherwise.

The India Meteorological department has issued an orange alert forecasting very heavy rainfall accompanied by gusty winds on Tuesday (August 4, 2026). The district administration has declared a holiday for the second consecutive day for educational institutions in view of the incessant rain in the upland areas and coastal regions. However, exams scheduled earlier and online classes will go on as usual.
As on Monday evening, 964 people belonging to 365 families are at present staying in 32 relief camps set up across the district. There are 376 men, 418 women, and 170 kids. The highest number of people are in Kozhikode taluk. As many as 701 people from 260 families have been put up at 15 camps. There are 165 people in Thamarassery taluk, 80 in Vadakara taluk, and 18 people in Koyilandy taluk.
Meanwhile, around 200 families were affected after many parts of Kannadikkal-Parambil Bazar area were inundated. This followed the rising of water levels in the Poonoor River. The residents were shifted to safer places after low-lying areas went under water. Power connection was switched off in the area. The IMD, which had issued a yellow alert predicting isolated heavy rainfall for Kozhikode district on Monday, had later revised it to an orange alert.
Autorickshaw driver Noushad and family from Velliparamba near the Government Medical College Hospital had a narrow escape in the early hours of Monday when his house partially collapsed in the heavy rain. A tragedy was averted when Mr. Noushad, his wife, and two children ran outside the house after hearing a big sound around 3 a.m. The kitchen, one of the washrooms, and work area were completely damaged. Some household utensils too were destroyed. Both Mr. Noushad and his wife were sleeping next to the kitchen, it is learnt.
It was a similar experience for Ajayakumar of Nadakkavu in Kozhikode city when a wall inside his house collapsed on Sunday night. The incident happened when Mr. Ajayakumar, his wife, and kids were watching television. They have been shifted to another house at present.
Wells reportedly caved in at Odumbra and Chalappuram areas. Low-lying areas Mavoor are facing water-logging. People staying on the banks of the Kuttiyadi River have been asked to be on alert as two spillway gates of the Kakkayam Dam have been opened to safely discharge water.

full_text:
Under fire for the sluggish response to the rain-related calamities in the State over the last few days, the State government on Monday sought to blame the India Meteorological Department (IMD) for a delay in relaying the weather forecast. But experts say it also unravels the absence of long-term mitigation plans to tackle increasingly frequent rain-induced calamities in the State.
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Monday said the flooding was triggered by extremely heavy rainfall, with some places receiving more than 350 mm of rain. He said the State received the IMD’s warning of an extreme rainfall event only around midnight, leaving little time for authorities to carry out large-scale evacuations.
However, the IMD’s 125-year rainfall dataset, covering 110 weather stations across Kerala from 1901 to 2025, shed enough light on the State’s most vulnerable regions during the monsoon, including areas prone to extreme rainfall. Using this historical dataset with machine learning and Geographic Information System (GIS) techniques, weather scientists have prepared a rainfall vulnerability map that highlights several disaster-prone regions.
Colour-coded zones
The map shows that many parts of north Kerala, Idukki and Pathanamthitta, particularly areas along the Western Ghats, are highly susceptible to extreme rainfall events. The map categorises the State into different colour-coded zones based on rainfall intensity. Areas marked in red have experienced extreme rainfall events repeatedly over the past 125 years, while orange zones receive heavy rainfall of lower intensity. Green, blue and light blue represent progressively lower rainfall categories.
Notably, the recent weather events in Idukki, Pathanamthitta and Kottayam, as well as the debris slip in Wayanad last month that claimed eight lives, occurred in areas classified as red zones. According to weather experts, these regions become particularly vulnerable whenever the offshore trough extends up to Kerala along India’s west coast. Their geographical characteristics, combined with prevailing monsoon conditions, make them highly susceptible to heavy and very heavy rainfall, they say. The State need not wait for weather alerts to be upgraded before initiating preparedness measures.
The challenges
According to Thara K.G., a geologist and disaster management expert, rainfall warnings are only one component of disaster preparedness. Kerala’s biggest challenge is the absence of a long-term disaster mitigation strategy. “The State cannot evacuate an entire population solely based on rainfall alerts,” she said. “What Kerala lacks is a comprehensive long-term plan to reduce the impact of extreme weather events. This problem is further aggravated by the absence of effective land-use planning,” said Ms. Thara.
A senior official associated with the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority said implementing major policy reforms remains difficult in a densely populated State like Kerala. Measures such as enforcing land-use regulations or removing accumulated silt, sand and soil from rivers and other waterbodies often face significant resistance. “Strong policy-level intervention is essential to bring about meaningful reforms in the sector,” the official said.

A total of 110 people remained in relief camps across the district on Monday (August 3) following heavy downpours over the past few days. The day passed without much rain-related trouble.
Eight camps remained active in the district—four in Muvattupuzha taluk and two each in Kunnathunad and Kothamangalam—while four had been closed. Those who have taken shelter in camps include 51 women, 40 men, and 19 children.
Though the district did not witness incessant rain on Monday, the authorities advised people residing along the Muvattupuzha and Thodupuzha rivers, as well as in low-lying areas, to remain alert as the water levels in the rivers remained above the warning marks.
Authorities said the water level at the Malankara dam had touched the red-alert mark of 41.30 metres in the evening as inflow from the catchment area remained heavy. Excess water had been discharged from the dam by gradually raising its shutters since Sunday night (August 2), they said.
Though a flood-like situation prevailed along the Pooyamkutty river in Kothamangalam following heavy rain on Sunday night, it eased later as weather conditions improved. The Manikandanchal causeway across the river, which serves as a critical link between interior tribal hamlets and villages such as Manikandanchal and Kallelimedu and the mainland, was submerged in the morning. However, the water receded by afternoon, officials said.
Minister visits Chellanam
Higher Education Minister Roji M. John, who is in charge of the district, visited different wards of the Chellanam grama panchayat that had been severely affected by heavy rain and sea surge. Stating that the situation in the region required a permanent solution, the Minister said the government would shortly initiate steps to complete the construction of a seawall. Mr. John was accompanied by Kochi MLA Muhammed Shiyas.
Holiday declared
All educational institutions in the district will remain closed on Tuesday (August 4) in view of the heavy rainfall the district has been receiving, according to a communication issued by the Ernakulam District Collector.

Search operations entered the third day on Monday (August 3, 2026) for two men who went missing after being swept away by swollen rivers in Kannur district following heavy rains.
The search is continuing for R. Rajesh, a native of Kalliyoor in Thiruvananthapuram, who went missing at Meenthully in the Kariangode river, and V.P. Hanifa, who was swept away in the Kanhirapuzha.
A 12-member team of expert swimmers from the Turkey Life Saving Committee in Kalpetta, Wayanad, joined the search for Hanifa. The team began operations at 7 a.m., covering a stretch of around 500 metres downstream from Thondayil bridge, where he was swept away.
Fire and rescue services personnel from Peravoor, Mattanur, and Kuthuparamba, along with civil defense volunteers, also participated in the search. With rainfall easing for about two hours on Monday, the river level receded and the previously muddy water began to clear, improving search conditions.
Thalassery Sub-Collector (in charge) Prakashan C.V., and Irrity Tahsildar N. Seema supervised the operations at the site.
The search for Rajesh at Meenthaly involved personnel from the Fire and Rescue Services, police, and members of various rafting associations. Teams searched riverbanks, islets, and rocky stretches, besides extending the operation to the Palavayal bridge area downstream from the spot where he went missing.

As the deadline for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls approaches, Maharashtra has distributed over 93% of enumeration forms and digitised nearly 73% of them, according to data released by the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) on Monday (August 3, 2026).
Wardha and Hingoli emerged as the best-performing districts, achieving 100% distribution of enumeration forms. Hingoli also topped the State in digitisation, with 90.47% of forms digitised, followed by Wardha at 89%.
In contrast, major urban centres lagged behind the State average. Pune recorded 80.72% distribution of forms and 59.67% digitisation, while Nagpur reported 87.62% distribution and 59.77% digitisation. Mumbai Suburban recorded 85.12% distribution and 53.21% digitisation, while Thane registered the lowest digitisation rate in the State at 46.55%, despite distributing 82.33% of the forms.
The enumeration phase of the SIR began on June 30 and will conclude on August 8. Maharashtra has around 9.79 crore registered voters. Of these, 9.18 crore enumeration forms (93.79%) have been distributed, while over 7.13 crore forms (72.89%) have been digitised.
According to the CEO’s office, 1,00,253 booth-level officers (BLOs) are engaged in the exercise across the State.
Besides Hingoli and Wardha, Ratnagiri (89.86%), Buldhana (89.19%) and Yavatmal (87.93%) recorded the highest levels of digitisation.

full_text:
The Supreme Court on Monday (August 3, 2026) summoned the Arunachal Pradesh Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary (Home) after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) alleged that the State government had failed to cooperate with its probe into allegations that Chief Minister Pema Khandu had favoured firms linked to his family members in the award of government contracts over the past decade.
A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta was examining a status report filed by the Central agency pursuant to the court’s earlier directions when it was informed that the Arunachal Pradesh Government had not cooperated in providing records sought by the CBI during its preliminary enquiry.
Taking note of the agency’s report, the Bench directed both senior officials to appear before it on August 24, 2026, and explain the State government’s alleged failure to comply with the court’s earlier directions.
“We deem it appropriate to issue notice to the Chief Secretary, State of Arunachal Pradesh, and the Principal Secretary (Home), Government of Arunachal Pradesh, making it returnable on August 24, 2026. Both the aforesaid officers shall remain present before this court along with their response to the aforementioned report of the CBI, and also explain as to why there is non-cooperation and non-compliance with the directions issued by this court,” the Bench said.
The order was passed in a public interest litigation filed by the Save Mon Region Federation and Voluntary Arunachal Sena, alleging that several high value contracts for development works in Tawang district were awarded to firms linked to the Chief Minister and his family members. The petitioners have alleged favouritism in the award of these contracts and sought an independent investigation into the matter.
Earlier, the top court had directed the State government to produce records relating to all contracts awarded across Arunachal Pradesh to the firms named in the petition.
On Monday (August 3), Justice Mehta questioned Additional Solicitor General K.M. Nataraj, appearing for the CBI, on the progress of the preliminary enquiry and asked whether the agency was giving a “long rope” to the Chief Minister despite having collected sufficient material.
Mr. Nataraj informed the Bench that the State government had not been cooperating with the inquiry and was yet to furnish all the documents sought by the agency. “The government is yet to furnish all the requisite documents... We will initiate steps in the proper manner. Let the State government cooperate,” he submitted.
Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for the petitioners, urged the court to direct the CBI to register a First Information Report (FIR), contending that the agency’s preliminary enquiry had already revealed prima facie material indicating irregularities in the award of government contracts.
“Normally, a preliminary enquiry is only for the purpose of deciding whether an FIR should be registered or not... Coercive steps have to be taken,” Mr. Bhushan submitted.
Justice Mehta also referred to the discrepancies recorded in the CBI’s status report and questioned why an FIR had not yet been registered despite the material already gathered by the agency.
“In your report, it says all discrepancies. None of the procurement manuals has been followed... Oral work orders, no approval records, nothing. Why do you need anything more? You are just giving a long rope,” Justice Mehta remarked.
Mr. Nataraj clarified that the agency would take appropriate action once all the requisite records had been furnished by the State government. Taking note of the submission and the CBI’s allegation of non-cooperation, the Bench directed the top State officials to remain personally present before the court on the next date of hearing on August 24, 2026.
Earlier, the top court had directed the CBI to conduct a preliminary enquiry into the allegations concerning the award of public works in Arunachal Pradesh between January 1, 2015 and December 31, 2025. The agency was asked to examine why open tenders were allegedly not invited for certain works, whether the absence of competitive bidding affected transparency in the award of contracts, and the flow of funds and payments made under them.
The court had also permitted the agency to examine the beneficial ownership of firms allegedly linked to Mr. Khandu, and the movement of funds through such entities.
The petitioners had also relied on observations made by the Comptroller and Auditor General in earlier proceedings before the apex court, pointing to alleged departures from the General Financial Rules, 2017; the Manual for Procurement of Consultancy and Other Services; and the Manual for Procurement of Works in the award of contracts. The procurement framework, they pointed out, prescribes safeguards concerning the integrity of the bidding process, conflicts of interest, confidentiality, independence, and transparency at different stages of procurement.
The State government, however, has relied on a law enacted in 2015 that permits awarding contracts for work costing up to ₹50 lakh through a “work order” where no special technical know-how is required. It has maintained that the practice was followed with the objective of generating employment opportunities for local villagers and contractors.

This year’s July was the worst month for Tamil Nadu in the last 50 years in terms of realisation of the State’s share of the Cauvery water.
For the entire month, the realisation this time did not even cross the one thousand million cubic feet (tmcft)-mark. It was 0.698 tmcft against the stipulated 31.24 tmcft. Biligundulu is the measuring site for the inflow since the enforcement of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal’s final award in 2013, whereas the Mettur dam was the reference point up to 2012.
As far as Bilingundulu is concerned, the previous lowest during July was 2.441 tmcft in 2003. The same month recorded the lowest for Mettur too, when the State got 1.5 tmcft. The other years of very low realisation include 1987 (Biligundulu-3.392 tmcft and Mettur-2.286 tmcft) and 2012 (4.153 tmcft and 1.033 tmcft).
A study carried out by the High Level Technical Team on Cauvery, which was constituted by the Supreme Court in 2016, shows that as regards to July, Mettur’s 25-year-long average realisation was 33.7 tmcft and the 42-year-long average realisation was 36.2 tmcft. In respect of Billigundulu, the respective average figures for July were 36.871 tmcft and 39.087 tmcft.
The reason why the team considered the average figures for 25 years and 42 years was that the year in question — 2016 — marked the completion of 25 years since the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal gave the interim order in June 1991. Also, the year pointed to the fact that 42 years had lapsed since certain clauses of the 1924 Cauvery Accord, which was signed between the then Madras Presidency and the princely State of Mysore, came up for review.
According to the application filed by the Tamil Nadu government before the Supreme Court on Monday, the realisation of the Cauvery water at Biligundulu as on August 2 was 3.687 tmcft. (June - 2.915 tmcft; July - 0.698 tmcft; and August - 0.074 tmcft). In the first two months, the State should have realised 40.43 tmcft as per the Tribunal’s final award, which has been amended by the Supreme Court.

At the end of Round One of counselling for the Tamil Nadu Engineering Admissions (TNEA) 2026, computer science and engineering (CSE) and allied subjects continue to be the most preferred choice of students, followed by electronics and communications engineering (ECE).
Electrical and electronics engineering (EEE), although way down the pecking order, did manage to register a gentle upward swing in the number of seats filled after the first round, prompting analysts to take note. “There is no doubt a greater interest was shown in core engineering subjects like the ECE, EEE, and even mechanical,” said Jayaprakash Gandhi, a long-time career consultant. “Intake for civil and other core subjects are, however, a bit down,” he added.
Agreeing with Mr. Gandhi, R. Ashwin, independent career counsellor and analyst, said that among the top 100 students at the TNEA counselling this year, 73 preferred CSE and allied courses, 26 opted for ECE, and only one opted for mechanical engineering. Overall, more than half the seats filled were CSE and allied courses, while over 20% belonged to ECE and EEE was close to 5%.
Around 140 colleges have recorded zero intake after the first round of counselling, with over 30 of them being autonomous institutions. “This either points at lack of awareness among students about the institutions or the fact that the process of award of autonomous status by the authorities should be revisited,” Mr. Gandhi said.
Students favour Coimbatore
In region-wise performance, the Coimbatore region fared much better than the Chennai region this year as well. Many factors, according to Mr. Gandhi, work in the favour of Coimbatore, whether it is locational access of the institutions, their reputation, the pleasant weather, or the fact that Coimbatore is a textile, information technology, and accessories manufacturing hub. “Institutions in Coimbatore are connected to students in a wider area across the west and south of the State. For example, a student from Salem, Dharmapuri, or Tirunelveli would prefer to study in Coimbatore rather than coming to Chennai,” Mr. Gandhi said.
At the first round of counselling, absenteeism has crawled up to 35%, up by about three percentage points compared to last year. This means that either students have opted for medicine or other courses of study or the fact that they did not get their choice filling right, Mr. Ashwin postulates. Mr. Gandhi echoes the same concern, adding that in some cases, he had come across students opting for tier-two colleges instead of NIRF-ranked institutions. “This shows lack of awareness. It is quite acute among rural students,” he added.
Another aspect pointed out by Mr. Ashwin was that in the top 10 institutions in terms of filled-up seats in the first round, three private colleges have managed to fill about 85% of their seats. “Students are perhaps preferring private colleges because of better placements and infrastructure,” he observed.
So, what do all these portend for students at the second round? Candidates with cut-off marks of 160-170 would still be able to get into top institutions, which was not the case last year, Mr. Gandhi says. Mr. Ashwin has a word of advice: students who scored below 160 should fill as many choice combinations as possible so that they have a better chance to get a good seat.

Chief Economic Adviser to the Government of India V. Anantha Nageswaran on Monday said water should be treated as infrastructure that “must be planned, built, and paid for”. He called for a policy that did not price water at zero and treat it as limitless. Mr. Nageswaran said the floor space index (FSI) was far below what other cities around the world allowed.
Addressing the special plenary session of CII Tamil Nadu Infrastructure Summit 2026 in Chennai, Mr. Nageswaran said: “The answer is to treat water the way we have finally learnt to treat roads and power: as infrastructure that must be planned, built, and paid for. We need a water buffer storage so that a good monsoon carries us through a bad one.”
He further said: “We price water at zero, so we treat it as limitless. So we waste it, and we underbuild for it. And then, we are shocked when it runs out. The thing we call free is the thing we destroy. This is not a paradox. It is a policy choice, and it can be chosen differently.”
Mr. Nageswaran also listed the floor space index as the second trap, one that was less visible than the first. “We hold the floor space index — the amount one may build on a given plot — far below what other cities around the world allow. If we cannot build upward, we spread outward. Every square metre of built space then ends up carrying more land beneath it, and land grows scarce and also dearer. When land is that dear, the cheapest plot left is often an old tank or a filled-in pond, the very catchment that once held our water,” he said.
“Underpricing does not help the poor. It helps whoever already holds the connection. The household with the piped supply pays a pittance. The household without one buys from the tanker at several times the rate. Cheap water for the connected is, in effect, a subsidy that reaches the comfortable more than the poor it is meant to help. If we get the pricing honest, the genuinely vulnerable can be protected directly and, more precisely, the asset earns enough to reach those who do not yet have it, he added.

The Supreme Court on Monday (August 3, 2026) decided to examine a petition filed by the Tamil Nadu government headed by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay challenging orders passed by the Madras High Court on lighting a lamp at a stone pillar near a dargah on the Thirupparankundram hill.
A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar issued notice to the Madurai District Collector, Joint Commissioner of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE), Sikkandar Badhusah Dargah, Hazarath Suitan, Sikkandar Badhsha Avuliya dargah, Archaeological Survey of India, Tamil Nadu Waqf Board and the petitioner in the High Court, Rama Ravikumar, and others on a plea filed by the Commissioner, HR&CE, Chennai.
The State, represented by senior advocate Jaideep Gupta, said the High Court has created a new tradition. It was not up to the courts to do that.
The Bench queried whether there was a prevailing tradition of lighting the lamp on the pillar. The State said there were no historical records of lighting the lamp on the stone pillar.
“A dangerous situation has been propped up. If it is done once, it would be repeated in the years after,” Mr. Gupta said.
The State said the High Court decisions had conferred upon individual devotees a right to dictate the manner and place of performance of temple rituals, a proposition wholly unknown to law.
“If permitted to stand, the judgments would seriously affect administration of Hindu religious institutions throughout the State and encourage repeated litigation concerning rituals, festivals and customs in public temples,” the Tamil Nadu appeal said.
The Bench refused to grant any interim relief to the court. It said the case would be heard comprehensively after the respondents file their affidavits in six weeks. The apex court listed the case for hearing in eight weeks.
The High Court’s Division Bench had, in early January this year, confirmed a previous Single Judge Bench order directing the Subramaniya Swamy Temple management in Thirupparankundram to light the Karthigai Deepam at the ‘deepathoon’ (stone pillar) atop the hill, besides the usual places.
The previous DMK regime in the State had been unable to convince the court that the lighting of the lamp may stir the hornet’s nest and lead to public disturbances. The Single Judge had dismissed the apprehensions of the State as an “imaginary ghost”. The Bench had remarked that such a turn of events would happen only with the State’s blessings, and not otherwise.
“It is ridiculous and hard to believe the fear of the mighty State that by allowing representatives of the Devasthanam [temple management] to light the lamp at the stone pillar near the top of the hill located within its territory of Devasthanam land, on a particular day in a year, will cause disturbance to public peace. Of course, it may happen only if such a disturbance is sponsored by the State itself,” the High Court Single Judge Bench had observed.
The High Court had urged the State to not “stoop” to that level to achieve a political agenda.
The court had reasoned that allowing a few persons to light the lamp and permitting worship was not an unmanageable task, the High Court had noted.

At least six blood banks in West Bengal are under investigation for allegedly selling blood to individuals and private blood banks outside the State in what Health Department officials have described as an inter-State, multi-crore racket.
The sale of blood is prohibited under the National Blood Policy, which was introduced in 2002. Officials said raids have been conducted at blood banks in Kolkata, Howrah, East Burdwan, West Burdwan, Nadia, and North Dinajpur districts over the past two weeks and large quantities of plasma were found to have been sold to entities in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat, among other States.
Officials said around 11 blood banks have been barred from organising donation drives until the investigation is over. However, they are still permitted to collect blood from donors at their centres. The restrictions came into effect on August 1. Popular medical facilities and pathology labs like Ashok Laboratory, Life Care, Kothari Medical, Health Point Hospital, and several others are on the list.
The racket, worth crores, kept the health department in the dark by selling blood illegally, health department officials said.
Last week, Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee told reporters that officials found that people who donated blood at a camp in South 24 Parganas were offered gifts. “You can give food, flowers, a badge or a certificate to a donor, but you cannot give gifts. We recorded instances of donors getting fans, mixer grinders, clocks and money,” said Dr. Mukherjee.

The court, however, made it clear that it would not examine at this stage the merits of the dispute over the legality of the freezing order, which remains pending before the Calcutta High Court.
A Bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and P.B. Varale was hearing the Trinamool’s appeal against a July 20 order of the High Court refusing to grant interim relief against the ED’s decision to freeze three HDFC Bank accounts belonging to the party as part of a money-laundering investigation.

22 children dead in Gujarat's Chandipura virus outbreak; 35 infections confirmed
Health teams are spraying pesticides in animal husbandry areas to control sandflies, which spread the virus, state health minister Praful Panseriya said.
As many as 22 children have died due to Chandipura virus (CHPV) in Gujarat this monsoon season, with 35 cases testing positive out of 184 suspected infections, state health minister Praful Panseriya said on Monday.
Seven patients remain under treatment across civil hospitals in Gandhinagar, Rajkot, and other districts, and government and private paediatric facilities have been instructed to immediately admit symptomatic patients to ICU beds to prevent organ failure, he said.
"A total of 184 suspected cases have been registered in the state so far, out of which 35 cases have tested positive and the results of 11 samples are still pending," Panseriya said.
Out of the cases reported so far, 22 children have died due to Chandipura virus, he said. All patients are under 15 years of age, he added.
Children under treatment, cases spread across districts
Children who are admitted to civil hospitals in Gandhinagar, Sabarkantha-Himmatnagar, Patan, Rajkot and Bhavnagar are being provided the best and super-specialist treatment and doctors are monitoring their condition, Panseriya said.
He further noted that cases are being reported from different areas and not concentrated in a particular village.
State steps up surveillance, treatment
Health teams are spraying pesticides in areas where animal husbandry is practised to target sandflies, which are responsible for spreading the encephalitis virus, he said.
Government and private paediatric facilities have been instructed to admit patients with symptoms of the virus to ICU beds with oxygen and ventilator facilities and not delay treatment so that serious conditions like multiple organ failure can be prevented, he said.
What is Chandipura virus?
Chandipura encephalitis is a viral disease that spreads mainly by sandflies and other insects and causes inflammation of the brain. The virus was first isolated from a patient from Chandipura village in Nagpur district of Maharashtra in 1965.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke said that the comparisons of the Jantar Mantar protest with the uprisings held in Nepal and Bangladesh were being done to “defame” the satirical outfit.
“We are different,” Dipke said.
He was responding to the remarks made by exiled Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasreen on the CJP protest. She said on Sunday that while she did not follow the CJP protest in India, a clip of it reminded her of the 2024 student uprising in Bangladesh which led to the ouster of then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.

"It was like that. That student movement in Bangladesh fooled us. Because we thought the students wanted to abolish the quota system. Sheikh Hasina had also agreed to their demands, but ultimately the government fell. Later, we found that jihadis (Islamic fundamentalists) were behind that movement. The fallout has not been good for Bangladesh. Jihadis have taken over power there," Nasreen had said, as quoted by news agency PTI.
Dipke said that the responsibility of the Cockroach Janta Party, which started as a satirical political outfit, has increased after leading nationwide student protests and that the team of the outfit will be expanded soon.
Dipke warns of another sit-in
The CJP founder on Monday warned the Centre that there could be another sit-in if the demands of the party are not met. He said that the Centre has not yet paid ₹1 crore compensation to the families of the students who died by suicide due to NEET-UG paper leak, which was one of core demands of the CJP during the protest.
“We want the government to do this (fulfil the demands agreed upon); otherwise, we will have to sit in protest again,” Dipke told news agency ANI.
"We had also demanded ₹1 crore each as compensation to the families (of NEET aspirants who died allegedly by suicide). None of the families has received the compensation from the government. I have got to know that the govt has said that it will have to look into the rules & norms for this. When you have to buy MPs/MLAs, you spend crores of rupees, but to give compensation, you need to first check the rules. It means their intention is not right," Dipke added.

The 37-day protest at Jantar Mantar was called off after Pradhan resigned and the Centre agreed to the othe demands of the CJP as well.
‘Don’t support Pralhad Joshi's appointment'
Dipke also said that while their demand of the resignation of education minister was met, he did not support the appointment of Pralhad Joshi in place of him.
"Our demand was the resignation of the Education Minister, and it was met. But in place of him (Dharmendra Pradhan), who was made the Education Minister? It was Pralhad Joshi. Airlines report 352 major flight defects till June, Akasa and Air India top list
Union minister of state for civil aviation Murlidhar Mohol said that of 352 significant defects, 334 were in domestic flights.
Over 350 significant technical defects were reported in domestic and international flight operations between January and June this year, the government said in a written reply in Rajya Sabha on Monday.
Responding to a question by Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas, Union minister of state for civil aviation Murlidhar Mohol said that 352 significant defects were recorded during the period, of which 334 were in domestic flights.
As per the government data, Akasa Air reported the highest number of defects at 152, followed by Air India Express with 53, IndiGo with 47 and Air India with 46 of what the ministry said were significant technical defects. Low cost airline SpiceJet accounted for nine such defects during the six-month period.
The data also showed that regional airlines like Star Air, Fly91 and India One Air reported 29, nine and five significant defects, respectively. Cargo airline Blue Dart reported two defects.
Flight defects over the years
Meanwhile, 487 defects were found in 2023, including 436 on domestic flights and 51 on international flights, 692 in 2024 with 649 on domestic flights, according to the data.
The highest number of defects was recorded in 2025 when 889 defects were reported, including 778 on domestic flights and 111 on international flights.
The total number of these significant defects, however, stood at 2,420 from 2023 till June 2026.
DGCA's show cause notices between 2024 and 2026
The minister also stated that the country’s aviation regulator, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) issued 382 show cause notices to airlines for safety violations during the period from January 2024 to June 2026, Mohol said. The enforcement action includes financial penalty, suspension of approval/ authorisation and warning, it stated.
The minister also stated that the DGCA took 51 enforcement actions against the Indian airlines for violating safety standards during the period from 2023 to 2025.
It also said that DGCA conducted special audits at major airports after June 19 last year. To be sure, India witnessed the deadliest crash in three decades on June 12, when an Air India flight 171 crashed seconds after take off killing 241 out of 242 people on board.

"The results of the 14th Preliminary Test (PT) were declared on the 2nd of last month, exactly a month ago today, marking the start of this controversy. We launched this agitation on July 5, met the Governor on July 7, and staged an effigy-burning protest on July 8. We met the Chief Minister on July 20 and submitted evidence, which triggered official action," he said, reported news agency ANI.
Mahato alleged that the government and the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) had failed to adequately address students' concerns despite weeks of protests.
"The current attitude of both the Jharkhand government and the Commission is demoralising students across the state... To uphold the students' morale and escalate this struggle, I am giving up food starting today... Our primary objective is to secure the cancellation of the 14th PT examination and an investigation into all exams conducted by the TDPL agency," he added.
Speaking to reporters, Mahato said he would continue his hunger strike until the demands submitted to Chief Minister Hemant Soren were met.
"To ensure that the students' morale is maintained, I am sitting on a hunger strike to take this fight forward. I will follow all the rules of this strike and ensure that the government comes to its knees. We will ensure that all the accused get strict punishment," he said.
He also reiterated the demand to cancel the 14th JPSC Combined Civil Services Preliminary Test and review all examinations conducted through TDPL.
"First, we will ensure that the Preliminary Test (PT) for the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) Combined Civil Services is cancelled and make sure that examinations happening through TDPL agencies are looked into. We will force reforms for JPSC, JSSC exams," he said.
Also Read | Jharkhand Govt concerned over students’ fate: Governor
Why are students protesting?
The protests stem from a series of alleged paper leaks, recruitment irregularities and administrative lapses that students say have repeatedly derailed their careers.
Aspirants have accused authorities of failing to ensure transparency in recruitment examinations, alleging that multiple competitive tests have been compromised, according to several reports.
"Be it any exam, like the JPSC or JSSC CGL, the papers are getting leaked," student protester Rekha Rana said, according to news agency ANI.
Another protester, Archana Kumari, argued that symbolic action was not enough.
"The JPSC and JSSC scams -- you might recall that the government only took cognisance of the JPSC issue after the OMR sheet went viral, and you likely saw what happened with the JPSC Chairman subsequently," she said.
The protesters are demanding structural reforms, greater transparency and accountability instead of isolated administrative action.
Also Read | Jharkhand man climbs 100 ft mobile tower after exam irregularities prevent wife from getting job
CJP extends support to protesters
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has backed the students' agitation over the alleged irregularities in JPSC, JSSC CGL and other recruitment examinations.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said he had spoken to the protesting students and voiced support for their demands.
"Spoke to the students who are protesting in Jharkhand over irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment exams. The CJP stands with all the students in Jharkhand and supports their demands," Dipke posted on X.
What are the protesters demanding?
The protesters have urged the Hemant Soren government to hold talks with students, ensure transparency in the examination process and investigate alleged irregularities.
"Jharkhand is a land where students are protesting peacefully... the only appeal being made to the government is to listen to the students. Engaging in dialogue is a sign of a healthy democracy," a protester said, ANI reported.
The protester also demanded the immediate cancellation of examinations linked to the blacklisted TDL company and accountability for alleged irregularities.
As part of the agitation, aspirants also organised a Mashal March in Ranchi.
Calls for CBI probe, exam cancellation
The protests entered their fifth consecutive day on Sunday, with hundreds of students continuing their indefinite sit-in that began on July 29, according to a PTI report.
The demonstrators have demanded cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test held on April 19, a CBI and Enforcement Directorate (ED) probe into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC, and the introduction of a fifth "not attempted" option in OMR sheets.
Meanwhile, BJP state general secretary Amar Kumar Bauri also criticised the Jharkhand government over the alleged examination irregularities and demanded that Chief Minister Hemant Soren resign, taking moral responsibility for the issue.

Arunachal Pradesh’s Glaw Lake is India’s 101st Ramsar site: Bhupender Yadav
Ramsar sites are recognised for their biodiversity, critical habitats for migratory birds, and ecological significance, such as carbon sequestration and flood control
Arunachal Pradesh’s Glaw Lake has been designated as India’s 101st ‘Ramsar’ site, a wetland of International importance, Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav announced on Monday.
This is also the state’s first Ramsar site, he said.
Any wetland can designated to be of ‘International importance’ under the Ramsar Convention, an environmental treaty signed in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran. These sites are recognised for their biodiversity, critical habitats for migratory birds, and ecological significance, such as carbon sequestration and flood control.
“Delighted to announce Glaw Lake as Arunachal Pradesh’s first Ramsar Site -- a significant milestone for biodiversity, water and climate security, and sustainable livelihoods,” the minister said in a post on X on Monday evening.
The lake lies within the Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary and is freshwater lake in the Eastern Himalayas, which acts as a biodiversity hotspot.
“Fed by perennial mountain streams, it is surrounded by lush vegetation, with more than 150 tree species and 49 orchid species recorded within the site and its catchment,” Yadav added, stating under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, the number of such sites in the country has grown from 26 in 2014 to 101 today.
“Every new Ramsar site strengthens our resolve to protect nature while securing the future of communities that depend on these invaluable ecosystems,” he added.
The government told the Lok Sabha in July that four new wetlands were in contention for being notified as Ramsar sites.
“The key reason for inclusion of these sites is the fulfillment of atleast one of the nine criteria of Ramsar Convention on Wetlands. Currently, proposals of four new wetlands namely, Glaw Lake (Arunachal Pradesh), Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh), Gosabara-Mokarsagar Wetland Complex (Gujarat) and Sauj Jheel (Uttar Pradesh) have recently been submitted to the Ramsar Secretariat for their designation as Ramsar sites,” Yadav said in the reply last month.

The Assam government on Monday transferred ₹15,000 each as immediate interim relief to flood-affected families in four districts namely Sibsagar, Charaideo, Golaghat and Jorhat.
“The affected people have been receiving relief materials from different sources, but in order to move back to their homes, buy essentials and take measures to clear the sludge in their houses, they need cash. That’s why we have released a sum of ₹15,000 each to the affected families”, chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said.
Sarma informed that a total of 62,696 families in the worst affected districts of Sibsagar (35,289), Charaideo (19,883), Golaghat (2,593) and Jorhat (4,922) were provided the amounts through bank transfer on Monday.
“But according to inputs by district authorities, the number of affected families could rise to 75,000. We are prepared to pay the same amount to another 15,000 affected families as and when their bank details are received and corroborated,” he said.

The CM stated that assessment of more affected families would continue till August 5 and the interim relief would be provided to them after completing all necessary formalities in the next two days.
“For those families from Sibsagar and Charaideo (the two most affected districts) who are not in a position to return to their homes till August 9 due to flooding and other issues, we will provide them with another sum of ₹10,000 each,” he said.
Sarma said that an assessment on the permanent damages incurred due to flooding will be carried out from next week and completed in ten days. After that compensation amounts to rebuild their homes would be disbursed.
The CM informed about the other measures undertaken by the state government to provide relief to those affected including providing ₹9 lakh each to families of those who have lost their kin in flooding.
A six month moratorium on loans and extension of loan repayment tenure by 1-2 years and an additional ₹2,500 each to families in flood-affected districts covered under the flagship Orunodoi poverty alleviation scheme are some of the other announcements made.
Sarma stated that the flood affected families won’t have to pay land taxes for a year and also waived off the electricity bill for July for them.
Heavy flooding in the worst-affected districts have claimed 85 lives till Sunday and according to figures released by Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) on Sunday, 1,36,203 persons in five districts were still affected while 10,844 persons were taking shelter in relief camps.

Bankipur by-poll: Prashant Kishor leads by 1,145 votes after 4 rounds of counting
Bankipur assembly by-election was necessitated by Nitin Nabin’s election as a Rajya Sabha member after his elevation as the BJP chief
Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor was leading by 1,145 votes after four rounds of counting for Bihar’s Bankipur assembly by-election necessitated by Nitin Nabin’s election as a Rajya Sabha member after his elevation as the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) chief. Kishor made his electoral debut in the July 30 bypoll, months after his party failed to win any of the 238 seats it contested in the 2025 Bihar assembly polls.
Kishor canvassed across the constituency and framed the contest as a referendum on the government’s performance and targeted chief minister Samrat Choudhary. Nabin assured voters that Bankipur shall remain his top priority despite new responsibilities.
Kishor polled 6,269 votes after three rounds, BJP’s Neeraj Kumar Sinha 5,124, and Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)’s Rekha Kumari 884. Kishor led by 862 votes after the first, 1161 after the second, and 1162 after the third round of counting. The lead declined marginally in the fourth round as Sinha polled 17 votes more than Kishor.
Officials said the counting is expected to be completed in 31 rounds across 14 counting tables, with the result likely to be declared later in the afternoon.
A dismal 34.30% voter turnout was recorded in the July 30 bypoll. Around 130,000 of the 3,79,616 electors voted. The turnout was nearly seven percentage points lower than the 41.35% in the 2025 assembly election.
The contest was effectively triangular among Sinha, Kishor and Kumari, even as 25 candidates were in the fray.
The byelection is a prestige battle and an organisational test for the BJP. Sinha, a former booth-level worker and district president, is seeking to retain a constituency that has been the BJP’s stronghold for over three decades. The party has held the seat since 1995. Nabin was first elected from the seat in the 2006 bypoll.
The 2026 bypoll was the first since Choudhary replaced Nitish Kumar after helming the state for nearly two decades and Nabin’s elevation as the BJP national president.

West Bengal police’s Special Task Force (STF) on Monday arrested a college student for his alleged links to Jaish-e-Mohammed operative Hamim Mondal.
“Aditya Singh was arrested from Howrah district. Singh lived in an apartment with his family on Howrah’s Belilious Road,” said a police officer.
The STF arrested Mondal from East Burdwan district on Friday and Arpita Sharma from Sahibganj in Jharkhand on Saturday for their alleged links to a Pakistan-based terror module run by Shahzad Bhatti.
Police said Mondal was setting up a network in West Bengal and planned to target chief minister Suvendu Adhikari.

Preliminary investigations suggested that Singh had shared information about Rai’s movements and pictures of Rai and his son, their residence and their vehicle with Mondal.
“These are actual enemies of our society. They help Pakistani terrorists in lieu of money,” Rai said.
