Don't look at Bangladesh or Nepal, follow Gandhi: CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke
Abhijeet Dipke said Indian student protesters should follow Gandhi's peaceful path, not Bangladesh or Nepal. He used the interview to press for NEET relief, recruitment reforms and higher priority for education.
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has rejected comparisons between his group's recent student protest in Delhi and the upheavals in Bangladesh and Nepal, saying Indian students should draw inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi instead.
In an interview to PTI, Dipke defended the protest over alleged exam irregularities and insisted that the demonstrators had followed the Constitution and maintained peace despite police action.
"Protests in Bangladesh, Nepal are being used to defame us; we are different," Dipke said.
"We showed during the recent protest in Delhi that we were following the Constitution and holding our demonstration peacefully. Parallels to the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal are being used to defame us," he added.
Rejecting remarks by exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen linking the Delhi protest to the 2024 agitation in Bangladesh that led to the fall of Sheikh Hasina's Awami League government, Dipke said India did not need to look outside for models of protest.
"We don't need to look at Bangladesh or Nepal when we have Mahatma Gandhi from whom the world takes inspiration to protest," he said.
'STUDENTS DISPLAYED RESTRAINT'
Dipke said some people may have drawn parallels with protests in Bangladesh and Nepal because of the police action during the Delhi demonstration.
"The students in India were not violent or aggressive. They got their heads, arms and legs broken but displayed restraint and sat peacefully at Jantar Mantar," he said.
He also argued that education should become a central issue in electoral politics.
"If you don't make education the main agenda in election, it means you are not thinking about the future. Education is an investment for the future of the country," Dipke said.
DEMAND FOR NEET VICTIMS' COMPENSATION
Dipke criticised the government over what he described as a delay in compensation to families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide.
"They have money to topple government overnight. You can buy MPs and MLAs by spending hundreds of crores of rupees, but when it comes to the NEET victims and their kin, they look at the norms," he said.
He warned that CJP could launch another agitation if its demands were not addressed.
"The government should meet our demands as soon as possible, or else we will launch another agitation," he said.
Dipke also urged Gen Z protesters to maintain restraint and not imitate the conduct of politicians.
He said young protesters should "not reach the level of BJP leaders" who, according to him, abuse even in Parliament and at public rallies.
"There is some difference between us and the goons and that difference should always be there," he said.
SUPPORT FOR JHARKHAND STUDENTS
Dipke extended CJP's support to students protesting in Jharkhand over alleged irregularities in the state public service examination and other recruitment tests.
He backed their demand for a CBI probe and reforms in recruitment agencies, saying the movement was against the system rather than any political party.
"Their fight is not against any political party but against the system. We stand with their demands. If they want a CBI probe, we are going to support them in pursuing that," he said.
He said CJP would support student movements over education and recruitment issues irrespective of which party was in power.
"Wherever agitations will happen for education and wherever students come forward to demand their rights, we are going to stand with them, irrespective of the ruling party in that state," Dipke said.
"The rules are the same as our fight is not against any political party. It is against the system that has let down the students of the country," he added.
OPPOSITION LEADERS' SUPPORT
Asked about opposition leaders who visited Jantar Mantar to support the student protest, Dipke said they did not use the platform for political promotion.
"Everyone was sensitive towards the students' agitation. They were very sensitive towards the cause and the students. When they were on the stage at Jantar Mantar, none of these leaders spoke about their political party, but said they were there to support the students," he said.
CJP PLANS EXPANSION
Dipke said CJP would discuss its future roadmap at a meeting at his residence in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on August 5.
Around 10 to 15 people are expected to attend the meeting, with other volunteers also expected to play a role in expanding the movement.
"The expansion of CJP will take place. Our responsibility has increased after the success of the recent protest. People's expectations about CJP have also gone up. In the meeting on Wednesday, we will discuss our future roadmap," Dipke said.
'EDUCATION MUST GET MAXIMUM SPENDING'
Dipke also criticised what he described as the gap between India's education system and those in other countries, particularly in infrastructure and practical learning.
"The biggest difference is that foreign countries have a good infrastructure when it comes to education," he said.
Drawing on his own experience in the US, Dipke said courses there were more practical and less theoretical, and argued that India needed to create greater scope for practical learning.
He also claimed that the present government was spending less on education than the previous regime.
"The maximum funds should go towards education. There is no dearth of funds with the government, so I don't understand why they are reducing expenditure on education. Education is something where the maximum spending should take place as it is the foundation of a nation," he said.
"We don't know how much money there is in the PM Cares Fund. I think the education department could really take some help from that fund," he added.
Dipke said education had become unaffordable and inaccessible for many people in India and called for greater government spending on the sector.

headline: 22 children die of Chandipura virus in Gujarat, 7 under treatment
cluster_text: 22 children die of Chandipura virus in Gujarat, 7 under treatment [SEP] 22 children die of Chandipura virus in Gujarat, 7 under treatment
full_text:
22 children die of Chandipura virus in Gujarat, 7 under treatment
Gujarat Health Minister Praful Panseriya said all confirmed patients are below the age of 15 and clarified that the infections are not concentrated in any one village or district.
The Chandipura virus has claimed the lives of 22 children in Gujarat this monsoon season, with 35 infections confirmed out of 184 suspected cases reported so far, state Health Minister Praful Panseriya said on Monday.
Test results of 11 samples are still awaited.
Seven children who tested positive are currently undergoing treatment at civil hospitals across the state, while six patients have recovered and been discharged. Children admitted to hospitals in Gandhinagar, Sabarkantha-Himmatnagar, Patan, Rajkot and Bhavnagar are receiving specialised treatment under the supervision of expert doctors, he said.
The minister said all confirmed patients are below the age of 15 and clarified that the infections are not concentrated in any one village or district. Cases have been reported from different parts of Gujarat, prompting health authorities to remain on high alert.
To curb the spread of the virus, health department teams have intensified surveillance and launched large-scale insecticide spraying, particularly in livestock-rearing areas where sandflies — the primary carriers of the virus — are commonly found. Residents have also been advised to seal cracks in mud houses and walls, which can serve as breeding spots for the insects.
The government has directed all government and private paediatric hospitals to immediately admit children showing symptoms such as high fever, vomiting, seizures or altered consciousness to intensive care units equipped with oxygen and ventilator support. Early treatment is crucial to prevent severe complications, including multiple organ failure, officials said.
There is currently no specific vaccine or antiviral treatment for the Chandipura virus.
Gujarat Health Minister Praful Panseriya urged people not to panic or pay attention to rumours and appealed to parents to seek immediate medical attention if children develop symptoms. He also asked citizens to cooperate with health teams conducting surveillance and preventive measures.
Chandipura encephalitis is a rare viral disease that primarily spreads through sandflies and causes inflammation of the brain. The virus was first identified in Chandipura village in Maharashtra's Nagpur district in 1965. It mainly affects children and can progress rapidly if not treated in time.

headline: Delhi to open Ghazipur modern poultry market by December amid wider revamp
cluster_text: Delhi to open Ghazipur modern poultry market by December amid wider revamp [SEP] Delhi to open Ghazipur modern poultry market by December amid wider revamp
full_text:
Delhi to open Ghazipur modern poultry market by December amid wider revamp
From a Rs 193-crore poultry hub nearing completion to new grain market sheds, Delhi is expanding its agricultural infrastructure while planning a phased modern flower market at Ghazipur.
Delhi is set for a major overhaul of its agricultural markets, with a Rs 193-crore modern poultry market at Ghazipur due for completion by December, two new steel sheds planned at Narela and a modern flower market proposed at the Integrated Freight Complex in Ghazipur.
Chief Minister Rekha Gupta reviewed the progress of ongoing and proposed infrastructure projects at Ghazipur, Narela and the Integrated Freight Complex and directed officials to ensure that the works are completed within their deadlines, according to an official statement.
Gupta said agricultural markets are a vital link between farmers, traders and consumers and need modern infrastructure to keep pace with changing requirements.
RS 193-CRORE POULTRY MARKET AT GHAZIPUR
The modern poultry market at Ghazipur, spread across nearly 15 acres, has been under construction since March 2019 and is scheduled to be completed by December 31.
The facility will accommodate 100 wholesale traders and have 120 poultry processing units, according to the government.
The project is among the major infrastructure works being monitored by the Delhi government as part of its efforts to upgrade agricultural markets in the capital.
MODERN FLOWER MARKET PLANNED AT GHAZIPUR
The government also reviewed plans for a modern flower market at the Integrated Freight Complex in Ghazipur.
Around 10 acres of land acquired from the Delhi Development Authority in 2001 has been earmarked for the project. The proposed market will be developed in phases.
The project is intended to add modern infrastructure for the city's flower trade alongside the existing agricultural market facilities in the Ghazipur area.
DRAINAGE, SANITATION WORK AT GHAZIPUR
At the Ghazipur Fruit, Vegetable and Flower Market, work is underway to address waterlogging through the construction of a 200-metre bypass drainage pipeline.
The project has been approved at a cost of Rs 17 lakh.
Officials also told the chief minister that regular drives are being conducted to remove stray animals from the market premises as part of efforts to improve sanitation.
TWO NEW SHEDS FOR NARELA GRAIN MARKET
The government has also proposed two additional steel sheds at the Narela Grain Market at an estimated cost of around Rs 11 crore.
The new structures are expected to be completed by July 2027.
The projects at Narela, Ghazipur and the Integrated Freight Complex formed part of the review meeting, with the chief minister asking officials to keep the works on schedule.
The overall plan covers the completion of the Ghazipur poultry market, drainage and sanitation improvements at the Ghazipur market, new infrastructure at Narela and the phased development of the proposed flower market.

headline: Zuckerberg apology sought over PM Modi video takedown, Meta faces panel heat

full_text:
Zuckerberg apology sought over PM Modi video takedown, Meta faces panel heat
A parliamentary panel has sought answers from Meta over why a PM Modi video disappeared from Facebook for hours. The episode has now raised questions over accountability, safe harbour and platform moderation.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg should personally apologise for the temporary removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's video from Facebook, Parliamentary Standing Committee on Information Technology chairman Nishikant Dubey said on Monday after a meeting with representatives of the social media giant.
Speaking after the more than three-hour meeting, Dubey said Meta had acknowledged that Modi's video remained unavailable on the platform for about five hours, from 12.30 am to 5 am.
"They themselves admitted that the video was taken down for five hours. This is a very serious matter and an apology must come from Zuckerberg's side," Dubey said, according to PTI.
He also warned that if Zuckerberg did not apologise, the government should consider withdrawing Meta's safe harbour protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act.
The provision protects intermediaries from liability for third-party content under certain conditions.
WHY WAS PM MODI'S VIDEO REMOVED?
The meeting was convened after a Facebook post by Modi on action against paper leaks was briefly removed from the platform.
Meta had earlier attributed the incident to a technical glitch, apologised and restored the post. However, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology described the explanation as "inadequate".
Sources said the parliamentary panel has asked Meta to submit a written response within 10 days.
During the meeting, several BJP MPs questioned Meta representatives over who authorised the removal of the Prime Minister's video and sought clarity on who was responsible.
Members also raised concerns over alleged algorithmic bias, arguing that objectionable material remained available on the platform while "genuine" content was removed.
META OFFICIALS EXPRESS REGRET
According to sources, Meta representatives expressed regret over the incident and indicated that they were willing to apologise before the committee.
BJP members, however, argued that the matter went beyond an apology and called for accountability to be fixed, with legal action to be considered if warranted.
Opposition MPs on the committee took a different position, arguing that social media platforms must preserve space for dissent in a democracy.
They also cautioned against treating criticism of the government as anti-national content.
GOOGLE, X, YOUTUBE ALSO APPEAR
The meeting was part of the parliamentary panel's broader examination of the regulation of social and digital platforms.
Apart from Meta representatives, Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, MeitY Secretary S Krishnan and officials from Google, X, YouTube and Snapchat also appeared before the committee.
The episode has put fresh focus on how major social media platforms moderate political content and the extent of accountability they should face when posts by public figures are removed, even temporarily.

headline: How a National Highway rumble strip row forced NHAI into an embarrassing U-turn
cluster_text: How a National Highway rumble strip row forced NHAI into an embarrassing U-turn [SEP] How a National Highway rumble strip row forced NHAI into an embarrassing U-turn
full_text:
How a National Highway rumble strip row forced NHAI into an embarrassing U-turn
After initially rejecting reports on faulty rumble strips on a Rajasthan National Highway, NHAI was forced into a U-turn, suspending its Project Director and ordering corrective measures after social media user-shared visuals exposed discrepancies in its earlier defence.
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has suspended a Project Director after reversing its earlier stand on a controversy over faulty rumble strips at a median opening near Prathvipura village on National Highway-25 in Rajasthan. The action came after several users on X shared visuals from the site, challenging the highway authority's initial claim that reports on the issue were misleading.
The controversy escalated when users pointed out that the images shared by NHAI to counter the reports were not from the same spot but from a different location altogether, prompting accusations that the official had misrepresented the ground situation.
Following a detailed review, NHAI acknowledged that there had been incorrect reporting by the concerned official on social media, placed the Project Director under suspension, and said corrective measures were being undertaken at the site to ensure it conforms to prescribed road safety standards.
"As reported by some sections of the media regarding construction of rumble strips at the median opening near Prathvipura village on NH-25 in Rajasthan, NHAI would like to inform that the media reportage does not depict the actual condition of the section. The construction of rumbling strips is being carried out at the request of the local public representative to enhance the safety of both National Highway users and the residents of the village," the authority had said in a post on X on Monday morning.
The post added, "NHAI appreciates the valuable feedback received from the Highway users and remains committed to ensure a safe travel experience for all commuters."
The issue first came to light after reports highlighted the construction of rumble strips at a median opening on NH-25, raising concerns over road safety.
NHAI had initially dismissed the reports, maintaining that the reports did not accurately depict the condition of the stretch and that the rumble strips had been constructed at the request of a local public representative to enhance safety for both highway users and nearby residents.
However, the explanation failed to convince many social media users, who continued posting photographs and videos from the site, showing that the visuals shared by NHAI were from a different location and did not address the reported problem.
One user commented, "It's not the same place. You think we're stupid or something?" Another pointed out, "It's not just another angle but the opposite lane altogether. We have a divider in between, so the speed breakers will also be different. Clearly, misinformation has been shared by NHAI."
A third user wrote, "So you are saying this video is a lie?" Another user mocked the authority's response by writing, "If that's a rumble strip, then this is a Maruti Alto," while posting a picture of a Tata Signa truck.
As criticism mounted, NHAI issued a fresh statement admitting that there had been incorrect reporting on social media by the concerned official.
"NHAI would like to inform that, following a detailed review of the matter, the concerned Project Director has been placed under suspension for wrong reporting in social media on rumble strips," the authority said.
It added that necessary corrective measures were being undertaken to ensure the stretch fully complies with prescribed road safety standards.
"NHAI remains committed to the highest standards of safety and quality on the National Highway network and values the constructive feedback received from National Highway users," the authority said in its latest statement.
The episode has sparked debate over accountability in official communication, with many on social media pointing to the gap between NHAI's initial denial and its subsequent admission of incorrect reporting.

In a bid to strengthen the judiciary's capacity and address the mounting pendency of cases, the Lok Sabha on Monday passed the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, clearing the way for an increase in the sanctioned strength of the apex court.
The legislation amends the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956 to raise the number of Supreme Court judges from 33 to 37, excluding the Chief Justice of India (CJI). Including the CJI, the court's total sanctioned strength will increase from 34 to 38 judges.
The Bill, introduced by Union Law and Justice Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal, replaces an ordinance promulgated by the President in May 2026.

What changed in 8 months that BJP lost Bankipur to Prashant Kishor? 5 big factors
The BJP won the Bankipur seat in the Assembly election in November 2025 by a margin of 52,000 votes. On Monday, Prashant Kishor of Jan Suraaj snatched the seat in a bypoll from the BJP by a margin of 19,000 votes. Here are the five big factors that swung fortunes completely in a span of eight months.
Of the three Assembly seats whose bypoll results were declared on Monday, Bihar's Bankipur emerged as the biggest setback for the BJP. Prashant Kishor, the chief of Jan Suraaj Party, emerged victorious, defeating the BJP candidate by a margin of over 19,000 votes.
There are three reasons why the result is particularly stinging for the BJP. One, this was a seat that was vacated by Nitin Nabin, who was promoted as the BJP national President. Two, this seat has been with the BJP since 1995. Three, the party in power in a state, which is the BJP in Bihar, is generally at an advantage of winning a bypoll in the state.
This is the debut election that Prashant Kishor, or PK as he is better known as, has contested. His victory also marks the first win for the Jan Suraaj Party, which made its debut during the Bihar Assembly election in November 2025.
What has really changed in eight months between November 2025 and July 30, 2026, when voting was held for the seat in Bankipur that led to the defeat of BJP's Neeraj Kumar by PK? In November Assembly elections, Nabin won the seat by a margin of nearly 52,000 votes.
Here are the five big factors that led to the BJP's defeat in the bypoll in Bankipur, a seat for which the party had assigned 40 star campaigners, including Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and Union Ministers like Nityanand Rai and Giriraj Singh.
1. REFERENDUM ON NITISH KUMAR'S SUCCESSOR SAMRAT CHOUDHARY
The Bankipur bypoll effectively became a referendum on Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary's leadership. This was the first electoral test for the BJP after it assumed the chief minister's office in Bihar.
Choudhary took over as the state's first BJP chief minister in April, succeeding JD(U) stalwart Nitish Kumar, who had dominated Bihar politics for nearly two decades.
Prashant Kishor sought to frame the contest as a direct battle between himself and Samrat Choudhary. Throughout the campaign, the Jan Suraaj founder repeatedly targeted Choudhary over alleged criminal cases and education qualifications, turning what was expected to be a routine bypoll into a high-stakes political showdown for the BJP's new face in Bihar.
This line of messaging was reflected in what PK said after he was declared a winner at Bankipur. "The people of Bankipur have sent a clear message to the BJP leadership: 'Please appoint a good person as the Chief Minister of Bihar.' If the BJP wants to replace Samrat Chaudhary with another leader from the Kushwaha community, that is entirely their decision. We have no objection. But whoever is chosen should be a capable and upright person from the Kushwaha community," news agency ANI quoted PK as saying.
2. ANTI-INCUMBENCY OF 30 YEARS AND LACK OF DEVELOPMENT
The Bankipur Assembly seat was with Nitin Nabin for 20 years. Before that, it was with his father, Nabin Kishore Prasad Sinha, for two terms. The seat has been with the Sinha family since 1995 and was prone to strong anti-incumbency sentiments.
Prabhu Chawla, Editorial Director of The New Indian Express, said Bankipur "wasn’t an ideological safe seat for the BJP. It was a family fiefdom of the Sinha's [Nitin Nabin family]."
"Bankipur saw a clash between two personalities. It was a giant Prashant Kishor vs an unknown pigmy, some Sinha. And a non-performing chief minister made it easier for Jan Suraaj to walk away with a trophy. No big lessons emerge from this non-battle," Chawla wrote on X.

Another factor that appears to have worked in PK's favour was the apparent fragmentation of the Rashtriya Janata Dal's (RJD) traditional Muslim-Yadav (M-Y) support base, long regarded as the party's electoral backbone.

If that trend continues, he said, Jan Suraaj could gradually occupy the opposition space that was once held by the RJD.
4. UPPER CASTE VOTES MOVED AWAY FROM BJP TO JAN SURAAJ
Political analyst Amitabh Tiwari said that a factor behind PK's victory was a possible erosion of the BJP's traditional upper-caste support base in Bankipur.

5. PK's CLEAN POLITICS VS BJP's PERCEIVED ARROGANCE
Beyond the caste arithmetic and anti-incumbency, the campaign narrative might also have influenced voters. Kishor's bypoll campaign, coming just months after he led a high-voltage statewide campaign during the 2025 Assembly election, centred on Bihar's local issues, might also have influenced voters. The bypoll also came amid some discontent over the student protests over paper leak controversies.
Prashant Kishor projected Jan Suraaj as an alternative focused on governance, accountability and clean politics, while some BJP leaders' confidence about retaining Bankipur became a talking point.
Political analyst Amitabh Tiwari argued that Bihar's electorate has historically reacted against perceived political arrogance.

The remark, made by some BJP leaders before the election to underline the party's dominance in Bankipur, resurfaced during the campaign and after the result, with Jan Suraaj supporters portraying it as a symbol of overconfidence.
The campaign in Bankipur was an opportunity for Kishor to present himself as a politician able to fight and seeking to build a new political culture in Bihar. Combined with the mood created by student protests and anti-incumbency sentiments, that messaging appeared to have resonated with at least a section of voters.
Bankipur hasn't changed Bihar's government, but it might have changed the political conversation that we would hear ahead of the next election. Was this a one-off bypoll upset or the first sign of a broader political realignment? Only the next Assembly election can answer that. For Prashant Kishor, however, the victory at Bankipur could well mark a major milestone in his journey from farsh to arsh.

Choudhary, who joined the BJP less than a decade ago and became the party's first leader to head a government in Bihar, congratulated Kishor in a post on X and described the contest as "the grand festival of democracy".

A senior BJP leader attributed the defeat to growing dissatisfaction among the party's traditional upper-caste support base.
"Prashant Kishor struck all the right notes. He tapped into the growing dissatisfaction among the upper castes by raising issues like the death after suspected rape of a NEET aspirant and the police encounter of Bharat Tiwari," the leader said on condition of anonymity.

The Bankipur victory marks Jan Suraaj's first electoral success after the party drew a blank in last year's Bihar Assembly election.

The bypoll was necessitated after fifth-term MLA Nitin Nabin resigned from Bankipur following his election to the Rajya Sabha after being elevated as the BJP's national president.

full_text:
PK's victory over BJP a freak voter experiment in Bihar?
Just eight months after the BJP won Bankipur by nearly 52,000 votes, poll strategist-turned-politician Prashant Kishor flipped one of the saffron party's safest seats with a margin of over 19,000 votes. Is this the first sign of a churn in Bihar or is it simply the kind of voter experiment that a bypoll can produce?
Poll strategist-turned-politician Prashant Kishor (PK)'s maiden electoral victory in the Bankipur Assembly bypoll on Monday has delivered the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) one of its most surprising defeats in recent years. Contesting for a seat the BJP had held continuously since 1995, the Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder defeated the BJPs' Neeraj Kumar Sinha by more than 19,000 votes. However, the victory for PK, months after the Jan Suraaj drew a black in the 2025 Assembly polls, has raised questions if the result reveals a political churn in Bihar. Or is it merely a peculiar nature of bypolls?
The result comes barely a few months after Jan Suraaj failed to win a single seat in its debut, where around 90% of its candidates lost their security deposits. Bankipur was considered a BJP fortress, with the party expecting a bigger margin than in the previous elections. So, why did the BJP lose the seat its national president had represented five times in the Bihar Assembly? Was it an experiment by the voters who said why not?
Political observers cautioned against reading too much into a bypoll. Some said it was a combination of anti-incumbency, youth anger and cracks in traditional vote banks behind Kishor's victory. Others argued that bypolls like the one in Bankipur encourage voters to experiment because they do not alter the balance of power.
BANKIPUR BYPOLL: A BIHAR POLL RESULT FEW SAW COMING
According to the Election Commission, Prashant Kishor secured 63,203 votes against the 44,250 by the BJP's Neeraj Kumar, while the RJD finished a distant third.
The outcome stunned some observers largely because Bankipur has been among the BJP's safest urban constituencies in Bihar. Earlier known as Patna West, the seat has remained with the BJP since 1995.
It fell vacant after BJP national president Nitin Nabin resigned following his election to the Rajya Sabha. Nabin himself had won the seat five consecutive times, including a victory last year by nearly 52,000 votes.
The BJP even changed its candidate midway, replacing Abhishek 'Bunty' with karyakarta Neeraj Kumar Sinha barely a day after the first nomination. But the seat, widely associated with the BJP's prestige, has slipped away.
What explains the BJP's slide from a 52,000-vote victory margin in November to a nearly 20,000-vote defeat just nine months later?
ARE BYPOLLS ANY DIFFERENT FROM MAIN ELECTIONS?
Political analyst and VoteVibe founder Amitabh Tiwari, speaking to India Today Digital, said that he believes the result cannot be explained by one reason alone.
"Every election result has multiple explanations. Bankipur is no different," he said.
According to Tiwari, anti-incumbency, the RJD's weakening support base, cracks in the BJP's traditional upper-caste coalition, and youth anger could be major factors behind PK's win at Bankipur. Tiwari, however, pointed to "the psychology unique to bypolls".
"Unlike a full Assembly election, the result could neither form nor topple the government. That might have encouraged voters to experiment, believing they could vote for change without affecting the stability of the BJP-led government," Tiwari, whose VoteVibe carried out extensive surveys at Bankipur, told India Today Digital.
New Delhi-based lawyer Nagendar Sharma on his X handle said that he believed that bypolls should not be treated as indicators of trends. According to him, victories of ruling parties in bypolls are usually considered almost inevitable because of "the might have state machinery and lukewarm voters' response", unless an extraordinary contest changes the equation.
"Since nothing changes due to bypoll results, it is difficult to bring alive voters' enthusiasm, unless a seat becomes high-profile and an upset can create ripples," he wrote. That, Sharma argued, is precisely why Bankipur has attracted attention beyond Bihar.
Whether the result of Bankipur would signal an erosion of BJP support, or acceptance of PK's Jan Suraaj, remains debatable. The bypoll battle in Bankipur was fought under unusual circumstances. There was a lower turnout of 34%. There was a high-profile challenger, PK. And, a constituency where dissatisfaction might have accumulated after three decades of uninterrupted BJP representation of the seat in Patna.
So, to sum up, whether the Bankipur verdict in favour of PK was a freak result, remains open to interpretation. But history suggests caution. Bypolls sometimes produce outcomes that do not repeat in general elections. Voters sometimes use bypolls to send messages without changing governments. But, history also has examples of those rare bypolls that are now called watershed moments. VP Singh's 1988 Allahabad bypoll victory is one such example.

full_text:
Not BJP, but RJD has more to worry after Prashant Kishor's Bankipur victory
While the BJP lost its 30-year fortress in the heart of Patna, the RJD might have suffered the more significant political setback. With anti-BJP votes likely getting consolidated with Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor, Bankipur could mark the beginning of a larger realignment in Bihar's opposition politics.
Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor's victory in the Bankipur bypoll on Monday will be remembered as the battle that ended the BJP's 35-year dominance in one of its safest constituencies in Bihar. Yet, beyond the celebration of PK's political breakthrough lies a bigger question. Was the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD), rather than the BJP, the real loser in the Bankipur verdict?
PK defeated the BJP's Neeraj Kumar by 19,324 votes, but the bypoll also exposed another emerging trend — the shrinking political space occupied by the RJD. The party's candidate, Rekha Kumari, finished third and managed to get only 14,273 votes.
The Bankipur Assembly seat has around four lakh voters, and the bypoll voter turnout was only 34.24%.
The BJP might have been decimated from one of its safest seats, but it remains the state's ruling party. For the RJD, however, finishing a distant third in a contest where anti-BJP votes appeared to consolidate behind PK's Jan Suraaj Party has raised deeper concerns.
If Bankipur is an indication of Bihar's changing political mood, PK might not just have dented the BJP's fortress, he might have begun eating into the RJD's position as the state's principal opposition.
The Bankipur Assembly seat fell vacant after BJP national president Nitin Nabin resigned as MLA following his election to the Rajya Sabha. For over 30 years, the constituency has been synonymous with the Nabin family — 20 years under BJP national president Nitin Nabin and the previous 15 under his father, Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha.
What was expected to be a routine BJP victory turned into the biggest political contest in Bihar after the 49-year-old poll strategist-turned-politician Prashant Kishor entered the fray with the party he established in 2024.
"One of the factors for PK's Bankipur victory is the RJD's decline. Its traditional Muslim-Yadav support base appeared to fragment," Political Analyst and VoteVibe founder Amitabh Tiwari told India Today Digital after the results were announced on Monday.
The JSP couldn't even manage to secure a single seat in the previously held state Assembly election in 2025, and now its founder has won its first seat in the 243-member Assembly.
BANKIPUR SETBACK: WILL PRASHANT KISHOR'S JSP EAT RJD?
For nearly three decades, Bihar's politics revolved around two poles, Lalu Prasad Yadav's RJD and Nitish Kumar's Janata Dal (United). The BJP's rise altered that equation, and the opposition space largely remained with the RJD.
That equation might now be changing in Bihar with Prashant Kishor's maiden electoral success.
With the JD(U)'s influence waning after Nitish Kumar stepped down as chief minister in April and the BJP taking direct control of the government under Samrat Choudhary, the RJD appeared well-placed to emerge as the principal challenger to the ruling alliance. Instead, Bankipur has now made the possibility of Prashant Kishor seizing that space from the RJD.
Political analyst Amitabh Tiwari believes the result is significant not merely because the BJP lost, but because the JSP appears to be occupying political ground once considered RJD territory.
"The RJD had been reduced to just 22 Assembly seats in 2010 before reviving to around 80 seats in 2015, with Nitish Kumar's support in the Mahagathbandhan. But by the 2025 Bihar Assembly election, it had slipped back to around 25 seats, almost returning to its 2010 position. Now, finishing third in Bankipur adds to concerns about the party's political trajectory," Tiwari told India Today Digital.
He argues that if Jan Suraaj Party continues expanding at this pace, it could eventually emerge as Bihar's principal opposition to the BJP.
"The shift is unlikely to happen immediately, but Bankipur may prove to be the first indication that the JSP is beginning to take political space once held by the RJD. With the Congress also appearing to drift away from the RJD-led alliance, Bihar's opposition politics could witness a major realignment," he said.
DID MUSLIMS DITCH RJD AND LEAN TOWARDS PRASHANT KISHOR'S JSP?
The RJD's political identity has long rested on the Muslim-Yadav (M-Y) alliance crafted by its patriarch Lalu Prasad Yadav in the 1990s.
Post-poll studies have consistently shown overwhelming support from both communities for the RJD. Around 74% of Yadavs and nearly 70% of Muslims backed the RJD in the 2025 Assembly elections, according to the CSDS Lok Niti survey. In 2020, the figures stood at 83% for Yadavs and 62% for Muslims.
That is why Bankipur has generated so much discussion at the moment.
According to Tiwari, the biggest shift in the bypoll came from Muslim voters, many of whom appeared to back the JSP instead of the RJD.
"The Muslim voters are consolidating behind Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj because it is the party that's best placed to take on the BJP," Tiwari had told India Today Digital on July 30 after polling was done.
"Many Muslim voters, who have historically opposed the BJP, viewed Prashant Kishor as the strongest challenger capable of defeating the BJP and shifted towards the JSP instead of backing the RJD. That appears to have pushed the RJD into third place," he said on Monday.
The logic, analysts say, is rooted less in ideology than in electoral arithmetic. Muslim voters have traditionally rallied behind whichever opposition party appears best positioned to defeat the BJP. In Bankipur, many seem to have concluded that Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj Party and not the RJD, offered the stronger challenge to the BJP.
If that perception spreads beyond one constituency, the implications for Bihar's opposition politics could be profound.
Bankipur was never just about one Assembly seat or just a mere bypoll.
For the BJP, it was the loss of a fortress it had defended for 30 years. For Prashant Kishor, it was the validation of a political experiment that many had dismissed after Jan Suraaj Party's poor showing in the 2025 Assembly elections.

Unexpected mandate: Nitin Nabin after Prashant Kishor wins BJP's Bankipur bastion
Prashant Kishor defeated BJP's Neeraj Kumar in the Bankipur bypoll, ending the party's three-decade hold on the seat. BJP chief Nitin Nabin accepted the verdict and said the losses in Bankipur and Datia would be reviewed seriously.
BJP chief Nitin Nabin on Monday said he accepted the verdict of the three Assembly bypolls, including a stunning defeat in his family bastion of Bihar's Bankipur, where Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor won, ending the saffron party's 30-year dominance.
In a post on X after the results, Nabin stressed that the results in Bankipur and Madhya Pradesh's Datia, where the Congress won, were unexpected, and an introspection would be done with "complete seriousness". He also thanked voters in Gujarat's Manjalpur, where the BJP retained the seat, for reposing faith in the party, and congratulated party workers on the victory there.
"We accept the mandate received in today's three assembly by-elections. We express our heartfelt gratitude to the people of Manjalpur assembly constituency in Gujarat for expressing their faith in the BJP. We extend our warm congratulations to all the dedicated workers and office-bearers of the BJP for this victory," Nabin tweeted in Hindi.
"In Bankipur and Datia, we did not receive the expected mandate. We will conduct a thorough introspection of the election results in both these areas with complete seriousness, and with renewed energy and determination, we will continue to go among the people and work tirelessly to further strengthen their trust, he said.
The remarks came after Kishor registered his first electoral victory, defeating BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar by 19,324 votes from the prestigious Bankipur seat in Patna. Kishor polled 64,151 votes against Kumar's 44,827, while RJD's Rekha Kumari finished a distant third with 14,273 votes.
The win marked a dramatic turnaround for the Jan Suraaj founder, whose party had failed to win a single seat in the November 2025 Assembly polls. Kishor had chosen not to contest those polls himself.
The result marked the end of the BJP's uninterrupted hold over the constituency since 1995. The bypoll was necessitated after Nabin vacated the seat following his election to the Rajya Sabha in April, and after winning the constituency for a fifth consecutive term in the Assembly polls.
The BJP's winning streak in the seat began in 1995, when it was known as the Patna West constituency, with Nabin's late father, Navin Chandra Sinha. Since then, both Sinha and Nabin had represented the constituency for three decades, making Bankipur one of the BJP's strongest bastions in Bihar.
The saffron party's Bankipur campaign also suffered a late setback after its original candidate, Abhishek "Bunty", withdrew from the contest at the eleventh hour citing "family reasons". The party subsequently fielded Neeraj Kumar.
Kishor, 49, had described the by-election as a "referendum" on the BJP-led government in Bihar. After his victory, he called it a "wake-up call" for Prime Minister Narendra Modi and demanded a change in the state's leadership.
"The victory is a wake-up call for Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who must install a new Chief Minister in place of Samrat Choudhary, a man with criminal antecedents," Kishor said. Choudhary had replaced long-time CM Nitish Kumar, who went to the Rajya Sabha, in April.
The by-election witnessed a voter turnout of 34.30 per cent among nearly 3.8 lakh eligible voters, significantly lower than the 41.45 per cent recorded in the Assembly polls held just nine months ago.

headline: WhatsApp accounts placed 'under review' without warning, app features blocked
cluster_text: WhatsApp accounts placed 'under review' without warning, app features blocked [SEP] WhatsApp accounts placed 'under review' without warning, app features blocked
full_text:
WhatsApp accounts placed 'under review' without warning, app features blocked
The issue surfaced at around 8 pm IST, when affected users said they were unable to use WhatsApp's features after receiving an in-app notification stating that their accounts were being reviewed for compliance with the platform's Terms of Service.
Several WhatsApp users, including many in India, reported that their accounts had been unexpectedly placed "under review" on Monday evening, temporarily restricting access to the Meta-owned messaging platform and prompting complaints across social media.
The issue surfaced at around 8 pm IST, when affected users said they were unable to use WhatsApp's features after receiving an in-app notification stating that their accounts were being reviewed for compliance with the platform's Terms of Service, reports news agency PTI
The message displayed on the app read: "Account in review. Date requested: 3 Aug 2026. Your account activity and device info is being checked to make sure it follows our terms of service. We will notify you of the result, typically within 24 hours."
Below these remarks, the app shows an option to learn about account issues, which includes "How to use WhatsApp responsibly. See guidance" and an option "About stolen phone and accounts."
Responding to the reports, a WhatsApp spokesperson said the platform continuously works to detect and prevent abuse while protecting legitimate users.
"We are always working to stay ahead of those trying to abuse our service and ban accounts to help keep other users safe. Sometimes we get this wrong and if we do, we try to fix it as quickly as possible to get people back to chatting," PTI quoted a WhatsApp spokesperson as saying.
The company did not disclose how many accounts were affected or whether the reviews were linked to a technical issue, an automated enforcement system, or a broader anti-spam initiative.
Many users claimed the review was triggered without any prior warning and said they had not engaged in any activity that would violate the platform's policies.
Several took to social media to question why their accounts had been restricted and to seek clarification from the company.
It remains unclear whether the issue was limited to specific regions or affected users globally.

headline: Row over Udhayanidhi's 'double-meaning' remark on Trisha, TVK MLA says disgusting
cluster_text: Row over Udhayanidhi's 'double-meaning' remark on Trisha, TVK MLA says disgusting [SEP] Row over Udhayanidhi's 'double-meaning' remark on Trisha, TVK MLA says disgusting
full_text:
Row over Udhayanidhi's 'double-meaning' remark on Trisha, TVK MLA says disgusting
A clip of the incident has since circulated widely on social media, with critics accusing the DMK leader of making an inappropriate, double-meaning reference to Trisha.
DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin has come under fire after a viral video from a Cauvery protest in Thanjavur showed him making a remark involving actor Trisha that critics described as a double entendre.
TVK MLA Rhevanth Charan condemned the comment as “disgusting” and unacceptable, accusing the DMK leadership of lowering political discourse and resorting to provocation.
Addressing a rally on the Cauvery issue, Udhayanidhi was interrupted by chants of "Trisha, Trisha" as he criticised Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay.
“Not even a drop of Cauvery water has been received. But has the Chief Minister opened his mouth about it? No. He is only concerned with filing “false cases” against the DMK,” Udhayanidhi was heard saying in a video that has gone viral.
As the chants continued, he paused, smiled and made a remark that many interpreted as an innuendo about actor Trisha, Vijay's co-star and close friend, amid longstanding social media speculation about their relationship.
“Whether the water reaches anywhere else or not, it should reach there,” before smiling and clarifying that he was referring to the Cauvery.
TVK MLA, BJP SLAM UDHAYANIDHI
Reacting to the viral video, Charan called the remark “absolutely disgusting” and said such comments against anyone were unacceptable. He alleged that the episode reflected the DMK’s political culture and declining standards.
Charan also claimed that the protest had failed to gain traction and accused the party of turning to “cheap provocation” to attract attention on social media.
He warned that continued “arrogance and indecency” would further erode the DMK’s public relevance.
"This is precisely why the people of Tamil Nadu rejected you and confined you to the position you are in today. Even by Arivalayam’s already abysmal standards, this is a new low," he said.
The Tamil Nadu unit of the BJP, too, criticised the Leader of Opposition over his remark, calling it “disgusting, obscene, vulgar and shameful."
State BJP spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy also criticised former CM MK Stalin for remaining silent and demanded Udhayanidhi’s arrest, saying legal action would enhance Chief Minister Vijay’s credibility.
TVK URGES WOMEN'S PANEL TO ACT
The ruling party has written to the National Commission for Women (NCW) seeking action against Udhayanidhi. Calling the remarks "deeply troubling," the TVK said the language "normalises the objectification and verbal harassment of women in public spaces," "severely degrades the decorum expected of public figures," and sets "a dangerous precedent" for the treatment of women in public life.
TVK urged the NCW to take formal cognisance of the speech and rally footage, issue a notice seeking an explanation and an unconditional public apology. It also called for the DMK leader to be booked for public obscenity and outraging the modesty of women.

[SEP] Chikkamagaluru: The hopes of Chikkamagaluru district securing representation in the Cabinet were dashed once again after Congress leader Gayathri Shanthegowda’s name was dropped from the final list of ministers, despite earlier indications that she would be sworn in..The district Congress unit was optimistic that Gayathri Shanthegowda would take an oath as a minister even before being sworn in as a member of the legislative council (MLC). The excitement was short-lived with the dropping of her name from the second list..Gayathri had contested the 2021 Legislative Council election from the Local Authorities constituency but lost by just six votes. Challenging the inclusion of nominated members in the voting process, she approached both the Karnataka High Court and the Supreme Court.After nearly four-and-a-half years, the High Court set aside the election of M K Pranesh, paving the way for Gayathri’s election to the Legislative Council. Her election was officially announced only three days ago, though she is yet to take the oath as an MLC..Serial number 17.On Monday morning, a list of 20 ministers circulated by the All India Congress Committee included Gayathri Shanthegowda’s name at serial number 17. The document, carrying the signature of AICC General Secretary K C Venugopal, was widely shared, prompting Gayathri to express her happiness before the media. However, within hours, the list was revised, and her name was removed..Reacting to the development, Gayathri said, “The high command has only postponed its decision for now. I am confident that I will be given a ministerial berth in the future.”.Unrealised hope.During previous Congress governments, Chikkamagaluru had witnessed ministers from other districts. With all five Assembly constituencies in the district currently represented by Congress MLAs, party workers had hoped the district would finally secure a Cabinet berth in this expansion. The High Court’s verdict in Gayathri’s favour, delivered just days before the Cabinet expansion, had further strengthened the expectations. Seen as a close associate of former chief minister Siddaramaiah, Gayathri Shanthegowda was widely considered a strong contender..Two-time MLAs T D Rajegowda and G H Srinivas were also among those aspiring for ministerial positions. Meanwhile, Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma’s name had also figured in discussions, with supporters believing she could be accommodated under both the Scheduled Caste and women’s quota..22-year dream.Chikkamagaluru has been without a local representative in the Cabinet for the past 22 years. During the Congress government led by former chief minister S M Krishna from 1999 to 2004, the district had three representatives in the Cabinet- Motamma, D B Chandregowda and Sagir Ahmed..Since the end of their tenure over two decades ago, no leader from Chikkamagaluru has been inducted into the Cabinet under successive Congress governments.

[SEP] Davangere/ Shivamogga/ Chitradurga: Of the 13 legislators belonging to the ruling Congress party in the central Karnataka region comprising Shivamogga, Davangere and Chitradurga districts, four MLAs have found a place in Chief Minister D K Shivakumar’s Cabinet. They are S S Mallikarjun of Davangere North, K S Basavanatappa of Mayakonda, S Madhu Bangarappa of Sorab and T Raghumurthy of Challakere..Among them, first-time MLA Basanavantappa and three-time MLA Raghumurthy have become the ministers for the first time. Luck, political equations and caste considerations are said to have worked in favour of Basavanatappa, who secured a ministerial berth in his maiden Assembly victory..Meanwhile, senior MLAs D G Shantanagowda of Honnali, Belur Gopalakrishna of Sagar and B K Sangameshwar of Bhadravathi have not become ministers even once despite being elected to the Assembly multiple times. .For first time in 30 years, Karnataka Cabinet has no Brahmin representation.Sources said Belur and Sangameshwar have reportedly expressed their desire to resign as MLAs, though it remains to be seen whether they will go ahead with the decision or continue in the Assembly..Sources in Congress said Mallikarjun’s name was not included in the initial list of 20 MLAs proposed for induction during the Cabinet expansion announced by the party high command. .After learning about his exclusion, Mallikarjun reportedly conveyed to state leaders that he, his wife Prabha Mallikarjun, MP, and his son Samarth Shamanur, Davangere South MLA, would resign from their positions if he was denied a ministerial berth..Yielding to the pressure, the party reportedly dropped Mankala Vaidya and included Mallikarjun’s name in the second list. However, Mallikarjun’s supporters claimed that his omission from the first list was due to a typographical error..The dream of three-time MLA Belur Gopalakrishna to become a minister remained unfulfilled, while his fellow three-time MLA T Raghumurthy of Challakere, an engineering graduate, secured a Cabinet berth for the first time..S S Mallikarjun and Madhu Bangarappa had earlier served as ministers in the previous Siddaramaiah-led Cabinet.

NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor took a swipe at the BJP on Monday as he surged towards a landmark victory in the Bankipur assembly bypoll, saying he had brought down the party's "30-year stronghold in just 30 days.""This is not an election to make an MLA, this is to give the message to the top leadership of the BJP that a good person should be made CM in Bihar, so that there is education, employment in Bihar, the people gave this message. I don't want to make grand promises... But the people of Bankipur have sent a clear message to the BJP leadership: appoint a good person as the chief minister of Bihar," he said.The result marks a major political upset in Bankipur, a BJP bastion since 1995 that was represented first by Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha and later by his son, Nitin Nabin, for five consecutive terms.The bypoll was necessitated after Nabin vacated the seat following his election to the Rajya Sabha.

headline: A seat for JSP's 'school bag': Why Prashant Kishor's Bankipur win is a warning for both BJP and RJD

full_text:
A seat for JSP's 'school bag': Why Prashant Kishor's Bankipur win is a warning for both BJP and RJD
Kunal Varma / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 04, 2026, 07:54 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
Prashant Kishor celebrates after winning the Bankipur Assembly bypoll (Image credit: PTI)
NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor has finally found a seat for his âschool bagâ in Bihar. The election strategist-turned-politician, whose party contests on a school bag symbol, has flipped the Bankipur assembly seat, an unassailable bastion of the BJP for the last 30 years. Before todayâs shock defeat, the BJP had registered 8 consecutive victories in Bankipur since 1995, when it won the seat for the first time.By-election in Bankipur was necessitated after Nitin Nabin resigned as BJP MLA from the seat in April after his election to Rajya Sabha. This followed Nitin Nabinâs elevation as BJP national president in January this year.To gauge the enormity of Prashant Kishorâs victory, look at these facts:
BJP has held Bankipur assembly seat from 1995 (Till 2005, the seat was known as Patna West)
BJP chief Nitin Nabin won from the Bankipur assembly seat four times in a row
Nitin Nabin won from Bankipur for first time in 2010 with a margin of 56%
From 1995 to 2010, the seat (known as Patna West) was represented by Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha (Nitin Nabinâs father)
Father-son duo has won the seat 8 consecutive times
For PK, as Prashant Kishor is popularly known, contesting the Bankipur byelection was a huge political gamble. PK, who made a high-pitched entry into Bihar politics with a padyatra spanning months ahead of the 2025 assembly elections, cut a sorry figure when his Jan Suraj Party failed to win even one seat less than a year ago. Such dismal was his first electoral show that JSP lost deposit in 236 of the 238 seats it contested. Prashant Kishor did not contest the election himself and instead led a high-voltage campaign for his party across the state.
Little wonder his decision to contest the Bankipur bypoll was fraught with the danger of becoming a make-or-break political move. But the gamble has paid off and Prashant Kishor with his debut win has propelled into the centrestage of Bihar politics.
âBankipurâs message to BJP central leadershipâ
Prashant Kishor polled over 64,151 votes and won the key electoral battle by a margin of 19,324 votes over BJPâs Neeraj Kumar. Prashant Kishorâs resounding success, nine months after his partyâs humiliating defeat, marks a remarkable turnaround.And making the most of his victory, Prashant Kishor immediately trained his guns at Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary."This is the victory of the people of Bankipur. As we stated during the election campaign, this was not just an election to choose an MLA. It was an attempt by the people of Bihar to send a message to the BJP's central leadership that they should appoint a good person as the chief minister of Bihar. They do not want a person with a criminal background or questionable conduct, character, or reputation to lead Bihar. They want a good chief minister who can improve education, create employment opportunities for the youth, and ensure that the children of Bihar do not have to migrate elsewhere for work," Kishor told reporters as his supporters celebrated his maiden electoral victory.
Prashant Kishor hits out at Bihar CM
Prashant Kishorâs use of his victory to target Samrat Choudhary did not come as a surprise. Ksihor been unrelenting in his attacks against the BJP leader ever since the election strategist became a full-time politician. He has targeted Samrat Choudhary over the chief ministerâs educational qualification and his alleged criminal past.
Kishor's development pitch or disappointment against BJP?
The Jan Suraaj chief also called upon the BJP's central leadership to focus on governance ahead of the next Lok Sabha elections, stating, "Before the Lok Sabha elections, Prime Minister Modi, the BJP, and Amit Shah should focus on improving Bihar, creating jobs for its youth, and stopping migration. That is our only objective. We do not want to become MLAs merely to award contracts. Our sole objective is the development of Bihar."These are the very themes on which Prashant Kishor fought the 2025 assembly elections and lost. Clearly, while he keeps focus on these issues, his victory in bankipur may less be about endorsement of his development focus and more about peopleâs disappointment with the BJP. The result is also perhaps a fallout of the studentsâ agitation against NEET-UG paper leak, which saw huge protests in Bihar. In Siwan, a police constable was suspended after a video purportedly showing him using an AK-47 rifle during a student protest on July 25 went viral on social media.Leader of opposition in Bihar assembly, Tejashwi Yadav, slammed Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary for the incident. He posted a video of the purported incident on X and, along with it, said, "During the protest in Siwan, police resorted to direct firing with an AK-47 on students. When a criminal becomes chief minister, then police fire bullets at innocent students.â
âVerdict by Bihar's youth against BJPâ
CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya in his message to Prashant Kishor described his victory as a significant verdict by Bihar's youth against the BJP-led state government.In a post on X, Bhattacharya termed Kishor's victory a "well-earned debut victory" and said the bypoll result reflected public anger against the ruling dispensation."Congratulations to Prashant Kishor on his well-earned debut victory in Bankipur bypoll. Kudos to the youth of Bihar for delivering such a telling blow to the supremely arrogant, incompetent and tyrannical BJP government of Bihar," he said.
Shock verdict for BJP
The BJP was quick to accept the verdict of the people. State BJP president Sanjay Saraogi said in a statement, "We bow before the will of the people. We shall draw lessons from the debacle, unlike our opponents who tend to blame every electoral loss of theirs on EVMs and the Election Commission".But for the BJP, this defeat comes as an embarrassment for both its national president Nitin Nabin and the partyâs first chief minister in the state Samrat Choudhary. Bankipur seat was literally a personal fiefdom of Nitin Nabinâs family which represented the constituency for 30 long years. A defeat in the backyard will surely embarrass the BJP chief.For Samrat Choudhary, this was the first electoral test of his government which was formed after the BJP took over the reins of the state from JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar. It was Nitish Kumar who had led the NDA to an emphatic triumph in the 2025 assembly elections. And the BJP would have hoped that Samrat Choudhary would have given it a winning start. But that was not to be.
Lalu's RJD pushed to fringes
The Bankipur bypoll result also has a worrying message for the main opposition party RJD. Tejashwi Yadavâs party seems to have learnt no lessons from the 2025 electoral drubbing. The party which has been reduced to 25 seats in the assembly did little to show intent on the ground.
Its candidate Rekha Kumari polled just 14,273 votes. This was over 32,000 votes less than the figure of 46,363, which she had polled in the 2025 assembly elections as the runnerup in the seat. Ironically, for the greater part of the campaign, RJDâs star campaigner Tejashwi Yadav was missing in action.
Time to pause, review
It may not be prudent to overexaggerate the outcome of one bypoll. The result of one seat, even though high-profile, may not be indicative of any larger trend. But for the BJP and the RJD to brush aside the defeat as a one-off setback would be doing harm to their cause. The BJP should remember that it rules Bihar but is still dependent on its allies for survival. The RJD, meanwhile, remains the main opposition party but seems to have lost the plot to factionalism and family feuds after its dismal 2025 show. Both need to pause and review what went wrong in Bankipur. MLA Prashant Kishor, on the other hand, will perhaps be now preparing for another bout with his political bete noir Samrat Choudhary - this time on the floor of Bihar assembly.

full_text:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat to interact with 2,000 teenagers in Mumbai on August 6 amid growing youth assertiveness
NEW DELHI: Days after saying that the era of unquestioned obedience was over and young people now sought reasons and logic, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat will interact with nearly 2,000 teenagers in Mumbai on August 6, bringing him face to face with the generation he has urged elders to engage through dialogue rather than commands.The students, aged between 15 and 19, will come from schools and colleges across more than 100 cities. The interaction will be held at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre as part of the 15th anniversary programme of Indiaâs International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN), a youth-led organisation.
The event comes against the backdrop of growing youth assertion in the country, with students increasingly using social media and street protests to demand answers from governments and institutions. The recent agitation over irregularities in NEET-UG and other examinations has also brought questions of transparency, accountability and the role of young people in public debate to the centre stage.Bhagwat did not refer to any particular agitation while speaking recently about changing relations between generations. He had said that, unlike in the past, children today expect reasons, examples and explanations and must be engaged through regular conversation.
The Mumbai interaction will, therefore, be watched for the issues raised by students and whether the session allows them to directly question the RSS chief on education, leadership, nation-building and social change.IIMUN founder Rishabh Shah said the gathering was aimed at creating a dialogue between senior leaders and young people.
âLeadership is not only about guiding the next generation, but also listening to it. At this critical juncture in Indiaâs journey, we need this dialogue more than ever before,â Shah said.Bhagwatâs address will mark the opening of the organisationâs annual championship conference, where students will debate national and international issues. This yearâs theme is âThe Role of Youth in Uniting the World, the Indian Wayâ.
Manash Pratim Gohain is a seasoned journalist with over two decades at The Times of India, where he has built a rich body of work spanning education policy, politics, and governance. Renowned for his incisive coverage of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, accreditation reforms, and skilling initiatives, he has also reported on student politics, urban policy, and social movements. Bankipur bypoll outcome highlights shifting political dynamics in Bihar. (Prashant Kishor - PTI image)
NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor on Monday won the Bankipur assembly bypoll, defeating BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar by 19,324 votes after securing 64,151 votes, marking a winning start to his electoral career.The bypoll, necessitated after BJP national president Nitin Nabin vacated the seat following his election to the Rajya Sabha, turned into much more than a contest for a single constituency. Bankipur had remained one of the BJP's safest urban seats for over three decades, with Nabin winning it four consecutive times by comfortable margins.Kishor's victory in the BJP's long-held bastion is likely to be seen as one of the biggest political upsets in Bihar after the assembly elections defeat. BJP's Neeraj Kumar secured 44,827 votes, while RJD candidate Rekha Kumari finished a distant third with 14,273 votes.
Here are the five biggest takeaways from the Bankipur bypoll:
1. Biggest political breakthrough for Prashant KishorBankipur marks Prashant Kishor's biggest electoral breakthrough since entering active politics and launching the Jan Suraaj Party. The victory is particularly significant because it came in a constituency long regarded as a BJP bastion.
The win marks a dramatic turnaround for Kishor. In the 2025 Bihar assembly elections, Jan Suraaj contested 238 seats but failed to win a single one, securing just a 3.44% vote share. In 68 constituencies, the party polled fewer votes than the NOTA option. The Bankipur victory signals improvement in the party's electoral fortunes and strengthens Kishor's claim of emerging as a credible political alternative in Bihar ahead of the next assembly election.2. BJP suffers a symbolic defeat in one of its safest seatsFor the BJP, the result is significant because Bankipur has long been among its strongest urban constituencies. Nitin Nabin won the seat in 2010, 2015, 2020 and 2025, each time by comfortable margins.In the 2025 assembly election, Nabin secured 98,299 votes, a 63.25% vote share, defeating the RJD candidate by 51,936 votes. Losing such a seat raises questions about the BJP's ability to retain its traditional urban support base and could prompt a reassessment of its campaign strategy in the next assembly elections.3. A bigger setback for BJP chief Nitin NabinThe result carries personal significance for BJP national president Nitin Nabin, who vacated the Bankipur seat after being elected to the Rajya Sabha. The constituency has been synonymous with his political career, with Nabin representing it continuously since 2015 and turning it into one of the BJP's strongest urban bastions in Bihar.Less than a year after Nabin registered a landslide victory in Bankipur, the BJP has lost the seat under his tenure as national president. The defeat is likely to raise questions about the party's organisational strength in his home turf and provide the opposition with an opportunity to challenge the BJP leadership's grip over one of its safest constituencies.4. Tejashwi Yadav and the RJD missing from the contestThe Bankipur bypoll has also exposed the RJD's inability to emerge as the principal challenger in a high-profile contest. Despite fielding Rekha Kumari, the party finished a distant third, with the election effectively turning into a direct fight between the BJP and Prashant Kishor. The result is likely to raise uncomfortable questions for Tejashwi Yadav, who has projected himself as the NDA's chief challenger in Bihar. His absence from the campaign also became a political issue, with NDA leaders, including Union minister Chirag Paswan, accusing him of remaining abroad during the bypoll. The outcome is likely to fuel speculation that sections of the anti-BJP electorate are looking beyond the RJD, with Prashant Kishor emerging as a potential alternative opposition face.
5. Does Bankipur open the door for a third front in Bihar?The biggest political implication may lie beyond the bypoll itself. Jan Suraaj's victory in Bankipur strengthens the argument that Bihar's politics may no longer remain confined to the NDA versus the RJD-led Mahagathbandhan contest.While one bypoll alone cannot establish a statewide trend, defeating the BJP in one of its strongest constituencies significantly boosts Jan Suraaj's credibility. The result could encourage voters seeking an alternative to the two established alliances and make Prashant Kishor's party a more consequential player in the upcoming Bihar assembly elections.

NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Monday said the party would undertake a "thorough introspection" after losing the Bankipur Assembly bypoll in Bihar, where Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar to end the party's three-decade dominance in the constituency.Kishor won the bypoll by 19,324 votes, polling 64,151 votes against Neeraj Kumar's 44,827 votes. The victory marked Kishor's first electoral win since launching the Jan Suraaj Party and came less than a year after the party failed to win a single seat in the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections.Reacting to the bypoll results, Nabin accepted the verdict and said the BJP would analyse the reasons behind its defeats.In a post on X, Nabin said, "We accept the mandate received in today's three assembly by-elections.We express our heartfelt gratitude to the people of Manjalpur assembly constituency in Gujarat for expressing their faith in the Bharatiya Janata Party. We extend our warm congratulations to all the dedicated workers and office-bearers of the BJP for this victory.In Bapni Pur and Datia, we did not receive the expected mandate. We will conduct a thorough introspection of the election results in both these areas with complete seriousness, and with renewed energy and determination, we will continue to go among the people and work tirelessly to further strengthen their trust."
Bankipur had been one of the BJP's strongest urban bastions since 1995. The seat was represented first by BJP leader Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha and later by his son, Nitin Nabin, who held it for five consecutive terms before vacating it after his election to the Rajya Sabha, triggering the bypoll.In the 2025 Bihar Assembly election, Nabin had retained the seat by a margin of more than 50,000 votes, making Kishor's victory one of the biggest political upsets in the state ahead of the Assembly elections.The bypoll also marked Prashant Kishor's electoral debut. After years as a political strategist, he launched the Jan Suraaj Party with a campaign centred on education, employment and governance reforms. His victory gives the fledgling party its first electoral success.
Earlier in the day, Kishor said the result carried a message beyond Bankipur."It was an attempt by the people of Bihar to send a message to the BJP's central leadership that they should appoint a good person as the Chief Minister of Bihar," he told reporters.Following the result, the Jan Suraaj Party posted on X, "In democracy, the fortress belongs only to the people. Thank you, Bankipur--this is your victory."Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary also congratulated Kishor on his victory."In the grand festival of democracy, the people have chosen Jan Suraaj in the Bankipur Assembly by-election. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to Shri Prashant Kishor ji on his victory, while respecting the people's decision," he said in a post on X.According to the Election Commission, the Bankipur bypoll recorded a voter turnout of 34.24 per cent.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday asked the Enforcement Directorate (ED) whether a portion of the funds from the frozen bank accounts of the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the Trinamool Congress (TMC) could be released to meet the partyâs day-to-day expenses through a Calcutta high court-appointed special officer.Additional Solicitor General (ASG) SV Raju, appearing for the central probe agency, told a bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale that he would seek instructions on the matter.
The bench subsequently posted the matter for hearing on August 11.During the hearing, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for the Banerjee-led faction, which is the petitioner in the case, argued that the party was unable to even pay salaries to its employees due to the freezing of its accounts.The top court is hearing a plea filed by the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool faction challenging the July 20 order of the Calcutta high court.The high court had refused to grant interim relief to the group to operate three TMC bank accounts that had been frozen by the ED.Referring to the high courtâs order, Sibal said, âWhat does the impugned order say? It says there are 36 separate accounts which are not seized. That is factually incorrect.â
Raju opposed the submissions and informed the bench that an investigation was underway. The ASG also alleged that money laundering had taken place through those accounts.The anti-money laundering law âis not only for actual money laundering but also for prevention of money laundering. We are preventing it,â the ASG added.When Raju claimed there was a âcontinuous offenceâ, Sibal countered the submission and questioned how such an argument could be made when the bank accounts had already been frozen.The bench was informed that the high court had appointed a former Calcutta high court judge as a special officer to oversee the operation of the three bank accounts for meeting the day-to-day expenses of running the political party.It was during this discussion that the Supreme Court suggested whether some amount could be released in favour of the special officer to meet the partyâs daily expenses.The ED froze the three bank accounts, with a combined balance of Rs 440.42 crore, as part of its money laundering probe stemming from an FIR registered by the West Bengal Police over alleged dishonest financial transactions, unlawful collection of funds and routing of suspected money through certain party accounts.In its order, the high court had noted that apart from the three accounts placed under a âdebit-freezeâ by the ED, there were 36 other accounts in the partyâs name, with around Rs 164 crore lying in them.Subsequently, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the TMC approached the high court challenging the initiation of ECIR (Enforcement Case Information Report) proceedings by the ED, which is equivalent to an FIR.

NEW DELHI: The population enumeration phase of Census 2027 â which will capture caste for the first time since 1931, and most likely also record the date and birthplace of parents, along with the respondentâs passport number (where available) and Aadhaar number (voluntary) â will start in Ladakh and the snow-bound areas, J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand on August 17.A home ministry notification on Monday said the population enumeration exercise in snow-bound areas of the four northern states/UTs will run from Sept 1 to 30, preceded by a self-enumeration window of August 17-30. This means that the questionnaire for Phase 2 of Census will also be notified soon.According to sources, caste will be recorded âas declared by the respondentâ. There will be a drop-down menu for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, while the âcasteâ field will only cater to those in non-SC, non-ST category. The drop-down menu will only show the SC/ST list of the state where the respondent is being enumeratedThe spelling of the declared âcasteâ will be recorded as cited by the respondent. No document or caste certificate is required to be shown to verify oneâs SC, ST or âcasteâ status. An officer said while the self-declaration template followed for the socio-economic caste census (SECC) in 2011 had thrown up over 45,000 castes, making the data unusable, modern digital tools and AI can now surmount compilation and segregation challenges.Census Phase 2, in a first, , will collect the date and place of birth of parents, the key factors that determine citizenship/nationality.
The national population register (NPR) exercise â conducted alongside Census 2011, intended to be repeated with Census 2021 before it was postponed, but now delinked from Census 2027 â had in 2010 collected details of nationality as declared by the respondent, with the rider that it would not confer any right of citizenship.Sources said the respondents will not be asked for proof of birth details of parents and these would be recorded âto the best knowledge of the respondentâ. In fact, where the respondents do not know the exact date of birth of parents but only the year, a default date like January 1 of that year will be accepted.The Phase 2 questionnaire will also log passport details where available. Aadhaar number will be collected on a voluntary basis.âThe purpose of collecting the birth data of parents is to know the total number of people who meet citizenship criteria based on their declaration, even though unverified. It will have no impact on the individual as the Census Act does not allow individual data to be used for âlegal evidence, govt benefits or public disclosure,â said an officer.Self-enumeration option for Phase 2, unlike Phase 1, may allow users to submit partially-filed enumeration forms, provided a minimum number of questions are answered. âThere is a realisation that even if some data fields are self-enumerated, the task of the enumerator becomes easier and less time-consuming,â said an officer.
As per convention, the population enumeration exercise â which records individual data like marital status, religion, SC/ST status, occupation, migration and fertility, besides arriving at the countryâs headcount â is conducted nationwide in February of the census reference year. However, it is advanced in pockets that face extreme cold and inclement weather during this window.
