FSSAI has prohibited adding rum or whisky flavour to spirits.
NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has said alcoholic beverage manufacturers cannot add "rum flavour" to rum or "whisky flavour" to whisky and market them as standard products, saying the practice misrepresents the true nature of the beverage and misleads consumers.The regulator said the issue is not the use of permitted flavouring substances, but addition of the flavour of the standardised alcoholic beverage itself, which serves no legitimate purpose. It said the characteristic taste and aroma of products such as rum and whisky should develop naturally through the base ingredients, fermentation, distillation and maturation. However, inspections found that some manufacturers were producing beverages largely from neutral alcohol, which has no characteristic flavour, and then adding identical flavouring substances to recreate the taste and aroma of rum or whisky. Such products, FSSAI said, should be labelled as "rum-flavoured spirit" or "whisky-flavoured spirit", with the front of the pack clearly disclosing their true nature. Laboratory testing of rum and whisky samples from multiple manufacturers found the addition of artificial or nature-identical flavours that masked the products' natural characteristics, rendering them sub-standard under existing regulations, FSSAI said.
Based on findings, it prohibited the sale of products manufactured by units of Mohan Rocky Springwater, United Spirits, INBREW Beverages and Associated Alcohol & Breweries. It also inspected Mandexi Distilleries & Breweries in Goa and issued notices to six producers in Maharashtra.FSSAI also objected to the "7 years old blended" claim on an Old Monk XXX Rum variant, saying the product predominantly contained neutral, unmatured spirit, while matured rum spirit accounted for less than 5% of the blend. It said the issue is not representative of the entire industry, noting that many manufacturers continue to produce beverages in compliance with the prescribed standards.

From 2025 washout to historic sweep: How Prashant Kishor put Jan Suraaj on Bihar's electoral map

Jan Suraj party workers celebrated the victory of Prashant Kishor in Bankipur assembly byelection results (Image/PTI)
NEW DELHI: Nearly nine months after Jan Suraaj failed to open its account in the 2025 Bihar assembly elections, party founder Prashant Kishor on Monday secured his first electoral victory. He won the high-profile Bankipur bypoll, giving the fledgling outfit its first-ever seat in the Bihar assembly.Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by 19,324 votes, polling 64,151 votes against Sinha's 44,827, according to the Election Commission.The victory marks Kishor's first electoral success since entering active politics and gives Jan Suraaj its first-ever representation in the Bihar Assembly, offering fresh momentum to a political project that had suffered a crushing setback during its electoral debut last year.
From assembly setback to bypoll comeback
The Bankipur result represents a significant political recovery for Kishor, whose Jan Suraaj Party failed to win even a single seat in the 2025 Bihar assembly elections despite contesting more than 200 constituencies.Launched after nearly two years of statewide outreach through the Jan Suraaj padyatra, the party had positioned itself as an alternative to both the NDA and the Mahagathbandhan, focusing on governance reforms, education, employment, migration and corruption rather than traditional caste-based politics.
However, the ambitious campaign failed to translate into electoral support.Following the defeat, Kishor publicly accepted full responsibility for the party's performance."We made an honest effort, but it was completely unsuccessful. There's no harm in admitting this. Forget about systemic change; we couldn't even bring about a change in power," he had said after the Assembly election results."There must have been some mistake in our efforts, in our thinking, in the way we explained things. If the public did not show faith in us, then the responsibility for that is completely mine. I take that responsibility 100 per cent on myself."As an act of atonement, Kishor also announced that he would observe a day-long silent fast, saying he had failed to convince the people of Bihar why they should support a new political alternative.At the same time, he ruled out stepping away from politics."I will work twice as hard as you've seen me work over the past three years. There's no question of backing down. There's no turning back until I fulfil my resolve to make Bihar better," he had said.
Why Bankipur mattered
The Bankipur bypoll attracted national attention because of the political stakes involved for both the BJP and Kishor.The election was necessitated after BJP state president Nitin Nabin vacated the seat following his election to the Rajya Sabha.For nearly three decades, Bankipur had remained one of the BJP's safest urban constituencies. Before Nitin Nabin represented the seat, it had been held by his father, Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha, making it one of the party's strongest bastions in Bihar.In the 2025 assembly elections, Nabin had retained the constituency comfortably by a margin of over 50,000 votes.For Kishor, however, the bypoll was much more than a contest for a single assembly seat.After Jan Suraaj's disappointing electoral debut, the election became a crucial test of whether the party could convert years of grassroots mobilisation into actual electoral success.The contest also marked Kishor's first direct electoral battle after years of shaping campaigns for other political leaders from behind the scenes.
From strategist to politician
Long before entering electoral politics himself, Prashant Kishor had built a reputation as one of India's most influential political strategists.Through his organisation Indian Political Action Committee (I-PAC), he worked on election campaigns for leaders across the political spectrum, including Narendra Modi, Nitish Kumar, Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal, MK Stalin, Jagan Mohan Reddy, Uddhav Thackeray and others.His success as an election strategist later brought him closer to Nitish Kumar, who appointed him as an adviser with cabinet rank after returning as Bihar chief minister in 2015.In 2018, Kishor formally joined the Janata Dal (United) and quickly rose to become the party's national vice-president.However, differences with Nitish Kumar over issues including the Citizenship (Amendment) Act eventually led to his expulsion from the JD(U) in 2020.After briefly attempting to revive the Congress through organisational reforms, Kishor shifted his focus entirely to Bihar.In October 2022, he launched the Jan Suraaj padyatra, travelling across the state to build what he described as a grassroots political movement that would eventually evolve into a full-fledged political party.Although the movement generated considerable public attention, it failed to produce electoral success in the 2025 assembly elections.The Bankipur bypoll now marks Kishor's first major political endorsement as a politician rather than as a strategist.
Breaking a BJP fortress
The BJP mounted an extensive campaign to retain Bankipur, deploying senior leaders, ministers and organisational workers to preserve its long-standing hold over the constituency.Despite the party's efforts, Kishor succeeded in wresting away one of the BJP's safest seats.The result is significant not because it alters the numerical balance of power in the Assembly, but because it breaks the perception that Jan Suraaj remains merely a political movement without electoral backing.It also establishes Kishor as an elected legislator for the first time.Beyond the numerical gain of a single seat, the victory gives Jan Suraaj institutional legitimacy.The party will now have a formal voice inside the Bihar assembly and is expected to use the legislative platform to strengthen its organisational presence ahead of future elections.Political observers believe the result could encourage more leaders and workers to join the party while helping it build credibility among voters who were hesitant to back it after the 2025 assembly elections.Although one bypoll does not erase the disappointment of last year's electoral performance, it significantly changes the political narrative around Jan Suraajâfrom that of an unsuccessful newcomer to a party capable of winning in one of Bihar's most politically significant constituencies.
Message to BJP leadership
Even before the counting concluded, Kishor had described the bypoll as something larger than a contest for one assembly seat."It was an attempt by the people of Bihar to send a message to the BJP's central leadership that they should appoint a good person as the Chief Minister of Bihar," he told reporters.Jan Suraaj also celebrated the result on social media, writing on X: "In democracy, the fortress belongs only to the people. Thank you, Bankipurâthis is your victory."
The Bankipur bypoll does not change Bihar's political arithmetic overnight. The NDA continues to enjoy a comfortable majority in the assembly with 122 seats.However, politically, the result marks an important milestone.After years of being known as the strategist behind other leaders' victories and after suffering a disappointing electoral debut in 2025, Prashant Kishor has finally secured an electoral mandate of his own."I am also congratulating those who lost the election. This is a democracy; there are wins and losses in elections. But the Bankipur election was not an election to elect an MLA. This election was to decide on the BJP-NDA government and its leadership. The people of Bankipur have voted that the central leadership of the BJP should consider it and, in the interest of Bihar, hand over the power of Bihar to a good person," he declared after victory.

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has suspended the licence of a packaged drinking water manufacturer in Tripura and prohibited the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of a dietary food supplement made by a Punjab-based company after inspections found serious food safety and regulatory violations.The licence of M/S Matri Drinking Water, Gomati, Tripura, was suspended with immediate effect following a complaint about foreign material in packaged drinking water. Inspectors found finished products stored outside the facility and on the floor alongside non-food materials, unhygienic processing and filling areas, rusted RO water storage tanks and chemical dosing containers, inadequate pest control and sanitation, and the absence of mandatory testing, maintenance and training records. A qualified technical supervisor was also not available during the inspection.In a separate action, FSSAI prohibited the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of Venolex Forte, marketed by M/S Noble Healthcare, Mohali, saying the dietary food supplement contained ingredients not permitted under the Food Safety and Standards (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use, Food for Special Medical Purpose, Functional Food and Novel Food) Regulations, 2022.
The regulator said the product contained pharmacologically active ingredients, including calcium dobesilate, diosmin and Euphorbia prostrata, which are not permitted in food supplements. It also found that the product contained 90 mg of vitamin C, which appeared to exceed the Recommended Dietary Allowance prescribed under the ICMR-NIN Guidelines, 2020.FSSAI also said the product's labelling was misleading, creating the impression of specific regulatory approval, and that it was manufactured and marketed beyond the scope of the firm's FSSAI licence. The prohibition order has been issued under Section 36(3)(b) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

full_text:
All new cars, passenger and goods vehicles would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication system. (PTI)
NEW DELHI: From Oct 2028, all new two- and three-wheelers, cars, passenger and goods vehicles (including buses and trucks) would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication system, as per a draft notification of the road transport ministry. The V2V technology is being rolled out to curb collisions and accidents.The recently published draft notification by road transport ministry proposes phased implementation of the V2V communication system and to start with all vehicles in categories L (two- and three-wheelers), M (passenger vehicles) and N (goods vehicles) manufactured from Oct 2027 would be required to comply with the newly-notified automotive standard, AIS-230, wherever they are equipped with V2V communication systems.The technology enables real-time exchange of speed, direction, position, and braking data between vehicles to prevent collisions at blind curves, intersections, or from drivers coming the wrong way without needing a cellular network. Each vehicle needs to be fitted with a device that will automatically detect approaching vehicles for preventing any crash.Unlike conventional vehicle-safety systems, which primarily depend on onboard sensors and driver reaction, V2V communication can provide information beyond the direct line of sight.
âIt is therefore expected to complement Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and support proactive accident prevention, connected mobility and future intelligent transport applications,â the ministry said.In this case, every vehicle fitted with the V2V communication system will continuously send out their locations, speed and direction as tiny radio signals. They will also relay information on sudden braking by a vehicle ahead, forward collision risks, unsafe lane changes, wrong-way driving and the approach of emergency vehicles.
The receiving vehicleâs system compares this information with its own location, speed and direction to predict a possible collision and alerts the driver for action.At a later stage, govt will also roll out the Vehicle to Infrastructure (V2I) communication system. In this case, sensors are installed with infrastructure, such as signal and power poles, edges of bridges and flyovers, and barricaded areas to alert vehicles.

Prashant Kishor broke the BJP's three-decade hold on Bankipur and reshaped Bihar's political landscape.
The first electoral verdict after the nationwide Gen Z protests has delivered one of the biggest political surprises in recent years. BJP has lost Bankipur, one of its safest seats in Bihar, to Prashant Kishor, giving Jan Suraaj its first-ever electoral victory.The result carries significance beyond a single assembly bypoll. It is also the first major electoral test for BJP in Bihar under the leadership of CM Samrat Choudhary after he assumed charge of the state government. The outcome suggests that the party failed to retain its grip over a constituency that had remained virtually impregnable for three decades.
The fall of a BJP fortress
Bankipur has been synonymous with BJP's dominance since 1995. The party won the seat four consecutive times through Navin Sinha before his son, BJP national president Nitin Nabin, retained it for five successive elections.The constituency had long been regarded as one of BJP's safest urban seats. Nitin Nabin secured more than 50% of the vote in every election he contested, including around 63% in the 2025 Assembly election. Against that backdrop, the bypoll result represents a dramatic political reversal.
From electoral debut disaster to historic victory
The bypoll attracted unusual national attention largely because Prashant Kishor decided to contest personally.Only nine months ago, Jan Suraaj had suffered a crushing setback in the Bihar Assembly elections. The party fielded candidates in 238 of the state's 243 constituencies but failed to win a single seat, while forfeiting deposits in 236 constituencies. Despite an extensive campaign built around Prashant Kishor's personal credibility, the party could not convert public attention into votes.The obvious question, therefore, is: what changed in just nine months?
A changing political mood
Political observers believe the 2025 Assembly election was heavily influenced by welfare promises, including direct financial assistance for women and free electricity, helping the NDA secure a decisive victory. Since then, Bihar's political environment appears to have shifted considerably.The transition from Nitish Kumar to Samrat Choudhary as Chief Minister coincided with a series of developments that reportedly generated dissatisfaction among sections of BJP's traditional support base. Controversies surrounding the UGC guidelines, the Bharat Tiwari encounter, and widespread anger over repeated paper leak incidents created fresh political fault lines, particularly among students and young voters.
Why youth turned towards Prashant Kishor
Education has remained at the centre of Prashant Kishor's political messaging. His repeated emphasis on education reforms appears to have resonated with young voters seeking systemic change.He has consistently questioned the academic credentials of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary while projecting education reform as one of Bihar's most urgent priorities. His image as an educated professional has helped him emerge as a credible alternative, especially among urban youth.Following the nationwide Gen Z protests, Bihar witnessed some of the strongest student mobilisations over paper leak controversies. While the state has made visible improvements in roads and infrastructure over the past decade, concerns over the quality of education and the continued migration of young people remain widespread.For many first-time and young voters, Prashant Kishor increasingly appeared to represent change.
Tejashwi Yadav's absence created political space
Equally significant was the growing disappointment among sections of the opposition's traditional support base.Many voters expected Leader of the Opposition Tejashwi Yadav to aggressively raise issues affecting students and other public concerns. According to political observers in Patna, his perceived lack of visibility during debates over the Bharat Tiwari encounter and student protests created a vacuum in opposition politics.Many voters reportedly believed that while one bypoll would not alter the government's stability, electing Prashant Kishor would strengthen the opposition's voice inside the Assembly.
Core voters turned away from the BJP, RJD
The final extent of vote transfer will become clearer only after the Election Commission releases detailed voting data. However, reporters on the ground believe Prashant Kishor attracted support from both BJP's and RJD's traditional voter bases.RJD candidate Rekha Kumari appears to have suffered the sharpest decline. After securing 46,363 votes in the 2025 Assembly election, she is now estimated to have polled fewer than 15,000 votes.There are also indications that sections of BJP's upper-caste support base were unhappy over issues such as paper leaks, the UGC guidelines and the Bharat Tiwari encounter.
BJP's candidate switch added to the narrative
The BJP's last-minute change of candidate also became a major talking point during the campaign. The party's nominee, Abhishek Kumar Sinha, withdrew his nomination on July 10 citing personal reasons. The withdrawal came just hours after Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary had campaigned for him in Bankipur.
BJP subsequently fielded Neeraj Kumar Sinha, who was widely perceived as a weaker candidate. Prashant Kishor seized on the development, arguing that the BJP was struggling to find a suitable candidate because voters now had a credible alternative.

NEW DELHI: India performed a record 20,138 organ transplants in 2025, crossing the 20,000-mark for the first time and registered a 6.5% increase over the previous year, according to National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisationâs (NOTTO) annual report. The figure marks a fourfold rise from 4,990 transplants in 2013.Delhi-NCR recorded the highest number of transplants in 2025 with 4,564 procedures, followed by Tamil Nadu (2,796), Maharashtra (2,136), Telangana (1,523) and Kerala (1,489). Tamil Nadu topped the country in deceased organ donors with 266, followed by Maharashtra (205), Telangana (198), Karnataka (154) and Kerala (152).India has emerged as the worldâs third-largest country in total organ transplants, after the US and China. Deceased donor transplants still far short of demandIndia continues to rank first globally in living donor organ transplants, according to Global Observatory on Donation and Transplantation report released in 2026.The 20,000-mark milestone coincided with the 16th Indian Organ Donation Day, when health ministry announced that more than five lakh Aadhaar-verified organ donation pledges have been recorded since the national digital pledge portal was launched in 2023.
Despite the gains, deceased organ donation remains Indiaâs biggest challenge. Deceased donor transplants rose from 837 in 2013 to 3,526 in 2025, but continue to fall far short of demand. âA substantial gap still exists between demand for organs and their availability. Addressing this gap remains a national priority,â MoS for health Anupriya Patel said.
To strengthen the programme, govt launched âJug Jug Jiyo Abhiyaanâ, a year-long awareness campaign, besides rolling out e-Pratyaropan, a digital platform for donor registration, waitlist management and organ allocation, NOTTO mobile app, and new Brain Stem Death Certification and Swap Transplantation guidelines.Govt has also expanded transplant services, with 10 new AIIMS now performing kidney transplants, while AIIMS Bhopal has started heart transplantation and AIIMS Jodhpur, Bhubaneswar, Patna, Rishikesh have launched liver transplant programmes.The report highlights reforms under âOne Nation, One Policyâ initiative, including removal of domicile requirements, the upper age limit and registration fees for patients seeking deceased donor organs. With nearly 1.73 lakh road traffic fatalities every year, the report says India has significant potential to increase deceased organ donation.

NEW DELHI: Indiaâs one more wetland, Glaw Lake of Arunachal Pradesh, has entered the global list of protected wetlands as a Ramsar site. It is the countryâs 101st such site and the stateâs first to join the elite club for additional care and conservation.Located within the Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary, Glaw Lake is a pristine freshwater lake in the Eastern Himalayas and a biodiversity hotspot. The lake is fed by perennial mountain streams and is surrounded by lush vegetation, supporting rich floral diversity.âEvery new Ramsar site strengthens our resolve to protect nature while securing the future of communities that depend on these invaluable ecosystems,â said Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav while announcing the development on X on Monday.The Glaw Lake wetland has over 150 tree species and 49 orchid species recorded within the site and its catchment, underscoring its ecological significance and surrounding landscape.âFrom 26 Ramsar sites in 2014 to 101 today, this remarkable journey reflects our unwavering commitment to environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable development,â said Yadav.
Globally, there are nearly 2,600 such designated wetlands under the Ramsar Convention.
India has the highest number of such wetlands in Asia and third highest in the world after the UK (176) and Mexico (144).Wetlands are land areas covered by water, either temporarily/ seasonally or permanently. These are critical ecosystems that play a significant role in supporting biodiversity, and providing various ecosystem services such as flood control, water supply, food, fibre and raw materials.

full_text:
NEW DELHI: The Asia pacific Group on money laundering in its latest report on cybercrime hubs in Myanmar, Lao PDR and Cambodia has revealed that Indian nationals are among victims of several countries trafficked to these cyber hubs and kept as slaves, trained to operate various scams like investment, romance, impersonation, social media and gaming.These cybercrime hubs are controlled by Chinese nationals who also tortured these âslavesâ through coercion methods, including electric shock, dark room and isolation room confinement, physical abuse, fines and mental torture.Cyber scam hubs are mainly located in the Golden Triangle region along border areas between Thailand, Myanmar, Lao PDR and Cambodia, besides the northern border of Myanmar with China and the Philippines. Some of them operated from special economic zones. An inter-governmental body like the Financial Action Task Force, the Sydney-based APG initiated this study led by Indonesia and UN Office on Drugs and Crime with a team comprised of 24 experts from the govts of Australia, Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Solomon Islands, Singapore, Vietnam and UAE.The study examined the emerging nexus between human trafficking and cyber-enabled financial crime, drawing upon the debriefings of 15 Indian nationals repatriated from Myanmar, Lao PDR, and Cambodia between 2023 and 2024.
The individuals were recruited under the pretext of high-paying customer-service or IT jobs, transported through Thailand, and then coerced to work in criminal âscam compoundsâ operated by transnational syndicates, it said.âVictims were mostly young men (20-35 age group) from nine Indian states, recruited via social media or personal networks, who paid upfront fees (Rs 50-70,000). Compounds were run by Chinese-speaking syndicates, with multi-national workforces and strict control (passport confiscation, physical/psychological abuse),â the report has said.The report further revealed that these slave workers were sold between scam compounds, where they were subjected to confinement, violence and debt bondage. âInterception operations and large-scale rescues have revealed victims from a variety of nationalities and regions, suggesting that recruitment practices have expanded beyond solely regional contexts. Workers are forced to conduct investment fraud, impersonation schemes, romance scams, and illegal online gambling platforms, with performance enforced through physical abuse and threats,â it added.
Crypto-based financial systems served as core enabling mechanisms.Other examples cited by the agency related to large-scale use of mule accounts and SIM cards from India, which exploited the âvulnerable populationâ, which were unemployed youth and drug addicts. In one case, muule bank accounts and SIM cards from Punjab were supplied to cyber fraudsters in the Philippines, facilitating scams totalling over Rs 40 crore. The unemployed youth were lured with fake jobs, asked to open accounts and provide their SIMs, which were couriered to the Philippines.

SC hears plea on Jantar Mantar as the protest venue site
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to examine a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking an alternative protest venue in Delhi, with the petitioner arguing that Jantar Mantar is no longer suitable for demonstrations because they inconvenience local residents and disrupt essential services.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notices to the Centre and other authorities and asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to seek instructions on the issues raised.The PIL, filed by Satish Chand Kaushik, contends that protests at Jantar Mantar create problems for local residents by affecting access, movement and the supply of essential goods and medical services.
During the hearing, the Chief Justice said the plea raised important concerns."It has been stated in the plea that Jantar Mantar is not a proper site anymore for such protests due to ingress and egress issues. Supply of medical essentials etc. I think this is important... Please take instructions, Mr Solicitor. Issue notice and list this separately," the CJI said.The petitioner's counsel also referred to a proposed political march and urged the court to ensure that 'another July 20 incident should be avoided'.
The bench, however, declined to comment on the proposed event."They know how to handle it. If they cannot, come to us for mishandling. I am sure they will handle (it)," the CJI observed.The matter has been directed to be listed separately.The hearing comes after the Supreme Court declined an oral request by an advocate to take suo motu cognisance of the police action during the July 20 'Chalo Sansad' protest at Jantar Mantar.
At the time, the bench had said it did not want to view videos of the incident during judicial proceedings and asked the advocate not to raise issues that were not before the court.Following the protests, the Supreme Court Bar Association had passed a resolution condemning the alleged use of excessive force against students and lawyers and called for an impartial, time-bound inquiry into the incident.

Karnataka cabinet expansion: 20 ministers inducted, DKS responds to MLAs left out
NEW DELHI: Twenty new ministers were inducted into the Karnataka government on Monday as chief minister DK Shivakumar expanded his Cabinet to its full strength, two months after taking office.The swearing-in ceremony took place at Lok Bhavan in Bengaluru after Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot approved the expansion.
The Cabinet expansion increased the strength of the ministry to the sanctioned limit of 34, including the chief minister.
Among those sworn in were PM Narendraswamy, Shivaraj Tangadagi, Rudrappa Lamani, KS Basavanthappa, B Nagendra, T Raghumoorthy, BZ Zameer Ahmed Khan, Rizwan Arshad, Santosh Lad, Madhu Bangarappa, Putturangashetty, SS Mallikarjun, Dr Ajay Singh, N Chaluvaraya Swamy, KM Shivalinge Gowda, HC Balakrishna, Gayathri Shanthegowda, Basavaraj Rayareddi, Vijayanand Kashappanavar and Laxman Savadi.
The Congress high command also approved GS Patil as the new Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and AS Ponnanna as the Deputy Speaker. Saleem Ahmed was named Chairman of the Legislative Council, while Umashree was appointed Deputy Chairperson.Ahead of the ceremony, Congress MLAs Yashavantarayagouda V Patil (Indi) and Belur Gopalakrishna (Sagar) resigned from the Karnataka Legislative assembly after being left out of the Cabinet.
Patil claimed his name had been included in the list until Monday morning but was removed from the final list released by the party."I was promised a ministerial post even before the 2023 Assembly polls. Later, I was told it would happen after 2.5 years, but the promise was not kept. I have no other choice," he said.He added that he was not resigning from the Congress but felt compelled to step down as MLA, calling it an insult to the people of his constituency. His supporters also staged a protest in Bengaluru over his exclusion.Reacting to the disappointment among party legislators, Shivakumar urged them to remain patient."There are many MLAs. It is not possible to accommodate everyone. Earlier, I too missed out on a ministerial berth in Siddaramaiah's Cabinet. But didn't I become a minister later? Similarly, we will provide opportunities to everyone in the future," the chief minister said.
He also said, "I request them to be patient. We will create opportunities for everyone."The expansion saw the return of several former ministers, including B Nagendra, who had resigned from the previous Siddaramaiah government in 2024 over allegations linked to the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation scam.
Former Deputy chief minister Laxman Savadi and senior leader Zameer Ahmed Khan were also among those inducted.However, several senior Congress leaders from the previous government, including H C Mahadevappa, H K Patil, Dinesh Gundu Rao, K Venkatesh, M C Sudhakar and Laxmi Hebbalkar were not included in the new Cabinet.Gayathri Shanthegowda is the only woman inducted in the expanded ministry. Three children of former chief ministers are now part of the Cabinet: Yathindra Siddaramaiah, Madhu Bangarappa and Dr Ajay Singh.

NEW DELHI: Chief minister VD Satheesan on Monday said that the death toll in rain-related incidents across Kerala has risen to 15 as heavy rainfall continued to batter the state and rescue operations intensified.Addressing a press conference after reviewing the flood situation with senior officials, Satheesan said 316 relief camps were functioning across Kerala, sheltering 11,018 people displaced by flooding and landslides.
He said Kottayam reported three deaths, including two in the Poonjar assembly constituency and a child who drowned after falling into a water tank. Ernakulam recorded two deaths, while one person each died in Idukki and Muvattupuzha. Four people died in Malappuram, two in Kollam and one each in Kannur and Kozhikode.The chief minister said seven people were still missing. He also said people returning home from flooded relief camps would receive Rs 10,000 as immediate assistance.
The chief minister directed the Agriculture Department to submit a proposal to revise crop compensation, saying the current relief was inadequate. According to preliminary estimates, 165 hectares of agricultural land have been damaged, affecting 3,596 farmers.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued rain alerts for all 14 districts in the state. Residents in landslide-prone hilly regions have also been advised to move to safer locations if necessary.

Meta apologises before Parliament panel over removal of PM Modi's Facebook video
NEW DELHI: Parliamentary standing committee on communications and information technology chairman Nishikant Dubey on Monday said Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg should personally apologise over the temporary removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Facebook video, warning that the social media giant could lose its safe harbour protection if it failed to do so.Dubey's remarks came after Meta apologised before the parliamentary panel, saying the PM Modi's video was removed due to an error. However, members of the committee said the issue went beyond an apology and demanded accountability for the incident.Addressing reporters after chairing the committee meeting, Dubey said, "...Understand the situation that has arisen within the algorithm. What Meta India did, what X did, and what YouTube did is a matter that the country should know. If you look at the viewership algorithm of the BJP, Congress, Samajwadi Party, and Aam Aadmi Party, the viewership is only 23 million. And those who are neither registered parties nor registered NGOs, their algorithm is 27 million. All political parties together are at 23-24 million. An anti-reservation forum has just been formed five or six days ago, and it reached 7 million. The reason for that is that they have a policy of giving preference to newcomers."
On the removal of the Prime Minister's video, he said, "The second question is that Meta India removed the Prime Minister's content. This is not the first time Meta India has done this. If you recall, Zuckerberg himself made a statement in January regarding the 2024 elections and later apologized. This shows that his intention is to destabilise the country. When a video of the Prime Minister of India can be removed, and they themselves admitted that the content was missing for five hours, from 12:30 am to 5:00 am, this is a very serious matter. Our committee has said two things and has clearly stated that the apology should come from Zuckerberg. If Zuckerberg does not give it, then the safe harbour protection under Section 79 should be withdrawn from him."Dubey also raised concerns over the handling of child sexual abuse material and other objectionable content on social media platforms.He said, "CSAM (Child Sexual Abuse Material) is another issue. YouTube also has that content. Meta also has that content, and they do not remove content related to child abuse. They do not remove content related to women. Both these rules of the Government of India are very strict, and on top of that, they do not listen to the Home Ministry. They do not listen to the IT Ministry either. So, we have said that in all these matters, and in many other matters, you know that the Chief Minister of the Congress government of Telangana has filed an FIR against Meta India. We have said that safe harbour should be removed in all these matters..."Earlier in the day, Meta apologised before the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Information Technology, saying the removal of PM Modi's Facebook video was the result of an error. According to ANI sources, several committee members questioned Meta officials and said the issue was not about an apology but about fixing accountability. Members also sought details on the company's action against controversial and objectionable content on its platforms.ANI sources said, "The Parliamentary Standing Committee on IT took a tough stance over the removal of PM Modiâs video from Facebook. Committee members also demanded legal action against the Meta official responsible for removing the video. Members further sought details from Meta on what action the company has taken regarding controversial and objectionable content present on its platforms. NDA states acted firmly against recruitment scams; opposition failed to curb irregularities: CM Dhami
Uttarakhand Chief MinisterPushkar Singh Dhami on Monday said that NDA-ruled states have taken firm action against recruitment scams and examination-related irregularities, while alleging that opposition-ruled states failed to curb such malpractices and were marked by widespread irregularities in recruitment processes.Speaking to reporters here, Dhami said that the Uttarakhand government had acted decisively against the "cheating mafia" by arresting and jailing over 100 people and enacting a stringent anti-cheating law."In all NDA-ruled states, wherever instances of cheating occurred, action was taken against the perpetrators. In Uttarakhand, we took action against a hundred members of the 'cheating mafia,' jailed them, and enacted a law specifically to curb cheating. Furthermore, recruitment drives were conducted and fully completed in strict accordance with the scheduled calendar," Dhami said.The Chief Minister contrasted this with states such as Jharkhand and Punjab and also referred to the previous Samajwadi Party government in Uttar Pradesh, alleging that recruitment processes between 2012 and 2017 were marred by irregularities."In contrast, consider states like Jharkhand, Punjab, or others.
Previously, between 2012 and 2017, Uttar Pradesh witnessed massive irregularities in recruitment and widespread cheating," he said.Targeting opposition parties, Dhami alleged that the Congress, Samajwadi Party, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), and their alliance partners were responsible for such irregularities."Be it the Congress Party, the Samajwadi Party, the AAP, or any of their alliance partners--they are the ones who committed all these wrongs, and the youth of the country understands this," he said.Referring to the Prime Minister's approach towards young people allegedly involved in such incidents, Dhami said the focus was on taking action against the masterminds rather than punishing those who may have been influenced."The PM chose not to subject these young people, who may have been misled or misguided for whatever reason, to legal hassles or punishment; instead, he forgave them," Dhami said.Launching a sharp attack on Opposition leaders following the registration of an FIR against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, Independent MP Pappu Yadav, and Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad over an alleged insult to Sanatan Dharma, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday stated that defaming saints represents the "lowest form of conduct imaginable."Addressing reporters in Dehradun, CM Dhami condemned the actions of the leaders, alleging that Pappu Yadav and his associates have consistently worked to malign Sanatan Dharma."To defame the saints is the lowest form of conduct imaginable. I had stated earlier as well that Pappu Yadav and the 'Pappu gang' have been working in tandem to continuously malign Sanatan Dharma," CM Dhami said.Taking a dig at the Opposition leaders over their stance on religious events, the Chief Minister pointed out that despite being extended invitations to the historic Ram Mandir Pran Pratishtha ceremony, none of them attended."When the Ram Mandir was being built, they were invited to the event, yet none of them attended; and today, they are engaging in this manner to defame our community of saints. I believe this reveals their true mindset regarding Sanatan Dharma," Dhami added.Highlighting his state administration's public outreach programs, Chief Minister Dhami also elaborated on the progress of the state government's 'Jan-Jan ki Sarkar' initiative. He emphasised that the drive is designed to bridge the gap between governance and citizens, especially those residing in remote regions."The objective of the 'Jan-Jan ki Sarkar' initiative is to bring the entire government administrative machinery to the people to resolve their issues," CM Dhami said. "This includes issuing certificates to those who lacked them and ensuring that people receive the benefits of various Central and State government schemes...
It provides facilities right at their doorstep for those living in the remotest areas."Providing key operational metrics on the public outreach campaign, the Chief Minister shared that the initiative has witnessed massive public participation across Uttarakhand."So far, over 6.5 lakh people have participated across both phases, and more than 60,000 individuals have received on-the-spot resolutions to their grievances," he stated.

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) leader Atul Limaye has alleged that the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led protest over the NEET-UG paper leak evolved into an "experiment for alternative politics", claiming that several political, student, labour and civil society organisations joined the agitation to propagate the idea of "subversion of democracy through democratic means."Addressing an ABVP event in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on July 30, Limaye said the protest should be "decoded" to understand its chronology, methodology, support system and ideological underpinnings. He also alleged that anti-Hindu and "anti-national" slogans were raised during the agitation and questioned how it transformed from a student-led protest into a broader political movement.
During his address, Limaye said, "In Today's times, CJP agitation should be studied as a case study. This has now come to the knowledge of everyone, but this was A phenomenon going on for years now. And if we have to study this whole agitation, we will have to see its full chronology, methodology and what their support system is, and the innovative system which they used and the ideology behind it. Of we see chronology, Abhijit Dipke was from our Marathwada itself. When he launched CJP, he got tremendous following (on social Media), and when he came back to India, he came back on 6th June and did his agitation on 7th."
Describing the course of the agitation, he added, "But he didn't receive the response which was expected. So, he roamed around the country from 7th to 19th. He started agitation in various cities of the country, or tried to start agitation, but even there did not get that kind of response. So, he started agitation, sit-in protest at Jantar Mantar from the 20th onwards, and gradually the face of the agitation got changed."According to Limaye, the movement later drew the participation of student organisations, labour unions, human rights groups, women's organisations, farmers' bodies and other civil society groups.He said, "What kind of things happened after that which changed the face of this agitation? What kind of support system did attach to this agitation? We need to see which organisations and institutions got attached to this agitation, and this will give us an idea of what kind of support system. This agitation obviously involved the youth, the students of the country. And that is why several student organisations got attached to it. Among the prominent organisations which were leading the stage in this protest was All India Student Association (AISA). And the second such Association was SFI."He further said, "Some human rights organisations, many tribal organisations, women organisations like Pinjra Tod joined them. Many Muslim organisations, Christian organisations, some institutions working in the legal sector, environment sector, journalistic associations also joined them. Some farmers' associations joined them, as Samyukta Kisan Morcha and Bharatiya Kisan Union joined them."Invoking Italian philosopher Antonio Gramsci's theory of cultural hegemony, Limaye argued that the protest was aimed at challenging democratic institutions and cultural values while operating within democratic processes.He said, "Why did the opposition to Hindus arise from the stage? Why were leaders from several political parties seen on the stage, and how did it convert from a student protest to a political protest? It was not limited to Delhi, but expanded in all the states. For this, we have to decode Yogendra Yadav's remark, 'Democracy's future now will not be decided in Parliament but on streets, elections will not decide, resistance will.' The cause of the protest was genuine, but who captured the movement? If we understand this, then we will understand this protest. There is a lot to learn. This protest was an experiment for an alternative politics."He added, "This theory states subversion of democracy through democratic means. This is well documented, and Italian scholar Gramsci gave the theory of cultural hegemony. He said that cultural hegemony needs to be destroyed for revolution. The deconstruction theory challenged Lord Ram and other figures. Alternative politics states that till there is a system, like our Parliamentary system, there cannot be revolution. All the systems, including the judiciary and police, need to be challenged."Claiming that such politics could be pursued either electorally or through weakening public faith in institutions, Limaye said, "There are two ways: one is election and the second is subversion of democracy through democratic means. There is infiltration in the judiciary, education system, and bureaucracy. Second is challenging the institutions and eroding faith in them. The results are so dangerous. Many police officers said the way the women were behaving, it was difficult to tolerate.
The way they were dressed and the language they used, we were ashamed. This was an attempt to degrade the culture."CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke rejected the allegations and said the RSS had no moral authority to describe others as anti-national. Responding to Limaye's remarks on Monday, Dipke referred to the period when the RSS was banned following Mahatma Gandhi's assassination.Abhijeet Dipke said, "People who murdered Mahatma Gandhi are calling us anti-national. The murderers of Mahatma Gandhi have no moral right to call anyone else anti-national. Nathuram Godse was the first anti-national."The CJP had led a 37-day protest at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak. The agitation was withdrawn on July 25 after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and the organisation said it had received assurances on its other key demands.

NEW DELHI: The Gujarat government has directed the state police to withdraw all criminal cases registered against students, youths and others who took part in recent protests over the alleged NEET-UG examination paper leak, officials said on Monday.With this, Gujarat has become the latest BJP-ruled state to withdraw FIRs against NEET protesters. Similar decisions have already been taken by the BJP governments in Assam, Bihar, Delhi and Maharashtra.In a July 31 letter to the state's Director General of Police GS Malik, the Gujarat home department cited the Supreme Court's July 28 judgment restraining police from taking coercive action against minor student protesters and directed the immediate withdrawal of all existing cases.The department instructed the police not to initiate any adverse legal or penal action against individuals who participated in the protests in the state. It further directed that if any FIRs or criminal cases had already been registered against protesters, the legal process for their withdrawal should be completed immediately.The communication, however, did not specify how many FIRs or criminal cases would be withdrawn.
Protests were held in Gujarat's Ahmedabad and several other cities in support of demonstrations at Delhi's Jantar Mantar against alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination.The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online satirical outfit that had been leading an indefinite sit-in at Jantar Mantar since June 21, called off its protest on July 25 following the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Besides seeking Pradhan's resignation, the CJP had demanded that no action be taken against its members or any NEET protesters across the country.The CJP has repeatedly warned that it would resume its agitation if the FIRs are not withdrawn.Meanwhile, the Supreme Court also clarified on Monday that the expression "criminal antecedents" in its July 28 order on releasing student protesters referred only to those involved in grave and heinous offences, and said states could close or withdraw FIRs against the remaining students in accordance with law.(With PTI inputs)

SC said states can withdraw FIRs against student who participated in NEET protests
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday observed that "neither a police officer using excessive force nor a hardened criminal under the garb of a student protest should be protected." These remarks came as it heard petitions related to the NEET-UG protest at Jantar Mantar on July 20.The apex court said states are free to close or withdraw FIRs registered against student protesters, provided it is done in accordance with law. The court also indicated that it may lay down guidelines on the use of pellet guns during protests.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana clarified that the term "criminal antecedents" refers only to grave and heinous offences, addressing concerns that students booked in minor or political cases could be denied relief.During the hearing, the CJI stressed that the court wanted to strike a balance between protecting peaceful protesters and ensuring accountability for serious offenders."A police officer involved in excessive force should not be unduly protected. And it should not be that a hardened criminal under the garb of student protest is also getting protected," the CJI observed.On allegations that pellet guns were used during the protest, the CJI said the court was considering issuing guidelines.
"We would like to lay down a protocol on how it can be used," he said.The bench noted that petitions had been filed both by protesters alleging excessive police force and by police personnel claiming they were injured during the violence.Appearing for the Centre, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the court that the Union government remained committed to its assurance that cases against student protesters would not be pursued, except in cases involving serious criminal offences.He said FIRs against more than 2,700 people with antecedents involving grave and heinous offences would not be withdrawn, according to ANI.Mehta also said there had been a misunderstanding regarding the government's stand on the issue. "Barring those with criminal antecedents, the government is prepared to address the cases against the student protesters. Let them sit with the government. There are some people who want to keep the pot boiling so we have to be cautious about the legal advice," he said.Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for some petitioners, urged the court to examine allegations of police excesses during the protest. He said the petitioners had submitted around 300 videos showing the alleged use of force."The videos are very shocking. We have given 300 videos to the court. Since directions have come from the top, the commissioner of police must look at all this," he said.He further submitted, "Ideally, we have identified un-uniformed individuals committing such police excess. A direction has to go to the Commissioner of Police and the RAF Director as to why police used pellet guns etc."Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi sought clarification on the expression "criminal antecedents", arguing that it should not include minor offences."These are students, somebody may have a driving violation or a petty offence, or due to a political case. The word criminal antecedent needs to be clarified," Singhvi said, according to Live Law.He urged the court to exclude petty offences and cases arising out of political protests from the definition. Last week, the apex court had indicated that it would constitute a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate the July 20 incident and directed authorities to preserve CCTV footage and other official records related to the protest.
The hearing comes days after the Supreme Court declined an oral plea seeking suo motu cognisance of the police action during the 'Chalo Sansad' protest.The court had earlier observed that police excesses or a lathi charge could not be justified merely because an agitation was taking place and underlined that the right to peaceful protest is "absolutely guaranteed."The matter has now been listed for further hearing on August 18.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday summoned Arunachal Pradesh chief secretary and principal secretary (home) over what it termed the state governmentâs ânon-cooperationâ in a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe involving family members of chief minister Pema Khandu.After perusing the CBIâs status report in the case, a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta directed both officers to appear before it on August 24 along with their responses to the report and explain the alleged non-cooperation.âWe have perused the status report given by the CBI dated July 17. They were backed by Shiv Sena, NCP-SP and other opposition MPs. Opposition also demanded a statement by Shah on police action on students.
Rijiju claimed there was no one in LS to guide Congress MPs. Opposition's demand is a separate issue. They must participate in discussions over the bills, he added. "Rahul Gandhi didn't even attend the House today. Congress has completely fallen apart. Such important bills are coming up but they are not participating," he said.Given the ongoing standoff in Parliament over opposition's twin demands, the BAC meeting indicated that the monsoon session may be headed towards a washout.Congress MP KC Venugopal said "Shah used to be very active in the previous sessions. Why is he not attending this session?" The Centre has provided assistance of Rs 2,536.96 crore in 263 flood mitigation projects in the northeastern states including Sikkim under the flood management and border areas programme (FMBAP), Jal Shakti ministry informed Rajya Sabha on Monday.
In a written reply, MoS (Jal Shakti) Raj Bhushan Choudhary said flood management and anti-erosion schemes are formulated and implemented by state governments as per respective priorities, while the Union government supplements their efforts through technical guidance and financial assistance for critical works.
Replying to a question on measures to tackle recurring floods and riverbank erosion in the Northeast, the minister said the FMBAP provides central assistance for flood control, anti-erosion and drainage development works.
"Since the inception of the programme up to March 2026, central assistance amounting to Rs 2,536.96 crore has been provided under FMBAP for 263 flood management projects in the North Eastern States, including Sikkim," he added.The Centre has provided assistance of Rs 2,536.96 crore in 263 flood mitigation projects in the northeastern states including Sikkim under the flood management and border areas programme (FMBAP), Jal Shakti ministry informed Rajya Sabha on Monday.
After inquiries into several complaints regarding poor food quality in trains and unhygienic pantry cars over the last three years, a fine of Rs 5.13 crore has been imposed on service providers, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has said in the Rajya Sabha.
“Indian Railways serve about 58 crore meals every year on average. About only 0.0008% complaints are received on average. Based on inquiry on these complaints during the last three years, a fine of Rs 5.13 crore has been imposed,” Vaishnaw said in a written reply on Friday.
“Indian Railways continuously endeavour to provide good quality and hygienic food items to the travelling passengers as per the prescribed norms. Necessary steps are accordingly taken by Indian Railways from time to time to ensure the same,” he said.
The minister highlighted several measures taken to improve quality, hygiene and food safety, including the supply of meals from designated base kitchens, the commissioning of modern base kitchens at identified locations and the installation of CCTV cameras in base kitchens for real-time monitoring of food preparation.
He also mentioned measures to promote electronic billing and digital payments on trains, including the installation of Point of Sale (POS) machines in pantry cars to facilitate digital billing and cashless transactions.

The Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) on the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, on Monday presented its report in Parliament, recommending adoption of the proposed legislation with a series of clause-wise modifications aimed at simplifying compliance, strengthening corporate governance and modernising India's corporate regulatory framework.
The report, tabled in Parliament - both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha follows months of consultations with government departments, regulators, industry bodies, legal experts, professional institutes and other stakeholders.
According to the committee, the Bill seeks to further ease compliance for businesses while improving investor protection and regulatory oversight through targeted amendments to the Companies Act, 2013 and the Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) Act, 2008.
According to the committee, the proposal strikes a balance between reducing procedural burdens and maintaining safeguards for incorporation.
The total annual passenger handling capacity at airports in the country has increased to more than 58 crore, the government said on Monday.
Minister of state for civil aviation Murlidhar Mohol told the Rajya Sabha that capacity augmentation and modernisation projects are undertaken from time to time by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) and other airport operators based on traffic growth, operational requirements, airline demand, financial viability and techno-economic considerations.
"As a result of these initiatives, the total passenger-handling capacity at airports across the country has been enhanced to over 580 million passengers per annum (MPPA), while passenger traffic handled during 2025-26 was about 420 million," he said in a written reply.
Currently, there are 166 airports in the country.
The pendency of GST refund claims has come down significantly over the past two years as of March 31, 2026, Parliament was informed on Monday.
In a written reply to the Lok Sabha, MoS (Finance) Pankaj Chaudhary said 64 claims involving a refund amount of about Rs 164 crore were pending for more than 60 days but up to 90 days as of March 31, 2026.
This is significantly lower than 907 claims involving a refund amount of Rs 274 crore at the end of FY24; and 374 claims involving a refund amount of Rs 246 crore as of FY25.
With regard to GST refunds, which are pending for more than 90 days, the number of claims has come down to 110 involving a claim of Rs 64 crore as of March 31, 2026.
This corresponds to 1,592 claims involving a refund of Rs 696 crore as of FY24 and 712 claims worth Rs 560 crore as of FY25.

Union minister for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Jitan Ram Manjhi moved the Bill for passage in the Upper House. The Bill was introduced in the Rajya Sabha on July 29.
The proposed legislation aims to improve cash flows for small businesses, curb delays in payments and simplify regulatory compliance, with the objective of enhancing the ease of doing business for micro, small and medium enterprises.
"This bill clearly indicates that the objective is to address the existing challenges of the MSME sector, reform the administrative framework, ease business payments, and promote regulatory compliance," said Jitan Ram Manjhi in the House.
The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026 seeks "to align the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 with the changing MSME landscape, to enhance the Ease of Doing Business and bring trust-based regulations in the MSME ecosystem."
The document further says the Bill proposes "to strengthen the mechanism for addressing delayed payments and provide for enforcement of arbitral awards for the MSEs, and to introduce flexibility and create enabling provisions for States to decide the composition of the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council (MSEFC), thereby forming more MSEFCs."

Before the Lok Sabha was adjourned for the day on Monday, the government introduced a Bill to replace British era legislation with the objective to include digital and virtual records as admissible evidence in the court of law in sync with digital dependence of the banking system.
Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman introduced the Bill.
The new law to be called the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 2026 is going to repeal or replace the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891.
"With the advancement of technology and growth of digital banking, bank records are increasingly created, stored and maintained using contemporary technology (instead of physical record). It has, therefore, become necessary to modernise and strengthen the existing legal framework to meet the requirements of the present banking system," the statement of objects and reasons of the Bill said.
The bill proposes to expand the scope of the definition of 'bankers' books' to include all forms of records maintained by banks, whether in physical, electronic, digital, virtual, cloud-based or in any other form, thereby providing a comprehensive, technology-neutral and future-ready legal framework, it said.
It proposes to provide for standardised certificate formats and authentication by manual or digital or electronic signature and to expressly recognise admissibility of electronic bank records and permit their production in either physical or electronic form.
It is also going to empower the central government to extend applicability of the proposed legislation to any entity or class of entities operating in the financial sector, subject to certain conditions, it said.
The Bill seeks to define the expression 'special cause', for which a court may, by order in writing, compel an officer of the bank to produce any bankers' books or to appear as witness to prove matters, transactions or accounts, in any legal proceeding where the bank is not a party.
The Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 was enacted during pre-independence era to facilitate the use of certified copies of bank records as evidence in legal proceedings without requiring production of the original records.
The Act was enacted at a time when banking records were predominantly maintained in physical form.

Parliament panel summons social media platforms at 4 pm
NEW DELHI: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology will meet representatives of major social media platforms, including Meta, X, Snapchat and Google on Monday to discuss online safety, user privacy and compliance with government rules.The meeting, scheduled for 4 pm, will focus on the digital safety of women and children, protection of data belonging to farmers, rural residents, labourers and the general public and how social media companies comply with laws related to public order.
BJP MP and committee chairperson Nishikant Dubey said the platforms had been summoned to explain the steps they were taking to safeguard user privacy and ensure compliance with government regulations."On 3 August 2026 at 4 PM, our Parliamentary Committee on IT and Communication has summoned Meta (Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp), X (Twitter), Snapchat, and Google," Dubey said."How will the privacy of women, children, farmers, rural folks, labourers, and the general public be protected? How do these companies ensure the government's public order?" he added.The meeting comes days after Meta briefly removed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Facebook video on action against examination paper leaks before restoring it.
Meta later said the video had been removed due to a technical error."The content was removed in error and has since been restored," a Meta spokesperson said.The video, released on July 23, was PM Modi's first direct address to Gen Z during the 36-day-long Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led agitation over alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG 2026 examination.
In the address, PM Modi assured students that the government would strengthen the legal framework against paper leaks by introducing stricter punishment and Special Fast-Track Courts.The Centre later introduced the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, proposing imprisonment of up to 10 years, higher monetary penalties and Special Fast-Track Courts for offences under the law.The student agitation ended on July 25 after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister. The Centre also reached an understanding with the CJP and activist Sonam Wangchuk to withdraw cases against protesters, prevent police intimidation and bring in stronger anti-paper leak legislation.

full_text:
An extremely rare pregnancy that developed outside the uterus, deep inside the abdomen near the kidneys (Representative image)
NEW DELHI: Doctors in Delhi have successfully treated a woman diagnosed with an extremely rare pregnancy that developed outside the uterus, deep inside the abdomen near the kidneys, using minimally invasive (keyhole) surgery.The woman, from Bengaluru, had initially presented for a routine pregnancy evaluation. During an ultrasound, doctors detected a 10-12 cm cystic structure, which was initially suspected to be a dermoid cyst because it appeared to contain fetal parts. However, an MRI revealed a far more unusual diagnosis.The scan showed uterine dehiscence, in which the uterine wall had ruptured, allowing the pregnancy to develop in the retroperitoneal space, close to the kidneys and major blood vessels, including the aorta and inferior vena cava. Doctors found a 12-week fetus measuring about 7-8 cm inside the cyst.Dr Mannan Gupta, Founder and Chairman, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Elantis Healthcare, said the pregnancy was neither inside the uterus nor in the fallopian tube or ovary, where most ectopic pregnancies occur.
"Initially, the ultrasound findings suggested a dermoid cyst. However, MRI revealed an exceptionally rare condition. The pregnancy was located in the retroperitoneal space near the kidneys and major blood vessels.
This is one of the rarest forms of pregnancy and the first such case I have encountered in my career," he said.Doctors performed the procedure laparoscopically, avoiding a major abdominal incision. Given the proximity of the pregnancy to vital organs and major blood vessels, the surgery required meticulous planning and precision. Doctors said the patient had an excellent postoperative outcome.According to the treating doctors, retroperitoneal pregnancy is estimated to occur in about one in 30,000 pregnancies. They said early diagnosis and timely intervention are critical, as delayed treatment can result in life-threatening complications because of the pregnancy's proximity to major blood vessels and vital organs.

headline: SC said that cruelty does not distinguish between married and unmarried women

full_text:
SC said that cruelty does not distinguish between married and unmarried women
NEW DELHI: Saying that "live-in relationships" are a reality particularly in urban areas and the law must adapt itself to serve those who choose this form of relationship and protect them from harassing partners, the Supreme Court Monday brought them under the ambit of Section 498A of the IPC or Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) where a husband or in-law shall be punished with imprisonment for a term up to three years for subjecting a woman to cruelty.A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and N K Singh rejected the plea that 498A is confined only to a husband married to a woman in the traditional sense. "Since the provision was aimed at solving a societal issue, it is this larger objective of securing equality for women, stepping away from the superiority of males that is an inheritance from bygone days, that has to inform the understanding in interpretation and implementation of the Section," SC said.It, however, clarified that only those "live-in relationships" which are in the nature of marriage will come within the ambit of Section 498A of IPC or Sec 85 of BNS. "Cruelty does not check at the door whether the house it's entering is that of a married woman or not. Once it enters, its propensity to destroy is aggravated," it said.SC, however, took note of the growing instances of alleged misuse of Section 498A. Describing as worrisome the trend of the section being misused and employed as a means of settling scores and ventilating grievances, SC said its verdict would be applicable to only those 'relationships in the nature of marriage' and the initial burden of proof would be on the female live-in partner seeking protection of the law.
"When the objective of the Section 498A was to provide coverage to those cases where harassment by husband or in-laws through wilful conduct causing mental or physical injury or driving the woman to suicide, then to say that such harassment can only be caused when they are married and not before that, in our considered view, would be a case of over simplification. Whether or not the woman in question is married or not, in the present day, does not have a proximate link to the objective of the section, which is to prevent cruelty in such a household setting," Justice Karol, who penned the verdict, said.The court said the law must respond to changing times, and bringing live-in relations within the ambit of Section 498A is needed. "Marriage was considered to be sacrosanct, which undoubtedly is a changing phenomenon. Living together, prior to marriage, is not unheard of or unacceptable anymore. In the same way, that same-sex relations, once criminalised and deemed to be a mental illness, have now been decriminalised and recognised as naturally occurring.
This is the evolution of societal standards," SC said."Not a single person goes into a relationship knowing or anticipating that cruelty may be meted out to them. When a couple sets out on their journey, it is always, one presumes, with the best of intentions and to bring joyfulness of all forms. With the passage of time, however, some relationships may go down this troublesome path. The law must provide for the same. This distinction between "married" and "live-in relationship in the nature of marriage", in as much as it relates to the protection envisaged by Section 498A, has no rational nexus with the object of preventing domestic violence and is as such offensive to Article 14 of the Constitution," the bench said.
