full_text:
Politics often comes wrapped in familiar assumptions. With the BJP, the ruling party at the Centre, now also in power in a majority of states, either alone or in alliance, one might expect a degree of sameness in the profiles of Indiaâs chief ministers. Yet the Association for Democratic Reforms reports show a more varied picture. The countryâs CMs come from different social strata, age groups, educational backgrounds and economic profiles, even within their own parties. There is no single formula for political ascent.That is what makes the comparison between ADRâs 2025 and 2026 reports more revealing than either report viewed alone. The 2025 study examined 30 chief ministers, since Manipur was then under Presidentâs Rule. The 2026 report covers 31, after the return of a chief minister in the state. More importantly, the occupants of the chief ministerâs office changed in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Bihar and West Bengal.
South pulls the wealth map
The combined assets declared by Indiaâs chief ministers rose from Rs 1,632 crore in the 2025 report to Rs 3,660 crore in 2026. Average assets more than doubled from Rs 54.42 crore to Rs 118.07 crore. The number of billionaire chief ministers rose from two to four.
In 2025, N Chandrababu Naidu, with assets of Rs 931.84 crore, and Pema Khandu, with Rs 332.57 crore, were the only billionaire chief ministers. Siddaramaiah was a distant third with Rs 51.94 crore. A year later, Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar is the clear number one with Rs 1,413.8 crore, while cine star and Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay declared assets of Rs 648.86 crore. Together, these four account for approximately Rs 3,327 crore, or 90.9% of the assets declared by all 31 chief ministers. The remaining 27 account for only around Rs 333 crore between them.
Analysing the assets held by CMs
A geographical cut makes the imbalance sharper. Using a broad four-zone grouping, not an ADR classification, the South has only six of the 31 CMs but accounts for roughly Rs 3,059 crore, or about 83.6% of all declared CM assets in 2026. That is because three of the four billionaire CMs, Shivakumar, Naidu and Vijay, are from southern states. So the South, in a way, lives up to the larger-than-life CM personalities. Naidu is a veteran politician who has survived many ebbs to rise again and regain his lost glory. D K Shivakumar finally got rewarded after a power tussle with Siddaramaiah, and Vijay was the new kid on the block who broke through the DMK-AIADMK binary, while also ticking the box of another cine star to become CM of Tamil Nadu. So the profiles of these billionaire CMs could not be more different.East and the Northeast together have the largest number of CMs in this grouping, 12, but account for about Rs 495 crore, helped substantially by Khanduâs declaration. North and Central India together have 10 CMs but only around Rs 75 crore in declared assets, while the West has three CMs and around Rs 31 crore.
Same party, different worlds
The party-wise picture is just as uneven. The BJP has 17 chief ministers in the 2026 list, but they are far from a single economic bloc. Its richest CM is Pema Khandu, with Rs 332.57 crore in declared assets. Its poorest is West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari, with about Rs 85.88 lakh. That is a nearly 387-fold gap within the same party.The Congress spread is smaller in headcount but sharper in scale. Of its four CMs, Shivakumar alone accounts for Rs 1,413.8 crore. At the other end is Kerala CM V D Satheesan, with Rs 6.66 crore. Revanth Reddy, at Rs 30.05 crore, and Himachal Pradesh CM Sukhvinder Singh, at Rs 7.82 crore, sit far below Shivakumarâs level. In effect, Congressâs CM asset profile is overwhelmingly shaped by one leader.This is why the average can mislead. A calculation based on individual entries puts the 2026 median at only around Rs 8.23 crore, barely higher than the 2025 median of about Rs 8.02 crore.Total declared liabilities rose from roughly Rs 242 crore in 2025 to nearly Rs 505 crore in 2026, though the number of CMs declaring liabilities of Rs 1 crore or more remained unchanged at 11. Khandu led the 2025 liability table with Rs 180.28 crore. In 2026, Shivakumar moved to the top with Rs 265.07 crore, followed by Khandu and Himanta Biswa Sarma.
Younger leaders, uneven party trend
The leadership profile also became younger. In 2025, 12 of the 30 chief ministers were in the 51-60 group. By 2026, that number had risen to 17. The number aged 61 or above fell from 10 to six. The 41-50 category remained unchanged at eight.
India now has younger CMs
The average reported age declined from 58.8 to 56.7, though the median remained 56. The shift reflects the exit of several older CMs, including Siddaramaiah, Pinarayi Vijayan, Nitish Kumar, M K Stalin and Mamata Banerjee. The ages are those recorded when election affidavits were filed, not necessarily current ages. So the actual decline is much sharper because the 2025 calculation accounted for many outgoing CMsâ 2021 affidavits.Here again, parties differ internally. Congressâs four CMs are tightly bunched. Revanth Reddy is 56, Sukhvinder Singh 58, Shivakumar 60 and Satheesan 61. The BJPâs spread is wider. It has Pema Khandu at 44 and Manik Saha at 70, with several CMs clustered in their 50s. In other words, the Congress CM cohort is smaller and more middle-aged, while the BJPâs larger pool stretches from younger leadership to older veterans.There was a reversal on gender. The 2025 report listed two women among 30 chief ministers. The 2026 report lists only one among 31. Mamata Banerjeeâs exit from the CM roster left Delhiâs Rekha Gupta as the sole woman in the group.
Degrees stay broadly stable
Many of the politicians are products of student politics. They may not have worked professionally, but they still believed in the inherent importance of formal education. In 2025, 25 of the 30 CMs were graduates, professional graduates, postgraduates or doctorate holders. In 2026, the number remained 25, despite the larger group. The proportion with graduate-level qualification or higher slipped slightly, from about 83% to 81%.Within parties, the BJP shows the widest educational spread. Its CM list includes doctorate holders such as Mohan Yadav, Himanta Biswa Sarma and Samrat Choudhary, but also leaders listed as Class 10 pass, diploma holders, graduates, professional graduates and postgraduates. Congressâs four CMs are more compact educationally: Shivakumar and Sukhvinder Singh are postgraduates, Revanth Reddy is a graduate and Satheesan is a graduate professional.
Cases rise, but cluster in five names
The criminal-record figures worsened modestly. In 2025, 12 of 30 chief ministers, or 40%, had declared criminal cases; 10 had cases classified by ADR as serious. By 2026, 14 of 31, or 45%, had declared criminal cases; 11 had serious cases.The combined number of declared cases rose from 187 to 195. The burden remained concentrated. Revanth Reddy continued to head the list with 89 cases, followed by Suvendu Adhikari with 29, Shivakumar and Naidu with 19 each, and Keralaâs V D Satheesan with 18. Five chief ministers accounted for 174 of the 195 cases, or 89.2%.
Criminal cases against CMs
Three of Congressâs four CMs are among the top five by declared cases: Revanth Reddy, Shivakumar and Satheesan. Among BJP CMs, Adhikari carries the highest declared case load, while several BJP chief ministers have no declared criminal cases. Geography shows a similar concentration, though for different reasons. The six southern CMs together account for 147 declared cases, driven mainly by Revanth Reddy, Shivakumar, Naidu and Satheesan. East and the Northeast account for 38 cases, led by Adhikari. North and Central India account for six, while the West accounts for four. It is perhaps not a coincidence that many of the CMs with high case loads were opposition leaders for a significant time.
Thus, criminal cases need to be treated with caution. A low case count may not strictly be a virtue; it may just be a case of friendly police administration. Disclosures arenât the only way to understand the nature of a politician. But they are an important starting point, particularly when compared over the years, to understand how the seat of power remains the same, but the nature of those who occupy it changes, perhaps as an inevitable reflection of the realities of the times.

Tamil Nadu moves SC over water allocation
NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu government on Monday approached the Supreme Court over the Cauvery water-sharing dispute, alleging that the quantum of water allocated by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) and the amount released by neighbouring Karnataka fell short of its entitlement.The petition was filed on the directions of chief minister C Joseph Vijay after consultations with senior advocates, according to an official release.
"On the direction of the chief minister, to find a solution to this issue and get Tamil Nadu's due share of water on time, a petition has been filed in the Supreme Court," the release said.The petition said that, as of August 3, the combined storage in Karnataka's four major Cauvery reservoirsâKrishna Raja Sagar (KRS), Kabini, Harangi and Hemavathiâstood at 77.537 thousand million cubic feet (TMC), and argued that the state was in a position to release Tamil Nadu's proportionate share without difficulty.It further stated that following recent rainfall in the catchment areas of the KRS and Kabini reservoirs, the proportionate flow due to Tamil Nadu at the Biligundlu gauging station should have been 26.954 TMC."Accordingly, the Cauvery Water Management Authority order allocating 4.536 TMC is very less," the release added.The petition alleged that Karnataka had "failed" to release Tamil Nadu's due share of Cauvery water, which it said stood at 26.954 TMC.
It added that Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay directed the state to move the Supreme Court, on the advice of senior advocates, to secure a "due order".The move comes amid renewed tensions between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu over the sharing of Cauvery waters during the ongoing monsoon season. Last week, the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) upheld the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee's recommendation directing Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of water per day to Tamil Nadu for 15 days.
The CWMA was constituted by the Centre in 2018 following the Supreme Court's final verdict on the decades-old Cauvery river water dispute involving Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala and Puducherry. The authority comprises representatives of the four riparian states along with a nominee of the central government and is tasked with overseeing the implementation of the court-mandated water-sharing arrangement.

TRAI MyCall app gives telecom service providers information on areas where network performance needs improvement
NEW DELHI: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India has revamped the "TRAI MyCall', a mobile application that enables telecom consumers to directly assess and report the voice-calling experience. A citizen-centric digital platform that allows telecom consumers to share real-time feedback on their voice-calling experience, TRAI MyCall app gives telecom service providers (TSPs) information on areas where network performance needs improvement and take targeted corrective measures.TRAI says the revamped app offers instant rating of voice calls through a simple 1-5 star feedback system; reporting of specific issues such as call drops, echo during calls, audio delay, cross connection, voice breaking, one party unable to hear the other, and calls taking too long to connect, which shall be available to respective service provider for corrective action; automatic post-call feedback and coverage test feature to assess signal strength.TRAI chairman Anil Kumar Lahoti said: âEvery telecom consumer experiences network quality first-hand. The revamped TRAI MyCall app is expected to strengthen consumer participation feedback on telecom service quality by enabling subscribers to provide immediate and perceived feedback on their call experience. The feedback will assist Telecom Service Providers in identifying network deficiencies and taking corrective measures, enhanced customer satisfaction, and a better overall mobile communication experience.
The initiative reinforces TRAI's commitment to a consumer-centric, transparent, and data-driven approach to improving the quality of telecom services. I encourage all mobile users to download the TRAI MyCall application and regularly share their feedback. Every feedback matters, and together we can build a better calling experience for every telecom consumer.ââWith over one billion telecom subscribers in India, voice calling remains the most fundamental telecom service and is often the first indicator of network quality experienced by consumers. While network performance is evaluated using technical quality of service (QoS) parameters, the quality of experience (QoE) perceived by consumers also provides an important perspective on service performance. TRAI MyCall bridges this gap by combining consumer feedback with relevant network information to facilitate a more comprehensive assessment of telecom service quality,â TRAI said in a statement.

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Monday told the Supreme Court that it wants to place on record the process and safeguards adopted right from the printing of the NEET question paper to its distribution among students.Appearing for the Centre, Solicitor General (SG) Tushar Mehta informed a bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe that the government would explain the methodology and place it on record through an affidavit. Mehta sought time for hearing on Thursday or Friday.The bench replied that it would also like to know the process and posted a batch of pleas seeking additional safeguards for NEET question papers for hearing on Thursday.During an earlier hearing on June 24 too, the Supreme Court had said it would "closely monitor" the steps taken to curb future NEET examination paper leaks.The top court was then hearing a batch of petitions, including one filed by the Federation of All India Medical Association (FAIMA). It told Mehta that the government should indicate the steps taken towards ensuring transparency, implementing the recommendations of the Radhakrishnan Committee and following the IIT model.
"Students' futures can't be jeopardised. We are going beyond the Radhakrishnan Committee. I assure you that the government is walking 10 extra miles. I can assure you everything is being supervised at the highest level," the ASG had submitted at the time.
On May 12, the National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the NEET-UG examination held on May 3 amid allegations of a paper leak. The retest was conducted on June 21.The paper leak allegations are being investigated by the CBI.After allegations of NEET-UG question paper leaks in 2024, the Supreme Court had refused to cancel the medical entrance test but issued various directions aimed at preventing paper leaks and laid down criteria for cancelling public examinations.Following the 2024 leak, the ministry of education had constituted a seven-member committee headed by former Isro chief K Radhakrishnan to recommend reforms in the examination process, improvement in data security protocols, and the structure and functioning of the NTA.(With PTI inputs)

The Supreme Court permitted governments to withdraw cases against student protesters.
NEW DELHI: Paving the way for the dropping of cases against student protesters, Supreme Court on Monday permitted Delhi and state govts to withdraw or close FIRs lodged during NEET paper leak protests in different parts of India and said these youngsters must be allowed to pursue their studies without the fear of getting prosecuted.The bench clarified its July 28 order in which it had stayed coercive action against student protesters but permitted police to proceed with the investigations. This had created an apprehension in the minds of students about the future consequences of the cases remaining live.The go-ahead came after solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that âgovt is serious about honouring the commitment (given to CJP) on withdrawal of cases against student protesters. We are discussing the modalities of dropping casesâ.However, Mehta said that FIRs registered during student protests against 2,738 people who had criminal antecedents â having been accused of rape, murder and child sexual abuse under Pocso Act â and had infiltrated the protests to indulge in violence and vandalism will not be dropped. The bench said the rider would apply to those accused of heinous and grave offences and not petty offences or political cases.
Want to lay down norms on use of graded force, says SCMehta said, âThose who were leading the protests are again in touch with govt to work out the modalities for dropping cases against genuine student protesters as withdrawal of cases may not be possible under the law.â The top court posted the matter for further hearing on Aug 18.CJI Kant was firm that student protesters must be freed from the fear of future prosecution. He said, âParameters for students are altogether different. Their cases should be considered in a different manner so that they remain in the mainstream and their education is not disturbed.âThe parents are spending their hard-earned money on their childrenâs education. We must not keep aside the expectations of the parents of these youngsters. If the children are unnecessarily dragged into such (police and court) processes, it is not going to serve any purpose,â the CJI said.The solicitor general agreed and said modalities for the withdrawal/dropping of cases against student protesters will be worked out soon. He added, âThere will be some people who would like to keep the pot boiling â we must be very careful even while taking legal steps.âJustice Bagchi said that when the parties agree to it, the court can engender and enable the process so that the FIRs do not remain hanging over studentsâ heads.Senior advocate Vrinda Grover said both CJP leaders and other students are in talks with the SG and govt to chart out an agreed modality for the dropping of cases. She cited a Patna FIR registered against 142 people and 5,000 unknown persons, and said this appeared to be âcatch allâ tactics to pick up anyone randomly in the future. A comprehensive mechanism needs to be evolved, she said.Justice Bagchi said, âThere are many options. The prosecution can file a closure report, the public prosecutor can advise withdrawal of cases or we can quash the FIRs.âThe CJI-led bench said that while the violence and police excesses would be investigated by an SIT, âwe want to lay down comprehensive guidelines for the future on use of graded force, whether it should include pellet guns or not, after getting recommendations from the high-powered committee we intend to constituteâ.
Senior advocate Shyam Divan said the committee/commission should be headed by a retired CJI. The bench said getting a former CJI to head the committee is difficult, and it will be chaired by a former SC judge. It asked Delhi Police, Centre and states to file their responses to the petition and give their suggestions on the terms of reference of the committee.Senior advocate N Hariharan questioned how Delhi Police could identify 2,738 criminals among the protesters and said they must have used face recognition devices on all protesters and profiled them, which is a serious violation of privacy of the individuals guaranteed under Article 21.

NEW DELHI: Former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh on Monday said he "had complete faith that justice would be done" and "never felt guilty" after a Delhi court acquitted him in the sexual harassment case filed by women wrestlers.Reiterating that the case was a "conspiracy", the ex-BJP MP said he had maintained from the very beginning that he would "hang myself" if even one of the allegations against him was proved.
His remarks came after Delhi's Rouse Avenue Court acquitted Singh and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar in the case.Reacting to the verdict, Brij Bhushan said, "I said this was a conspiracy, and if any of the allegations against me are found to be true, I will hang myself. To this day, I've stood by that statement. Today, after almost three years, the court has honorably acquitted me and Vinod... I always stood up for those who were weak, those whose rights were violated.""I had complete faith that justice would be done to me, and I never felt guilty... We were fighting for the junior athletes whose rights were being violated, and I am happy that we won that fight," he added.
Referring to the court's verdict, the former WFI chief further noted, "The honourable judge said that Brij Bhushan Singh and Vinod Tomar are acquitted with honour.
From the very first day, I had said that if even a single allegation against me was proved, I would be ready to face the harshest punishment."He further noted, "I have not just been acquitted, I have been acquitted with honour... Struggle brings refinement... I have nothing to say to those who were against me."Calling the verdict a "moment of happiness", he added, "Today, the court has acquitted us with honour and it is a matter of happiness for me. What I had said on the first day has turned out to be true. I did not know what the other side was thinking, but my first reaction was that the truth would prevail. Today is a moment of happiness."Brij Bhushan also quoted a verse from the Ramcharitmanas after the judgment saying, "à¤¹à¥à¤à¤¹à¤¿ à¤¸à¥à¤ à¤à¥ à¤°à¤¾à¤® à¤°à¤à¤¿ à¤°à¤¾à¤à¤¾à¥¤" (What is meant to be will be, as destined by Lord Ram.)
The case stemmed from allegations made by six women wrestlers, following which Delhi Police filed a chargesheet against the former BJP MP on June 15, 2023. He was charged under sections 354 (assault or criminal force to a woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 354A (sexual harassment), 354D (stalking) and 506 (criminal intimidation) of the Indian Penal Code.Following protests by the wrestlers at Delhi's Jantar Mantar in 2023, Delhi Police registered an FIR and later filed a nearly 1,500-page chargesheet against Brij Bhushan, invoking provisions related to sexual harassment, assault or criminal force against a woman, stalking and criminal intimidation under the Indian Penal Code.
Tomar was also named as a co-accused.After hearing final arguments from both the prosecution and the defence, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (ACJM) Ashwani Panwar had reserved the judgment last month. The proceedings were conducted in a closed courtroom, and August 3 was fixed for pronouncement of the verdict.During the trial, the court heard submissions from senior advocate Rebecca John, appearing for the complainants, while the defence was led by advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati. The court also examined members of the Special Investigation Team (SIT) and the investigating officer before delivering its verdict.
